papers.title: Countable models of one-dimensional Peano continua
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that a one-dimensional Peano continuum $X$ admits a weak homotopy equivalence $X\to C$ to a countable space $C$ if and only if the wild set $\mathbf{w}(X)$ is countable.

papers.title: There Are Exactly $2^\mathfrak{c}$ Simultaneously Bireflective and Bicoreflective Subconstructs of $\mathbf{FTS}$
papers.abstract: We prove that there are exactly $2^\mathfrak{c}$ simultaneously bireflective and bicoreflective subconstructs of $\mathbf{FTS}$. By the Lowen--Wuyts bijection, these correspond to the total fuzzy topologies contained in $M$, the fuzzy topology consisting of all nondecreasing left-continuous self-maps of the unit interval. The upper bound follows from a cardinality estimate. The matching lower bound is obtained by encoding $2^{\mathfrak c}$ ultrafilters on $\mathbb N$ into total fuzzy topologies contained in $M$.

papers.title: On the Luxemburg Functional in the Concave Regime with an Application to Nonlocal Differential Equations
papers.abstract: For $p:[0,1]\to(0,1)$ a continuous function, we consider the Luxemburg functional \[ \Lambda_{p(\cdot)}(u):=\inf\left\{\delta>0:\int_0^1\left|\frac{u(t)}{\delta}\right|^{p(t)}\,dt\leq 1\right\}. \] We develop a suitable functional analytic framework for $\Lambda_{p(\cdot)}$ so that it can be incorporated into a positive order cone, which can then be used in the analysis of nonlocal differential equations having the general form \[ -A\left(\int_0^1 b(1-s)(u(s))^{p(s)}\,ds\right)u''(t) =\lambda f(t,u(t)),\qquad t\in(0,1). \] By means of a specific numerical example, we demonstrate that, as opposed to a methodology relying only on the supremum norm, our methodology via the Luxemburg functional yields an appreciably sharper localisation of any solutions of the nonlocal equation.

papers.title: Soft normed linear spaces via soft elements: decomposition, convergence, and operators
papers.abstract: Let $F\colon A\to\mathcal{P}(X)$ be a soft linear subspace of a linear space $X$ over $\mathbb{K}$. Its soft elements form the product $\prod_{t\in A}F(t)$. We use this representation to characterize selection spaces, decompose soft norms and soft linear operators into their sectionwise parts, and compare soft, uniform, and componentwise convergence. We also characterize completeness and continuity in the box, extended-supremum, and product settings. Neumann-series and fixed-point results are obtained as applications.

papers.title: A functional model for hyponormal contractions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical model for a class of hyponormal contractions $T$ satisfying $Ran[T^*,T] \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}\ominus \mathcal D_T$, where $\mathcal D_{T^*}$ and $\mathcal D_T$ are the associated defect spaces for $T$. We also show that, under a certain condition, a contraction $T$ with $\mathcal D_T \subseteq \mathcal D_{T^*}$ is hyponormal.

papers.title: Quaternionic Buzano-Dragomir Inequality and Deutsch Entropic Uncertainty Principle
papers.abstract: We show that the Buzano-Dragomir inequality holds for quaternionic Hilbert spaces. Using this generalization, we derive the Dragomir inequality for the quaternionic numerical radius and Deutsch entropic uncertainty principle for quaternionic Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: A Counterexample to a Bourgain-Brezis Sum-Space Estimate
papers.abstract: A question of Bourgain and Brezis, later restated as Open Problem 7.1 by Brezis, asks whether the $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ norm of a mean-zero scalar function is controlled by the ambient $H^{-1/2}+L^1$ sum norm of its gradient. We show that this estimate fails in every dimension $N\geq 2$. More precisely, for every integer $K\geq 16$, we construct a smooth real-valued mean-zero function $\Phi_K$ on $\mathbb{T}^N$ such that $|\nabla\Phi_K|{H^{-1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+L^1(\mathbb{T}^N)}\leq C$ and $|\Phi_K|{H^{1/2}(\mathbb{T}^N)+W^{1,1}(\mathbb{T}^N)}\geq cK^{1/4}-C$, where the absolute constants $c,C>0$ are independent of $N$ and $K$. Equivalently, the ratio of the gradient-constrained decomposition cost to the ambient decomposition cost is unbounded. The construction applies the Hodge projection to a smooth approximation of a normal vector measure on a codimension-one sheet. Its potential records lacunary partial sums at geometrically separated distances from the sheet. A scale-path lower bound, combined with an odd critical Hardy inequality, excludes uniformly bounded $H^{1/2}+W^{1,1}$ decompositions.

papers.title: A Radon-Nikod\'{y}m theorem for Fuzzy Number Multimeasures in Locally Convex Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a Radon-Nikodym theorem for dominated fuzzy number multimeasures defined on $\Sigma$ and taking values in $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$, where $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ is a complete finite measure space and $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$ is the family of generalized fuzzy numbers on a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space $X$, i.e., a map $u: X \to [0,1]$ is a member of $\mathcal{F}_{cwk}(X)$, if and only if for each $\alpha \in (0,1]$ the $\alpha$-cut $[u]^{\alpha}$ of $u$ is a member of the family $cwk(X)$ of all nonempty convex and weakly compact subsets of $X$, ($[u]^{\alpha} = \{x \in X: u(x) \geq \alpha \}$).

papers.title: Exact $L^2$ convergence through the wavelet and tent space characterizations of $h^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $0<p\le 1$
papers.abstract: We extend the wavelet and tent space characterization of $h^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ to $0<p\le 1$ via a local dyadic tent space $t_p$, and derive the unconditional $L^2$-convergence of the resulting atomic decomposition, with an exact error identity refining Ding, Jiang and Zhu (2019).

papers.title: Observable diameter of product measures with a power-type interior zero
papers.abstract: We determine the asymptotic order of the observable diameter of $\ell^p$-product spaces associated with a probability measure on $[0,1]$ whose density has a power-type interior zero. Different vanishing orders are allowed on the two sides of the zero. For every $1 \le p \le \infty$, we obtain sharp two-sided estimates and show that the asymptotic order is governed by the larger of the two vanishing orders. In the case $p=2$, the transition occurs exactly at the threshold for the spectral gap.

papers.title: Accelerating Langevin Dynamics with Weighted Laplacian Flow: Global Well-Posedness and Exponential Convergence
papers.authors: Ziyue Cai, Weiye Gan, Borui Miao, Zuoqiang Shi
papers.abstract: We study an accelerated Langevin equation in which the classical overdamped Langevin drift is supplemented by a nonlocal gradient velocity determined through a target-weighted Poisson equation. The target $p$ is only assumed to be strictly positive and need not be normalized. Writing the dynamics in terms of $\omega=\log(p/q)$ yields a coupled parabolic-elliptic system whose parabolic component contains the usual Langevin diffusion, whereas the elliptic component generates a global transport. The system is invariant under multiplication of $p$ by a positive constant. On a bounded smooth domain with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, we establish global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for strictly positive $C^{2+\alpha}$ target weights and compatible $C^{2+\alpha}$ initial data. For long-time behavior, the oscillation of $\omega$ decays at the explicit rate $e^{-t}$ and the solution density exponentially converges to target density. Moreover, an exact entropy-dissipation identity holds relative to the target density, in which the relative Fisher information and the Jeffreys divergence give the two dissipation mechanisms associated with the Langevin and weighted-Poisson components. In particular, KL divergence also converges to zero with rate $e^{-t}$ without a convexity assumption on the target.

papers.title: Algebraic properties of Truncated Toeplitz $+$ Truncated Hankel operators
papers.authors: Kritika Babbar, Satyabrata Majee, Amit Maji
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the algebraic properties of $\mathcal{S}_\theta$---the class of truncated Toeplitz plus truncated Hankel operators --- on the model space $\mathcal{K}_\theta$. We also give a complete characterization of the intersection class of truncated Toeplitz and truncated Hankel operators under certain conditions. As applications, we describe the non-uniqueness of a decomposition $T=A+B$, show that self-adjoint operators admit self-adjoint decompositions, give a necessary and sufficient inclusion criterion for $\mathcal{S}_\theta$ when $\theta$ is a finite Blaschke product, and, from a first-order commutator characterization of $\mathcal{S}_\theta$, describe the products of its elements and the operators commuting with $S_\theta+ S_\theta^{*}$.

papers.title: Elementary Moves on Ideal Webs, Local Monodromies on Hitchin Fibrations, and Tropical Mutations on $\mathrm{K_0}$ Groups
papers.abstract:
This paper builds on the work of Goncharov by studying the correspondence between topological spectral covers constructed from generic $A_{m-1}$-webs with rank $m\ge2$, Hitchin spectral curves over good Hitchin loci, and the Grothendieck groups $K_0(\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma})$ associated with the quivers with potential $(Q_{\Gamma},W_{\Gamma})$ assigned to corresponding bipartite $A_{m-1}$-graphs.
  We show that the automorphisms on the non-frozen quiver lattices $\Lambda_{\Gamma}^{\circ}$ induced by compositions of elementary moves on ideal webs/bipartite graphs are the same as the Gauss--Manin monodromy actions on the $SL_m$ Hitchin fiber lattices $H_1(\operatorname{Prym}(\Sigma);\mathbb{Z})$ locally around discriminant loci. And the Gauss--Manin monodromy actions agree with the automorphisms on the Grothendieck groups $K_0(\mathcal{D}_{\Gamma}^{\circ})$ induced by compositions of mutations on the quivers with potential $(Q_{\Gamma},W_{\Gamma})$.

papers.title: K3 surfaces with finite automorphism group in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We classify K3 surfaces with finite automorphism group in positive characteristic. The classification is the same as over the complex numbers, except when the base field is $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$.

papers.title: Two-sided logarithmic estimates of the Lebesgue constants with respect to Vilenkin systems
papers.abstract: We introduce a new logarithmic digit variation for Vilenkin--Fourier partial sums and establish two-sided estimates for the corresponding Lebesgue constants with universal constants. These estimates hold for both bounded and unbounded Vilenkin systems. As an application, we show that bounded logarithmic variation yields uniform boundedness of the corresponding partial-sum operators on \(L_1\), \(L_1\)-norm convergence for every integrable function, and almost everywhere convergence.

papers.title: Character cyclic amenability of Banach algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the notion of character cyclic amenability for Banach algebras, which combines the cyclicity condition on derivations with the character-dependent module structure arising in character amenability. We establish several basic properties of this notion and investigate its behavior under standard Banach algebra constructions. In particular, we study character cyclic amenability for opposite algebras, projective tensor products, l1-direct sums, quotient algebras, dense homomorphic images, and theta-Lau products. We also provide examples illustrating the relationship between character cyclic amenability and other amenability-type properties, including examples showing that character cyclic amenability does not imply cyclic amenability. Finally, we characterize character cyclic amenability for module extension Banach algebras in terms of phi-cyclic derivations and derivations associated with the underlying Banach module.

papers.title: Motivic $C_p$-power operations in $\mathrm{MGL}$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a new proof of the Hopkins-Morel-Hoyois theorem for fields $k$ of characteristic unequal to $p$ containing all primitive $p$-power roots of unity for a fixed prime $p$. This new proof follows Quillen's proof for the structure of the homotopy groups of $\mathrm{MU}$ which utilizes topological power operations. To this end we define a motivic analog of the Steenrod power operations, using the theory of normed motivic spectra as developed by Bachmann--Hoyois and their application for the definition of motivic colimits as developed by Bachmann-Elmanto-Heller.

papers.title: Bornologies and Kuratowski-Painlev\'e Convergence to the Empty Set Revisited
papers.authors: Basile Beyer de Ryke, Gerald Beer
papers.abstract: Let $(X,\tau)$ be a noncompact metrizable space and let $\langle T_n\rangle$ be a sequence of nonempty closed sets converging to the empty set in the sense of Kuratowski--Painlev\'e. The subsets of $X$ whose closures meet at most finitely many terms form a bornology $\mathcal B_\tau(\langle T_n\rangle)$. We give an internal criterion for inclusion between two such bornologies and recover each of them from a canonical free filter of closed sets. In fact, a nontrivial bornology is sequence-induced exactly when it has the enlargement property and its closed polar has countable character. Our principal result says that the bornology of relatively compact sets is sequence-induced precisely when $X$ is locally compact and separable; in the locally compact case the character of its closed polar is the density of $X$. In the penultimate section, we make a clever use of the sequence $T_n=\{n\}$ in the real line to give a negative answer to a conjecture posed in 2001 about a coarsest topology making the associated bornology a nontrivial metric bornology. Finally, we end the paper with a more general result: a coarsest such supertopology exists if and only if the original topology already makes the induced bornology a nontrivial metric bornology, in which case the coarsest supertopology is the original topology itself.

papers.title: Closed Lindel\"of $\Sigma$ Kernels of Neighborhood Assignments in Charming Spaces
papers.abstract: Every neighborhood assignment on a charming space $X$ has a countable kernel whose closure in $X$ is Lindel\"of $\Sigma$. Consequently, for any two neighborhood assignments $M$ and $N$ on $X$, there is a closed discrete set $D\subseteq X$ such that $M[N[D]]=X$. We give an exact one-step formulation of the remaining $D$-space problem and identify the universal pointwise square-refinement condition with the classical $z$-space condition. For continuous closed surjections, we prove a fixed-assignment lifting equivalence. We also show that every uncountable $\mathrm{HFC}_{\mathrm w}$ subspace of $[\omega_1]^{\leq\omega}$ is dually closed countable but not charming. For a fixed Lindel\"of $\Sigma$ kernel $Y$, we iterate the Hu--Yin boundary reduction by a transfinite closed-core process. At every stage, the current iterate is a $D$-space if and only if $X$ is a $D$-space. The iteration stabilizes before $hL(Y)^+$ at the largest closed subspace in which the kernel trace and its complement are both dense. The bound is sharp: for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$ and every $\gamma<\kappa^+$, there is a compact example with a dense $\sigma$-compact Lindel\"of $\Sigma$ kernel $Y$ satisfying $hL(Y)=|Y|=\kappa$ whose first stabilization stage is $\gamma$.

papers.title: A vanishing-cycle obstruction to smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.abstract: We prove a homological obstruction to smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees six and seven. On a crepant resolution that is small over the nodes and blows up the cone vertices, any smoothing forces a relation among link classes bounding in the local Milnor fibers. The relation is nonzero at every node and degree-seven point, and at each degree-six point smoothed through the one-dimensional component. The proof uses vanishing periods and applies to smoothing arcs of arbitrary contact order, extending the necessity direction of Friedman's criterion. We apply the obstruction to a Batyrev hypersurface whose thirty singularities are individually smoothable but which admits no smoothing, even formally. On its mirror partner, two nodes cannot be smoothed by any analytic deformation, independently of a locally nonsmoothable cone point.

papers.title: On families of copulas and quasi-copulas homeomorphic to the Hilbert cube and related results
papers.authors: Fabrizio Durante, Juan Fern\'andez S\'anchez, Wolfgang Trutschnig
papers.abstract: Working with tools from infinite-dimensional topology and using measure-theoretic ideas we analyze numerous well-known fami\-lies of copu\-las and quasi-copulas from a topological perspective, prove that most of them are homeomorphic to the Hilbert cube $\mathcal{H}$ and hence have the Fixed Point as well as the Disjoint Cells property. Working with so-called $Z$-sets, we then study how large one set is within another. Doing so, in order to show that a set $A$ is small/topologically negligible within a compact metric space $(\Omega,m)$, we construct a homeomorphism $h: [0,1] \times \mathcal{H} \to \Omega$ mapping $\{0\} \times \mathcal{H}$ to $A$. The obtained results are to a certain extent surprising since various supposedly small families are topologically large.

papers.title: Nonvanishing implies abundance
papers.abstract: We prove that the nonvanishing conjecture implies the abundance conjecture.

papers.title: There are no unexpected toric positroid varieties
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a positroid. We prove that the positroid variety $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to some algebraic torus if and only if $\mathcal{M}$ is regular. In that case, $\Pi_{\mathcal{M}}$ is toric with respect to the standard diagonal torus. Thus, there are no unexpected toric positroid varieties.

papers.title: Smoothing Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and del Pezzo cone points
papers.abstract: We give a necessary and sufficient homological criterion for smoothing projective Calabi-Yau threefolds with nodes and anticanonical cones over smooth del Pezzo surfaces of degrees five, six and seven, or over a smooth quadric surface. For some choice of local smoothing components, the criterion requires a relation on a crepant resolution among link classes whose associated local parameters avoid every discriminant. The complexified relation space describes first-order deformations modulo locally trivial ones. Necessity follows from local period and vanishing-cycle arguments; sufficiency applies Friedman's unobstructedness theorem to a crepant partial resolution. Whenever the criterion holds, the deformation space on the chosen components is smooth. A nonsmoothable example, whose deformation space is reduced with four smooth components, shows why nonvanishing at every singular point is insufficient. We also construct a smoothable Batyrev hypersurface admitting no smoothing induced by proper ambient families obtained from Minkowski decompositions at a single lattice degree.

papers.title: Finite Symplectic Automorphisms of Hyperk\"ahler Manifolds of $K3^{[n]}$-Type Act Trivially on Discriminant Groups
papers.authors: Jie Fu, Shihao Wang, Zhiwei Zheng
papers.abstract: We give an alternative proof of Mongardi's result that every finite group of symplectic automorphisms of a hyperk\"ahler manifold of $K3^{[n]}$-type acts trivially on the discriminant groups of its second cohomology lattice and its coinvariant lattice. The proof combines sphere-packing bounds, Vinberg's reflection chambers and structure results on even $2$-elementary lattices.

papers.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
papers.abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.

papers.title: University Research and Leadership in the Age of AI: Mobilizing Intellectual Capacity and Building the Infrastructure for Discovery
papers.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) raise the prospect of substantial changes in how research is conducted and who can direct discovery. This perspective argues that universities should prepare for these changes by developing AI as well as using it, rather than relying primarily on capabilities designed elsewhere. The relationship is reciprocal: AI can advance disciplinary research, while scientific questions, experimental evidence, and observed failures can guide AI development. The proposal distinguishes three complementary commitments: shared operation of existing AI models, disciplinary AI development, and foundational AI research. Their resource requirements differ, and no single university needs to reproduce a frontier AI company. Shared computational services should be connected to sustained technical teams, laboratory experimentation, and knowledge records that make findings traceable and reusable. Independent evaluation, alignment research, transparent resource allocation, and inclusive academic governance are integral to this infrastructure. Consortia and national facilities can support capabilities beyond individual campuses while preserving room for investigator-led inquiry. Initial programs in experimental and mathematical research would test scientific value, the effort required to validate results, and improvements to AI before expansion. The argument concerns research rather than educational reform and calls for building institutional capacity before the extent and timing of disruption are settled.

papers.title: Geometric priors for single-patch neural Calabi--Yau metrics on the quintic: a conservative fixed-$\psi$ Ablation study
papers.abstract: We investigate how geometric priors shape neural approximations of the complex Monge--Amp`ere equation on the quintic Calabi--Yau threefold. This fixed-$\psi$ diagnostic compares four single-patch ans"atze: a coordinate SIREN potential model, a direct-metric Cholesky baseline, an algebraic section ansatz, and a section-plus-neural hybrid. In a 96-run learning-rate and frequency archive, section-based models reach validation $\sigma=4.14$--$4.16%$, whereas SIREN and Cholesky remain at $41.29%$ and $44.27%$. Multi-seed controls use a shared affine-$\eta$ evaluator and five fresh validation clouds. Stable section settings give $3.84$--$4.77%$, compared with $28.46$--$30.59%$ for Cholesky and $34.73$--$38.13%$ for SIREN. Hybrid projective features do not improve best-case accuracy, but they stabilise the stressed regime. They limit $\sigma$ to $4.26$--$4.41%$, versus $4.45$--$205.45%$ for raw coordinates. Within this protocol, section-based geometric structure is the main driver of accuracy; coordinate-only models plateau at substantially higher error, and raw hybrid flexibility can amplify instability. We provide a projective-scaling derivation, document protocol asymmetries, and identify projectively consistent hybrid corrections as the next step.

papers.title: On Baireness of the Wijsman Topology
papers.abstract:
We give negative answers to Questions 4.4 and 4.5 in Cao's survey on the Wijsman topology. We construct a metrizable space $Y$ and a compatible metric $d$ such that every finite power $Y^n$ is Baire, while $(\mathrm{CL}(Y),\tau_W(d))$ is not Baire. The construction realizes the Vietoris hyperspace of a suitable metric space as an open subspace of a ball hyperspace.
  We also study the set $S_d$ of points having an open $\sigma$-$d$-totally bounded neighborhood. We prove that Baireness of $(\mathrm{CL}(X),\tau_W(d))$ implies Baireness of $S_d$, and that, whenever $S_d$ is dense in $X$, the following three conditions are equivalent: $(\mathrm{CL}(X),\tau_W(d))$ is Baire, $X$ is Baire, and $S_d$ is Baire.
  As consequences, we obtain complete characterizations for locally $\sigma$-$d$-totally bounded metric spaces, countable metric spaces, and $\sigma$-compact metrizable spaces. In our counterexample, $S_e$ coincides with a non-dense discrete component for every compatible metric $e$, showing that the density assumption is essential.

papers.title: On Thom Polynomials for $\mathcal{A}$-singularities of parametric curves and degeneracy loci formulas
papers.abstract: In this research article, we make an in-depth investigation of the computations for Thom Polynomials for $\mathcal{A}$-singularities of parametric curves germs in the plane and space cases using the framework established by Ohmoto and the Restriction Method introduced by Rim\'anyi, and we also propose a geometric way for such computations using degeneracy loci Chern classes formulas proven by Fulton, which seems a promising way to generalize the Thom Polynomial expression for the stabilization of such singularities in $\mathbb{C}^N$, depending exclusively on $N$ as a parameter.

papers.title: On Open Borel Orbits in Conormal Bundles to Schubert Cells
papers.abstract: Let $C(v)$ denote a Schubert cell in the flag variety $\operatorname{GL}_n/B$, and let $X(w)$ be a Schubert variety containing $C(v)$. Mellit has conjectured that, if $X(w)$ is smooth, the existence of an open $B$-orbit in the conormal bundle to $C(v)$ in $X(w)$ is equivalent to $C(w_0w)$ being contained in the smooth locus of $X(w_0v)$. We prove a stronger version of this conjecture, requiring only that $X(w)$ is factorial. We prove our result by constructing a sequence of graphs associated to the pair $v,w$ such that the existence of a cycle in one of these graphs is equivalent to the non-existence of such an open orbit.

papers.title: A direct proof of Infinity in NF-0
papers.abstract: We give a direct proof of Infinity in the no-empty version of New Foundations, denoted NF-0, by establishing that every model of the specified theory contains an object that is not finite in a precise, internally defined sense. The version considered has extensionality, at least two distinct objects, no empty objects, and inhabited stratified comprehension: a stratified extension is supplied whenever it has a member. Finiteness combines a two-sided internally represented well-order with the exclusion of internally represented nonterminating strict transitive relations on inhabited subsets. Assuming all objects finite, partial bijections yield comparison and finite extrema of positive Frege cardinals. Positive exponentiation, singleton type-raising, and the least orbit of the genuine two-cardinal lead to the equation n = T(n) + 1. We prove separately, and in detail, that adjoining one point reverses internally defined parity: the key ingredients are a graph-rewiring proof of invariance under adjoining two points and one instance of stratified induction derived from the all-finite assumption. Since type-raising preserves parity, the cardinal equation is impossible. We identify the corresponding Lean 4 declarations and make explicit the scope of the formal verification. No model-existence or consistency theorem for ordinary NF is claimed.

papers.title: Stability analysis of the Lane--Emden equation of index $n=5$ describing polytropic gas spheres
papers.abstract:
We study the Lane--Emden equation of index $n=5$, the critical polytropic case separating finite-radius from infinite-radius self-gravitating equilibria. The scaling family $	heta_\lambda(\xi)=\lambda^{1/2}	heta(\lambda\xi)$ generates a neutral mode $\phi_0=	frac12	heta+\xi	heta'$ about the Schuster profile. Schuster's transformation and a logarithmic variable reduce the equation to the autonomous Hamiltonian system $\ddot
u=	frac14(
u-
u^5)$ with a first integral. Besides the Schuster (separatrix) and Srivastava solutions, every orbit crossing $
u=0$ is given in closed form by a Weierstrass $\wp$-function, and the closed forms agree with direct numerical integration to about $10^{-12}$. Up to scaling and sign, the Schuster solution is the only solution regular at the center, and it separates positive solutions from solutions with infinitely many zeros. In homology-invariant variables the singular solution $	heta=(2\xi)^{-1/2}$ is a center exactly at $n=5$, where its stability changes. For a distance-varying Emden--Fowler system with a shifted equilibrium we prove that at $n=5$ the unique equilibrium is linearly and nonlinearly unstable. Finally, the linearization about the Schuster profile is the Schr"odinger operator $L=-\Delta_r-5	heta_S^4$ on $L^2((0,\infty),\xi^2d\xi)$. Its Friedrichs extension has essential spectrum $[0,\infty)$, a threshold resonance at $0$ carried by the non-normalizable scaling mode, and exactly one negative eigenvalue, $\lambda_0\approx-1.21$, so the Schuster profile is a saddle point of the associated energy functional.

papers.title: Deterministic Causal Quantization with Representative States and Bounded Error
papers.abstract:
We study deterministic causal quantization with pathwise error at most $\varepsilon$, using $\omega$ shared representatives updated from transmitted addresses alone. For a midpoint realization with first-in, first-out replacement, we compare address entropy rates with process $\varepsilon$-entropy, the least entropy rate of any block quantizer meeting the same constraint. From $\varepsilon$-separated initialization, the gap is at most two bits per sample for every stationary source with finite scalar $\varepsilon$-entropy, without density, independence or mixing assumptions. A causal address-tree argument extends this comparison to any synchronized quantizer with cell overlap $m$, giving $\log_2 m$ bits. Lattice initialization with consistent boundary ownership realizes uniform grids with sharp one-bit scalar and process comparisons. Under an entropy condition and finite Fisher information rate $J$, the gap is at most $2J\varepsilon^2/(\pi^2\ln 2)$; general initializations add a term of order $\omega\varepsilon\sqrt{J}$. The scalar grid estimate gives a nonasymptotic form of R\'enyi's theorem. Since a grid is causal, the price of causality is at most $\min\{1,2J\varepsilon^2/(\pi^2\ln 2)\}$ bits per sample, versus the high-resolution squared-error loss $\tfrac12\log_2(\pi e/6)$. These bounds certify $\varepsilon$-entropy brackets for autoregressive Laplace and Gaussian sources. For memoryless sources, the optimal causal rate equals the scalar $\varepsilon$-entropy.
  For a stationary process on finitely many $2\varepsilon$-separated centers, adding independent uniform noise of width $2\varepsilon$ gives exact Shannon lower-bound equality at every block length, attained by storing those centers. This includes histograms with finitely many bins. Storing two non-lattice centers beats every uniform grid of the same cell width by half a bit per sample.

papers.title: Formal Neighborhood Equivariant Cohomology and Kirwan Surjectivity at Singular Values
papers.abstract:
Let \(G\) be a compact Lie group acting Hamiltonianly on a symplectic manifold \(M\) with moment map \(\mu:M\to\g^*\). For a singular value \(a\) of \(\mu\), the symplectic quotient \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\) is stratified and the classical Kirwan map is not defined. We introduce a \emph{formal neighborhood equivariant cohomology} \(\cH_G^*(a)\) using the slice-groupoid Cartan sheaf and the closed embedding \(\mu^{-1}(a)/G\hookrightarrow \mu^{-1}(U_a)/G\) for a \(G\)-invariant neighborhood \(U_a\) of \(a\). We define a formal Kirwan map
  \[
  \kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}:H_G^*(M)\longrightarrow \cH_G^*(a).
  \]
  We prove that \(\kappa_{\mathrm{formal}}\) is surjective under a local \emph{equivariant homotopy retraction} condition on the slice level sets
  \[
  C_x=\mu_x^{-1}(a|_{\g_x})\subset S_x,
  \]
  which is satisfied, for example, when \(a\) is a regular value of every slice moment map, or when \(a=0\) and \(C_x\) is a \(G_x\)-equivariant cone. The weakest condition we identify is the existence, for each \(x\in\mu^{-1}(a)\), of a local quasi-isomorphism
  \[
  \Car(S_x,G_x)\simeq \cC^\bullet_{C_x}
  \]
  in a \(G_x\)-equivariant neighborhood of the orbit, without requiring a global tubular neighborhood. As an application we recover, in the formal framework, the even-degree surjectivity theorem of Delarue--Ramacher--Schmitt for \(S^1\)-actions and clarify why odd-degree surjectivity fails in general.

papers.title: Rigidity and Affine Deformations of Foliations on Nilpotent and Solvable Contact Lie Algebras
papers.abstract: Let g be a Lie algebra of dimension 2n+1, let beta be a contact form, and let alpha be a nonzero integrable 1-form. We study when the affine path alpha_t = (1-t)alpha + t beta consists of contact forms with the orientation determined by beta \wedge (d beta)^n. We first establish an algebraic criterion: affine deformability is equivalent to the non-negativity of a scalar obtained from the interaction form Theta(alpha, beta) = alpha \wedge (d beta)^n + n beta \wedge d alpha \wedge (d beta)^{n-1}. For unimodular Lie algebras this scalar is (n+1)alpha(Z_beta), where Z_beta is the Reeb vector. We also derive a formula involving the modular character tau(X) = tr(ad_X) in the non-unimodular case. On nilpotent contact Lie algebras, every integrable 1-form is closed; using the standard structural properties of nilpotent contact Lie algebras, this implies that every left-invariant foliation is an affine origin for every fixed contact form. An explicit three-dimensional example illustrates that the modular term can yield affine deformability even when alpha(Z_beta) = 0. We discuss the implications for left-invariant forms on Lie groups and compact quotients. We do not claim a general obstruction example in the non-unimodular case; establishing such an example requires a separate verified construction.

papers.title: Minimal Alt(6)-modules with additive dimension on characteristic non 3
papers.abstract: We classify the minimal faithful Alt(6)-modules with an additive dimension in characteristic not 3. We also highlight the remaining work needed to complete the classification of minimal faithful Alt(n)- and Sym(n)-modules with an additive dimension

papers.title: Combinatorial description of the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit correspondence between the irreducible finite dimensional representations of the mirabolic quantum group $MU(n)$ and those of the mirabolic Hecke algebra $MH_d$ given by the mirabolic quantum Schur-Weyl duality. In particular, this resolves a generalization of a conjecture by the second author. The proof is via a careful analysis of the $MU(n)$-weight spaces and the eigenvalues of the Jucys Murphy elements of $MH_d$ on the mirabolic tensor space.

papers.title: When Polynomial Multiplication Counts Geometry: Schubert Polynomials and Monk's Rule
papers.abstract: We give a geometric introduction to Schubert polynomial multiplication through point-line flags in the complex projective plane. Moving a prescribed point onto a prescribed line gives a family with local equation $au=\lambda$, whose limiting curve has two components. The incidence equations and their local multiplicities give a two-term divisor product, using the standard intersection product on classes of algebraic cycles. Permutation labels and Schubert polynomials express the same decomposition as an instance of Monk's rule. For three incidence conditions, each allowing either a point on a prescribed line or a line through a prescribed point, the product has degree six. Under explicit general-position assumptions, direct construction and local equations give six distinct solutions of multiplicity one.

papers.title: A Separated Bump Theorem in $L^2$
papers.abstract: We prove a separated entropy bump theorem for two-weight $L^2$ inequalities for positive operators defined by Carleson sequences on a probability space with a general filtration. The bump conditions use conditional averages of martingale maximal functions and involve the first power of the entropy penalty, removing the square appearing in the separated condition of Treil and Volberg. As a consequence, we obtain separated Orlicz bump estimates for a class of doubling Young functions. These results apply, in particular, to sparse operators. The proof uses principal sequences, a natural global extension of principal sets, and combines a good-$\lambda$ estimate with a weighted Carleson embedding to obtain the required testing inequalities.

papers.title: Structured Time-Frequency Representation for Channel Prediction
papers.authors: Ning Yang, Yuming Xian, Tong Li, Ning Gao, Haijun Zhang
papers.abstract: Accurate CSI forecasting is essential for mitigating channel aging and supporting reliable downlink transmission in high-mobility wireless systems. In FDD systems, forecasting future DL CSI from historical UL observations requires joint temporal extrapolation and cross-band inference. However, defining historical UL as the input and future DL as the target does not specify how elapsed time and UL-to-DL band separation should be represented in a pretrained predictor's positional space. FAR-CSI establishes an FDD-aware representation of channel forecasting within a joint temporal and operating-band positional field. Within this field, historical UL observations and future DL targets occupy segregated regions according to their temporal and operating-band roles, preserving the distinction between observed UL context and unobserved DL prediction targets. This representation is instantiated through a unified structured routing rule that governs encoder positional assignment, decoder-field reconstruction, and future-DL target selection, ensuring the same FDD geometry is preserved from contextual encoding to prediction readout. Under matched backbone, initialization, and training conditions, FDD-aware routing reduces NMSE by 21.44\% relative to generic routing. Across the evaluated FDD baselines, FAR-CSI achieves higher CSI prediction accuracy and MRT-based spectral efficiency, while retaining its predictive advantage across mobility conditions, prediction horizons, reduced training-data regimes, and noisy historical observations.

papers.title: On the frieze patterns by Conway and Coxeter
papers.abstract: The story of frieze patterns started in 1970s with a paper by Coxeter and two short papers by Conway and Coxeter, one listing questions and the other providing brief answers. During the first three decades it was followed by only a handful of papers observing some further properties of the same objects. Then Propp (2005) and Caldero and Chapoton (2006) established connections between frieze patterns and the recent theory of cluster algebras introduced by Fomin and Zelevinsky in early 2000s. Since then the theory of frieze patterns exploded with new results, and frieze patterns found a wide spectrum of connections in various domains of mathematics, including combinatorics, geometry, representation theory and integrable systems. The literature on frieze patterns grew vastly and continues to expand. In this note we give a brief overview of some of the directions emerging from the papers by Conway and Coxeter and single out core ideas which were later replayed in different contexts.

papers.title: Average eccentricity in k-connected tournaments
papers.abstract: The average eccentricity $\avec(D)$ of a strong digraph $D$ is the mean eccentricity of all vertices in $D$. A tournament $T$ is an orientation of a complete graph. In this paper, we prove that the average eccentricity satisfies $2 \le \avec(T) < \frac{n}{2k} + \frac{11}{2} + \frac{k}{8n}$ for a $k$-connected tournament $T$ of order $n$. We further examine the case for strong tournaments where $k = 1$, and show that $\avec(T) \le \frac{n+11}{2} + \frac{1}{8n}$ for any strong tournament $T$. Moreover, we show that the lower bound $2$ is sharp and that the upper bounds are best possible apart from an additive constant.

papers.title: On Hamilton cycles in quasiprimitive graphs of order $2pq$
papers.abstract: Let $p>q>5$ be primes. We determine the socles and corresponding actions of quasiprimitive imprimitive groups of degree $2pq$, all of which are almost simple. Using this classification, we prove that a connected graph of order $2pq$ admitting a quasiprimitive automorphism group contains a Hamilton cycle, except possibly for three specified families of actions with socle $\PSL(2,p)$ or $\PSL(2,q^2)$.

papers.title: A generalization of pseudocomplementation in semilattices, lattices and posets with 0
papers.abstract: Pseudocomplemented lattices satisfy a lot of nice properties and were studied by a number of algebraists. However, even when a poset P with 0 is not pseudocomplemented, we can assign to every element a of P the set $a^p$ of all maximal elements being orthogonal to a. This assignment $^p$ is a non-trivial operator provided P satisfies the so-called Ascending Chain Condition (ACC). In particular, we investigate this operator when the poset P in question is a semilattice or a lattice. We characterize this operator and describe its properties that turn out to be similar to the corresponding properties of pseudocomplementation. Moreover, we introduce an equivalence relation $\Theta_p$ on P induced by $^p$ similarly as it was done by V. I. Glivenko for distributive pseudocomplemented lattices. Finally, we investigate for which lattices L with 0 satisfying the ACC this equivalence relation turns out to be a congruence and when the quotient lattice $L/\Theta_p$ is complemented respectively modular.

papers.title: Quadratic Reciprocity via Vandermonde Matrix
papers.abstract: This paper presents a proof of the law of quadratic reciprocity using the Vandermonde matrix and Zolotarev's lemma.

papers.title: Using the Blackwell-Cover Guessing Strategy to Separate Unobserved Bernoulli Trials - II
papers.abstract: In a prior paper, we investigated what could be said about the number in the pair that was not observed when we employed the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy. In this paper, we generalize prior results to arbitrary distributions. We use a variant of the BlackwellCover strategy ro take pairs of coins chosen from a mixture of two different distributions G and H such that one of the coins is flipped, and as a result of that flip the unobserved (unflipped) coin is placed in one of two sets A and B. We show that, regardless of which distributions are used for G and H, there are situations in which this can be done so that the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in A is less than the mean of the heads probabilities of the unobserved coins in B. What makes this result surprising, in addition to its generality, is a comparison with a corresponding result for marbles. If one knows that one will always be weighing one of two marbles with different specific weights, such as 10g and 20g, knowing the weight of the marble being weighed automatically determines the weight of the other. However, even if one knows that one will be flipping one of two coins with specific heads probabilities such as 1/3 and 2/3, the outcome of the flip of one of the coins will not immediately enable one to conclude anything about the heads probability of the unflipped coin, which is where the BlackwellCover Guessing Strategy comes into play.

papers.title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
papers.abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the McShane-Rivin unit ball.

papers.title: Some Coble surfaces admit only Bertini involutions
papers.abstract: In this article we show that a biregular involution $i : X \to X$ defined on an unnodal Coble surface $X$ with irreducible boundary curve $\{C\} = |- 2 K_X|$ is necessarily a lift of a Bertini involution. Then we show with counterexamples that the hypothesis of irreducibility of $C$ and unnodality of $X$ are both necessary.

papers.title: Setting Things Straight: On the Straightness and Non-Straightness of Two-Step Rectified Flow
papers.authors: Tuan Pham, Saptarshi Roy, Alessandro Rinaldo, Purnamrita Sarkar
papers.abstract: Rectified flow (RF) is an ODE-based generative modeling framework that has achieved remarkable success in practice over the past few years. By design, RF seeks to produce flows that have a high degree of straightness, in the sense that the resulting ODE trajectories can be obtained with relatively few (ideally, one) sampling steps. However, a rigorous analysis of straightness or near-straightness of RF flows remains missing in the literature. In this paper, we study settings in which the coupling generated by two-step RF is provably straight at the population level. We provide a complete characterization in two popular classes of data distributions: (i) smooth, strongly log-concave densities and (ii) Gaussian mixture models. Our main results yield sharp conditions for the coupling generated by two-step RF to be straight. Non-straight couplings are constructed when these conditions fail, which demonstrate the sharpness of these conditions. Using the theory developed on the straightness of two-step RF, we propose a notion of approximate straightness that measures the straightness of the learned couplings and can be estimated from the data. We describe a procedure for constructing asymptotic confidence intervals for our proposed notion of approximate straightness and propose a data-driven method for selecting the number of reflow rounds in multiple iterations of RF.

papers.title: Spectral $\Gamma_2$ inequalities for the $V$-Laplacian with evolving weighted measures
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish spectral Bakry-\'{E}mery $\Gamma_2$ criteria and their modified counterparts for the $V$-Laplacian on closed Riemannian manifolds equipped with evolving weighted measures. The estimates yield jointly optimized spectral bounds and sharp endpoint constants. When the measures evolve according to the Fokker-Planck equation, these estimates yield monotonicity formulas for the Fisher information associated with Shannon and Tsallis entropies, together with quantitative propagation of Poincar\'e, logarithmic Sobolev, and nonlinear interpolation inequalities. In the stationary reversible setting, our results specialize to the Witten Laplacian and recover the unweighted Cai-Wang estimates \cite{Cai}.

papers.title: Non-local to local limit for stochastic conservation laws
papers.abstract: This work proves the convergence of stochastic nonlocal conservation laws, with spatially inhomogeneous noise, to stochastic conservation laws when the range of particle interaction vanishes. This provides rigorous justification for a class of stochastic conservation laws that has received considerable attention in the last decade. To handle technical challenges such as gradient-dependent noise, modified versions of the equations with specific cutoff boundaries are utilized and new uniform estimates to ensure stability during the limiting process are established. In addition, the work demonstrates that this convergence depends on the presence of a viscous term, as a counterexample shows that without it, the limiting solution may fail to be an entropy solution.

papers.title: Simultaneous Recovery of Wave Speeds and Initial Sources on Graphs via Redundant Frontier Propagation
papers.abstract: We study the simultaneous recovery of an unknown initial signal and unknown vertex wave speeds for the wave equation on a finite graph from time-dependent measurements on a prescribed set of vertices. With the graph geometry known, we first show that a single experiment determines both quantities under a new two-witness zero forcing condition and generic nondegeneracy assumptions. We then develop a more general frontier-propagation framework in which the redundancy required for simultaneous recovery is distributed across successive graph contours rather than localized at individual forcing vertices. We derive Lipschitz stability estimates for the frontier propagation problem. We also show the recovery and stability results extend to positively weighted graphs.

papers.title: Uniqueness and large-time continuous dependence in a doubly degenerate nutrient taxis system
papers.abstract:
\[
  u_t = \nabla \cdot (uv\nabla u) - \chi \nabla\cdot (u^2 v\nabla v) + \ell uv,
  \qquad \qquad
  v_t = \Delta v - uv, \] is considered in a smoothly bounded domain $\Omega\subset {\mathbb{R}}^n$ and with $\chi\ge 0$ and $\ell\ge 0$.
  Within a suitable concept of solvability, a statement on uniqueness of solutions emanating from initial data $(u_0,v_0)$ is derived under the mere assumption that $u_0\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ and $v_0\in W^{1,\infty}(\Omega)$ are such that $u_0\ge 0$ and $v_0>0$ in $\overline{\Omega}$; in particular, no condition on continuity of $u_0$ is imposed.
  This result is thereafter used to reveal that in physcally meaningful scenarios, for any initial data which are additionally assumed to be continuous and nontrivial, such solutions can always be found, and that these solutions depend continuously on the initial distributions not only in bounded sets of the form $\Omega\times (0,T)$, but actually throughout $\Omega\times (0,\infty)$, in a suitable sense.

papers.title: Fukaya categories of surfaces with DG coefficients
papers.abstract:
Given a compact surface $S$ admitting a Liouville form, a finite set $Q \subset S$, a line field on $S$, and a local system of dg-categories on $S \setminus Q$ together with a section of the monodromy functor around each interior $q \in Q$, we construct a Fukaya category. We give examples where such Fukaya categories are quasi-equivalent to derived categories of projective completions of line bundles and of iterated blow-ups of the affine plane; and to wrapped Fukaya categories of cotangent bundles of spheres.
  We define two versions of the Fukaya category, a topological, which is constructed combinatorially from a full arc system, and a geometric, which includes all Lagrangian branes supported on immersed curves. We prove that the topological category embeds into the geometric category in an essentially unique way. To define Lagrangian branes we develop a generalisation of the Chekanov--Eliashberg algebra incorporating dg-coefficients and wrapping along the boundary.

papers.title: Existence of uniformly most reliable two-terminal graphs with distance constraints
papers.abstract: A two-terminal graph is a simple graph equipped with two distinguished vertices, called terminals. Let $T_{n,m}$ be the class consisting of all non-isomorphic two-terminal graphs on $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. Let $G$ be any two-terminal graph in $T_{n,m}$, and let $d$ be any positive integer. For every $\rho\in [0,1]$, the \emph{$d$-constrained two-terminal reliability of $G$ at $\rho$}, denoted $R_G^d(\rho)$, is the probability that $G$ has some path of length at most $d$ joining its terminals after each of its edges is independently deleted with probability $\rho$. We say $G$ is a \emph{$d$-uniformly most reliable two-terminal graph} ($d$-UMRTTG) if for each $H$ in $T_{n,m}$ and every $\rho \in [0,1]$ it holds that $R_{G}^d(\rho)\geq R_{H}^{d}(\rho)$. Previous works studied the existence of $d$-UMRTTG in $T_{n,m}$ when $d$ is greater than or equal to $n-1$, or equivalently, when the distance constraint is dropped. In this work, a characterization of all $1$-UMRTTGs and $2$-UMRTTGs is given. Several structural properties of 3-UMRTTGs are established. For every $d\geq 3$, we prove the existence of a unique $d$-UMRTTG in $T_{n,\binom{n}{2}-1}$. In contrast, for every $d\geq 4$ and every $n\geq 11$, no $d$-UMRTTG exists in $T_{n,m}$ whenever $20\leq m\leq 3n-9$ or $3n-5\leq m\leq \binom{n}{2}-2$. Additionally, for each $d\geq 5$, it is proved that no $d$-UMRTTG exists in $T_{n,m}$ when $n\geq 11$ and $m=3n-8$.

papers.title: Non-comparable invariant metrics and failure of Gromov hyperbolicity on a real-analytic pseudoconvex domain
papers.abstract:
We study the explicit bounded pseudoconvex domain \[
  \Omega=\{(z_1,z_2,w)\in\mathbb C^3:
  |w|^2+|z_1z_2(z_1-z_2)|^2+|z_1|^8+|z_2|^8<1\}. \] Its boundary is real analytic and has finite D'Angelo type everywhere. We prove two assertions about the invariant metrics of this domain. First, $(\Omega,k_\Omega)$ is not Gromov hyperbolic; in fact arbitrarily fat Kobayashi geodesic triangles occur in every neighborhood of the type-$8$ point $(0,0,1)$. Second, the Carath\'eodory--Reiffen and Kobayashi--Royden metrics are not uniformly comparable. Along an explicit family of tangential directions the Carath\'eodory metric tends to zero while the Kobayashi metric has a positive limit. For the corresponding distances there are points $x_j,y_j\to(0,0,1)$ such that $c_\Omega(x_j,y_j)\to0$ while $k_\Omega(x_j,y_j)\to\infty$. This gives, among bounded real-analytic pseudoconvex domains, an affirmative answer to Problem~7.3.2 of the Several Complex Variables Problem List.

papers.title: $L^p$ Convergence of AMV Laplacians on completions of Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study conditions for the $L^p$ convergence of the AMV Laplacian $\Delta_r$ on completions of Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$. The condition invloves the Minkowski dimension of the set $\overline{M} \setminus M$ and how much the curvature is blowing up around $S$. We build a concrete family of sets that satisfies these conditions, and provide an example of non convergence when these conditions are not met.

papers.title: Trace-minimal graphs maximizing the number of spanning trees
papers.abstract:
A classical problem in spectral graph theory is to determine, among all simple graphs with a fixed number of vertices and edges, those that maximize the number of spanning trees. Such graphs are called $t$-optimal. Petingi and Rodr'iguez [Discr. Math. 244 (2002), 351-373] reduced the construction of infinitely many $t$-optimal graphs to the determination of almost-regular graphs with a minimum number of induced $3$-paths, known as almost-regular $
u$-min graphs. They conjectured that the class of $d$-regular $
u$-min graphs is invariant under the addition or deletion of copies of the complete graph $K_{d+1}$, which would provide a method to construct large families of $t$-optimal graphs. This conjecture was recently verified for $d\in \{1,2,3,4,5\}$ by Gong et al. [Discr. Math. 349(4), 2026].
  In this work, we establish an asymptotic version of this conjecture. We prove that the class of $d$-regular $
u$-min graphs on at least $n$ vertices is invariant under the addition or deletion of copies of $K_{d+1}$ whenever $d\geq 3$ and $n\geq d^3$. In addition, we introduce a new method to construct $t$-optimal graphs based on the concept of trace-minimal graphs, originally introduced by 'Abrego et al. [Linear Algebra Appl. 412 (2006), 161-221]. As a consequence, we obtain infinitely many graphs that are both trace-minimal and $t$-optimal.

papers.title: Uniform local models of quasi-unipotent $p$-adic differential equations
papers.abstract: We construct uniform analytic models of quasi-unipotent differential modules over Robba rings. For modules of rank at most $r$ and highest ramification break at most $b$, the inner radius of the model annulus depends only on $r,b$ and the residue characteristic $p$. At each radius, the model admits a basis, possibly depending on the radius, in which the connection matrix is bounded by a constant depending only on $r,b,p$. Both bounds are independent of the coefficient field, and these analytic models require no coefficient extension. A prescribed absolute Frobenius structure extends to such a bounded model with the same radius and connection bound. After a finite coefficient extension, we also realize quasi-constant modules, which carry the finite local monodromy, as differential direct summands of sums of pushforwards of rank-one modules, with uniformly bounded cover degrees and highest breaks of the inducing modules.

papers.title: Universal Critical Jump for Inverse-Square Ising Ferromagnets
papers.abstract: For every translation-invariant ferromagnetic Ising chain with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, we prove $2\beta_cBm_c^2=1$, without restrictions on the finite core or the tail convergence rate. The proof bounds the energy of macroscopic interfaces and rules them out if the critical product exceeds one. Despite the nonzero jump, connected susceptibility is infinite both at criticality and in a neighboring ordered interval. At the critical coupling, the excess magnetization decays more slowly than any positive power of the field as the field tends to zero. We also prove the jump relation in continuous time, for a positive-Stieltjes class of Ohmic spin-boson models.

papers.title: Hankel determinants for the $(n+2)$-shifted $q$-metallic numbers
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi_n(q)$ denote the $q$-deformation (in the sense of Morier-Genoud & Ovsienko) of the metallic number $\phi_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$. This is a power series with integer coefficients. We prove that the Hankel continued fraction of the $(n+2)$-shifted series $\Phi_n^{(n+2)}$ is eventually periodic, and that the corresponding Hankel determinant sequence $\Delta^{(n+2)}$ is $2n(n+1)$-periodic if $n$ is even, $2n(n+1)$-antiperiodic if $n$ is odd, and that it takes only the values $-2,-1,0,1,2$. This confirms part of a former conjecture of ours and complements similar results we obtained for all $\ell$-shifts of $\Phi_n$ with $0\le\ell\le n+1$. In addition, we formulate a new conjecture of quasi-polynomiality for higher shifts $\ell\ge n+3$. The determinant values arise as telescoping products of the partial numerators of the Hankel continued fraction. Most of the technically involved and lengthy verifications are carried out by a symbolic computation program, whose code is publicly available on GitHub for independent verification.

papers.title: Computations in weight 3 of higher Bloch groups
papers.authors: Herbert Gangl, Paul E. Gunnells, Dan Yasaki
papers.abstract: We computationally investigate a weight 3 analogue of the relationship between higher Bloch groups, algebraic K-theory, higher regulators, and special values of Dedekind zeta functions. In particular, for F a number field F, we define the pruned Bloch group B _3(F) and compare the covolume of its regulator lattice with zeta_F(3). We define a quantity kappa_3(F), which is conjecturally an integer, that is expected to be closely related to the order of K_4(O_F).

papers.title: A note on the Besov spaces ${\rm B}_1^{\Phi_2}$
papers.abstract: Regarding the Besov space ${\rm B}_1^{\Phi_2}$, defined by S. Geiss and Ylinen (Memoirs AMS 1335, 2021) by a coupling method, we prove for $\xi\in{\rm B}_1^{\Phi_2} \cap L_2$ a distributional estimate in terms of the Lorentz-Zygmund space $L_{1,\infty}(\ln L)^{-1}$ for the Malliavin derivative ${\rm D}(T_u\xi)$ uniformly in $u>0$, where $(T_u)_{u\ge }$ is the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semi-group. Here $\xi$ is not necessarily Malliavin differentiable in the ${\rm D}_{1,1}$-sense. This provides for Theorem 4.22 of the aforementioned reference an extension to the borderline case $p=1$.

papers.title: Delooping levels on Morita context algebras
papers.authors: Marcos Barrios, Marcelo Lanzilotta, Gustavo Mata
papers.abstract: We study the behavior of various delooping levels in the setting of Morita context algebras with zero bimodule homomorphisms. Building on the notion of syzygies for modules over such algebras, we establish conditions under which the delooping level (see [6]) of a Morita context algebra is finite, provided that the component algebras also have finite delooping levels. We further extend these results to other invariants, the global delooping level (see [2]) and the derived delooping level (see [8]), showing how their finiteness is preserved in the Morita context. Several examples illustrate both the applicability of our criteria and the necessity of the hypotheses, highlighting cases where the delooping level of the whole algebra can be smaller than that of its components.

papers.title: From boundary geometry to counterexamples in Smale's mean value problem
papers.abstract: This paper provides a human digestion of the recent counterexample to Smale's mean value problem found by GPT-6 Astra. We give a geometric mechanism for constructing counterexamples. An outward normal that re-enters an analytic Jordan domain, subject to a curvature condition, yields a holomorphic model whose normalized divided differences exceed one in modulus on the boundary. Polynomial perturbations then concentrate every critical point near the boundary whilst preserving the strict inequality. This turns boundary geometry into counterexamples in every sufficiently large degree. We also locate these critical points to first order and show that their limiting distribution is the logarithmic equilibrium measure on the boundary. We end with an explicit example of degree $29\,984$, verified by interval arithmetic.

papers.title: A new infinite family of covers of complete graphs that admit a half-transitive action of a Suzuki simple group
papers.abstract: We construct a new infinite family of antipodal $2(q-1)$-covers of complete graphs $K_{q^2+1}$ of diameter $3$, where $q=2^{2e+1}\ge 8$, admitting a half-transitive action of the Suzuki simple group $Sz(q)$. We further show that each constructed cover admits an involutory automorphism interchanging the two $Sz(q)$-orbits on arcs, which yields that its full automorphism group is arc-transitive.

papers.title: Stability of Doubly Indexed Discrete Linear Systems
papers.abstract:
We study the stability of the two-dimensional discrete dynamical system defined by
  \[ x_{i,j} = A x_{i-1,j} + B x_{i,j-1},\]
  where $A, B \in \mathcal{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$. Although this system, commonly known as the Fornasini-Marchesini model, has been examined for decades, several key stability results have lacked rigorous proofs. This paper establishes precise and self-contained criteria for Lyapunov, asymptotic, and neutral stability under general bounded boundary conditions. In particular, we prove that asymptotic stability is equivalent to the spectral condition $ \rho(z_1 A + z_2 B) < 1 $ for all $ |z_1| \leq 1, |z_2| \leq 1 $. We further analyze the commutative case, derive recurrence relations for anti-diagonal sums, and present new examples and counterexamples illustrating the nuances of stability. The results are complemented by sufficient conditions based on matrix norms, Lyapunov functions, and the joint spectral radius.

papers.title: Finite Non-Commutative Centrally Essential Rings of Minimal Order
papers.authors: Adel Abyzov, Oleg Lyubimtsev, Askar Tuganbaev
papers.abstract: A ring $R$ with non-zero identity element is said to be centrally essential if for any non-zero element $a$ of $R$, there exist non-zero central elements $x$ and $y$ such that $ax = y$. In the paper, we prove that the minimal order of a finite non-commutative centrally essential ring is equal to $64$. A partial classification of such rings is presented, and the existence of non-isomorphic non-commutative centrally essential rings of minimal order is proved.

papers.title: Mutation-acyclicity in rank four is decidable but not semialgebraic
papers.authors: Kymani T. K. Armstrong-Williams, Edward Hirst, Blake Jackson, Kyu-Hwan Lee
papers.abstract: We prove that mutation-acyclicity of quivers on four vertices is decidable. If a four-vertex quiver $Q$ is mutation-acyclic, then some sequence of mutations takes it to an acyclic quiver without any arrow multiplicity exceeding $\operatorname{max}\{\operatorname{ht}(Q),m(Q)\}$, where $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ is the largest arrow multiplicity of $Q$ and $m(Q)$ is the Markov invariant of Fomin and Neville evaluated on the totally proper wiggle class of $Q$. A search within a computable form of this bound decides mutation-acyclicity of four-vertex quivers with $O(h^{24})$ states for input height $h\ge1$. Together with a theorem of Caldero and Keller, it also decides mutation equivalence of two four-vertex quivers up to relabeling whenever one of them is mutation-acyclic. We conjecture that $\operatorname{ht}(Q)$ alone suffices as the bound, which would reduce the search to $O(h^{6})$ states, and we verify this for all four-vertex quivers of height at most three. In the other direction, for every $n\ge4$ we construct an affine family of connected $n$-vertex quivers whose nonnegative even members are mutation-acyclic and whose positive odd members are mutation-cyclic. Consequently, unlike in rank three, no fixed finite Boolean combination of polynomial equations and strict polynomial inequalities in the arrow weights (i.e., a semialgebraic criterion) decides mutation-acyclicity of $n$-vertex quivers, even allowing polynomials that are not mutation-invariant. Finally, we correct the criterion for four-vertex quivers of height at most two stated in our earlier paper, and recover its classification counts with short certificates. The calculations in the proof of the height bound are verified by computer for all values of their parameters.

papers.title: Kwapie\'n's property (K) in Lipschitz-free spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a Lipschitz-free space $\F(M)$ fails Kwapie\'n's property (K) whenever its underlying metric space $M$ contains a bi-Lipschitz copy of $C\times K$, where $C\subset\R$ is closed with positive measure and $K$ contains a Cantor metric space. Consequently, this holds for every subset of $\R^n$, $n\geqslant2$, whose closure has positive measure, and for a compact planar set of Assouad dimension one. These Lipschitz-free spaces embed into no strongly weakly compactly generated space and no $L_1$-space; in the separable case their duals are not isomorphic to $\ell_\infty$. Combining our result with a decomposition of Aliaga and Medina, we show that $\F(\R^n\times\Z^m)$ is strongly weakly compactly generated if and only if it has (K), and this occurs precisely when $n\leqslant1$. In particular, $\F(\R^2)$ does not embed isomorphically into $\F(\R\times\Z)$, answering a question of Aliaga. The planar examples nevertheless have the Dunford--Pettis property and Pe{\l}czy\'nski's property $(V^*)$ and are weakly sequentially complete.

papers.title: One-dimensional second-gradient elasticity: pantograph-inspired energies and solitary waves
papers.authors: R. S. Hallyburton, I. Giorgio, C. Rodriguez
papers.abstract: We present a self-contained formulation of longitudinal motion in one-dimensional second-gradient continua. Starting from finite-strain kinematics, we then apply the Principle of Virtual Power to identify the governing field equation and contact actions, derive the balance laws, and establish the mechanical-energy identity for hyperelastic materials. Motivated by pantographic microstructures, we study a class of finite-strain energies formulated in terms of normalized strain measures and deformation-dependent strain-gradient moduli. For the associated equation of motion, a traveling-wave first integral yields a turning-point criterion for the existence of solitary waves with positive stretch, exponential decay, and finite mechanical energy, as well as uniqueness at each fixed speed within a prescribed strain interval. For suitable spring energies, a change of strain variable reduces this integral to a polynomial equation, yielding explicit tensile and compressive profiles for Green--Lagrange and Hencky strains under appropriate parameter and kinematic conditions. Under the positivity condition on the quartic potential, the constructed Hencky energy has several physically natural properties: it is nonnegative, admits the natural state as its unique zero and global minimizer, has a positive linearized modulus, penalizes stretch gradients, and diverges under both material collapse and unlimited extension. Furthermore, the stored energy is coercive with respect to the $H^1$ norm of logarithmic strain. Together with mechanical-energy conservation, this yields uniform upper and positive lower bounds on stretch throughout the lifespan of smooth solutions. The theory's accessible mechanical origin, relatively simple mathematical foundation, and diverse solitary waves offer a tractable entry point to studying the rich nonlinear dispersive equations governing higher-gradient elastic continua.

papers.title: On the diameter and distribution of Sidon sets
papers.authors: Daniel Carter, Kevin O'Bryant, Terence Tao
papers.abstract:
A Sidon set is a set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers with the property that if $0\neq a-b=c-d$ and $a,b,c,d\in\mathcal{A}$, then $(a,b)=(c,d)$. Our main result is an improved and explicit bound on the diameter of a Sidon set: if $\mathcal{A}$ is a Sidon set with $k\ge 1$ elements, then
  \[\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge k^2 \left(\frac{1}{1 + 0.945/\sqrt{k}}-\frac{0.945}{\sqrt k}\right) -1;\] in particular, $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A})\ge k^2-1.89 k^{3/2}$. This implies that if $\mathcal{A}\subseteq[1,N]$ is a Sidon set, then $|\mathcal{A}| \le N^{1/2}+0.945 \, N^{1/4}+0.447$. Our technique also gives an improved bound for the case of large $k$, namely $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A}) \ge k^2-1.88607 k^{3/2}$ for $k\ge 483$. A $\gamma$-Golomb ruler is a set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers with the property that there are not $\gamma+1$ distinct pairs $(a_i,b_i)\in\mathcal{A}^2$ with $0\neq a_1-b_1=\cdots=a_{\gamma+1}-b_{\gamma+1}$. Our diameter bounds extend in a natural way to the case of Golomb rulers. Our techniques can also be adapted to address a number of questions on the distribution of Golomb rulers: we provide upper bounds on the two quantities $\left|a_\ell-a_1 -\frac{\ell-1}{k-1}(a_k-a_1)\right|$ and $\max_{1\le i<k} (a_{i+1}-a_i)$, where $\mathcal{A}=\{a_1<\dots<a_k\}$ is a $\gamma$-Golomb ruler with $\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{A})\le (k^2-bk^{3/2})/\gamma$ (where $b\in \mathbb{R}$ is a free parameter).

papers.title: Recognizing convergence actions as proper isometric actions on hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: Relying merely on B.I. (a.k.a. Bowditch's intelligence), we show that whenever a group $G$ admits a convergence action on a compact perfect metrizable space $M$, there is a hyperbolic space $X$ along with a proper isometric action of $G$ on $X$ inducing a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $f:M \rightarrow \partial X.$ This answers a question by Misha Kapovich.

papers.title: Contact topology and intrinsic characterization of transversely vanishing curl eigenforms
papers.abstract: We study the geometry and topology of transversely vanishing eigenforms of the curl operator on $3$-manifolds, placing them in the broader framework of near-contact forms. We prove a Gray-type stability theorem for the kernels of near-contact forms, which we call near-contact structures, and derive a local neighborhood theorem around their singularities. As applications, we obtain a stability result for the contact topology of curl eigenforms, a classification of near-contact structures in terms of formal homotopical data, and a proof of the existence of contact structures on closed orientable 3-manifolds based on the spectral theory of the curl operator. We also study the symplectization of curl eigenforms as a possible bridge to symplectic dynamics. Finally, we characterize those transversely vanishing $1$-forms which are curl eigenforms for some smooth Riemannian metric. We deduce a generalization of the classical correspondence, due to Etnyre and Ghrist, between Reeb-like fields of contact forms and nowhere-vanishing rotational Beltrami fields to the setting of transversely vanishing vector fields.

papers.title: Explicit Reed-Solomon Subspace Designs: Optimal List and Line Decoding
papers.authors: Omar Alrabiah, Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami
papers.abstract:
For any desired rate $R \in (0,1)$, and gap to list-decoding capacity $\varepsilon > 0$, we give an explicit $n^{O_{\varepsilon}(1)}$ time construction of Reed-Solomon codes over extension fields of size polynomial in the block length $n$ that can be list-decoded from a fraction $1-R-\varepsilon$ of errors with the optimal list-size of $O(\frac{1-R}{\varepsilon})$. We also give a simpler, strongly explicit construction of evaluation points for which the associated Reed-Solomon code can be list-decoded from $1-R-\varepsilon$ errors with list size $(1/\varepsilon)^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$. We provide a deterministic list-decoding algorithm for both constructions running in time $O_{\epsilon}(1)\mathsf{poly}(n)$.
  In fact, our Reed-Solomon codes are near-optimal subspace-design codes over a subfield. Via known results, this directly implies the combinatorial list-decoding guarantee, as well as near-optimal list-recovery bounds. We also present a new reduction showing that the subspace-design guarantee also implies line decoding over the extension field itself, which then yields proximity gaps and mutual correlated agreement up to proximity parameter approaching the optimal $1-R$ radius.
  Compared to the recent algorithm of Brakensiek, Chen, Putterman, Zhang, and Zheng (2026), which list decodes every Reed-Solomon code over prime fields up to capacity, our approach achieves constant (in fact, near-optimal) list size rather than a polynomially growing one, at the cost of carefully choosing the code's evaluation points. In a companion paper, we show that these respective restrictions are unavoidable.

papers.title: Computer-assisted proofs of periodic solutions of state-dependent delay equations beyond perturbative regimes
papers.authors: Jan Bouwe van den Berg, Maxime Breden, Matthieu Cadiot, Kevin E. M. Church, Jean-Philippe Lessard
papers.abstract: Rigorous existence results for periodic solutions of state-dependent delay differential equations (SDDEs) are scarce outside perturbative regimes, where the equation is close to an ordinary or constant-delay differential equation. We develop a computer-assisted framework that proves the existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs directly. The numerical approximation is a trigonometric polynomial, and a true periodic solution nearby is obtained by a Newton--Kantorovich argument in the space of $C^1$ periodic functions. The main difficulty lies in the terms in which the solution is evaluated at a time that itself depends on the solution. We obtain rigorous enclosures of their Fourier coefficients by adapting validated discrete Fourier transform techniques for analytic nonlinearities. We apply the framework to three representative examples of increasing complexity: a periodically forced toy model, an autonomous scalar equation with two state-dependent delays, and a threshold-type delay model from operon dynamics in gene regulation. To our knowledge, these are the first computer-assisted proofs of existence of periodic solutions of SDDEs outside perturbative regimes. This opens the way to computer-assisted proofs for SDDEs more broadly. All computer-assisted proofs, including the requisite codes and the approximate objects, are accessible on GitHub at \cite{code_proof}.

papers.title: Finite-Branch Multipliers on a H\"older Algebra: Commutants, Norm Closures, and Essential Spectra
papers.abstract: Noninjective multiplication symbols allow commuting operators to mix function values along their fibers, while H\"older regularity constrains this mixing at branch points. We study these operators on the Banach algebra $A_\beta$, $0<\beta<1$, defined by a restricted interval-variation condition. For $u(t)=t(1-t)$, we determine the full commutant $\{M_u\}'=\mathscr C_\beta$, including operators whose reflection coefficients need not belong to $A_\beta$. Separately, we characterize the operator-norm closure $J_\beta$ of the regular multiplication--reflection subalgebra of $\mathscr C_\beta$, obtain two-sided norm-distance estimates, and find a complemented copy of $\ell^\infty/c_0$ in the Banach-space quotient $\mathscr C_\beta/J_\beta$. Every $T\in\mathscr C_\beta$ satisfies $\sigma(T)=\sigma_{\mathrm{ap}}(T)=\sigma_{\mathrm{usf}}(T)=\sigma_{\mathrm{ess}}(T)$, and Fredholmness is equivalent to invertibility. For multipliers with finitely many full bi-Lipschitz branches, we also characterize their full commutants and establish the same spectral equalities for every commuting operator. For the regular finite-branch algebra, we establish an exact norm-closure criterion using weighted local H\"older defects and separate row-difference conditions, even when several folds share a level.

papers.title: The reverse isoperimetric inequality for convex shapes included in a triangle
papers.authors: Rida Ait El Manssour, Zakaria Fattah, Ilias Ftouhi
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp reverse isoperimetric inequality for convex subsets of a triangle under a prescribed area constraint. Given a triangle $T$ and an area fraction $\eta\in(0,1)$, we determine the set with maximal perimeter among convex bodies $K\subset T$ satisfying $|K|=\eta|T|$ and characterize the equality cases. Every maximizer is a triangle, and the optimal configuration is obtained by retaining a longest side of $T$ and placing the third vertex on a shortest side, at the position determined by the area constraint. This characterization yields an explicit expression for the maximal perimeter in terms of $\eta$ and the side lengths of $T$.

papers.title: On the existence of polarized varieties without weakly Ulrich bundles
papers.abstract: We give an obstruction to the existence of bundles $\mathcal E$ on a smooth $n$-dimensional polarized variety such that $\mathcal E$ is $a$-regular and ${\mathcal E}^*(K_X+(n+1)H)$ is $b$-regular. In particular, this gives an obstruction to the existence of weakly Ulrich bundles. Using the latter and some recent examples of [A1] in dimension $2$, we prove that for any $n \ge 2$ there exist many smooth $n$-dimensional varieties $X$ with a very ample line bundle $H$, such that there is no weakly Ulrich bundle for $(X,H)$.

papers.title: Cost benefits of designing carbon capture processes for part-load operation of power plants
papers.authors: David Yang Shu, Boxun Huang, Yurim Kim, Rahul Gandhi, Randall Field, Sungho Shin
papers.abstract: As fossil power plants increasingly cycle to balance variable renewable generation, carbon capture plants must be designed for a wide range of part-load operating conditions, to avoid excessive capital costs. However, accounting for the variability in design optimization yields higher computational complexity, and is therefore not a current design methodology. Here, we apply two-stage stochastic optimization to identify optimal carbon capture plant designs accounting for part-load flue gas conditions. We reduce computational complexity through a data-driven approach-to-equilibrium model of the absorption and desorption processes. Operating scenarios are derived from real-world part-load operation data of coal and natural gas combined cycle power plants.
