We provide a compactness result and prove that the {\Gamma}-limit of the energy is a multiple of the perimeter. In particular, using the recently introduced unfolding operator for multiple scales, we show that the taking the limit of all of the scales together is equivalent to taking one limit at the time, starting from the smaller scale and keeping the larger fixed.

papers.title: Free boundary regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem
papers.abstract: We study the regularity and well-posedness of physical solutions to the supercooled Stefan problem. Assuming only that the initial temperature is integrable, we prove that the free boundary, known to have jump discontinuities as a function of the time variable, is $C^1$ as a function of the space variable, and is $C^{\infty}$ outside of a closed, countable set, which we describe explicitly. We also prove that, as conjectured in arXiv:1902.05174, the set of positive times when a jump occurs cannot have accumulation points. In addition, we prove that short-time uniqueness of physical solutions implies global uniqueness, which allows us to obtain uniqueness for very general initial data that fall outside the scope of the current well-posedness regime. In particular, we answer two questions left open in arXiv:1811.12356, arXiv:2302.13097, regarding the global uniqueness of solutions. We proceed by deriving a weighted obstacle problem satisfied by the solutions, which we exploit to establish regularity and non-degeneracy estimates and to classify the free boundary points. We also establish a backward propagation of oscillation property, which allows us to control the occurrence of future jumps in terms of the past oscillation of the solution.

papers.title: Shape differentials and sensitivity of the heat equation
papers.authors: Matteo Dalla Riva, Paolo Luzzini, Paolo Musolino
papers.abstract: We consider Dirichlet and Neumann problems for the heat equation in a domain containing an interior hole. The domain has a fixed outer boundary and a variable inner boundary determined by a diffeomorphism $\phi$. We analyze the maps that assign to the infinite-dimensional shape parameter $\phi$ the corresponding solutions, and we prove that they are smooth. Motivated by applications to inverse problems, we then compute the differentials with respect to $\phi$ of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann and Neumann-to-Dirichlet maps.

papers.title: A general approach to permutation polynomials from quadratic forms
papers.abstract: We investigate a family of polynomials over finite fields of characteristic $2$ related to quadratic forms, and present a general treatment to study permutation properties of those polynomials. By determining some character sums associated with quadratic forms, we explicitly describe several classes of permutation polynomials.

papers.title: Perturbed Gradient Descent Algorithms are Small-Disturbance Input-to-State Stable
papers.authors: Leilei Cui, Zhong-Ping Jiang, Eduardo D. Sontag, Richard D. Braatz
papers.abstract: This article investigates the robustness of gradient descent algorithms under perturbations. The concept of small-disturbance input-to-state stability (ISS) for discrete-time nonlinear dynamical systems is introduced, along with its Lyapunov characterization. The conventional linear Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition is then extended to a nonlinear version, and it is shown that the gradient descent algorithm is small-disturbance ISS provided the objective function satisfies the generalized nonlinear PL condition. This small-disturbance ISS property guarantees that the gradient descent algorithm converges to a small neighborhood of the optimum under sufficiently small perturbations. As a direct application of the developed framework, we demonstrate that the LQR cost satisfies the generalized nonlinear PL condition, thereby establishing that the policy gradient algorithm for LQR is small-disturbance ISS. Additionally, other popular policy gradient algorithms, including natural policy gradient and Gauss-Newton method, are also proven to be small-disturbance ISS.

papers.title: A Li-Yau gradient estimate for the Finslerian logarithmic Schr\"{o}dinger equation
papers.abstract: We establish a local Li--Yau type gradient estimate for a nonlinear parabolic equation with logarithmic reaction on a forward complete Finsler metric measure manifold. The coefficients may depend on both space and time. The estimate uses a weighted Ricci curvature lower bound and explicit cutoff bounds for the divergence-form linearized Laplacian. We explain the role of this localization assumption when the reference direction varies with the solution. Applications include a local Harnack inequality for the equation with a potential and an upper bound for positive stationary solutions under a suitable cutoff exhaustion. An appendix gives a variational existence proof for positive bounded initial data, with quantitative bounds on every finite time interval, which is new as far as the authors know.

papers.title: On Fermat's Last Theorem over the $\mathbb{Z}_3$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and other fields
papers.abstract: The main result of the present article is a proof that, over certain totally real number fields $K$, the Fermat equation $x^p+y^p+z^p=0$ has no non-trivial primitive solutions in $\mathcal{O}_K$ for sufficiently large prime exponents $p$ with $p \equiv 2 \pmod{3}$. A particular case of these fields are the maximal real subfields of the cyclotomic extensions $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{3^n})$ for every $n$. Our strategy consists in combining the modular method with a generalization of an arithmetic result of Pomey to these fields.

papers.title: Submanifolds with boundary in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg Groups
papers.abstract: We discuss the notion of submanifolds with boundary with intrinsic $C^1$ regularity in sub-Riemannian Heisenberg groups and we provide some examples. Eventually, we present a Stokes' Theorem for such submanifolds involving the integration of Rumin's differential forms in Heisenberg groups.

papers.title: Ehrhart non-positivity and unimodular triangulations for classes of s-lecture hall simplices
papers.authors: Jhon B. Caicedo, Martina Juhnke, Germain Poullot
papers.abstract: Counting lattice points and triangulating polytopes is a prominent subject in discrete geometry, yet proving Ehrhart positivity or existence of unimodular triangulations remain of utmost difficulty in general, even for ``easy'' simplices. We study these problems for classes of s-lecture hall simplices. Inspired by a question of Olsen, we present a new natural class of sequences s for which the s-lecture hall simplices are not Ehrhart positive, by explicitly estimating a negative coefficient. Meanwhile, motivated by a conjecture of Hibi, Olsen and Tsuchiya, we extend the previously known classes of sequences s for which the s-lecture hall simplex admits a flag, regular and unimodular triangulation. The triangulations we construct are explicit.

papers.title: Hypergeometric Motives from Toric Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study two compactifications of general hypersurfaces defined by the vanishing of linear combinations of $d+2$ monomials in $d$-dimensional algebraic tori. We prove that the number of their $\mathbb{F}_q$-points is given by finite hypergeometric sums under certain general conditions. In the process, we introduce the notion of a gamma triple, which allows us to extend the classical definition of finite hypergeometric sums to prime powers corresponding to the cyclotomic field of definition of the associated monodromy representation. As a special case of our main results, we study the Dwork family and obtain a formula for the number of its $\mathbb{F}_q$-points. Our results generalise the work of Beukers, Cohen, and Mellit for finite hypergeometric sums defined over $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: Affine super Yangian and Weyl groupoid(extended)
papers.abstract: We study affine super Yangians of type $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n)$ over $\mathbb C[\hbar]$ for arbitrary cyclic parity sequences, with $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. We prove the equivalence of the full current and degree-zero-and-one presentations by reconstructing all current relations. A finite-type RTT calculation and a cut-diagram argument give explicit normalized quantum odd reflections, including the affine vertex. Together with even braid lifts and diagonal sign automorphisms, these maps satisfy the defining relations of an extended reflection groupoid. We compare the positive-root tensors under odd reflection and identify their difference with the reduced coproduct of the quadratic Cartan correction. Starting from the distinguished coproduct, this establishes the prescribed coassociative coproduct for every cyclic parity sequence. We specify the compatible degreewise completions needed for coproduct comparison at the affine vertex.

papers.title: Semisimple module categories with fusion rules of the compact flag manifold type
papers.abstract: We classify semisimple left module categories over the representation category of a type A quantum group whose fusion rules arise from Levi subalgebras. The classification is connected to equivariant Poisson structures on compact flag manifolds in the operator-algebraic setting, and on semisimple coadjoint orbits in the algebraic setting. We also provide an explicit construction based on the BGG categories of deformed quantum enveloping algebras, whose unitarizability corresponds to being of quotient type. Finally, we present a brief discussion of the non-quantum group case

papers.title: Nonrelativistic limit of nonlinear Dirac ground states on noncompact quantum graphs
papers.authors: Guangze Gu, Michael Ruzhansky, Guoyan Wei, Zhipeng Yang
papers.abstract: We study the nonrelativistic limit of nonlinear Dirac ground states on finite noncompact metric graphs with Kirchhoff-type conditions. For a nondecreasing nonlinearity of arbitrary finite superquadratic growth, a sufficiently long pendant path guarantees ground states whose nonrelativistic limits are Schr\"odinger ground states. Every choice of these states is relatively compact in $H^1$ and satisfies a uniform exponential decay estimate. On general graphs, we prove a compactness alternative: loss of compactness requires at least the action of a full-line ground state. Translated line profiles show that the loss constants are sharp. The proof combines an $H^1$ estimate in terms of the action with convergence of Dirac fiber maxima to Schr\"odinger ray maxima. For power nonlinearities, we give an integral criterion in terms of the dimensionless pendant length and obtain the same conclusions for arbitrary edge lengths on four graph topologies.

papers.title: Minimal depth $K$-types for wild double covers and Shimura correspondences
papers.abstract:
Using distinguished pseudo-spherical representations of covering tori constructed in a companion work and Dat's parahoric induction, we construct a distinguished family of representations for an Iwahori subgroup $\bar{I}$ in $\bar{G}$, an $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne (BD) cover of a split connected reductive $p$-adic group $G$, under explicit hypotheses on the BD datum. No tameness assumption $\mathrm{gcd}(p,n)=1$ is imposed.
  The construction suggests a conjectural theory of Iwahori-types for BD covers beyond the tame case. We verify this for $2$-fold covers of almost simple simply-laced simply-connected Chevalley groups of rank at least $2$ over $2$-adic fields. In particular, for these non-tame $2$-fold covers we prove:
  1) The pair $(\bar{I},\sigma)$ is a Bushnell-Kutzko type for the Bernstein block analogous to the block of unramified principal series in a linear reductive group. This is a non-tame analogue of the Borel-Casselman theorem.
  2) The Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}(\bar{G},\bar{I},\sigma^{\vee})$ has an Iwahori-Matsumoto presentation up to normalization. In types $A_{r},D_{2r+1},E_{6},E_{7}$ we obtain the complete presentation and show that $\mathcal{H}(\bar{G},\bar{I},\sigma^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of an explicit linear group. This determines an equivalence of Bernstein blocks producing a local Shimura correspondence.
  3) The representation $\sigma$ extends to a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup $\bar{K}$. Among the genuine $\bar{K}$-representations, $\sigma$ has minimal depth with respect to the principal congruence filtration. It also yields a finite Shimura correspondence, generalizing a result of Savin.

papers.title: Re-framing the classification of ideals in noncommutative tensor triangular geometry
papers.authors: Timothy De Deyn, Sam K. Miller
papers.abstract: We prove that a 'pseudo-Hochster dual' of the noncommutative Balmer spectrum of a monoidal triangulated category classifies its semiprime thick tensor ideals. This extends Balmer's classification of radical thick tensor ideals to noncommutative tensor triangular geometry. To achieve this, we utilize the notion of support data for lattices and frames, under which the classification follows via Stone duality. We also give a characterization for when the noncommutative Balmer spectrum behaves as it does in tensor triangular geometry, that is, when it is a spectral space with quasi-compact opens given by complements of supports. Finally, we show that rigid centrally generated monoidal triangulated categories satisfy this property, and we answer a question posed by Negron--Pevtsova regarding classification of one-sided tensor ideals via cohomological support.

papers.title: Deformation of nef adjoint canonical line bundles
papers.authors: Mu-Lin Li, Sheng Rao, Kai Wang
papers.abstract:
Much inspired by J. A. Wi\'sniewski's nef-value function method, we prove that in a smooth projective family over the unit disk, if the adjoint bundle of the canonical line bundle with a relatively semiample line bundle is nef on one fiber, then it remains nef on all fibers. We further extend this result to the semiampleness of the adjoint canonical line bundles. Using these, we prove the deformation invariance of any generalized plurigenera by assuming that only one fiber admits the semiample canonical line bundle and improve the first author--Xiao-Lei Liu's recent deformation rigidity of projective manifolds with semiample canonical line bundles. In particular, also by E. Viehweg--K. Zuo's result on the minimal number of singular fibers in a family and the first author--X. Liu's isotriviality result, if a projective family over $\mathbb{P}^1$ or an elliptic curve has one fiber with the big and nef (or more generally semiample) canonical line bundle, then all fibers are isomorphic to this fiber.
  Next, much inspired by M. Andreatta--T. Peternell's deformation theoretical approach, we prove that, in a smooth K\"ahler family of threefolds, if the canonical line bundle of one fiber is not nef, then none of its small deformations admits a nef canonical line bundle either. This partially confirms a problem posed by F. Campana--T. Peternell and the global stability of semiampleness of canonical line bundles of threefolds under a K\"ahler smooth deformation.

papers.title: Foundations of Double Operator Integrals with a Variant Approach to the Nonseparable Case
papers.abstract: We aim to give a self-contained and detailed yet simplified account of the foundations of the theory of double operator integrals, in order to provide an accessible entry point to the theory. We make two new contributions to these foundations: (1) a new proof of the existence of the product of two projection-valued measures, which allows for the definition of the double operator integral for Hilbert-Schmidt operators, and (2) a variant approach to the integral projective tensor product on arbitrary (not necessarily separable) Hilbert spaces using a somewhat more explicit norm than has previously been given. We prove the Daletskii-Krein formula for strongly differentiable perturbations of a densely-defined self-adjoint operator and conclude by reviewing an application of the theory to quantum statistical mechanics.

papers.title: Inverse stability for hyperbolic equations with different initial conditions
papers.abstract: We establish Lipschitz stability for both the potential and the initial conditions from a single boundary measurement in the context of a hyperbolic boundary initial value problem. In our setting, the initial conditions are allowed to differ for different potentials. Compared to the traditional B-K method, our approach does not require the time reflection step. This advantage opens a route towards applying our method to the fixed angle inverse scattering problem, which remains unresolved for the single incident wave case. To achieve our result, we impose a pointwise comparison estimate on the Laplacian of the differences of the initial conditions, together with a positivity condition on one of the initial positions. The assumption generalizes previous stability results that usually assume the difference to be zero. We propose the initial-potential problem and establish a Lipschitz stability, then propose an iterative reconstruction scheme and show its geometric convergence. The initial-potential problem serves as an attempt to relate initial boundary value problem to the scattering problem, and to explore the possibility of relaxing the positivity requirement on the initial data. We also establish a new pointwise Carleman estimate, whose proof is significantly shorter and the reasoning is much clearer than existing proofs.

papers.title: Data-Driven Distributionally Robust Planning of Coastal Distribution Networks and PV-Storage-EV Stations for Low-Carbon Energy Transition
papers.authors: Wenhao Gao, Yongheng Wang, Yangfan Luo, Xinwei Shen
papers.abstract: Coastal distribution networks (DNs) are becoming key infrastructure for the low-carbon energy transition as electric vehicle (EV) charging, photovoltaic (PV) generation, energy storage, and marine renewable procurement are increasingly coupled at the planning stage. Existing planning models, however, usually treat network expansion, PV-storage-EV station (PSES) deployment, low-carbon operation, and coastal asset degradation separately. This paper proposes a data-driven distributionally robust planning framework for coastal DNs and PSESs. The framework jointly optimizes radial network topology and PSES siting while incorporating salt-spray degradation costs, carbon-emission-flow (CEF)-based nodal carbon accounting, and tidal-generation-driven procurement costs. To represent heterogeneous uncertainty, the model combines continuous box uncertainty for load and PV availability with probability ambiguity over EV-charging scenarios generated from historical charging profiles. The resulting two-stage distributionally robust optimization problem is reformulated through exact relaxation of ESS mode binaries and KKT-based decomposition, and is solved by an inexact column-and-constraint generation (i-C&CG) algorithm. Case studies on a realistic 47-node coastal feeder show that salt-spray exposure can alter the selected topology and PSES siting, while the proposed planning scheme improves voltage quality, reduces annualized total cost, and reveals the cost--carbon trade-off of tidal procurement. The tailored i-C&CG algorithm obtains the same optimal design as conventional C&CG with about an order-of-magnitude reduction in solution time.

papers.title: A derivative-free trust-region approach for Low Order-Value Optimization problems
papers.authors: Anderson E. Schwertner, Francisco N. C. Sobral
papers.abstract: The Low Order-Value Optimization (LOVO) problem involves minimizing the minimum among a finite number of function values within a feasible set. LOVO has several practical applications such as robust parameter estimation, protein alignment, portfolio optimization, among others. In this work, we are interested in the constrained nonlinear optimization LOVO problem of minimizing the minimum between a finite number of function values subject to a nonempty closed convex set where each function is a black-box and continuously differentiable, but the derivatives are not available. We develop the first derivative-free trust-region algorithm for constrained LOVO problems with convergence to weakly critical points. Under suitable conditions, we establish the global convergence of the algorithm and also its worst-case iteration complexity analysis. An initial open-source implementation using only linear interpolation models is developed. Extensive numerical experiments and comparison with existing alternatives show the properties and the efficiency of the proposed approach when solving LOVO problems.

papers.title: Terminal Geometry of Rank-Two Nielsen Reduction on Simplicial Trees
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a locally finite simplicial tree, and let $\Gamma=\langle\gamma_1,\gamma_2\rangle\leq\mathrm{Aut}(X)$ be a discrete subgroup generated by hyperbolic automorphisms acting without inversions, whose axes have finite edge intersection. We locate explicitly, using the Euclidean algorithm, the first stopping state of rank-two Nielsen reduction and determine the exact characteristic-set geometry of its terminal Nielsen pair. Write $m_1\geq m_2>0$ for the normalized translation lengths, $l$ for the axis-overlap length, and $d=\gcd(m_1,m_2)$. If $l=0$, the initial pair satisfies the Schottky criterion. If $l>0$, Euclidean quotients and remainders partition $0<l\leq m_1+m_2-d$ into intervals locating the first stopping state and its ordered Nielsen generators. Interior points yield terminal Schottky pairs. At nonfinal right endpoints, an auxiliary translated-axis overlap $l_0$ distinguishes Schottky terminal pairs from pairs containing a nontrivial elliptic generator. At the final endpoint and for larger overlaps, a nontrivial elliptic terminal generator occurs. We compute the terminal translation lengths and the relative geometry of axes or fixed subtrees in every case. Each terminal pair is Nielsen-equivalent to the initial pair and generates $\Gamma$. If both terminal generators are hyperbolic, they form a Schottky pair; otherwise exactly one is nontrivial elliptic. By local finiteness and discreteness, this element has finite order, so $\Gamma$ contains nontrivial torsion and is not free of rank two.

papers.title: The Lefschetz standard conjectures for 4d-dimensional Kummer-type hyper-Kaehler varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the Lefschetz standard conjectures for 4d-dimensional projective varieties of generalized Kummer deformation type. Along the way, we prove a generalization of a theorem of Buchweitz and Flenner in the analytic setting

papers.title: Two Non--Commutative U(1)-Gauge Laplacians in the Quantum Hyperboloid
papers.abstract: In this paper, we will characterize the spectrum of two $U(1)$--gauge Laplacians, which do not commute with each other, on the upper sheet of a two--sheet quantum hyperboloid equipped with a concrete differential calculus; while we provide a thorough and comprehensive study of the geometric structures on the related quantum spaces.

papers.title: Stability conditions on products of curves and Hilbert schemes of surfaces
papers.authors: Chunyi Li, Emanuele Macr\`i, Alexander Perry, Paolo Stellari, Xiaolei Zhao
papers.abstract: We prove that stability conditions on the derived category of a product of curves of positive genus are uniquely determined by their central charge and the phase of skyscraper sheaves. As an application, we construct stability conditions on Hilbert schemes of points on certain surfaces, including some K3 surfaces of Kummer type.

papers.title: On the distribution kernels of Toeplitz operators on CR manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the distribution kernel of a Toeplitz operator associated with a classical pseudodifferential operator on a compact, embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold. The main result consists of a formula for the values at the diagonal of the second coefficient in the expansion of the symbol of the kernel. We also establish asymptotic expansions for Toeplitz operators on the positive part of a compact not necessary strictly pseudoconvex CR orbifold under certain natural assumptions.

papers.title: A combinatorial description of when a self-associated set of points fails to be arithmetically Gorenstein
papers.authors: Gonzalo Rodr\'iguez-Pajares, Diego Ruano, Flavio Salizzoni
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial proof that the set of points associated to a self-dual code with no proportional columns is arithmetically Gorenstein if and only if the code is indecomposable. This answers a question asked by Toh\u{a}neanu. We do so by providing a combinatorial way to compute the dimension of the Schur square of a self-dual code through a zero-one symmetrization of a systematic generator matrix. Our approach also allows us to compute the Gorenstein defect. As a consequence, we obtain a combinatorial characterization of arithmetically Gorenstein self-associated sets of points over an algebraically closed field. We also show that, for any finite field, almost all self-dual codes of large length are indecomposable, and hence their associated sets of points are arithmetically Gorenstein.

papers.title: Limit theorems for the distance between two random points in $l_p^n$-balls
papers.authors: David Alonso-Guti\'errez, Javier Mart\'in Go\~ni, Joscha Prochno
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the Euclidean distance between two independent random vectors uniformly distributed on $l_p^n$-balls ($1\leq p\leq\infty$) or on their boundaries according to the cone measure satisfies a central limit theorem as $n\to\infty$. Also, we give a compact proof of the case of the sphere, which was proved by Hammersley. Furthermore, we complement our central limit theorems by providing large deviation principles for points in the balls and on their boundaries when $1\leq p\leq\infty$. The speed is $n$ for $p\geq2$, whereas the regime $1\leq p<2$ has speed $n^{p/2}$ and an explicit rate function.

papers.title: Limit Computation Over Posets via Minimal Initial Functors
papers.abstract: It is well known that limits can be computed by restricting along an initial functor, and that this often simplifies limit computation. We systematically study the algorithmic implications of this idea for diagrams indexed by a poset. We say an initial functor $F\colon C\to D$ with $C$ small is minimal if the sets of objects and morphisms of $C$ each have minimum cardinality, among the sources of all initial functors with target $D$. For $Q$ a finite poset or $Q\subseteq \mathbb N^d$ an interval (i.e., a convex, connected subposet), we describe all minimal initial functors $F\colon P\to Q$. In particular, we show that such $F$ is always a subposet inclusion, up to isomorphism. We give efficient algorithms to compute a choice of minimal initial functor. In the case that $Q\subseteq \mathbb N^d$ is an interval, we give asymptotically optimal bounds on $|\hom P|$, the number of relations in $P$ (including identities), in terms of the number $n$ of minima of $Q$: We show that $|\hom P|=\Theta(n)$ for $d\leq 3$, and $|\hom P|=\Theta(n^2)$ for $d>3$. We apply these results to give new bounds on the cost of computing $\lim G$ for a functor $G \colon Q\to \mathbf{Vec}$ valued in vector spaces. For $Q$ connected, we also give new bounds on the cost of computing the generalized rank of $G$ (i.e., the rank of the induced map $\lim G\to \operatorname{colim} G$), which is of interest in topological data analysis.

papers.title: A Constructive Method to Maximize Entropy under Marginal Constraints
papers.abstract: We study the problem of maximizing R{\'e}nyi entropy of order $2$ (equivalently, minimizing the index of coincidence) over the set of joint distributions with prescribed marginals. A closed-form optimizer is known under a feasibility condition on the marginals; we show that this condition is highly restrictive. We then provide an explicit construction of an optimal coupling for arbitrary marginals. Our approach characterizes the optimizer's structure and yields an iterative algorithm that terminates in finite time, returning an exact solution after at most $p-1$ updates, where $p$ is the number of rows.

papers.title: Total curvature of convex hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that if the curvature of a Cartan-Hadamard $n$-manifold is constant near a convex hypersurface $\Gamma$, then the total Gauss-Kronecker curvature $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$ is not less than that of any convex hypersurface nested inside $\Gamma$. This extends Borb\'{e}ly's monotonicity theorem in hyperbolic space. It follows that $\mathcal{G}(\Gamma)$ is bounded below by the volume of the unit sphere in Euclidean space $\mathbf{R}^n$. If $n=3$ or $\Gamma$ is $\mathcal{C}^{1,1}$, it suffices that the curvature be constant on $\Gamma$.

papers.title: Unimodular random ideal hyperbolic polyhedra: geometric characteristics and random walks
papers.authors: Huabin Ge, Yangxiang Lu, Chuwen Wang, Tian Zhou
papers.abstract:
We initiate a systematic study of unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra in three-dimensional hyperbolic space, developing a geometric and probabilistic theory of their global behavior. At the heart of this theory is an intrinsic geometric characteristic, determined entirely by the dihedral angles surrounding a polyhedral face. We establish a unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity and show that the expectation of this local geometric invariant completely determines the global conformal type: under suitable assumptions, a random ideal polyhedron is almost surely parabolic precisely when the expected characteristic vanishes, and hyperbolic precisely when it is negative. This provides a sharp geometric classification of random infinite ideal polyhedra.
  Building on the correspondence with ideal circle patterns, we further develop a refined Ring Lemma that yields quantitative geometric control without bounded-degree assumptions. Combining these geometric tools with unimodular probability methods, we identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Together, these results establish a local-to-global framework linking intrinsic dihedral geometry, conformal uniformization, and stochastic behavior at infinity for unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra.

papers.title: Counting Saddle Connections on Hyperelliptic Translation Surfaces with a Slit
papers.authors: David Aulicino, Howard Masur, Huiping Pan, Weixu Su
papers.abstract: We consider saddle connections on a translation surface in a hyperelliptic connected component of a stratum that do not intersect the interior of a distinguished saddle connection. For this restricted set of saddle connections, we show that it satisfies an $L (\log L)^{d-2}$ growth rate, where $d$ is the complex dimension of the hyperelliptic stratum. The upper bound holds for all translation surfaces in the hyperelliptic stratum while the lower bound holds for almost every surface in the hyperelliptic stratum. The proof of the lower bound uses horocycle renormalization.

papers.title: Information Contraction under $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-Differentially Private Mechanisms
papers.authors: Theshani Nuradha, Ian George, Christoph Hirche
papers.abstract: The distinguishability quantified by information measures after being processed by a private mechanism has been a useful tool in studying various statistical and operational tasks while ensuring privacy. To this end, standard data-processing inequalities and strong data-processing inequalities (SDPI) are employed. Most of the previously known and even tight characterizations of contraction of information measures, including total variation distance, hockey-stick divergences, and $f$-divergences, are applicable for $(\varepsilon,0)$-local differential private (LDP) mechanisms. In this work, we derive both linear and non-linear strong data-processing inequalities for hockey-stick divergence and $f$-divergences that are valid for all $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-LDP mechanisms even when $\delta \neq 0$. Our results either generalize or improve the previously known bounds on the contraction of these distinguishability measures.

papers.title: Quantitative stability and strict inequalities for the Escobar functional
papers.abstract: For Euclidean domains whose boundaries are sufficiently close to a sphere in $C^2$, we bound the deficit of the Escobar constant from below by the squared $H^{3/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, after fixing its constant and first spherical harmonics. This holds in every dimension $n\ge3$ and implies a bound in Fraenkel asymmetry with optimal quadratic power. Under fixed $C^{6,\alpha}$ and size bounds, the asymmetry estimate also holds for star-shaped domains in dimensions $n\ge6$. For compact Riemannian manifolds with minimal boundary and uniform geometric bounds, we prove $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4/\log(\Lambda/a)$ in dimension six and $S_\ast-C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)\ge ca^4$ in higher dimensions, where $a=\|\mathring{\mathrm{II}}\|_{L^\infty}>0$. A family satisfying the same bounds has deficit comparable to $a^{8/3}$, excluding uniform lower bounds with smaller powers. We also compute the cubic coefficient of the standard boundary bubble quotient and give uniform remainder estimates.

papers.title: New explanations and inference for least angle regression
papers.authors: Karl B. Gregory, Daniel J. Nordman
papers.abstract: Efron et al. (2004) introduced least angle regression (LAR) as an algorithm for linear predictions, intended as an alternative to forward selection with connections to penalized regression. However, LAR has remained somewhat of a "black box," where some basic behavioral properties of LAR output are not well understood, including an appropriate termination point for the algorithm. We provide a novel framework for inference with LAR, which also allows LAR to be understood from new perspectives with several newly developed mathematical properties. The LAR algorithm at a data level can viewed as estimating a population counterpart "path" that organizes a response mean along regressor variables which are ordered according to a decreasing series of population "correlation" parameters; such parameters are shown to have meaningful interpretations for explaining variable contributions whereby zero correlations denote unimportant variables. In the output of LAR, estimates of all non-zero population correlations turn out to have independent normal distributions for use in inference, while estimates of zero-valued population correlations have a certain non-normal joint distribution. These properties help to provide a formal rule for stopping the LAR algorithm. While the standard bootstrap for regression can fail for LAR, a modified bootstrap provides a practical and formally justified tool for interpreting the entrance of variables and quantifying uncertainty in estimation. The LAR inference method is studied through simulation and illustrated with data examples.

papers.title: Derivation of the 3D quintic Gross--Pitaevskii equation
papers.authors: Arnaud Triay, Fran\c{c}ois L. A. Visconti
papers.abstract: We study the time evolution of Bose--Einstein condensates with three-body interactions in the Gross--Pitaevskii regime. We show that Bose--Einstein condensation is preserved under many-body evolution and that the condensate wavefunction evolves according to the quintic Gross--Pitaevskii equation in $\mathbb{R}^3$, which is energy critical. In particular, we show that the effective coupling constant is universal and depends only on a three-body scattering hypervolume.

papers.title: Some notes on tensor triangular geometry
papers.abstract:
These are notes from the lectures I gave at the Oberwolfach seminar `Tensor Triangular Geometry and Interactions' which was held in October 2025.
  The aim of these notes is to give an introduction to tensor triangular geometry, for both small and large categories, through the lens of lattice theory. We do not try to be exhaustive and this is reflected in both the content and the bibliography. For instance we are quite light on triangulated preliminaries, especially for compactly generated categories.
  The first three sections treat the essentially small case and conclude with a tensor triangular proof of Thomason's theorem computing the spectrum of the perfect complexes on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. The last section treats the compactly generated case. This final section is somewhat experimental and contains some new thoughts.

papers.title: Learning to Control: The iUzawa-Net for Nonsmooth Optimal Control of Linear PDEs
papers.authors: Yongcun Song, Xiaoming Yuan, Hangrui Yue, Tianyou Zeng
papers.abstract: We propose an optimization-informed deep neural network approach, named iUzawa-Net, aiming for the first solver that enables real-time solutions for a class of nonsmooth optimal control problems of linear partial differential equations (PDEs). The iUzawa-Net unrolls an inexact Uzawa method for saddle point problems, replacing classical preconditioners and PDE solvers with specifically designed learnable neural networks. We prove universal approximation properties and establish the asymptotic $\varepsilon$-optimality for the iUzawa-Net, and validate its promising numerical efficiency through nonsmooth elliptic and parabolic optimal control problems. Our techniques offer a versatile framework for designing and analyzing various optimization-informed deep learning approaches to optimal control and other PDE-constrained optimization problems. The proposed learning-to-control approach synergizes model-based optimization algorithms and data-driven deep learning techniques, inheriting the merits of both methodologies.

papers.title: Dehn quandles of surfaces and their bounded cohomology
papers.authors: Pankaj Kapari, Deepanshi Saraf, Mahender Singh
papers.abstract: We introduce new families of quandles associated with closed orientable surfaces that can distinguish surfaces up to homeomorphism. These quandles generalize the classical Dehn quandle and are defined, respectively, on isotopy classes of unoriented essential closed curves and on integral weighted multicurves. We establish their fundamental algebraic properties and construct a natural quandle covering relating the two families. We further investigate their large-scale geometry and prove that they are unbounded with respect to the quandle metric. We determine their second bounded quandle cohomology and show that its dimension equals the cardinality of the continuum. We also establish a quandle-theoretic analogue of the Gromov Mapping Theorem, showing that the natural projection from an abelian quandle extension onto its base quandle induces an injection on bounded quandle cohomology in every degree. Finally, motivated by recent developments in quandle algebras, we study idempotents in the integral quandle algebras associated with the classical Dehn quandle. In particular, we prove that the integral quandle algebra of the Dehn quandle of the torus admits no non-trivial idempotents.

papers.title: Local Differential Privacy for Molecular Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Molecular communication (MC) enables information exchange in nanoscale sensor networks operating in biological environments, yet privacy remains largely unaddressed. We integrate local differential privacy (LDP) into diffusion-based MC by privatizing each user's measurement at the transmitter and conveying the resulting randomized report over the MC channel. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic LDP implementation for diffusion-based MC, enabling privacy-preserving aggregate data analysis for in-body health monitoring and other population-scale sensing applications. We benchmark major LDP mechanisms under a realistic channel model. Simulation results show that Optimized Local Hashing (OLH) achieves the lowest average $\ell_1$ distribution-estimation error under the MC channel when channel resources are sufficient and the number of possible user values (alphabet size) $k$ is moderate to large, whereas k-ary Randomized Response (KRR) and, for privacy budget $\epsilon=1$, Binary Local Hashing (BLH), which have shorter reports, are more robust as the MC transmission quality deteriorates. We further propose RLIM-LDP, which combines run-length-limited ISI-mitigation (RLIM) coding with LDP coding. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that RLIM-LDP improves end-to-end reliability and reduces the final distribution-estimation error when time and molecule resources are limited.

papers.title: From Global Optimization to Exact Coordinates: Heilbronn's Triangle Problem on the Unit Square Using Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) approach for the Heilbronn triangle problem on the unit square. The formulation exploits the boundary structure of optimal configurations, which we establish rigorously, to fix coordinates and orientation variables a priori. With this formulation, a general-purpose global solver solves the case $n=9$ to global optimality within its numerical tolerances in about eight minutes on a laptop and without any precomputation, compared with about 23 hours of total computation for the best previous approach. The same model also solves $n=10$ for the first time, in under seven hours, and confirms the configuration of Comellas and Yebra (2002). The numerical solutions then guide an exact symbolic reconstruction, and the minimum triangle area of every reconstructed configuration is verified in exact arithmetic. This yields exact coordinates for all $n\le 10$, including the configurations of Comellas and Yebra (2002) for $n=9$ and $n=10$, together with rigorous lower bounds. Finally, we derive structural properties of optimal configurations, formulate a conjecture on the number of critical triangles, and pose an open question. All code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: Generic small-scale creation in the two-dimensional Euler equation
papers.abstract: The Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation is globally well-posed for smooth initial data. We prove that, for all $p>2$ and for a dense $G_\delta$ set of initial vorticities in $W^{1,p}$, the solutions lose regularity in infinite time, in the sense that the $L^p$ norm of the gradient of the vorticity is unbounded. This confirms a long-standing conjecture of Yudovich.

papers.title: Wavefront sets for genuine representations of $\rm GL$-covers of Kazhdan--Patterson or Savin types
papers.authors: Fan Gao, Runze Wang, Jiandi Zou
papers.abstract: First, we consider general Brylinski--Deligne covers of the $p$-adic general linear groups, and discuss the theory of Bernstein--Zelevinsky derivatives. We also recall the Zelevinsky-type classification of the irreducible genuine spectrum for the Kazhdan--Patterson and Savin covers. Following this, for these two special families of covers, we determine the wavefront sets of their irreducible genuine representations, expressed in terms of the iterated degrees of the highest Bernstein--Zelevinsky derivatives. Finally, for Kazhdan--Patterson covers, we reinterpret this result on the wavefront set using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and the covering Barbasch--Vogan duality.

papers.title: Solvable Lie Foliations on Compact Five-Manifolds: Classification, Cohomological Obstruction, and Non-Homogeneous Examples
papers.abstract: We study $\GA$-Lie foliations on compact five-manifolds. We establish a structural classification of the holonomy group $\Gamma$ into five types according to its algebraic structure inside $\GA$. For three of these types (I, II, IIIa) we prove homogeneity via Meigniez's theorem and the Matsumoto--Tsuchiya theorem. For Type~IIIb we prove non-homogeneity by exhibiting a non-polycyclic holonomy group, extending the Dathe--Ndiaye construction \cite{DN11}. We introduce a cohomological class $[F]\in H^2(\Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}},[\Gamma,\Gamma])$ as a \emph{necessary} obstruction to homogeneity: if $\mathcal{F}$ is homogeneous and $\Gamma$ is polycyclic then $[F]=0$. We show that Type IIIb foliations satisfy $[F]\neq 0$. For Type IIIc, we prove that certain foliations are non-homogeneous by a direct argument when the generating translations are $\Q(\lambda)$-linearly independent; we exhibit explicit homogeneous examples showing that this type is \emph{not} universally non-homogeneous. Finally, we construct the first known non-homogeneous $\mathrm{Sol}$-Lie foliation in dimension five by a verified lattice deformation.

papers.title: Mixed Hodge Modules and Canonical Perverse Extensions for Multi-Node Conifold Degenerations
papers.abstract: We study one-parameter conifold degenerations whose central fiber \(X_0\) has finitely many ordinary double points and construct a mixed-Hodge-module refinement of the corrected perverse variation-cone object associated with the degeneration. At each node \(p_k\), the local \(\can^H/\Var^H/N\) geometry determines a rank-one point-supported interface block \(W_k^H\simeq i_{k*}\Q^H_{\{p_k\}}(-1)\). These blocks assemble canonically into \(Q_\Sigma^H=\bigoplus_{k=1}^r W_k^H\), through which the node-supported monodromy factors. We prove that the perverse-normalized cone \(\Cone(\Var^H)\) is concentrated in the mixed-Hodge-module heart, thereby defining \(\mathcal P^H\in MHM(X_0)\), and that \(\rat(\mathcal P^H)\simeq\mathcal P\). In the forward Yoneda orientation, the point-supported quotient is instead \(R_\Sigma^H\simeq\bigoplus_{k=1}^r i_{k*}\Q^H_{\{p_k\}}(-2)\), exhibiting a Hodge-theoretic distinction invisible after rational realization. We further prove a canonical nodewise decomposition of the rational perverse extension space and construct a morphism from the formal local Hodge sector to the independently defined limiting mixed Hodge structure. Its image records the node contributions that survive in global limiting cohomology, allowing nontrivial global relations among vanishing cycles.

papers.title: Unified Communication Compression Beyond Global Error Bounds for Distributed Nonconvex Optimization
papers.authors: Haonan Wang, Minghui Liwang, Yiguang Hong, Karl H. Johansson, Xinlei Yi
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a unified compression algorithm for distributed nonconvex opitmization with both the locally- and globally-bounded communication compressors, including 1-bit compressors, saturating quantizers, and the globally-bounded compressors with both relative and absolute compression errors, as well as additional arbitrary bounded noise. We provide a rigorous convergence analysis in nonconvex settings and establish linear convergence under the Polyak-Lojasiewicz (P-L) condition. Notably, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{T})$ convergence rate for the locally-bounded class in the distributed nonconvex setting, matching that achieved by the centralized algorithms with 1-bit compressors, where $T$ denotes the total number of iterations. Moreover, one initial uncompressed communication round further yields an order-wise improvement to $\mathcal{O}(1/T^{2/3})$. For the P-L setting and the globally-bounded class, we recover state-of-the-art convergence rates.

papers.title: Restricted Projections to Hyperplanes in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: We study dimensions of sets projected to an $(n-2)$-dimensional family of hyperplanes in $\mathbb{R}^n$ under curvature conditions. Let $n\ge 4$, $\Sigma \subset S^{n-1}$ be an $(n-2)$-dimensional $C^2$ manifold such that $\Sigma$ has sectional curvature $>1$ and $Z \subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$ be analytic. If $\dim\pi_{T_yS^{n-1}}(Z) \le n-2$ for some $y \in S^{n-1}$, then $\dim \pi_{T_xS^{n-1}}(Z) = \dim Z$ for $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-a.e. $x \in \Sigma$.

papers.title: Locally invariant manifolds and foliations
papers.abstract: Invariant manifolds and foliations associated to invariant pseudo-hyperbolic reference geometries have been well-studied in the context of dynamics implemented by a diffeomorphism. In this paper, we provide sufficient conditions for the existence of maximally smooth, \emph{locally} invariant manifolds and foliations containing a given \emph{locally} invariant, pseudo-hyperbolic reference geometry, in the context of dynamics implemented by a smooth map which need not be invertible. The theory is motivated by applications to the developing theory of large-step optimisation.

papers.title: Analytical properties of $q$-metallic numbers
papers.abstract: For an integer $n\geq 1$, consider the $n$-th metallic number $\phi_n=\frac{n+\sqrt{n^2+4}}{2}$ (e.g. $\phi_1$ is the golden number) and denote by $[\phi_n]_q$ its $q$-deformation in the sense of S. Morier-Genoud and V. Ovsienko. This is an algebraic continued fraction which admits an expansion into a power series $[\phi_n]_q =\sum_{l=0}^{+\infty} \kappa_l(\phi_n) q^l$ around $q=0$, with integral coefficients. By using techniques from analytic combinatorics, we establish several properties of the sequence $( \kappa_l(\phi_n))_{l\geq 0}$ of Taylor coefficients: characterisation by recurrences or by differential equations, closed-form expressions when $n=1,2,3$, and asymptotics. We also present some remarkable identities induced by the action of the modular group $PSL(2,Z)$ and address, mainly through computer experimentations, the question of the logarithmic behaviour of the sequence $( \kappa_l(\phi_n))_{l\geq 0}$. A particular accent is put on the comparison between the $q$-deformation $[\phi_1]_q$ of the golden ratio and RNA secondary structures, the former being actually a signed version of the latter. By doing so, we would be pleased to bring the interest of combinatoricians to the newly discovered world of $q$-numbers.

papers.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
papers.abstract: We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization, and something like blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.

papers.title: On $q$-convex hypersurfaces in Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that any closed, convex hypersurface in an $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-positive curvature operator is a rational homology sphere with finite fundamental group. The same conclusion holds for any $\lceil \frac{n}{2} \rceil$-convex hypersurface, provided that the mean curvature satisfies a sharp pinching condition. Both results follow from more general vanishing and estimation theorems for the Betti numbers of closed $q$-convex immersed hypersurfaces in $(n+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds, under a lower bound on the average of the smallest $(n-p)$ eigenvalues of the curvature operator.

papers.title: Parametric Statistical Inference in the Zone of Moderate Deviation Probabilities
papers.abstract: A parametric theory of statistical inference is developed for the moderate deviation probability zone. The new approach to the proofs is based on the Taylor series expansion of the logarithm of the likelihood ratio based on the Hellinger distance. The Large Deviation Principle in the moderate deviation probability zone is proven for Bayesian estimators and maximum likelihood estimators. A uniform approximation of the logarithm of the likelihood ratio and Theorem on concentration of the posterior Bayesian measure are also established for the zone of moderate deviation probabilities.

papers.title: A polynomial-time solvable class of sparse box-constrained polynomial optimization problems
papers.abstract: We study the problem of minimizing a multivariate polynomial function over the unit hypercube. Exploiting sparsity in the interaction graph or hypergraph, we identify variables that can be restricted to binary values and eliminate the remaining continuous variables component-wise, reducing the problem to structured binary polynomial optimization. For quadratic objectives, we obtain polynomial-time solvability in the standard Turing model under conditions on treewidth and a nonconvexity measure of the continuous components. For higher-degree objectives, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm in the unit-cost algebraic RAM model under logarithmic incidence treewidth and small, weakly coupled continuous components.

papers.title: Volumetric density estimates for nonlocal minimal surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that viscosity subsolutions to nonlocal mean curvature-type equations satisfy universal volumetric estimates at all scales provided their boundary has zero Lebesgue measure. Our results hold for a general class of symmetric kernels including kernels that are comparable to the fractional Laplacian. Furthermore, we prove that subsolutions with low density (with respect to a universal constant) necessarily have `fat boundary', that is, have topological boundary with positive Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: Phases of Muon: When Muon Eclipses SignSGD
papers.authors: Elliot Paquette, Noah Marshall, Lucas Benigni, Guangyuan Wang, Atish Agarwala, Courtney Paquette
papers.abstract: Muon and related spectral optimizers have recently demonstrated strong empirical performance as scalable stochastic methods, often outperforming Adam. Yet their behavior remains poorly understood. We analyze stochastic Muon, which orthogonalizes an exponential moving average of minibatch gradients, on a high-dimensional matrix-valued least squares problem, and we compare it with stochastic SignSGD, a simple baseline comparable to Adam. We derive explicit deterministic dynamics that provide a tractable framework for studying learning behavior. We show that Muon has non-linear sensitivity to the effective batch $B_{\rm eff}=B(1+\beta)/(1-\beta)$. With exact whitening and small $B_{\rm eff}$ Muon fails to resolve smaller eigenmodes, slowing down convergence. Momentum and finite Newton--Shulz iterations can act as a ridge which lessen this effect. This behavior is in contrast with SignSGD which has no transition, leading to different optimal learning rates, but with matching convergence rate up to a constant factor in the isotropic setting. For anisotropic data, large batch setting Muon performs a square-root preconditioning with respect to the data covariance spectrum while SignSGD provides no preconditioning for generic covariances. We analyze time to target loss in a power law covariance model and derive a phase diagram in the data exponent $\alpha$ and target exponent $\zeta$. Muon is favored for steep covariance spectra with rich targets ($\alpha>2$, $\zeta<\alpha+1$), SignSGD is favored for flat spectra ($\alpha<1$), and in other regions the winner depends on how the target loss scales with dimension. Our results shed light on why replacing Adam with Muon is not trivial even from a pure optimization perspective.

papers.title: Tautological modular forms of level two and degree two
papers.authors: Fabien Cl\'ery, Gerard van der Geer
papers.abstract: We show how to use divisors on the projectivized Hodge bundle to construct special vector-valued modular forms and then apply invariant theory to construct all vector-valued Siegel modular forms of level two and degree two. Thus we construct all modular forms in terms of certain basic modular forms that are intimately connected to the moduli of curves of genus two.

papers.title: Minimal submanifolds confined in space
papers.authors: Tobias Holck Colding, William P. Minicozzi II
papers.abstract:
Already in $\mathbb{R}^4$, there are many minimal hypersurfaces but few structural results. The half-space theorem fails there: higher-dimensional catenoids are among the many examples contained in a slab. Nevertheless, we show that in any dimension and codimension, the height of a minimal submanifold controls its volume growth: confinement to a narrow cone forces polynomial growth, and sublinear height forces Euclidean growth, the slowest possible. Thus volume bounds, which regularity theory assumes, follow from height alone.
  The key is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: if an $n$-dimensional stationary integral varifold lies in a thin slab at a given scale, then its volume doubling ratio at that scale is bounded by a universal constant. Iterating this gives the polynomial growth bounds above. Sublinear height is exactly the borderline for Euclidean growth: examples grow at least like $r^{n+4\epsilon^2/5}$ in cones of aperture $\epsilon$. From Euclidean volume growth, we obtain an optimal Bernstein theorem, in all dimensions, for stable minimal hypersurfaces with sublinear height growth, generalizing results of Moser, Bombieri--De Giorgi--Miranda, Trudinger, Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck, and Ecker--Huisken.

papers.title: Where solitons are in a KdV soliton gas
papers.abstract: The Korteweg-De Vries (KdV) equation is a paradigmatic model of integrable classical fields, with solitonic solutions where localised profiles interact by elastic, factorised scattering. When solitons interact, their shapes are modified, and individual solitons cannot be identified. This is a key problem in soliton gas where one needs a density of solitons per unit distance: can we locate asymptotic objects, quasiparticles, even at finite times in the macroscopic limit? Quasiparticles' positions should satisfy locality properties, the field in mesoscopic regions being determined by quasiparticles lying there. We solve this problem for the KdV equation. We define solitons' positions as functions of spectral and impact parameters via an expansion bijection generalising that of hard rods. These ``KdV rods'' solve the semiclassical Bethe equations, implementing the collision rate ansatz, and satisfy a repulsion condition generalising the rods' lengths to the KdV scattering shifts and related to the condensate condition. This gives an explicit characterisation of multi-soliton fields in terms of solitons' positions instead of impact parameters. We construct fluid-cell projections, that project out solitons lying outside mesoscopic regions: the resulting field is unchanged in this region and supported there up to small corrections. We show that in the weak limit, conserved densities are given by the empirical density for these solitons' positions. Thus we have associated a kinetic theory of quasiparticles to the KdV equation. The results hold under natural assumptions on spectral and impact parameters, and no randomness is required. Our proof is based on novel solitonic tau functions. This is a crucial step towards rigorously deriving the kinetic equation of the KdV soliton gas, first proposed by Gennady El in 2003. We believe the methods are generalisable to other solitonic models.

papers.title: A Sharp Regularity Threshold for Uniqueness in Riemannian Calder\'on-type Problems
papers.authors: Thierry Daud\'e, Alberto Enciso, Bernard Helffer, Niky Kamran, Fran\c{c}ois Nicoleau
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp regularity threshold for uniqueness in two anisotropic Calder\'on-type inverse problems in dimension $n\ge 3$. The main setting is the Riemannian Schr\"odinger problem with fixed scalar potential: for a prescribed nonconstant analytic function $V$, we study whether the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of $-\Delta_g+V$ on a domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ determines the unknown metric $g$. The natural gauge is the group of boundary-fixing diffeomorphisms preserving $V$. We show that, while analytic metrics are uniquely determined modulo this gauge by a minor adaptation of the Lassas--Uhlmann reconstruction theorem, uniqueness fails densely in every non-analytic Gevrey class $G^\sigma$, $\sigma>1$. In fact, our counterexamples are not isometric in the sense that they are not connected by the pushforward of any diffeomorphism of $\overline\Omega$. We also prove the analogous sharp threshold for the anisotropic Calder\'on problem at fixed nonzero frequency, thereby upgrading the previously known finite-regularity counterexamples to Gevrey and $C^\infty$ regularity. The two constructions use different scalar mechanisms: for fixed potentials, the nonconstant potential itself provides a local coordinate, while at nonzero frequency one uses a compactly supported prescribed-Jacobian lemma in Gevrey spaces. Thus analyticity is the exact threshold for uniqueness in both problems.

papers.title: Continuum-wise hyperbolicity is exactly the pseudo-Anosov dynamics with spine singularities
papers.authors: Rodrigo Arruda, Bernardo Carvalho, Piotr Oprocha, Alberto Sarmiento
papers.abstract: We establish a complete structural classification for cw$_F$-hyperbolic surface homeomorphisms. Specifically, we prove that a surface homeomorphism is cw$_F$-hyperbolic if, and only if, it is a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism whose singularities consist exclusively of spines (1-prongs). Furthermore, we classify these systems up to topological conjugacy, showing that every such homeomorphism is conjugate to either an Anosov automorphism on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2$ or to a standard hyperelliptic quotient on $\mathbb{S}^2$ of a hyperbolic affine toral map. As a rigid consequence of this classification, we show that such dynamics are strictly obstructed on surfaces of genus greater than one, the Klein bottle, and the projective plane.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the blow-up for some Alt-Phillips cones
papers.abstract:
We establish uniqueness of blow-ups, with sharp quantitative convergence, for several classes of singular minimizing cones in the Alt-Phillips problem, in the range $\gamma\in(0,2)$. As a consequence, we obtain uniqueness at every free boundary point in dimensions $d=2,3,4$ for $\gamma\in(1,2)$, and in dimensions $d\geq 5$ for $\gamma\in\left(1,\frac32\right)$.
  The proof of uniqueness is based on three new logarithmic epiperimetric inequalities. The sharp distinction between polynomial and logarithmic convergence is governed by a finite-dimensional integrability condition (sub-integrability) for the spherical linearized problem.
  We prove this sharpness for the radial cone and its cylindrical extensions through an explicit integrability and bifurcation analysis, showing in particular that logarithmic convergence may be sharp even in dimension two. In contrast, we show that the one-dimensional cone is exceptional: although the integrability condition fails, the convergence is polynomial.
  Finally, we characterize the minimality of the radial cone in terms of $d$ and $\gamma$ by means of a one-dimensional calibration argument, exhibiting in dimension $d\geq6$ a nontrivial regime in which the radial cone is stable but not minimizing.

papers.title: Derived categories of log del Pezzo surfaces with $\frac13(1,1)$ singularities
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a log del Pezzo surface with only $\frac13(1,1)$ singularities. We compare the derived categories of its minimal resolution, canonical stack, and singular surface. For every family in the Corti--Heuberger classification, Orlov's blow-up formula and the Ishii--Ueda correspondence give explicit full exceptional collections on the canonical stacks, of length $12-K_X^2+\frac{4k}{3}$ when $X$ has $k$ singular points. In the one-point index-one cascade, the canonical stacks are blow-ups of the weighted projective stack $\mathbb P(1,1,3)$ at distinct smooth points and admit explicit full strong exceptional collections of line bundles. For quasismooth hypersurfaces $X_{10}\subset\mathbb P(1,2,3,5)$, we construct a full strong exceptional collection of $13$ objects with an explicitly computed Euler matrix. The exceptional lattice determines the Brauer group: $\mathrm{Br}(X)=0$ for $k\leq5$, while $\mathrm{Br}(X)\cong\mathbb Z/3$ for $k=6$. We construct semiorthogonal decompositions of $D^b(\mathrm{coh}\,X)$ for the one- and three-point cascades and of a Brauer-twisted derived category for the six-point cascade.

papers.title: An Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian solver for relativistic detonation waves
papers.authors: Sara Rinaldi, Olindo Zanotti, Michael Dumbser
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the dynamics of relativistic detonation waves theoretically and numerically. The reaction is physically accounted for by an extra term in the definition of the total energy density and by an additional equation for the evolution of the mass fraction of the reactant, while leaving formally unmodified the equations of mass and energy-momentum conservation. In this way, the Rankine-Hugoniot relations maintain the same formal structure of the inert version. For the numerical solution we use a finite volume ALE scheme with a second order TVD space-time reconstruction for the homogeneous part of the system, where the mesh velocity is chosen equal to the shock speed, and we combine it through operator splitting with a locally implicit algorithm for the potentially stiff reaction source terms that arise in the equation of the reactant. We furthermore propose a particularly efficient algorithm for the conversion from the conserved to the primitive variables, which for the relativistic Euler equations is known to be nontrivial. Following this approach, we can successfully solve the Zel'dovich-von Neumann-Doering profile of a relativistic detonation wave, up to Lorentz factors of the shock front $\gamma_s\sim 7$. Our analysis allowed us to highlight a new special relativistic effect, which has remained unnoticed so far. While in Newtonian detonations the Zel'dovich pressure jump decreases monotonically with the mass flux through the shock front, in the relativistic case it shows a minimum and then rises monotonically as a function of the mass flux. This may have interesting physical implications on the amount of energy that can be extracted from a relativistic detonation wave.

papers.title: General position on Brauer--Severi surfaces
papers.abstract: The blowing-up of the projective plane at a finite set of points yields a del Pezzo surface if and only if the points lie in general position. In this note, we generalize this result to Brauer--Severi surfaces over arbitrary ground fields. Using Galois descent, intersection theory and combinatorial arguments, we provide explicit arithmetic and geometric conditions on the centre of the blowing-up.

papers.title: Null Cartan Normal Helices in Minkowski Space-Time
papers.abstract: A complete theory of null Cartan normal helices in Minkowski space-time $\mathbb{E}^4_1$ is developed. Two algebraic conditions, obtained by successive differentiation of the helix invariant along a unit $C$-constant normal field, fully characterize null Cartan helices; the quadratic condition yields two mutually orthogonal helix axes in the Lorentzian metric. Special field types are analyzed and null Cartan cubics are shown to be normal helices. On a timelike hypersurface, a Darboux frame with six curvature functions is constructed from first principles, the normal isophotic condition is shown to reduce to a linear first-order ODE, and the existence of normal silhouettes in $\mathbb{E}^4_1$ is established.

papers.title: Statistics on Yau's conjecture: Variance asymptotics
papers.abstract: We investigate the probabilistic counterpart of Yau's conjecture on the nodal volume of Laplace eigenfunctions on compact manifolds, by studying the high-frequency variance asymptotics of Riemannian random waves. Theorem A gives quantitative bounds on the fluctuations of their nodal volume for all regimes of spectral windows, including the monochromatic one, of spectral size 1. For every non-monochromatic window the variance has the exact order $1/N$, where $N$ is the dimension of the underlying space of eigenfunctions, on any compact manifold. In the monochromatic regime, on manifolds without conjugate points and in particular on negatively curved ones, we prove that the variance is $o(1/N)$: this improves the previous best bound, cf. Canzani and Hanin 2020, to its square divided by a logarithmic factor, and exhibits a form of Berry's cancellation, relative to the natural scale $1/N$, for monochromatic random waves on such chaotic manifolds. Our proofs rely on a local and global analysis combining the Kac-Rice formula, the Wiener--It\^o chaos decomposition recently obtained by the authors Stecconi and Todino 2025, and a sharp analysis of the error in the pointwise Weyl law associated to an arbitrary spectral window (Theorem B). We also introduce a general machinery (Theorem C) that yields variance decay for the nodal volume of an arbitrary Gaussian field under broad geometric conditions, subject to correlation decay assumptions.

papers.title: Sketch-and-Restart: Randomized Sketching in Quadrature-Based Restarting for Matrix Functions
papers.authors: Stefan G\"uttel, Jingyu Liu, Lauri Nyman
papers.abstract: We develop a sketch-and-restart framework for computing the action of a matrix function on a vector, $f(A) b$, where $A$ is large, sparse, and non-Hermitian. The framework combines quadrature-based restarting with Arnoldi-like decompositions generated by sketched or truncated Arnoldi processes. Within this framework, we develop two classes of restarted algorithms. The first uses a fixed Krylov subspace dimension and is based either on the sketched Arnoldi process or on a new sketched harmonic Arnoldi process proposed in this work. The second class chooses the Krylov subspace dimension adaptively by running the truncated Arnoldi process until the condition number of the generated basis, estimated from its sketch, exceeds a prescribed threshold. We also establish the convergence of the restarted sketched harmonic Arnoldi method for Stieltjes functions under the assumption that $A$ is positive real. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, including the computational savings achieved through sketching, the storage reduction enabled by adaptive truncation, and the acceleration obtained from thick restarting.

papers.title: p-adic Properties of Translated Division Polynomials and Somos Sequences
papers.abstract: We study the periodicity and $p$-adic convergence of sequences of values of the translated division polynomials $(\Psi_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$, $(\Phi_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$, and $(\Omega_n(P))_{n\geq 0}$ evaluated at a pair of points on an elliptic curve. We prove that these sequences are purely periodic over finite fields. We then use their periodicity properties to prove that certain subsequences are $\mathbb{Z}_p$-Cauchy. Applying this result to Somos 4 and Somos 5 sequences yields analogous convergence results. We also establish pure periodicity modulo prime powers for the even- and odd-indexed subsequences of Somos 5 sequences under suitable hypotheses.

papers.title: Elliptic Superlevel Sets in the Class $\OO_C$: Boundary-Layer Geometry and Stability of the Return Map
papers.abstract:
We study elliptic superlevel geometry and return dynamics for the class $\mathcal{O}_{C}$. Let $C \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$ be a compact strictly convex core, and $\Omega \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$ a bounded domain whose boundary is a global normal graph over $\partial C$ with inward normals returning to $\operatorname{int} C$. For $-\Delta u = f$ in $\Omega$ ($u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$), with $f \geq 0$, $f \not\equiv 0$, $\operatorname{supp} f \Subset \operatorname{int} C$, we analyze the superlevel sets $\Omega_{t} = \{u > t\}$ for $t \downarrow 0$.
  We prove that for small $t > 0$, $\partial\Omega_{t}$ is a global normal graph given by $\partial\Omega_{t} = \{c + d_{t}(c)\nu(c) : c \in \partial C\}$, satisfying $\|d_{t} - d_{0}\|_{C^{1}} = O(t)$ and $d_{t} = d_{0} - t b_{0} + o_{C^{1}}(t)$, where $b_{0}$ depends on the Hopf derivative and transversality. Using normal-graph formulas, we show $\Omega_{t} \in \mathcal{O}_{C}$.
  The return maps $F_{t} : \partial C \to \partial C$ are well-defined, satisfying $\|F_{t} - F_{0}\|_{L^{\infty}} = O(t)$ and $F_{t} = F_{0} + t \mathcal{A}_{0} + o_{L^{\infty}}(t)$. For any sequence $t_{n} \downarrow 0$, the non-autonomous system $x_{n+1} = F_{t_{n}}(x_{n})$ is asymptotically autonomous with background map $F_{0}$. These results bridge elliptic boundary-layer deformation and return-map dynamics relative to a convex core.

papers.title: On the embedding rigidity problem for uniformly locally finite coarse spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct countable uniformly locally finite metric spaces $X$ and $Y$ such that $C_u^*(X)$ is isomorphic to a hereditary $C^*$-subalgebra of $C_u^*(Y)$, but neither space coarsely embeds into the other. This gives a negative answer to the embedding rigidity problem for uniformly locally finite coarse spaces. On the positive side, we prove that a hereditary embedding $C_u^*(X)\to C_u^*(Y)$ implies an injective coarse embedding $X\to Y$ whenever $C_u^*(Y)$ contains no block-rank-one ghost projection. In particular, this strengthens the coarse embedding theorem of Braga, Farah, and Vignati by obtaining injectivity under the same hypothesis that every sparse subspace of $Y$ yields only compact ghost projections.

papers.title: Essential-Surface Complexes of Knot Exteriors: Image, Kernel, and Reconstruction
papers.abstract: This is an expository article. The curve complex of a surface is deliberately forgetful, yet in most cases its automorphism group recovers the mapping class group. We explain what happens when the same question is asked for the essential-surface complex $\mathcal{ES}(E)$ of a knot exterior $E=E(K)$, equivalently Schultens's initial surface complex $\mathcal{S}_0(E)$. The discussion is organized around three questions: which combinatorial symmetries are geometric (the image), which homeomorphisms are invisible (the kernel), and how much of $E$ can be read off from the complex (reconstruction). The basic objects are first drawn in classical examples, and the general framework is introduced only afterwards. We collect the elementary structural facts that organize the subject -- the flag property, the layering by boundary slope, finite dimension, unbounded dimension for iterated cables, and Kakimizu's complexes as full subcomplexes -- and compare with handlebodies and connected sums of $S^2\times S^1$, where image and kernel are known completely. Along the way we record two short consequences that we have not found stated in this form: for a slope-separated knot every orientation-preserving mapping class acts trivially, and the image is $\mathbb{Z}/2$ exactly when the knot is amphichiral and a nonzero boundary slope occurs; and for a connected sum of nonfibered prime knots the decomposing-annulus twist translates Banks's winding coordinate. A table separates what is classical from what is recorded here. The article closes with a three-task formulation of the rigidity problem, a list of problems with their current status, a worked two-bridge recipe, and a guide to further reading.

papers.title: Improved Lower Bounds on Tree Covers
papers.authors: Yu Chen, Shengtang Huang, Zihan Tan, Hangyu Xu
papers.abstract:
A tree cover of an $n$-point metric space is a collection of $k$ trees such that every pairwise distance is approximately preserved in at least one tree. For fixed $k$, the best known distortion upper bound is $\tilde{O}(n^{1/k})$ and the best known lower bound is $\Omega_k(n^{1/2^{k-1}})$.
  In this paper, we prove a lower bound of $\Omega_k(n^{1/(k-1)^2})$ for all $k\ge 3$, significantly narrowing the gap towards the upper bound.
  Our approach makes use of a novel algebraic topological notion that we call the \emph{agreement index}: the equivariant topological index of a simplicial complex encoding pairwise agreement among tree labels. This notion helps characterize the power and limit of algebraic and topological methods for analyzing tree covers, and we believe it will also find applications to other problems.

papers.title: A dichotomy for minimal submanifolds
papers.authors: Tobias Holck Colding, William P. Minicozzi II
papers.abstract:
We survey a circle of recent results showing that a minimal submanifold obeys a dichotomy: either it fills up space, spreading out like a space-filling curve, or it is confined, and confinement forces quantitative restrictions. On the confined side these restrictions are both geometric and function-theoretic: Euclidean volume growth, an optimal rate of convergence of the density, complex-curve rigidity for stable surfaces in $\bf{R}^4$, and a Liouville theorem forcing slowly growing harmonic functions on minimal disks to be constant. A prototypical restriction is Euclidean volume growth, which in these results is forced by the geometry rather than assumed. The mechanism is a volume doubling theorem that converts geometric confinement into quantitative rigidity: a stationary integral varifold trapped in a thin slab at a given scale cannot double its volume by more than a universal factor. We explain how this principle, and the height-excess bounds behind it, produce Euclidean volume growth for submanifolds of sublinearly growing height in every dimension and codimension, the optimal density rate in a slab, the complex-curve and Liouville rigidity above, a higher-codimension Bernstein theorem for disks, one-sided volume bounds, and an optimal stable Bernstein theorem in all dimensions generalizing Moser, Bombieri-De Giorgi-Miranda, Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck and Ecker-Huisken. We describe three regimes with sharp borderlines. In narrow cones the volume grows polynomially with exponent $n+O(\varepsilon^2)$, and the order $\varepsilon^2$ is attained; in wide cones the growth can be arbitrarily fast. For holomorphic curves in $\mathbb{C}^2$, there are also three regimes and
  the borderline is determined by the K\"ahler angle.

papers.title: A Fitting criterion for quasi-Gorenstein local rings
papers.abstract: We prove that a Noetherian local ring $R$ with canonical module $\omega_R$ is quasi-Gorenstein if and only if $\Fitt_1^R(\omega_R) \cong \omega_R$. This settles the expectation of Eisenbud, Ficarra, Herzog, and Moradi on canonical ideals.
