Its projective closure is an elliptic normal sextic, and representation by two ordered products selects the modulus $m=1/2$.

papers.title: Sharp gradient comparison and rigidity for semilinear equations on manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove sharp amplitude and gradient comparisons for positive solutions of a class of semilinear elliptic equations on complete manifolds under a Ricci lower bound. Equality at one point characterizes hyperbolic space and the corresponding radial solution. The local estimates are uniform in the mixing coefficients and number of terms for positive mixtures of subcritical powers. For a class of conformal compactifications defined by a source equation, we obtain sharp boundary scalar-curvature bounds and hyperbolic rigidity. We also construct non-Einstein examples whose normalization persists under small compactly supported metric perturbations.

papers.title: Finiteness of ergodic measures of maximal entropy for certain skew product systems
papers.abstract:
Consider a $C^{1+\beta}$ skew product $F$ over a topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphism $f$, with fiber dynamics driven by a $C^{1+\beta}$ $\mathbb{R}^k$-action $\{\rho_{\bf t}\}$ on a closed manifold $Y$ through a $C^{1+\beta}$ cocycle $\tau$. Suppose that the fiber action preserves an ergodic smooth measure of maximal entropy $m_{\operatorname{MME}}$. Under a nondegeneracy condition called joint nontriviality, and assuming that each element $\rho_{\bf t}$ is either of class $C^\infty$ or hyperbolic, we prove that $F$ admits only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy.
  Moreover, every such measure is of the form $\mu\times m_{\operatorname{MME}}$, where $\mu$ is an ergodic equilibrium state for a H\"older potential on the base. If, in addition, the fiber action is exponentially mixing of all orders, then every ergodic MME is Bernoulli, exponentially mixing of all orders, and satisfies the Central Limit Theorem.
  Our main novelties are entropy formulas for skew products, obtained through the cone property and $r$-neutralized entropy, and a relative Ledrappier--Young theorem that converts the fiber entropy contribution into absolute continuity of fiberwise conditional measures. Combined with nonlinear thermodynamic formalism, rotation theory and Yomdin theory, these yield the finiteness of the base projections and the product rigidity of ergodic MMEs.

papers.title: Word Trace Formulas over Compact Groups and Connected Cumulants
papers.abstract: We compute the expected value of the product of traces for a finite set of words within any compact subgroup of $\mathcal(N)$. Furthermore, we establish a sufficient condition under which these values determine that the product of the conjugacy classes of the words contains the identity.

papers.title: Hyperbolic complex tangencies on a four-sphere
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth embedding of $S^4$ into $\mathbb C^4$ whose CR-singular locus is a connected surface of genus two consisting entirely of nondegenerate hyperbolic points. Its image is locally polynomially convex and admits a basis of smoothly bounded, strongly pseudoconvex Stein tubular neighbourhoods.

papers.title: Quasicircularity of the Zakeri Curve and Capture Component Boundaries
papers.abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number of bounded type, we prove that the locus of critically marked cubic polynomials whose two critical points lie on the boundary of the fixed Siegel disk is a quasicircle. This locus is known as the Zakeri curve. The main step is a boundary correspondence lemma for holomorphic families of disks with uniformly quasiconformal extensions. We further prove that every capture component in this family is a quasidisk, including components attached to the Zakeri curve.

papers.title: Bistable fronts in periodic media: phase reduction and realization of circle flows
papers.authors: Weiwei Ding, Xing Liang, Linfeng Xu
papers.abstract: We establish a phase reduction and a converse realization theorem for front dynamics in one-dimensional periodic reaction-diffusion-advection equations. For sufficiently large periods under local bistability, and sufficiently small periods when the homogenized equation admits a stationary front, we construct strictly ordered invariant front families that are normally exponentially attracting and locally complete for entire orbits. Modulo spatial-period translations, the dynamics on each family reduces exactly to a circle flow: rotations correspond to propagating pulsating fronts, equilibria to stationary fronts, and connecting orbits to transition fronts between stationary fronts. Conversely, every smooth circle flow can be realized, up to time-preserving topological conjugacy, as the quotient dynamics of such a family for a periodic, locally bistable equation with constant diffusion and no advection. Realizations with a Cantor set of stationary phases and a connecting orbit in each complementary interval illustrate the richness of front dynamics in these media. We also obtain first-order phase-velocity expansions in both period limits, quantitative propagation laws near zero frozen speed, and global exponential orbital stability of propagating pulsating fronts.

papers.title: Gaussian zero-count fluctuations in annuli
papers.abstract: We determine joint zero-count fluctuations of the self-dual weighted Szeg\H{o} Gaussian analytic function in fixed and thinning annuli. For a fixed annulus, the counts near its two boundary components converge jointly to independent standard normal variables after centering and marginal normalization, at arbitrary relative rates of boundary approach. This answers the simultaneous central limit question of Katori and Shirai for this model. The unscaled covariance converges to a negative constant, which we evaluate in complete elliptic integrals. A sharp variance asymptotic for the difference between an annular winding number and its coupled disk count yields quantitative normal approximation bounds. For thinning annuli with inner radius $q=e^{-h}$, the counts in every fixed finite family of interior transverse bands converge jointly to a Gaussian vector after centering and multiplication by $\sqrt h$. We give its spectral covariance matrix, prove strict negative covariance for disjoint bands, and identify its nullspace from the interval indicators. The fixed-annulus proof couples the Laurent series to two independent Gaussian power series. For thinning annuli, we combine exact periodization of a strip kernel, a uniform Laguerre-chaos tail bound, and connected Gaussian diagrams.

papers.title: Almost global existence for quadratic Schr\"odinger equations in two dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the two-dimensional quadratic Schr\"odinger equation $(i\partial_t+\Delta)u=\lambda_1u^2+\lambda_2\overline u^{\,2}$ with initial data of size $\varepsilon$ in a weighted $H^2$ space. We prove almost global existence, with a lifespan of at least $\exp(c/\varepsilon)$ and decay at the optimal linear dispersive rate $t^{-1}$. Our proof is based on the space--time resonance method introduced by Germain, Masmoudi, and Shatah. The main new ingredient is a Besov-type profile norm $\mathcal Z$, which allows us to close the bootstrap argument without controlling the global second spatial momentof the free profile, thereby avoiding the substantial time-dependent losses arising from direct second-moment estimates.

papers.title: Temporal central limit theorem for mixed-radix odometer discrepancy
papers.abstract: We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of $0$ under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence. This extends and strengthens the fixed-base temporal central limit theorem of Levin and Merzbach to the mixed-radix setting.

papers.title: ESPC-Transolver: An Equivalent-Surface Physics-Guided Coupling-Aware Transolver for 3D Multiple Scattering
papers.authors: Guoqing Zhao, Liang Li, Xing Li, Hao Kuang
papers.abstract: Cross-geometry generalization is particularly challenging because geometry-conditioned multiple-scattering surrogates must infer unseen objects' scattering properties from geometric features while accurately capturing complex, phase-sensitive interactions arising from repeated wave exchange. We introduce ESPC-Transolver, an equivalent-surface physics-guided, coupling-aware Transolver that separates local scattering-response representations from inter-object interaction modeling. For each sound-hard scatterer, canonical scattered-pressure responses are constructed under a shared set of spherical-wave excitations. A local Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) map and modal scattering conversion express these responses on an enclosing sphere, providing physically consistent input channels across geometries. Shared object-local Transolver blocks encode these responses and incident-field traces, while relative-position-aware slice attention models inter-object coupling. Predicted interface pressure and normal flux recovered from the local operator define equivalent sources for reconstructing exterior near- and far-field scattering. We evaluate the method on three-dimensional acoustic multiple-scattering problems at a fixed frequency, comparing it with geometry-conditioned predictors and alternative neural network backbones. ESPC-Transolver achieves lower scattered-field prediction errors on held-out instances of familiar geometry families and generalizes effectively to previously unseen Peanut and Torus geometries. Exterior-field reconstructions reproduce multiple-scattering interference patterns, linking cross-geometry interface prediction to near-field pressure and far-field scattering recovery.

papers.title: General-position sets and linear hypergraphs
papers.authors: Thang Pham, Le Quang-Ham, Boqing Xue
papers.abstract: We prove that every linear hypergraph on $N$ vertices with edge sizes $O(\sqrt N)$ and $O(N^2\log N)$ triples contained in its edges has a subset of size $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ meeting each edge in at most two vertices. As an application, every set of $N$ planar points with at most $\sqrt N$ collinear points contains $\Omega(\sqrt N)$ points in general position. This proves a conjecture of Payne and Wood and gives the optimal quadratic bound for a geometric Ramsey problem posed by Gowers.

papers.title: A marked scheme representation for Voronoi volumes in the Brownian map
papers.abstract: For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of independent volume-sampled sites in the unit-area Brownian map, we represent the negative-power transform of their ordinary Voronoi volumes as a finite sum of marked planar scheme integrals. These integrals arise from the critical asymptotics of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps. To connect them to Voronoi volumes, we use Miermont's zero-delay correspondence to interpret the labelled maps as quadrangulations with distinguished sites and then pass to the Brownian map scaling limit.

papers.title: Clifford-weighted residues, partial spectral curvature, and torsion
papers.abstract: We study Clifford-weighted noncommutative residues associated with Dirac operators and connections. On closed spin manifolds a double commutator of the square of the Dirac operator, paired with a Clifford commutator, recovers the localized Riemann curvature tensor. We prove presentation independence for its extension to arbitrary classical one-forms, recompute four-Clifford functionals, and give explicit Weyl, Schouten and Einstein curvature combinations. For spectral triples with an admissible residue calculus we define a partial spectral curvature functional on two arbitrary represented one-forms and two exact represented one-forms. Its well-definedness is distinguished from module tensoriality: explicit flat noncommutative-torus computations exhibit both a failure of general presentation descent and nonzero partial pairings. A connection-based curvature pairing provides a separate construction, including noncentral pure Clifford-degree-two examples. We also derive ordered first- and second-derivative torsion residues on free torus modules and prove an obstruction to ordinary alternation for unrestricted noncentral inputs. All constants, coefficient orders and hypotheses are kept explicit.

papers.title: Network of limit sets in dynamical systems
papers.abstract: Points within a topological dynamical systems can be separated into transient and recurrent points. Most of the asymptotic properties of the dynamics is borne by the closure of the collection of recurrent points. This article presents a representation scheme for dynamics using the connectivity information in terms of the recurrent set. This representation is functorial and represents certain compositional features of dynamical systems.

papers.title: Blow-up, critical norm inflation, and global well-posedness for the Geng--Xue system
papers.abstract: We study finite-time blow-up, critical norm inflation, and global well-posedness for the Geng--Xue system, an integrable two-component extension of the Novikov equation. For initial velocities $(u_0,v_0)\in(H^s)^2$, $s>3/2$, with second momentum $n_0=v_0-v_{0,xx}\in L^1_{\rm uloc}$, we derive explicit blow-up conditions and upper bounds on the lifespan. The blow-up proof uses a cancellation in the equation for $nu_x$ to close the convolution estimates without an a priori bound on $\|u_x\|_{L^\infty}$. Combined with a continuation criterion involving only $u$, these estimates yield critical Besov norm inflation around the initial data in $(H^{3/2})^2$. For initial momenta in $(H^\sigma)^2$, $\sigma>-1/2$, each with a fixed sign, we prove global well-posedness. The blow-up and norm-inflation results also extend to the three-component Degasperis--Procesi system.

papers.title: $(p,q)$-weighted dual curvature measures
papers.abstract: We study (p,q)-weighted dual curvature measures associated with a fixed nonnegative locally integrable Borel density satisfying a trace-regularity condition. These measures arise naturally from a variational formula for Wulff shapes. We establish the trace-regularity condition when g is pointwise \alpha-homogeneous for some \alpha\in R, or when g is radially non-increasing and continuous. For nontrivial even densities in either class, we prove existence results for the even version of the associated Minkowski problem under suitable assumptions. We also establish uniqueness when the prescribed measure has finite support, under a strict positivity assumption on the density and additional restrictions on the parameters. In the case of Lebesgue measure, our curvature measures reduce to those introduced by Lutwak, Yang, and Zhang, and our variational formulas recover their corresponding variational formula. For Gaussian measure, our results are related to those of Feng, Hu, and Xu, and Feng, Li, and Xu. Finally, we investigate the affine properties of the new measures and the associated mixed volumes.

papers.title: Operator systems in \'etale groupoid C*-algebras
papers.authors: Georgios Baziotis, Douglas Farenick, Evgenios T. A. Kakariadis, Malte Leimbach, Lyudmila Turowska, Walter D. van Suijlekom
papers.abstract: We study operator systems arising from positivity domains of \'etale groupoids with compact unit space. Extending Kavruk's enough unitaries principle we show that such operator systems are hyperrigid in the C$^*$-algebra they generate. We focus on operator systems of positivity domains in UHF algebras and, by identifying them with Cantor graph operator systems, we show that they are hyperrigid. Furthermore, we show that in general, such a characterization is not possible when the \'etaleness condition of the underlying groupoid is removed, due to the failure of reduced spectral and compact operator synthesis.

papers.title: Length bounds and rigidity for ancient curve shortening flow on warped product surfaces
papers.abstract: We study ancient solutions to curve shortening flow on a class of warped product surfaces. For closed embedded ancient solutions whose curves are not null-homotopic, we prove that graphicality at every time is equivalent to a uniform length bound as $t\to-\infty$, and that these properties hold whenever the length is $o(\sqrt{-t})$. Under an additional positivity condition on the linearized height equation, every such solution with bounded length is a family of slices. We derive backward convergence to a limiting circle from the length bound and prove slice rigidity by an $L^2$ estimate for the height perturbation.

papers.title: Recovering fractal boundary dimensions from Robin eigenvalues
papers.authors: Habib Ammari, Yat Tin Chow, Fuqun Han
papers.abstract: We study Robin problems in which a small local boundary coefficient competes with the increasing surface measure of a finite-depth fractal approximation. For a fixed smooth domain, layer potentials give Green function and eigenpair expansions; contour residues and a finite-rank reduction yield a quantitative spectral-gap-dependent eigenvalue remainder. For varying Lipschitz domains, a uniform Poincar\'e inequality and a trace estimate with respect to normalized surface measure give a uniform ground-state expansion and a rank-one resolvent singularity as the total Robin boundary mass tends to zero. Under the boundary-resolution hypothesis and the condition on the approximation scales, ground-state measurements with known Robin coefficients recover the lower and upper Minkowski dimensions for sequences with bounded total Robin boundary mass. We describe Neumann, generalized Robin, and Dirichlet-type operator limits under the corresponding compact Mosco convergence hypotheses. Koch snowflake computations illustrate the reconstruction formulas, and an exact finite-stage area correction improves the adjacent-stage dimension estimator.

papers.title: Robust Observability for Schr\"odinger Equations with Singular Potentials on 2D Compact Hyperbolic Surfaces
papers.authors: Jiayan Wu, Ting Zhang, Ruze Zhou
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the robustness of quantum observability on compact hyperbolic surfaces subject to $L^q$ potential perturbations with $2<q\leq \infty$. Since $L^q$ regularity is strictly subcritical in dimension two, for every non-empty open set $\Omega\subset M$ and $T>0$, the solution of $(i\partial_t+\Delta-V)u=0$ satisfies the space-time observability estimate $$ \|u_0\|_{L^2(M)}^2 \leq C\int_0^T \|e^{-it(-\Delta+V)}u_0\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2\,dt. $$ A cornerstone of our analysis is Sogge's spectral cluster estimate, which allows us to obtain refined spectrally localized semiclassical Strichartz estimates adapted to rough potentials and to show that the potential's contribution vanishes in the propagation of semiclassical measures. The full-support property of invariant semiclassical measures on hyperbolic surfaces associated with the eigenfunctions then yields the desired observability by contradiction. By the Hilbert Uniqueness Method, the corresponding internal controllability result follows.

papers.title: Cross numbers and the characterization of finite abelian groups by length sets
Remarks on the Brascamp--Lieb inequality
papers.authors: Dario Cordero-Erausquin, Galyna V. Livshyts, Liran Rotem
papers.abstract: We prove several variants of the Brascamp--Lieb inequality which are adapted to additional symmetries, weights, and non-Euclidean radial structures. First, an improved Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions yields a strengthened Pr\'ekopa--Leindler theorem for even strongly log-concave functions. We also record a Legendre-transform proof of a generalized log-Sobolev inequality for log-concave functions. Further results include a Brascamp--Lieb inequality with a concave weight, an unconditional second-order Poincar\'e inequality, a rotation-trick improvement for arbitrary even log-concave measures, and a Poincar\'e-type inequality associated with smooth norms.

papers.title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets
papers.authors: Bocong Chen, Jing Huang, Gaojun Luo
papers.abstract:
We prove that for all $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the Lee ball $B_n(r)$ does not
  tile $\Z^n$ by translations, resolving the Golomb--Welch conjecture for
  arbitrary centre sets and completing the existence classification of
  perfect Lee codes in $\Z^n$.
  The proof combines translation-invariant averaging, boundary contact
  identities, and integer moment inequalities with coefficient comparisons
  in stable symmetric functions.
  Consequently, we obtain finite local obstructions, strict Banach density
  gaps for packings and coverings, and the nonexistence of exact measurable
  Lee-ball towers.
  In the lattice specialization, our result classifies the attainability of
  the Lee bound for even-degree abelian Cayley graphs, excludes normal
  topological coverings and Galois graph coverings for Lee-ball completions,
  and gives a strict node bound for lattice cubature as well as the
  nonexistence of subgroup-indexed orthogonal exponential bases on $B_n(r)$.

papers.title: Three Quadratic Recurrences Modulo 3: What We Can Prove and What We Can Guess
papers.abstract: We study three innocent-looking recurrences modulo $3$, each built from squares of two earlier terms. One of them turns out to be secretly $\textit{linear}$, and we can compute its periods exactly. One is a $\textit{permutation}$ hiding a small, perfectly orderly piece inside a large, random-looking one. The third looks thoroughly random, but it still has a few provable features. Along the way we meet open problems that need nothing beyond a first course in abstract algebra to state. This paper is a starting point, not the final word in any sense.

papers.title: Pointwise ergodic theorems along oscillating sequences
papers.abstract: We establish the first pointwise convergence result for nonconventional ergodic averages modeled along a large class of oscillating sequences, treating, for example, orbits of the form $\big(\lfloor n^d\sin(e\pi n)\rfloor\big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$. More specifically, for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ equipped with an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T\colon X\to X$ and every $f\in L^p_{\mu}(X)$ with $p\in(1,\infty]$, we prove that the limit \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^Nf\big(T^{\lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor}x\big)\quad\text{exists for $\mu$-a.e. $x\in X$,} \] where $P$ is a non-constant polynomial with real coefficients, $\psi$ is $1$-periodic and real-analytic, and $\alpha$ has irrationality exponent smaller than $1+\sqrt{\operatorname{deg}(P)+1}$. On the one hand, the latter assumption is satisfied by a.e. $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, and, on the other hand, our result covers any of the following concrete orbits \[ \lfloor n\cos(e\pi n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\lfloor n^{37}\sin(n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\big\lfloor \sqrt{2}n^{10}e^{\sin(\pi (\sqrt[5]{7}+1) n)}\big\rfloor\text{,}\quad \big\lfloor \big((\log 2) n^3+e n\big)e^{e^{\cos(\pi \sqrt{2} n)}}\big\rfloor\text{.} \] The proof employs the so-called one-frequency circle method for estimating exponential sums with phases $\big(\xi \lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor\big)_{1\le n\le N}$, but the major arc approximants of our exponential sums do not consist of their direct continuous counterparts. In the major arc regime we decouple the $\psi$-oscillatory part of the phase from the polynomial one, and approximate the exponential sum by $\int_0^1\big(\frac{1}{N}\int_0^Ne^{2\pi i\xi P(t)\psi( s)}dt\big)ds$. This represents a novel phenomenon for problems of this kind, and, interestingly, our proof exploits the coefficient-free variational estimates of Radon-type operators.

papers.title: Constellations for Lyapunov exponents
papers.abstract:
We study the maximal Lyapunov exponent of random products of positive matrices, and prove that it can be calculated to arbitrary precision with arithmetic work polynomial in the number of requested digits. In nondegenerate settings, the complexity of our method depends on the intrinsic complexity of the dynamics---which we characterize---and not on the Euclidean dimension of the ambient space in which the dynamics live. As numerical applications, we determine the Hausdorff dimension of random intersections of Sierpi\'nski gaskets, and Viswanath's constant---the growth rate of the random Fibonacci sequence.
  We first establish a general inequality for nonnegative matrix families showing that, if a signed measure with finite support is sufficiently close to being stationary, then it predicts the Lyapunov exponent accurately. This framework also encompasses Pollicott's Fredholm determinant approximation. We then show that, just like drawing a constellation by picking bright stars, one can construct a sequence of signed measures approximating stationarity by picking informative orbits of the projective dynamics. Furthermore, we prove that our construction uses an asymptotically optimal number of atoms, which is governed by an intrinsic quantity we call constellation dimension.

papers.title: Sharp bounds for Duke--Erd\H{o}s--R\"odl problems on cycle-connected subgraphs
papers.abstract: For $k\ge2$, a graph is $C_{2k}$-connected if every two distinct edges lie together on an even cycle of length at most $2k$ in that graph. Let $f_k(n,m)$ be the largest number of edges in a $C_{2k}$-connected subgraph that every $n$-vertex graph with $m$ edges must contain. In this paper, we study two cycle-connected problems raised by Duke, Erd\H{o}s and R\"odl. First, Duke, Erd\H{o}s and R\"odl showed that $f_3(n,\lfloor n^{2-\beta}\rfloor)=\Theta(n^{2-3\beta})$ for every fixed $0< \beta<1/2$ and ask for the case of $\beta\ge 1/2$. We solve this problem in a stronger form by determining that the optimal range of $\beta$ is $(0,2/3]$. Second, we prove that $f_2(n,\binom n2-s)=(1/(2e)+o(1))n^3/s$ whenever $\frac{s}{n}\to\infty$ and $s=o(n^2)$, determining the leading constant in an estimate of Duke, Erd\H{o}s, and R\"odl. The first result uses a finite-field construction and a count of three-edge paths. The second uses the known structure of $C_4$-connected graphs and estimates for complete bipartite subgraphs in a random graph.

papers.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincar\'e prior that neither test decides
papers.abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $\delta_F$ is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincar\'e inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincar\'e, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincar\'e class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.

papers.title: The measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups
papers.authors: Damien Gaboriau, Antoine Poulin, Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob, Konrad Wr\'obel
papers.abstract:
In this article we show that all the nonamenable Baumslag-Solitar groups with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree, i.e., $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ with $|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p|
eq |q|$, are measure equivalent to each other, thereby completing the measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups: each $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ belongs to one of three measure equivalence classes according to whether it is amenable ($|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$), virtually isomorphic to $\mathbf{F}_n 	imes \mathbf{Z}$ ($|p|=|q|
eq 1$), or is nonamenable with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree ($|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p| 
eq |q|$). More generally, we obtain the similar classification of the generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups of rank $1$ (i.e., groups that act cocompactly on a tree with edge and vertex stabilizers infinite cyclic).
  Our proof also establishes a classification of all treeable lcsc groups into exactly six measure equivalence classes. Our new contribution which completes this taxonomy is: all nonunimodular nonamenable treeable lcsc groups are measure equivalent.
  Along the way we obtain several results about type $\mathrm{III}$ equivalence relations and graphings of independent interest. For example, we show that every ergodic type $\mathrm{III}_0$ graphing admits an ergodic hyperfinite subgraph for which the natural factor map of Krieger flows is an isomorphism.

papers.title: Optimal solution ranks in the Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation
papers.abstract: For every $n$ and $r$ with $1\le r$ and $\binom{r+1}{2}\le n$, we construct a connected unweighted graph on $n$ vertices whose Max-Cut semidefinite relaxation has a unique optimal solution of rank $r$. The main examples are the Kneser graphs $K(m,2)$, whose unique optima have rank $m-1$. A six-vertex wheel supplies rank three, and attaching pendant vertices preserves both rank and uniqueness. For dense random graphs, we also prove a polynomial lower bound on the optimal rank.

papers.title: A geometric construction of supercuspidal representations
papers.authors: Ben Liu, Sian Nie, Zhihang Yu
papers.abstract: We extend the framework of deep level Deligne-Lusztig varieties to the case of arbitrary residue characteristics $p > 0$. As an application, we provide a construction of a large class of (new) supercuspidal representations for unramified $p$-adic groups with arbitrary residue fields, in a purely geometric way.

papers.title: On first-order limiting probabilities for small permutation classes
papers.authors: Victor Falgas-Ravry, Klas Markstr\"om, Eero R\"aty, Fiona Skerman
papers.abstract:
Given a small permutation class $\mathcal{P}$, we consider the set of possible limits of the probability $\mathbb{P}\big(\mathbf{\sigma}_n \models \Psi\big)$ that a uniformly chosen random permutation $\mathbf{\sigma}_n\in \mathcal{P}_n$ satisfies a fixed first-order sentence in Theory of Two Orders (TOTO). In the case of small permutation classes with polynomial growth, we show this limit set is finite, and characterize the set explicitly. In particular, we prove that many natural small permutation classes of polynomial growth arising from permutation matrices satisfy a $0$-$1$ convergence law, and have an infinite model.
  In the case of small permutation classes with exponential growth we show that the limit set is dense in $[0,1]$, thereby extending a result of Albert--Bouvel--F\'eray--Noy, using different methods, to this range.

papers.title: Automatic cocommutativity for the quantum-group comonad
papers.abstract:
We prove that the cofree Hopf algebra on a cocommutative bialgebra is again cocommutative, and in fact coincides with the latter's largest Hopf subalgebra. This answers a question of Ardizzoni-Menini-Saracco and provides a proof for a statement to the same effect in the literature, whose original justification contains an apparent gap. The result relies on (and is in fact equivalent to) the observation that cocommutative bialgebra quotients of arbitrary Hopf algebras are automatically Hopf. This latter statement strengthens the analogue due to Newman, which assumes cocommutativity for the Hopf domain.
  One application of the above is the following quantum-rigidity result for Hopf algebras acted upon by a covariant quantum group: an action by one Hopf algebra on another which preserves the unital-algebra structure and the comultiplication factors through an action by a cocommutative Hopf algebra which moreover preserves the entire Hopf structure.

papers.title: Small eigenvalues of negatively curved manifolds with finite volume
papers.abstract: We obtain upper bounds for the number of small eigenvalues of complete Riemannian manifolds with negative sectional curvature and finite volume.

papers.title: Quantitative hyperconvexity and the Bergman distance
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded hyperconvex domain admitting a negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion function $u$ such that $-u(z)\le C\exp[-\eta(\log(1/\delta_\Omega(z)))]$ near the boundary, where $\eta$ is nondecreasing with $\lim_{t\rightarrow+\infty}\eta(t)=+\infty$. We present a lower bound for the Bergman distance $d_{B,\Omega}(z_0,z)$ by counting the iterates of a function determined by the generalized inverse of $\eta$. The bound tends to infinity as $z\rightarrow\partial\Omega$ for every such $\eta$; moreover, it recovers several known estimates. The proof combines a one-sided localization of Green sublevel sets with boundary estimates for the Bergman kernel and a capacity--volume inequality. We also obtain an upper bound for the Bergman distance along the axis of a family of complete Hartogs domains whose fiber radii decay faster than every positive power of the boundary distance in the base disc.

papers.title: Pseudo-Calabi Flow on Toric Variety
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the long time existence of the pseudo-Calabi flow on a compact toric variety for any $T^n$-invariant initial K\"ahler metric. If the Mabuchi functional is proper modulo automorphisms, the flow converges exponentially to a constant scalar curvature K\"ahler (cscK) metric. In particular, this gives a flow proof that properness of the K-energy implies the existence of a cscK metric in the toric setting.

papers.title: Lie Symmetry-Guided Adaptive Sampling for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising mesh-free framework for solving partial differential equations (PDEs), with broad applications in physics, engineering, and medicine. However, their performance is highly sensitive to the sampling strategy for training points. Conventional uniform sampling often fails to adequately resolve regions with complex solution features, leading to low efficiency and limited accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose a Lie symmetry-driven adaptive sampling framework for PINNs, termed Lie-AS-ISC. For PDEs admitting Lie symmetry groups, symmetry transformations are exploited to derive intrinsic functional relationships between the solution and its variables, enabling the construction of basis points with exact solutions that span the solution domain. Building on this, an adaptive sampling strategy is developed by jointly considering absolute error and invariant surface conditions, while a dual-index loss is introduced to enhance training constraints. The proposed method significantly improves prediction accuracy. The experimental results show that this method consistently outperforms existing methods in accuracy.

papers.title: A functional central limit theorem for particle systems under polynomial growth conditions, with applications to statistics
papers.abstract: We establish a functional central limit theorem (CLT) for fluctuations of time-integrated functionals of empirical measures arising from interacting McKean--Vlasov particle systems. Our framework allows for coefficients with unbounded spatial growth and dependence on arbitrarily high-order moments of the measure variable, extending the scope of the existing fluctuation theory. The proof uses a novel approach combining linear functional differentiation with new well-posedness results and estimates for perturbed backward parabolic equations in polynomially weighted Schauder spaces, yielding a martingale-type representation of the fluctuations with an asymptotically negligible remainder. The limiting process is shown to be centred Gaussian with an explicit covariance structure. As a statistical application, we derive the asymptotic theory underlying hypothesis tests for both the temporal constancy of population characteristics and parametric restrictions on the drift coefficient.

papers.title: Lempert left inverses of the Royal and Flat geodesics of the symmetrized bidisc
papers.abstract: In this note, we give complete description of the Lempert left inverses of the royal and flat geodesics of the symmetrized bidisc. It is further proved that the collection of all such Lempert left inverses to the royal and flat geodesics is path connected. This, in particular, answers a question asked by Zwonek \cite[~Remark 4.4, 4.5]{zwonek}.

papers.title: Global Stability of the Kolmogorov--Zakharov Spectrum for the Wave Kinetic Equation
papers.abstract:
We prove global nonlinear stability near the mass Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectrum $f_M(\omega)=\omega^{-7/6}$ for the isotropic cubic wave kinetic equation, including small time-dependent external forces. For sufficiently small initial perturbations and forcing, the solution remains uniformly close to $f_M$ for all time in a weighted norm. This norm allows $f(t,\omega)\sim a_0(t)\omega^{-7/6}$ as $\omega\to0$ and $f(t,\omega)\sim a_\infty(t)\omega^{-7/6}$ as $\omega\to\infty$.
  When the external force $\phi$ is independent of time, the solution converges at an algebraic rate to a stationary solution in weaker weighted norms. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition on the initial perturbation for convergence in the original weighted norm. These results resolve, for small perturbations of the Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectrum, the question of convergence to a stationary solution under time-independent forcing raised by Collot, Dietert, and Germain (arXiv:2208.00947, Section 1.3).
  To establish this stability, the collision integral is expanded around $a_0(t)f_M$ at low frequencies and $a_\infty(t)f_M$ at high frequencies, separating it into a linear term with time-dependent coefficients and a nonlinear remainder. This decomposition yields improved control of the nonlinear remainder.
  The main difficulty is that $a_0(t)$ may vary in time, so the linear operator itself changes with time and its evolution cannot be represented by the semigroup of a single fixed operator. To address this difficulty, we use a parametrix construction to explicitly construct the evolution operator $U_{a_0,a_\infty}$ and establish the required uniform bounds. Moreover, our arguments provide a general framework for proving global stability that may also apply to other evolution equations.

papers.title: A general algebraic characterization of extremal $\Delta$-trees and $k$-cyclic graphs for degree-homogeneous VDB indices
papers.abstract: We present a general algebraic method for maximizing a vertex-degree-based (VDB) topological index $TI(G) = \sum_{uv \in E(G)} f(d(u),d(v))$ over the class of $n$-vertex trees with a prescribed maximum degree $\Delta \ge 3$. By expressing the edge multiplicities of the basis $\mathcal{B} = \{(1,\Delta), (\Delta,\Delta)\}$ via degree-sum identities, we reduce the maximization of $TI(T)$ to the minimization of an explicit discrete penalty function $G(x,y)$ over the non-basic edges. We formulate five analytical conditions on the weight function $f(x,y)$ that dictate the optimal edge distributions, yielding a complete characterization of the extremal trees across all congruence classes of $n \pmod{\Delta - 1}$. Additionally, we provide their explicit construction by attaching leaves to a core of internal vertices. Applying this framework, we obtain the complete characterization of extremal $\Delta$-trees for the Degree-Ratio Sombor ($DRSO$), Symmetric Division Deg ($SDD$), and Hyperbolic Sombor ($HSO$) indices for all $\Delta \ge 3$. Furthermore, the analytical conditions identify the exact degree thresholds for the Arithmetic-Geometric ($AG$) and Diminished Sombor ($DSO$) indices, showing that the same extremal family maximizes $AG$ if and only if $3 \le \Delta \le 8$, and $DSO$ if and only if $3 \le \Delta \le 4$. Finally, since changing the edge count from $m = n - 1$ to $m = n - 1 + k$ affects only the constant term in the decomposition while leaving the penalty function $G(x,y)$ invariant, the method extends directly to connected $k$-cyclic graphs.

papers.title: On derived equivalences of exact structures on the category of representations $k[x]/(x^n)$
papers.abstract: From the perspective of homological algebra, exact categories are interesting because they possess derived categories. Typically, an additive category admits many exact structures. If the original category is sufficiently nice (for example, quasi-abelian), a classification of exact structures can be given in terms of certain Serre subcategories in the category of contravariant functors. It turns out that the derived categories of different exact structures are functorially related. This work is concerned with sufficient conditions for the derived equivalence of different exact structures on certain categories.

papers.title: Sharp diameter estimates via integral geometry
papers.abstract: We prove that the diameter of a closed embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is always less than the integral of the magnitude of the mean curvature, divided by $\pi$. We also prove a sharp variant for surfaces with boundary, and apply it to address a conjecture of Miura.

papers.title: Critical measures and coefficient limits for non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
papers.abstract: We study critical holomorphic multiplicative chaos with circular iid inputs of unit variance. Writing $R=|X_1|$, we prove that the radially normalized boundary measures converge in probability to a finite measure with almost surely positive mass if and only if $\mathbb{E}[R^2\log(2+R)]<\infty$; otherwise they converge to zero. We obtain distinct sharp criteria for convergence at each fractional order $0<q<1$ for radial approximations and for the full Fourier-radial family. Convergence at every such order is equivalent to an exponential-moment radius of at least two. In the positive-limit class, coefficient vectors normalized by $(\log n)^{1/4}$ and their analytic windows converge stably to Gaussian mixtures determined by the same critical measure. This measure is nonatomic, has full support, and is carried by a set of Hausdorff dimension zero. Coefficient periodograms recover the measure, while scalar and matrix energy normalizations give universal Gaussian limits. Exact weighted tails under $\mathbb{E} I_0(2R)<\infty$, where $I_0$ is the modified Bessel function, and negative mass moments distinguish uncountably many coefficient-limit laws, even modulo deterministic scalar rescaling, within a uniformly bounded input family. This disproves the common-law clause of Gu-Zhang's Question 2 at its fixed normalization. We give conditions for convergence of the original coefficient moments and show that finiteness of the limiting moments alone does not suffice. For inputs with $\log\mathbb{P}(R>u)\sim-\lambda u^\alpha$, $0<\alpha<1$, the coefficient normalization and Gaussian-mixture form persist, but the limit has no finite positive moments; we determine its logarithmic tails. Finally, we prove Hardy nonmembership under finite variance alone and, in the positive-limit class, sharp weighted Bergman criteria for $0<p\le2$ and the boundary Sobolev threshold $s=-1/2$.

papers.title: Counting Admissible Sets of Integers: A Proof of the Erd\H{o}s--Nicolas--S\'ark\"ozy Conjecture
papers.abstract: A finite set of positive integers is admissible if any two of its subsets with the same sum have the same cardinality. In 1991, Erd\H{o}s, Nicolas and S\'ark\"ozy conjectured that $\log a(N)\asymp\sqrt N$, where $a(N)$ denotes the number of nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. We prove this conjecture by showing that there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that $\exp(c\sqrt N)\le a(N)\le\exp(C\sqrt N)$ for every integer $N\ge4$. The same bounds hold for the number of admissible sets with maximum $N$. For the upper bound, we show that every sufficiently large admissible set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ contains a subset of proportional size whose doubling constant is $O(N/|A|^2)$.

papers.title: Exact Minimum Extension Degrees for Reed Solomon Codes under Linear and Nonlinear Repair at the Cut Set Bound
papers.abstract: We study the minimum extension degree required for a Reed--Solomon code to admit exact $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear repair at the cut-set bound from every prescribed set of $d$ helpers. Let $s=d-k+1$, and let $Q_s(n)$ be the minimum product of $n$ pairwise coprime integers, each at least $s$. For every prime power $q$ and all $3\le k<d<n\le2d-2$, we prove that the minimum degree over $\mathbb{F}_q$ is exactly $sQ_s(n)$. When all surviving nodes are helpers, we also characterize the admissible extension degrees and bound the number of coordinates that can attain the cut-set bound. The required achievability follows from existing construction methods; we give a short existence proof using splitting subspaces. For a family of parameters with $n>2d-2$, we obtain strictly smaller extension degrees, showing that the range restriction cannot be omitted altogether. Finally, we prove that a nonlinear repair scheme attaining the cut-set bound induces an $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear repair scheme on the same code, where $p$ is the characteristic. Consequently, the extension-degree lower bounds over the prime field remain valid without a linearity assumption.

papers.title: Contact 3-manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings
papers.abstract: We construct the first examples of contact $3$-manifolds admitting infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings which are rational homology balls. Our examples are planar. They are obtained by a simple modification of Baykur's recent planar contact $3$-manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings, and the fillings are distinguished by their fundamental groups. For one of these rational homology balls we give an explicit Kirby diagram, with a single $1$-handle and a single $2$-handle attached along a trefoil, which exhibits its boundary as $(0,-8)$-surgery on a two-component link. We also identify the smooth topology of Baykur's example: $Y$ is obtained by $(0,-8)$-surgery on the link $7^2_4$, and it is Seifert fibered over the Klein bottle with one exceptional fiber. Finally, we construct further Stein fillings of $(Y,\xi)$, which realize all the groups $\mathbb Z/m\rtimes_{-1}\mathbb Z$, $m\ge0$, as their fundamental groups.

papers.title: Holomorphic Tischler fibration theorem for Stein spaces
papers.abstract: We study a holomorphic analogue of Tischler approximation for closed differential forms normalized by a prescribed holomorphic vector field. The main setting consists of connected normal Stein spaces satisfying a degree-one reflexive Poincar\'e property, with finitely generated first integral homology and a holomorphic $\mathbb C^*$-action admitting a closed normalized reflexive one-form. Under these hypotheses, the given form can be approximated on compact subsets of the regular locus by closed normalized reflexive forms with discrete period groups. When the first Betti number is at least two, the approximating forms may be chosen with rank-two lattice periods. We relate these approximations to holomorphic locally trivial fibrations over quotients of $\mathbb C$, with connected Stein analytic fibers that may be singular. We also establish a finite-equivariant version for suitable Stein quotients and discuss the associated normalization obstructions, including those arising from local singularity topology. Further results concern closed holomorphic time forms, transverse foliations, and the relation between the period groups and the dynamics of complete holomorphic flows. Examples illustrate both the applicability and the limitations of the hypotheses.

papers.title: How characterisations of traces and central elements fail: sharp violation constants via michelson contrast and noncentrality
papers.authors: Sami Abdullah Abed, Irina Nikolaeva, Andrej Novikov
papers.abstract: A positive functional is a trace if and only if it satisfies any one of many inequalities, the first being Gardner's $|\varphi(X)|\le\varphi(|X|)$; positive central elements are characterised similarly. We ask how strongly these characterisations fail. For $\varphi=\mathrm{Tr}(\rho\,\cdot)$ on a matrix algebra the natural scale is the Michelson contrast $\delta$ of the density. For Gardner's inequality the sharp constant depends on $\delta$ and on the contrast $\delta'$ of $|X|$ only through their product: it is $(1-\delta^2\delta'^2)^{-1/2}$, the secant of the angle whose sine is $\delta\delta'$. On a finite von Neumann algebra the contrast is the wrong parameter, since every central density gives a trace; the governing parameter is the noncentrality, defined through the central condition number $\kappa_Z(\rho)$ of the central envelopes of $\rho$ (the largest and smallest elements of Halpern's central spectrum). A transfer principle lifts sharp matrix constants to exact constants in terms of $\kappa_Z$ in every finite von Neumann algebra. For 38 trace characterisations the constant is exact in 23 cases, has proved bounds in 13 and is known only numerically in two; for instance it is $\cosh(\frac12\ln\kappa_Z)$ for Gardner's inequality and for the subadditivity of the modulus. On matrix algebras the finite exact violations vanish at the trace to the orders $\delta$, $\delta^2$ or $\delta^4$, and outside factors and abelian algebras no function of the contrast describes the constants. We also find the sharp constants of the Novikov-Tikhonov characterisations of central elements, sharp bounds for three unnormalised trace functionals, and sharp contrast thresholds below which subadditivity of the square root and the power-mean inequality cannot fail. A numerical search, certified as a lower bound for each supremum, supports conjectured values for the remaining inequalities.

papers.title: The ascending chain condition for radical well-mixed difference ideals
papers.abstract: We establish a finite-basis theorem for radical well-mixed difference ideals in a difference polynomial ring with one endomorphism over an arbitrary difference field. The result extends to every finitely difference-generated difference algebra over such a field and is equivalent to the ascending chain condition for radical well-mixed difference ideals, hence resolving a long-standing open problem in difference algebra. The proof proceeds in two stages. Over an inversive difference coefficient field, we establish a uniform inverse-transform bound relating the perfect closure of a finite system to its radical well-mixed closure. This uses Noetherian induction in a fixed truncated polynomial ring, together with generic freeness and going-down for flat ring homomorphisms. We then prove that the radical well-mixed closure of a system over a difference field $K$ is the contraction of its radical well-mixed closure over the inversive closure of $K$. This contraction result follows from successive prime lifting along flat extensions and removes the inversiveness assumption without requiring the coefficient-field extension to be finitely generated.

papers.title: Controlled Block Proximal Linearized Method for Nonconvex and Nonsmooth Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider multiblock nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization without assuming bounded iterates or coercivity of the original objective. We propose the Controlled Block Proximal Linearized (CBPL) method, which incorporates a control potential into block updates while retaining the original objective, variables, and constraints. Under explicit control design conditions and the KL property, the control yields boundedness, finite length, whole-sequence convergence of the original variables, and convergence of objective values. At the limit, one limiting subgradient of the original objective vanishes on all effective comparison directions. We apply CBPL to graph-regularized nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF), CP decomposition, and independent-core matrix tri-factorization (NMTF) with $\ell_0$ norm sparsity constraints. We characterize their reconstruction-preserving scale degeneracies, proving that scale criticality is equivalent to graph collapse and that full criticality forces such collapse. Explicit controls provide compact sublevel sets and a uniform positive lower bound on graph action, including with an independent Tucker core, while retaining genuine reconstruction-changing directions. Each block admits an explicit projection and a computable safe step parameter. For ordinary NMF and CP models, whole-sequence convergence to a full critical point follows. Experiments with direct safe updates demonstrate convergence, sustained graph action, and controlled factor and core scales.

papers.title: Recovering the Topology of a Real Plane Algebraic Curve by Tropical Homotopy
papers.abstract: We present a tropical homotopy method for computing the numbers of ovals and unbounded components of a real plane algebraic curve, together with the pairing of its ends at infinity. Under explicit support and nondegeneracy assumptions, the homotopy starts from a tropical patchwork and encounters finitely many events. At Morse event points, the curve changes by local surgery. To determine the global attachments, we follow descending separatrices of a single gradient-like field to a fixed collection of base curves. The order of their landing points defines a finite combinatorial state, updated by local rules that also handle events at infinity and simultaneous event points. This recovers component data without tracing the intervening curves. For the dequantizing lifting, given by the negative logarithms of coefficient magnitudes, we prove an explicit event window when the lifting is generic. For fixed support and coefficient signs, with independent, identically distributed log-normal magnitudes, the expected number of events is bounded by a constant divided by the standard deviation of the logarithms. When all event points are Morse, correctness is conditional on complete, correctly classified event data, a sufficiently small starting parameter, and correctly labelled and ordered landing points. A numerical implementation illustrates its behaviour on sparse curves of high degree and on coefficients spanning many scales; these conditions are not certified.

papers.title: Global Strong Solution to Multi-Dimensional Compressible Quantum Navier-Stokes Equation in Bounded Domains with Large Initial Data
papers.authors: Jiaxu Li, Boqiang L\"u, Huixiang Zhou
papers.abstract:
We consider the compressible quantum Navier-Stokes (QNS) system in a smooth bounded domain, supplemented with a curvature Navier-slip boundary condition for the velocity and a homogeneous Neumann boundary condition for the density. For arbitrarily large initial data away from vacuum, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions when the adiabatic index
  \[ \gamma\in[1,\infty)\quad\text{for }N=2, \qquad \gamma\in\left[1,3\right)\quad\text{for }N=3. \] The argument relies on the effective velocity $v=u+\nabla\log\rho$, which reveals the parabolic structure of the system. Compared with previous works in the periodic and Cauchy cases, additional difficulties arise from the treatment of boundary terms. We also use a bootstrap argument between the density integrability and the weighted integrability of the effective velocity to enlarge the admissible range of $\gamma$ from $\left[1,11/4\right)$ to $\left[1,3\right)$. Combining this bootstrap argument with a De Giorgi iteration for the density upper bound and a Nash-Moser type iteration for the positive lower bound, we derive a priori estimates on every finite time interval and extend the local strong solution globally in time. As far as we know, this is the first result on global strong solutions with large initial data for the initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) of the QNS system in bounded domains with compatibility boundary conditions.

papers.title: A note on consequences of Mahler's inequalities
papers.abstract: We derive Makai's inequality $\vol_n(K)\vol_n((K-K)^\circ)\ge(n+1)/n!$ in every dimension from the symmetric Mahler theorem in one higher dimension, with equality precisely for simplices. The proof uses a classical two-layer construction, an identity for its polar volume, and a Rogers--Shephard volume estimate. We then record basic consequences of the Mahler and Makai inequalities for polar successive minima, successive minima at the Santal\'o point, critical determinants, first covering minima, and non-separable lattice arrangements. We also combine Alexandrov--Fenchel with the volume-product inequalities to obtain sharp bounds for paired mixed volumes.

papers.title: Lifting $\tau$-exceptional sequences
papers.authors: Aslak B. Buan, Eric J. Hanson, Bethany R. Marsh
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of $\tau$-exceptional sequences under passage from a finite-dimensional algebra $\Lambda$ to a factor algebra $\Lambda/I$. Assuming that $\Lambda$ is $\tau$-tilting finite and that $I\subseteq \operatorname{rad}\Lambda$, we construct, for every $r$ less than or equal to the number of simple $\Lambda$-modules, an injective map from the $\tau$-exceptional sequences of length $r$ over $\Lambda/I$ to those over $\Lambda$. The construction is recursive and is based on lifting indecomposable $\tau$-rigid modules and comparing their associated $\tau$-perpendicular categories. At each stage, we construct a right exact functor between the relevant $\tau$-perpendicular categories which, after identifying them with module categories, is naturally isomorphic to extension of scalars along a quotient $\Gamma\to\Gamma/J$, where $J\subseteq \operatorname{rad}\Gamma$. These functors send each lifted term to an object in the additive closure of the corresponding original term. Finally, we conjecture connections with known bijections for representations of quivers over local algebras and for Nakayama algebras.

papers.title: On real biquadratic number fields for which the $2$-Iwasawa module has rank $3$
papers.abstract: We investigate the stability of the $2$-rank in the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of real biquadratic number fields. We determine several families of real biquadratic fields $F$ for which the ranks of the $2$-class group $A(F)$ and the associated $2$-Iwasawa module $A_\infty(F)$ are both equal to $3$. More precisely, we provide a complete classification of all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d$ is an odd positive square-free integer, and all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ is a positive square-free integer, for which $ \operatorname{rank}(A(F))=\operatorname{rank}(A_\infty(F))=3.$

papers.title: Path-Specific Geometric-Stochastic Channel Model for Scattering from ISAC Targets: A Unified Measurement-Based Characterization of Robots, Humans, and Automobiles at 28 GHz
papers.authors: Neeraj Varshney, Jelena Senic, Jack Chuang, Samuel Berweger, Steve Blandino, Jian Wang, Camillo Gentile, Nada Golmie
papers.abstract: This paper develops a channel model for scattering from a broad class of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) targets-robots, humans, and automobiles-based on a unified measurement campaign at 28~GHz. Nine targets are characterized from numerous transmitter--receiver configurations per target, spanning full bistatic and aspect angles and thus covering backward to forward scattering. Repeated acquisitions are collected for each configuration to capture target motion and dynamics, yielding nearly 117\,000 acquisitions in total. Measurements are collected with a 2~GHz-wide channel sounder equipped with a 256-element phased-array antenna, followed by digital beamforming and super-resolution processing for reliable extraction of multiple paths in delay and 2D angle, with average estimation errors of 0.1~ns and 0.2$^\circ$ respectively. From these measurements, we reduce a \emph{path-specific} channel representation in which the scattering is modeled as a cluster of paths whose center is defined by the bistatic specular \emph{geometry}; the cluster shape is described \emph{stochastically}. To ensure physically grounded spatio--temporal consistency, extracted paths are mapped to incident points on the target, each with an associated radar cross section (RCS) that is compatible with the 3GPP TR~38.901 ISAC channel model, and are subsequently mapped back to path properties for channel synthesis. The resulting statistical distributions are well behaved, physically interpretable, and consistent across targets, geometries, and motion. Comparison between measured and synthesized channel realizations demonstrates close agreement in pathloss trends and fluctuation behavior. Together, these results yield a high-fidelity, measurement-derived channel representation suitable for ISAC simulation, target modeling, and system design.

papers.title: The silp--spli equality for group rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be an arbitrary associative ring with an identity. In this paper, we show that the equality $\silp(R)=\spli(R)$ implies $\silp(RG)=\spli(RG)$ for any group $G$.

papers.title: The Plane-Saturation Ratio of Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: For a planar graph \(G\), a plane subgraph \(H\) is plane-saturated with respect to \(G\) if adding any edge to the fixed drawing of \(H\), possibly together with new vertices, either creates a crossing or results in a graph that is not a subgraph of \(G\). The plane-saturation ratio \(\psr(G)\) is the minimum of \(e(H)/e(G)\) over all plane-saturated subgraphs \(H\) of \(G\). For nonnegative integers \(k_1\) and \(k_2\), let \(\cG_{k_1,k_2}\) denote the class of planar graphs in which, for each \(i\in\{1,2\}\), at most \(k_i\) vertices of degree \(i\) have any prescribed neighborhood, where \(k_i=0\) means that vertices of degree \(i\) are forbidden. We prove that every \(G\in\cG_{k_1,k_2}\) with at least one edge satisfies $\psr(G)>\frac{1}{9+k_1+6k_2}.$ This settles two conjectures of Clifton and Salia.

papers.title: Positive solutions of Yamabe-type equations with general potentials
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$, and let $\psi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. We prove that the equation $$ -\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}\Delta_g u+\psi u=u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} $$ has a smooth positive solution if and only if its linear part has positive first eigenvalue. In dimensions $n\ge6$, the proof combines an energy estimate under exact local mass constraints with an intersection argument for finite cycles of atomic measures; dimensions $3\le n\le5$ follow from the theorem of Bahri and Brezis.

papers.title: On the isomorphism of the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$
papers.abstract: Let $1 \leqslant p \leqslant q < \infty$, let $\mathsf{X}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_p$-space and let $\mathsf{Y}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_q$-space. We show that the space $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ of bounded linear operators from $\mathsf{X}$ into $\mathsf{Y}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(\ell_p,\ell_q)$ if, and only if, $\mathsf{Y}$ is complemented in its bidual. We also show that $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{Z},\ell_{\infty})$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(c_0,\ell_{\infty})$ for every separable $\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$-space $\mathsf{Z}$. This extends and complements the earlier result of Arias and Farmer [On the structure of tensor products of $\ell_p$-spaces, Pacific J. Math.]. Based on this general result, we give a completely different proof of the main result of Astashkin, Le\'snik and Maligranda [Isomorphic structure of Ces\`aro and Tandori spaces, Canad. J. Math.], which states that the space $\mathcal{K}$ and its sequence counterpart $\mathcal{k}$ are isomorphic. Furthermore, we complete the picture by showing that the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$, although isomorphic, are not isometric. Along the way, we show that for every infinite compact metrizable space $K$ the $\ell_{\infty}$-sum of copies of the space $\mathscr{M}(K)$ of regular Borel measures on $K$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} L_1[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}} \approx \mathfrak{L}(\ell_1,L_1[0,1])$. This provides an abstract blueprint for another result of Astashkin, Le\'snik and Maligranda, namely that $\mathcal{K}$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{M}[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}}$. Finally, we show that there are models of set theory without the Axiom of Choice in which the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ are no longer isomorphic. This last part was inspired by V\"ath's paper [The dual space of $L_{\infty}$ is $L_1$, Indag. Math. (N.S.)].

papers.title: Graham's rearrangement conjecture in finite abelian groups
papers.abstract:
Graham conjectured in 1971 that every subset of the nonzero elements of a prime cyclic group admits an ordering with pairwise distinct nonempty partial sums. Recently, the work of Pham and Sauermann, together with earlier results, settled this conjecture for all sufficiently large primes. In this paper, we prove that there is an absolute integer $n_0$ such that every subset $S\subseteq G\setminus\{0\}$ of a finite abelian group with $|S|\ge n_0$ admits such an ordering, which also solves a conjecture of Alspach and Liversidge for all sufficiently large sets.
  A key ingredient of our proof is a sufficient condition via additive dimension: If $|S|=n$ and $S$ contains a dissociated subset of size at least $\Omega((\log n)^2/\log\log n)$, then $S$ has an ordering in which no proper nonempty interval of consecutive terms sums to zero. This bound is within a factor of $O(\log n/\log\log n)$ of the smallest possible additive dimension of an $n$-element set.

papers.title: A Levi-form criterion for Oka complements
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a connected Stein manifold of complex dimension at least three with the density property, then $M\setminus K$ is a connected Oka manifold for every nonempty compact $K\Subset M$ with smooth boundary whose Levi form has at least two nonnegative eigenvalues at every boundary point for local defining functions negative on $\operatorname{int}K$. For compact sets in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth boundary, this settles both implications between pseudoconvexity of $\partial K$ and the Oka property of $\mathbb{C}^n\setminus K$: pseudoconvexity is sufficient but not necessary for $n\geq3$, and necessary but not sufficient for $n=2$. In dimension two, we give an explicit compact set in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with strongly pseudoconvex boundary and non-Oka complement.

papers.title: Indeterminacy of period map and Griffiths heights for hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the period map $\overline {\mathcal P}$, from the GIT moduli space of degree $d$ hypersurface $X$ in $\mathbb P^n$ to the Baily-Borel compactification of the period image associated to the middle cohomology $H^{n-1}_{\rm prim}(X,\mathbb Z)$, extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has at worst nodal singularities (resp. suspensions of slc surface singularities) when $n$ is even (resp. $n$ is odd). This verifies and generalizes Laza-O'Grady's prediction on the indeterminacy locus of the period map for quartic K3s to arbitrary hypersurfaces. For Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces, we prove that the birational map from the GIT moduli space to the BBH compactification extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has semi-log canonical singularities. The results apply to distinguish the Baily-Borel and BBH compactifications. In the process, we answer two questions of Mordant on the Griffiths height for families of hypersurfaces over curves, which are crucial to the proofs of the main results.

papers.title: Non-Ergodic Markovian Mirror Descent with Unbounded Noise
papers.abstract: We analyze stochastic mirror descent for minimizing a convex objective expressed as an expectation under the stationary distribution of a Markov chain, using noisy subgradient observations along a single sample path. Through Poisson's equation, we decompose the Markovian noise and control its contribution under regularity and moment conditions that allow the stochastic subgradients and the Poisson solution to be unbounded across the state space. We establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the expected suboptimality gap of the weighted-average iterate for an appropriately chosen step size. The analysis does not require aperiodicity or convergence of the chain's marginal distributions to stationarity. For irreducible finite-state chains, we verify the required conditions on the Poisson solution and derive explicit bounds that quantify the effect of periodicity. For irreducible countable-state chains, we verify the required regularity and moment conditions under a geometric Lyapunov drift condition and suitable growth bounds on the stochastic subgradients.

papers.title: On Khovanov homology of virtual links
papers.abstract: We show that the Khovanov homology of virtual knots defined by V.O. Manturov and the Khovanov homology defined by D. Tubbenhauer coincide.

papers.title: On maximum likelihood estimation in the $\beta$-model for random hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We study maximum likelihood estimation in the $\beta$-model for random hypergraphs, in which a group of vertices succeeds with a probability that depends on the sum of its members' parameters. The data are independent binary outcomes of experiments on groups of vertices, tested according to an arbitrary, possibly incomplete design. Suppose that every tested group has $k$ vertices and success probability in $[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]$. For complete designs in which every group is tested at least $r$ times, a unique maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) exists with high probability if $r\geq C_k\epsilon^{-1}\log n/n^{k-1}$, and for $m$ experiments on uniformly random groups, it suffices that $m\geq C_k\epsilon^{-1}n\log n$, where $C_k$ depends only on $k$. Both conditions are linear in $\epsilon^{-1}$ and, for fixed $k$, cannot be improved in general beyond the constant; they follow from finite-sample bounds for arbitrary designs. We bound the mean squared error of the MLE over a parameter box by the smallest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix of the design, and show that the rate is minimax optimal for balanced complete designs. Among $k$-uniform designs with a given number of experiments, designs in which every pair of vertices takes part together in the same number of experiments maximize this eigenvalue, and uniform random designs nearly do so with high probability. Finally, the design matrix of a uniform random design has full column rank with high probability if $m\geq\max\{n,c(n/k)\log n\}$ for fixed $c>2$ and $k=o(n/\log n)$, or $m\geq n$ when $k\geq(1+\xi)\log n$. For fixed $k$, the threshold $(n/k)\log n$ is sharp, and above it rank deficiency is asymptotically as likely as some vertex taking part in no experiment.

papers.title: Proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: an exposition
papers.abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$ is exactly $\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor$. We present a streamlined variant of the proof of this conjecture recently announced by OpenAI (2026). Although the original proof is relatively short, it is quite difficult to follow. We simplify several steps and provide a concise and accessible exposition of the proof. We also combine this new result with known reductions to determine the crossing numbers of several other graph families.

papers.title: An Alt-Caffarelli problem for elastic graphs
papers.abstract: We study an Alt-Caffarelli-type free boundary problem for symmetric elastic graphs with fixed boundary height. Our results concern existence of minimizers and their description in terms of regularity and shape. It turns out that the weight coefficient in front of the measure term is decisive for existence. We identify a sharp threshold for this coefficient below which existence is guaranteed. Moreover, we find that all sign-changing minimizers are described by a system of three Eulerian elasticae, none of which are lines. Another result shows non-flatness of free boundary points, a classical question in the study of Alt-Caffarelli problems. These properties lead to a better understanding of the nonexistence phenomenon above the aforementioned weight threshold.

papers.title: Slow blowup solutions for the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract:
We consider the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schr"odinger equation  egin{equation*} i\partial_t\psi+\Delta\psi+|\psi|^{2p}\psi=0 \end{equation*} in dimensions $d\geq11$, with $p\in\mathbb N^\ast$, under the Joseph--Lundgren condition $2p+1>p_{JL}(d)$. For every $
u>
u_0(d,p)$, there exists a radial finite-time type II blow-up solution concentrating the ground state $Q$ in the form  egin{equation*} \psi(t,x)=\lambda^{ rac{1}{p}}(t)Q(\lambda(t)x)+\zeta(t,x),\quad \lambda(t)=t^{- rac12-
u}. \end{equation*} All homogeneous Sobolev norms $\|\psi(t)\|_{\dot H^s}$, $1\leq s<s_c$, remain bounded. The radiation converges to a limiting profile  egin{equation*}
  \zeta^*\in \dot H^s(\mathbb R^d), \qquad s_c<s<s_c+2
u|\lambda_+|, \end{equation*} where $\lambda_+$ is determined by the leading correction in the asymptotic expansion of $Q$ at infinity. Our proof combines matched asymptotic expansions across three spatial scales with modified energy estimates. The key ingredient is the systematic treatment of the singular nonlinear background and coupled oscillations generated by the slow algebraic tail of $Q$.

papers.title: New results on nil rings
papers.abstract: For every field~$\Bbbk$, we construct a non-nilpotent nil algebra~$A$ whose Lie algebra $A^{(-)}$ is generated by ten elements. For $\Bbbk = \mathbb Z_p$, its adjoint group can also be generated by ten elements. Moreover, for every field $\Bbbk$ algebraic over its prime subfield, we construct a finitely presented algebra $B$ over $\Bbbk$ whose Jacobson radical is not nil. These results were found with the assistance of Aristotle (Harmonic).

papers.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.

papers.title: Nonparametric Regression on the Circle with Applications to Climate and Environmental Science
papers.authors: Athanasios G. Georgiadis, Andrew P. Percival
papers.abstract: Two important indicators of climate change are the decline in Arctic sea ice area and the increase in average temperatures globally. Both sea ice and temperature exhibit seasonal patterns, making circular regression a natural approach for their analysis. In this paper, we construct computationally tractable Nadaraya-Watson type kernel regression estimators on the unit circle, using rate-optimal kernel density estimators. We introduce a leave-one-out cross-validation procedure for the data-driven selection of the smoothness parameter and evaluate the performance of the proposed estimators through a simulation study covering 48 scenarios, including comparisons with existing local polynomial estimators. We then apply our methodology to historical Arctic sea ice area data and daily temperature observations in Stockholm. The fitted regression functions and their derivatives or finite differences allow us to investigate changes in both the levels and seasonal dynamics of these environmental indicators. In particular, we observe a decline in fitted sea ice area and substantial changes in its seasonal rates of growth and retreat, together with higher fitted temperatures across most of the year in Stockholm during the more recent period in comparison to historical data.

papers.title: Rigorous Lower Bounds for Atomic and Ionic Ground-State Energies
papers.abstract: We establish a new iterative method for computing rigorous lower bounds for the ground-state energies of all atoms and ions. The accuracy of the resulting bounds depends on two ingredients: the quality of the initial energy estimate and the quality of the used upper bound for the maximum number of bound electrons, $N_c(Z)$, as a function of the nuclear charge $Z>0$. In particular, this new method allows us to establish the explicit lower bound $E(N,Z) \geq -0.8710\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for the ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$ of the atom/ion with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ electrons and nuclear charge $Z \in (0,N]$, thereby considerably improving the best known constant $A=(3/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.1447$ in the estimate $E(N,Z) \geq -A\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for $0 < Z \leq N$ and coming much closer to the best possible constant given by the Thomas-Fermi asymptotics $\lim_{N \to \infty} |E(N,N)|N^{-7/3}= -E_{\text{TF}}(1)\approx 0.7687$ derived in Adv.
