Graph Theory 103 (2023), 661--673] showed that ${\rm diss}(G)\ge n-\frac{1}{3}(m+k+c_1)$ where $n, m, k, c_1$ denote the numbers of vertices, edges, components and induced cycles of length $1$ modulo $3$ in $G$ and they also established a complete characterization of extremal graphs under the vertex-disjoint cycle constraint. Although this partial characterization offers very valuable structural insights, it excludes many simple extremal graphs. So they posed a natural question: How can all extremal graphs be comprehensively characterized without restrictions? In this paper, we give a recursive characterization of all graphs attaining equality in this bound.

papers.title: Modular Existential Closedness
papers.abstract:
We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$.
  The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.

papers.title: Compact linear combination of composition operators on weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights
papers.authors: Yucheng Li, Zhiyu Wang, Liankuo Zhao
papers.abstract: Let $A^{\Psi}_{\omega}(\mathbb{D})$ be the weighted Bergman-Orlicz spaces induced by doubling weights $\omega$ on the unit disk $\mathbb D$. Suppose Orlicz function $\Psi$ satisfies the $\Delta_{2}$-condition. In this paper, the compactness of finite linear combination of composition operators on $A^{\Psi}_{\omega}(\mathbb{D})$ are completely characterized in terms of Julia-Carath\'eodory type conditions and vanishing Carleson measure, respectively.

papers.title: Solvability and nilpotence of ind-groups via tangent curves
papers.abstract: Answering a question of Kraft and the second-named author, we prove that a connected ind-group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is solvable, respectively nilpotent, if and only if its Lie algebra is. Their derived lengths, respectively nilpotency classes, coincide. We also obtain bounds on the derived length and nilpotency class for regular linear representations of connected ind-groups and for subgroups generated by connected algebraic subgroups. As an application, we give a new proof of the geometric case of a theorem of Belabbas: a solvable Lie algebra of vector fields on an affine variety generated by finitely many locally finite Lie subalgebras is locally finite and finite dimensional.

papers.title: A framework for trackable and modular rounding error analysis
papers.authors: Erin Carson, Yuxin Ma, Meiyue Shao
papers.abstract: Robust and meaningful rounding error analysis is becoming increasingly challenging as modern numerical computations involve a rapidly evolving variety of arithmetic formats, precisions, and computational kernels. We propose a trackable and modular framework for rounding error analysis, together with a new notation for bounding accumulated rounding errors. The analysis is trackable in the sense that the origin and propagation of individual error terms remain explicit in the final result, and modular in the sense that local error bounds can be replaced according to the arithmetic, precision, or computational kernel without repeating the structural analysis. We also introduce the notation $\gamma_n=(1-{\bm u})^{-n}-1$, which provides an alternative to the classical $\gamma_n^{\mathrm h}=n{\bm u}/(1-n{\bm u})$ notation. A key feature is that our notation does not require the restriction $n{\bm u}<1$ and conveniently handles errors arising from division. Using block LU factorization as a representative example, we show that the framework distinguishes the error sources of different algorithmic variants and permits improved kernels, such as compensated summation and accurate matrix multiplication, to be incorporated directly into the resulting error bounds.

papers.title: The sparse regularity method for graphs with few even-cycle homomorphisms
papers.abstract: Let $C_k$ denote a cycle on $k$ vertices. Pascadi (2026) established a removal lemma for $C_{2k+1}$ in graphs with few $C_{2k}$-homomorphisms under a dense-pairs condition, using Schatten--von Neumann norms and entropy methods. We give a short proof of a version with more restrictive partition and diagonal requirements, extending the combinatorial approach of Conlon, Fox, Sudakov and Zhao (2021) without using Pascadi's Schatten-norm regularity framework. We illustrate the method with a known sparse removal statement for odd product equations in finite groups.

papers.title: Gevrey Regularity for a Sum of Two Squares in Two Variables
papers.abstract: We study the Gevrey hypoellipticity of a sum of two squares in two variables, satisfying the H\"ormander hypothesis, assuming that the function, $ q $, describing (the space projection of) its characteristic variety vanishes only at a single point, which can be assumed to be the origin. A hypoellipticity result is given in a Gevrey class, depending on $ q $. In some examples the found regularity is known to be optimal.

papers.title: Log-Concavity and Fundamental Gaps on Complex Projective Domains
papers.abstract: We prove quantitative log-concavity and fundamental-gap estimates for Dirichlet Schr\"odinger operators on complex projective domains. With holomorphic sectional curvature four, the boundary condition $\mathrm{II}\ge\sqrt{44/5}\,g$ suffices in every complex dimension under $\operatorname{Hess} V\ge2|\nabla V|g$ and $\operatorname{osc}V\le4n$. It yields $\operatorname{Hess}(-\log\phi_1)>g$ and $\lambda_2-\lambda_1>\max\{n+2+\sqrt{n^2+5n+11},\,2n+14/3\}$. The main difficulty is to control the distinguished Hopf direction together with a transverse Hessian block whose dimension grows with $n$. We extend modified-Hessian first-contact arguments by retaining the Hopf term and using longitudinal and transverse rotational tests. A trace minimization reduces all gradient orientations to three extreme directions. A dimension-scaled logarithmic barrier then compares their contact costs with a single limiting profile. A radial spectral estimate supplies the required quadratic-in-dimension spectral threshold from a dimension-independent boundary curvature bound. For $n\ge3$ these are, to our knowledge, the first log-concavity estimates for domains in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ without symmetry assumptions. We also prove a sharp diameter bound and Hessian levels linear in $n$ under larger dimension-free curvature bounds.

papers.title: Influence of Anthropisation on a Mosquito Community in a Tropical Forest-Village Interface
papers.authors: Dumont Yves, H\'etier Marc, Yatat-Djeumen Valaire
papers.abstract: Tropical forests are undergoing deep changes caused by human activities, which have repercussions on the habitats of wild animal, particularly mammals. As mammals serve as a main source of blood meals for forest mosquitoes, their decline may affect the mosquitoes, as do changes in their habitats and abiotic conditions, such as rainfall, temperature, etc. Finally, along with humans come new species of mosquitoes-more generalist and more anthropophilic-that adapt to these new conditions and, moreover, serve as vectors for re-emerging diseases against which local populations have no more immunity. In this work, we derive a deterministic model which includes the effects of anthropisation, two species of mosquito that interact with one another (one is a generalist, whilst the other is sedentary and lives in the forest), and blood feeding preferences between multiple blood sources. We consider two socio-ecological areas, corresponding to a domestic area (for instance, a village), and a wild area (for instance, a tropical forest). A comprehensive analysis of the system is carried out using classical theory and monotone systems theory. We analyse the efficiency of individual protective measures, such as mosquito nets and repellents, against the domestic mosquito species. We investigate the risk of invasion of the wild area by a generalist mosquito species. We show that habitat anthropisation and high interspecific competition facilitate the invasion. When the mathematical system converges towards a periodic cycle, we provide numerical estimates for the periodic invasion threshold. Using a global sensitivity analysis, we show that the model is sensitive to the level of anthropisation, the adaptability of the invasive species to the forest area, and its fitness. The more efficient way to control the invasion is, therefore, to limit, as much as possible, the forest anthropisation.

papers.title: The role of density in phase transitions and new perspectives on theta functions
papers.abstract:
Let $z\in \mathbb{H}:=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\Im(z)>0\}$ and $\Lambda:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Im(z)}}\big({\mathbb Z}\oplus z{\mathbb Z}\big)$, and set $
\theta(\alpha;z):=\theta(\alpha;\Lambda)=\sum_{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2}e^{-\pi\alpha \frac{|m+nz|^2}{\Im(z)}}. $
We study the minimization of the functional $\theta(\alpha;z)-b\theta(2\alpha;z)$ and establish a complete phase diagram for all $\alpha>0$ and $b\in(0,\sqrt{2})$. For $0<b<\sqrt{2}$, an explicit threshold $b_1=0.0767767081\cdots\in(0,1/10)$ separates two distinct types of phase transitions.
  Type I: $0<b<b_1$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--rhombic--square--rectangular'' phase transition.
  Type II: $b_1\le b<\sqrt{2}$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--square--rectangular'' phase transition, without passing through the rhombic lattices.
  These phase transitions contrast with Montgomery's theorem \cite{Mon1988}, where the hexagonal lattice minimizes the single theta function at all scales, and the recent B\'{e}termin-Faulhuber-Steinerberger theorem \cite{BFS2026} for translated Gaussian lattice sums, where the hexagonal lattice prevails in a min-max structure. In our setting, the density parameter $\alpha$ governs the sequence of optimal lattice shapes, while the competition parameter $b$ controls the emergence of the rhombic phase, which exists for $b<b_1$ and vanishes for $b\ge b_1$.
  As an application, we resolve B\'etermin's conjecture \cite{Betermin2021AHP}. B\'etermin predicted a Type I phase transition for the functional $\theta(\alpha;z)-(1/10)\theta(2\alpha;z)$ with $b=1/10$. We instead rigorously establish that no rhombic lattice is a global minimizer at any density and prove that the system undergoes a Type II phase transition, thereby settling the conjecture in corrected form.

papers.title: Boundary Layer Criterion for the Low Mach Number and Inviscid Limits in Compressible Fluid-Rigid Body Interaction
papers.abstract: We investigate the simultaneous low Mach number and vanishing viscosity limit for a three-dimensional compressible viscous fluid interacting with a freely moving rigid body. The fluid satisfies the compressible Navier-Stokes equations and the no-slip condition on the body surface, while the body evolves according to Newton's laws driven by the fluid stresses. We establish convergence of finite-energy weak solutions to a strong solution of the corresponding incompressible Euler-rigid body system on its interval of existence. Assuming that the initial relative energy tends to zero, convergence holds under a Kato-type condition in a boundary layer whose thickness is proportional to the viscosity. This condition combines vanishing viscous dissipation with a weighted estimate on the fluid momentum relative to the rigid body motion. The proof uses the relative entropy method and a boundary layer corrector adapted to the fluid-rigid body coupling, providing a sufficient condition for convergence in relative energy as the Mach number and viscosity tend to zero simultaneously.

papers.title: Pentagon Equation in Deformation Quantization of Character Varieties
papers.abstract: Deformation quantizations of the moduli space of framed flat bundles live naturally in the Drinfeld category. Such quantizations were constructed using the so-called quantum fusion by Li-Bland and \v{S}evera. We give a complete characterization of the dependence of this quantization on combinatorial choices, and prove that these quantizations are all isomorphic, forming vertices of an explicitly constructed complete commuting graph of algebra isomorphism. To this end, we extend the Kontsevich integral methods of Le and Murakami from even associators to all associators. Finally, we also prove that bi-invariant Haar measures provide traces on these quantizations.

papers.title: Geometry of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra
papers.authors: A. V. Petukhov, M. D. Sulimov
papers.abstract: We give a geometric description of the formal local data of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra, the algebra of differential operators in one variable. The exponential part of the associated formal meromorphic connection is encoded by a truncated jet of an affine plane curve at infinity, and the regular part by a regular formal meromorphic connection. We prove that these geometric data uniquely determine the `elementary' blocks in the formal decomposition of holonomic modules. The resulting correspondence is equivariant under automorphisms of the first Weyl algebra, including the Fourier transform.

papers.title: The divergence of continuously differentiable vector fields
papers.abstract: For $m\geq 2$, we give a complete characterisation of the continuous functions on $\mathbb{R}^m$ that are divergences of continuously differentiable vector fields. The characterisation is formulated in terms of distributions and, equivalently, in terms of the continuous dual of a suitably topologised subspace of the Arens--Eells space. The two implications yield contrasting applications. First, there exists a compactly supported continuous function which is the divergence of a bounded Lipschitz vector field but not of any continuously differentiable vector field. Second, every continuous function whose distributional partial derivatives are locally $m$-integrable (the critical exponent for Sobolev embedding) is the divergence of a continuously differentiable vector field.

papers.title: The Formal Critical Coupling of the Four-Dimensional Anderson Model
papers.abstract:
In this work we present a formal renormalization-group (RG) calculation for the weakly coupled four-dimensional elliptic Anderson model. Under a scale-independent bare-coupling convention, and with the normalization $\lambda_{\varepsilon}$, the bubble-chain resummation yields the geometric series $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(\lambda)$, with a formal pole at $\lambda_c$. We stress that this pole is a feature of the formal bare bubble series. The argument combines Bogoliubov-Parasiuk-Hepp-Zimmermann (BPHZ) renormalization, a Hepp-sector motivated restriction to the bubble-chain subclass for explicit resummation, and an explicit summation of the resulting geometric series.
  Numerically, we illustrate the analytic building blocks of the formal expansion: the massive Green function, the bubble integral, the geometric resummation, the extraction of the formal pole from synthetic noisy data, a kurtosis diagnostic, and a phase diagram of the formal variance. These computations visualize the deterministic kernels and the formal resummation used above. Using spectral methods and nonlinear least-squares fitting, we verify the short-distance asymptotic behaviour of the massive Green function for $G=(1-\Delta)^{-1}\delta_0$, reproduce the logarithmic divergence of the bubble integral in four dimensions, compute the formal effective variance $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(\lambda)$ arising from the bubble-chain resummation, locate the formal pole at $\lambda_c$, and draw a schematic phase diagram of the formal variance in the $(\lambda,\log\varepsilon)$ plane. The kurtosis diagnostic uses a synthetic proxy for the non-Gaussian regime; the sharp change is imposed by construction. Nonlinear fitting of synthetic data recovers the formal pole within the statistical uncertainty of the synthetic noise. Our results illustrate the analytic formulas and the fitting procedure.

papers.title: Periodic data conjugacy for diffeomorphism cocycles
papers.abstract: We consider H\"older continuous cocycles over a hyperbolic dynamical system with values in the group of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold. We focus on establishing conjugacy between two cocycles from conjugacy of their periodic data. We obtain such a result under bunching, or domination, assumption on the cocycles and a mild regularity assumption in $C^0$ topology on the maps conjugating the periodic data. We also obtain conjugacy to a constant cocycle assuming boundedness in $C^1$ or pre-compactness in $C^0$ for the constant cocycle and the conjugating maps.

papers.title: Poisson closures and Poisson $A$-algebras
papers.authors: Amir Fern\'andez Ouaridi, Salvatore Siciliano, David A. Towers
papers.abstract: We study the interaction between the Lie and Poisson subalgebras of a Poisson algebra. Given a Lie subalgebra $U$ of the underlying Lie algebra $\mathcal P_L$, we consider the Poisson subalgebra generated by $U$, called its {Poisson closure}, and investigate when Lie-theoretic properties such as nilpotency and solvability are preserved under this construction. We also study the stability under Poisson closure of several distinguished Lie subalgebras, including maximal nilpotent and solvable subalgebras, Engel and Cartan subalgebras and the derived algebra. As an application, we investigate Poisson $A$-algebras, defined by the condition that every nilpotent subalgebra is a zero algebra. In the finite-dimensional case, we obtain structural results relating Poisson $A$-algebras to Lie $A$-algebras and to the associative structure of the algebra.

papers.title: The Schur positivity of Lucas binomial differences
papers.authors: Lilan Dai, Dun Qiu, Weichen Wang, Minhao Zhang
papers.abstract: For positive integers $a\le b\le c\le d$ with $ad=bc$, we prove that the Lucas binomial coefficients satisfy $(-1)^{a+1}(L_{b,c}[X]-L_{a,d}[X])\in\mathbb{N}[e_1[X],e_2[X],h_2[X]]$, resolving Bergeron's conjecture on Schur positivity in two variables. We also prove the same positivity for $L_{u,v}[X]-e_1[X]^{uv-rs}L_{r,s}[X]$ when $rs<uv$. Using Lucas atoms, we establish $e$-positivity for degree-adjusted Lucas multinomial differences under dominance order.

papers.title: Finite determinacy and rigidity of quiver potentials
papers.abstract: We prove that a quiver potential over a field of characteristic zero is finitely determined if and only if the trace space of its Jacobian algebra is finite dimensional. In particular, Jacobi-finite potentials are finitely determined. We further prove that rigid potentials are finitely determined and, over an algebraically closed field, unique up to right equivalence on a fixed quiver. For finitely determined weighted-homogeneous potentials, we give an explicit bound on the jet order sufficient for finite determinacy in terms of the arrow weights, the weight of the potential, and the highest nonzero weight of the trace space of its Jacobian algebra. We also establish new invariance results for weighted-homogeneous potentials under right equivalence.

papers.title: Extremal Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities
papers.abstract: We study the boundedness of extremal 2D Trudinger-Moser inequality associated with many point vortices with multi-intensities. Sufficient conditions for continuously-distributed measures are given in one-sided and two-sided cases.

papers.title: Acceleration of the BSS Algorithm
papers.abstract: Bartel, Sch\"{a}fer and Ullrich investigated the BSS subsampling algorithm, which is based on the work by Batson, Spielman and Srivastava. While this algorithm works well, the bottleneck is its complexity of $\mathcal{O}(\sigma^2nm^3)$ for a frame of $n$ vectors of dimension $m$ and oversampling $\sigma^2$. We continue their work by showing that the algorithm can be implemented in $\mathcal{O}(\sigma^2nm^{2.5})$. Moreover, for some special cases, an even faster implementation is possible. In particular, BSS subsampling of Fourier-type frames on a full frequency cube can be implemented in essentially $\mathcal{O}(\sigma^2m^2(n+m^{1.5}))$.}

papers.title: Differentiability and Convexity of the Solution Maps for Fully Non-linear Parabolic HJB Equations
papers.authors: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Chassagneux, St\'ephane Cr\'epey, Gr\'egoire Loeper, Justin Ruelland
papers.abstract: We study the dependence on the terminal condition of solutions to a fully nonlinear parabolic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation, when the terminal condition varies along a finite-dimensional family. This problem is motivated by a dual formulation of semimartingale optimal transport. The equation is posed as a terminal-value Cauchy problem on an unbounded spatial domain. Under structural ellipticity and regularity assumptions on the nonlinear operator, we recall local parabolic H\"older estimates and stability results for bounded uniformly continuous terminal data. We then establish continuous directional differentiability of the solution map with respect to the finite-dimensional parameter, and identify its derivative through the corresponding linearized Cauchy problem. Under an additional convexity assumption on the Hamiltonian and a non-degeneracy condition on the terminal data, we prove local strong convexity of the point-evaluated solution map. The analysis relies on Evans--Krylov theory for fully nonlinear parabolic equations and combines PDE arguments with probabilistic representations. Finally, we extend the differentiability and convexity results to cascades of Cauchy problems in which successive equations are coupled through terminal conditions at several prescribed times. This structure is motivated, for instance, by optimal transport problems with marginal constraints imposed at several maturities.

papers.title: A Mathematical Murmuration
papers.abstract: We give a summary of a large group activity presented to primary school children as part of a STEAM (STEM plus The Arts) event. We describe the routine we demonstrated, this was based upon the tutting dance form, and the murmuration of starlings. Indeed, this demonstrates movement/dance as both a viable and engaging form of teaching mathematics.

papers.title: Minimax Rates for Conditional Generative Learning under Wasserstein Loss
papers.authors: Sungwon Park, Kyoung-Sook Moon, Hongjoong Kim
papers.abstract: We study minimax rates for conditional generative learning under integrated Wasserstein loss, with H\"older continuous conditional laws and an unrestricted covariate distribution. We evaluate unrestricted generators through their conditional output distributions. For expected Wasserstein loss, the minimax rate agrees with the rate under uniform covariates and follows from balancing localization bias against unconditional distribution estimation error. Higher moments of the loss can instead be dominated by unobserved covariate regions, which force an additional risk contribution of order $n^{-1}$, where $n$ is the sample size. An adaptive localization argument gives matching upper bounds. The results cover unrestricted response laws and possibly vanishing Besov densities for $W_1$, and extend to higher Wasserstein orders under uniform response density bounds and integrability conditions. A multiscale lower bound closes the logarithmic gap in unconditional $W_1$ minimax rates in dimension two for both unrestricted distributions and Besov density classes. We also establish minimax rates for conditional Brenier maps under density, integrability, and uniform curvature conditions.

papers.title: Survey on Favard length and rectifiability
papers.abstract: We overview recent results quantifying the Besicovitch projection theorem, focusing on the theory of quantitative rectifiability and connection to Vitushkin's conjecture.

papers.title: Constraint Learning by Optimizing over Trained Neural Networks: A Pragmatic Tutorial
papers.abstract: Constraint learning is an emerging paradigm of modeling optimization problems with the help of machine learning. In this paradigm, trained machine learning models are embedded into the optimization model. For example, we can learn constraints empirically from available data, or we can avoid using a nonlinear objective function by learning a simpler approximation for it. Neural networks become a compelling option if the machine learning models must capture more elaborate and nuanced relationships. However, optimization models embedding neural networks may become too large or too slow to solve. In this tutorial, we present practical considerations for an effective and efficient use of constraint learning with neural networks and validate it with a case study highlighting the benefit of smaller and sparser networks.

papers.title: Symplectic singularity as hyperK\"ahler cone
papers.abstract: We prove that any symplectic singularity has a structure of hyperK\"ahler cone. In particular, it is equivalent to the vertex of a conical symplectic variety, and it is automatically K-polystable.

papers.title: Existence of a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations enjoying the energy equality
papers.abstract: To date, a Leray's weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations enjoys an energy inequality. We prove the existence of a weak solution that enjoys the energy equality. The existence of the weak solution is achieved as limit of solutions to the mollified Navier-Stokes system (Leray's approach). Since no uniqueness result is known for weak solutions we are not able to claim that any weak solution in the sense of Leray-Hopf enjoys the energy equality.

papers.title: Periodic measures for time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations driven by multiplicative $\alpha$-stable processes: Existence, uniqueness and numerical approximation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the periodic measures within the context of time-inhomogeneous Markov processes. By extending the Hairer--Mattingly method to the time-inhomogeneous case, we first establish the existence, uniqueness and exponential ergodicity of periodic measures for general time-periodic Markov processes. These results are subsequently applied to time-inhomogeneous stochastic differential equations under the assumption that the drift is weakly dissipative and locally Lipschitz. We further employ the truncated Euler--Maruyama scheme to study numerical approximations of the periodic measures and derive the convergence rate between the exact and discrete periodic measures. These numerical results are new even in the time-homogeneous case under the assumptions considered in this paper.

papers.title: On generators and relations for $O_n^\circ(V)$ in higher-level Zhu algebras, Part II
papers.abstract:
We study circle relations in the higher-level Zhu algebra of a vertex operator algebra $V$. For regular vacuum words in homogeneous letters, we prove the termwise correction-residue conjecture of Part I: every correction in the one-sided iterate expansion belongs separately to the finite-length plus subspace. The first correction formed with the left truncated field vanishes identically. Multiplying the diagonal commutator kernel by a power of $1+x$ turns it into a Laurent polynomial. This proves the vanishing and writes every other correction as a finite combination of product residues with fewer $Y_L$ factors, coming from the word obtained by replacing one negative mode by a nonnegative one. These results hold at all levels $n\ge0$, without an auxiliary-degree hypothesis.
  For $n\ge1$ and a homogeneous ordered pair $(u,v)$, two explicit triangular families span the quadratic residue operators modulo the length-one and singular-iterate relations, giving $\dim\mathcal{Q}_n((u,v))\le n(n+1)$. The universal product-coefficient arrays have dimension exactly $n(n+1)$ and three natural bases; restriction to the regular mode square is an isomorphism. This proves operator spanning and gives invertible matrices for two complementary diagonal eliminations. For equal inputs, mode interchange reduces the families to their odd-indexed members, giving $\dim\mathcal{Q}_n((u,u))\le 2\lfloor (n+1)^2/4\rfloor$. The pairwise estimates give an explicit global quadratic bound for any finite homogeneous strong generating set. Heisenberg, Virasoro, and affine $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ examples illustrate equality and strict inequality in the operator bounds.

papers.title: Local Algebraic Stability of Wasserstein Gradient Descent-Ascent and Mean Field Langevin Dynamics without Spectral Gap
papers.abstract: We study the local stability of Wasserstein gradient descent-ascent (GDA) for entropy regularized two-player zero-sum games on noncompact domains. When one or both equilibrium measures fail to satisfy a Poincar\'e inequality, the spectral gap arguments underlying local exponential convergence are unavailable. we show that Wasserstein GDA converges algebraically to the mixed Nash equilibrium in chi-squared divergence, provided the initial relative density is a small perturbation in $L^2$ with bounded algebraic moments. The proof has two main ingredients: a cancellation in a negative Sobolev energy estimate, and a bootstrap argument that keeps the moments bounded uniformly in time. For polynomial-tailed equilibria, we construct perturbations supported far out in the tails that survive over diffusive time scales, which gives algebraic lower bounds on the worst-case relaxation rate. We also establish analogous local algebraic stability and lower bound results for mean-field Langevin dynamics, when the equilibrium fails to satisfy a spectral gap.

papers.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
papers.abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.

papers.title: 2-generation of Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields
papers.authors: Ram Karan Choudhary, Harish Kishnani, Anupam Singh
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that every split simple Chevalley Lie algebra over a finite field of characteristic $p\neq 2$ of classical types $B_n$, $C_n$, and $D_n$, and exceptional types $G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, is $2$-generated. Combined with the result of Cantor, Jezernik, and Zozaya for the classical type $A_n$ [Two-generation of traceless matrices over finite fields, Linear Algebra Appl. (2025)], this establishes $2$-generation for all split simple Chevalley Lie algebras over finite fields of characteristic $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: Berry--Esseen bounds for stochastic approximation with Markovian noise
papers.authors: Zhijun Cai, YUjie Qin, Zhuosong Zhang
papers.abstract: This paper studies the convergence rate of the Polyak-Ruppert average estimator in one-dimensional linear stochastic approximation recursion driven by Markov chains, allowing the Markov chain to start from any initial distribution. Under the conditions of positive Harris recurrence, non-periodicity, and one-step domination, combined with the fourth-moment condition of the coefficient function with respect to the stationary distribution, this paper uses the exchangeable pair technique to prove that after deterministic bias correction for the average estimator, a Berry--Esseen bound of order $n^{-\alpha/2}$ can be obtained, where the step size exponent is $\alpha \in (1/2, 1)$. Moreover, for the statistics without bias correction and after variance normalization, the asymptotic normal approximation error is asymptotically equivalent to a normal constant multiplied by $n^{1/2 - \alpha}$.

papers.title: On the number of pioneers in high-dimensional critical percolation
papers.abstract: We prove that for critical percolation in high dimension the expected number of pioneers on any set containing the origin is of the same order as the probability that a simple random walk starting from the origin exits the set. Our proof works in all dimensions $d>6$, under the usual assumption that the two-point function is of the same order as the Green's function. As an application we obtain a sharp uniform quantitative bound on the probability that the cluster of the origin intersects any given ball.

papers.title: Pure Type-One Generalized Hypercomplex Structures in Dimension Four
papers.abstract: We classify untwisted generalized hypercomplex structures on four-manifolds whose entire sphere has type one. The three Poisson tensors determine a canonical line field, and the local data are Gauduchon--Tod coframes. We determine local equivalence under diffeomorphisms, common closed real $B$-fields and constant rotations of the triple. On a closed manifold the canonical foliation is automatically Riemannian: a nonzero period obstructs the exact twist required by the non-Riemannian models. The compact structures form four families, distinguished by $b_1=1,2,3,4$: Berger quotients, flat axis quotients, nontrivial circle bundles over flat three-tori, and constant tori. We determine their parameters, equivalences and finite ordered quotients, including nonorientable canonical lines. The underlying manifolds are parallelizable, satisfy $b_2=2b_1-2$, and are symplectic exactly when the intrinsic Gauduchon--Tod invariant vanishes. A twisted Hopf example shows why the untwisted hypothesis is essential. The classification is intrinsic and assumes no initial circle action. These results address the four-dimensional untwisted case of the intermediate-type question of Fino and Grantcharov.

papers.title: On Hecke algebras at exceptional Eisenstein primes
papers.abstract: We study the structure over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of the Hecke algebra acting on ordinary cusp forms in the Eisenstein, non-$p$-distinguished case. Our results and methods draw on four complementary approaches: deformation theory, through $R=\mathbf{T}$ theorems; Iwasawa theory, through connections to Sharifi's conjecture; $p$-adic $L$-functions, through an exceptional zero formula; and computational experiments using Magma. We also obtain new results regarding the Coleman--Greenberg conjecture.

papers.title: Cutoff for random walks on nilpotent groups
papers.authors: Jonathan Hermon, Xiangying Huang, Justin Salez
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time random walks on finite nilpotent groups, allowing non-symmetric and nonuniform increment measures. Under a simple degree condition, sharp up to an absolute constant factor, we prove that total variation cutoff occurs if and only if the relaxation time is of smaller order than the mixing time. We establish a quantitative reduction to the Abelianization that preserves relaxation times and compares mixing profiles. Combining this reduction with a Gaussian approximation and the third-named author's cutoff criterion for diffusions yields the cutoff characterization.

papers.title: A Liouville Theorem for the Real k-Hessian Equation with a One-Sided Growth Condition
papers.abstract:
We establish a scale-invariant interior $C^2$ estimate for smooth solutions of the real $k$-Hessian equation. As an application, we prove that every smooth entire solution of $\sigma_k(D^2u)=1$ satisfying $u(x)\ge b|x|^2-B$ for some constants $b,B$ with $b>0$ is a quadratic polynomial. For smooth solutions, admissibility is forced by the growth condition.
  The results also hold for viscosity solutions and for weak solutions in Trudinger's sense. Admissibility is required in the latter case.

papers.title: Higher Spherical Scissors Congruence II: Comodules
papers.authors: Inbar Klang, Josefien Kuijper, Cary Malkiewich, David Mehrle, Thor Wittich
papers.abstract: We define the higher Dehn invariant on the Euclidean, hyperbolic, and spherical variants of scissors congruence $K$-theory, and prove that it makes these spectra into comodules over the spectral Sah algebra. This allows us to make the first formulation of the conjecture that the higher volume and Dehn invariants are jointly injective.

papers.title: ADACT: PDE-Constrained Thermal Hardware/Software Co-Design Adjoint-Driven Optimal Control via Finite Difference Discretization
papers.abstract: By virtue of the sheer compute demands of large-scale artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC), modern multi-core microprocessors suffer from severe power density limits and thermal throttling, entailing an urgent need for principled methods for predictive, physics-informed dynamical thermal management (DTM). Here, we introduce a hardware/software co-design physics-informed PDE-constrained DTM throttling optimal control algorithm, ADACT (Adjoint-Driven Adaptive Co-Design Thermal Control), that minimizes thermal risk and cooling energy overhead while maximizing core execution throughput. The underlying physical temperature field is governed by a two-dimensional nonhomogeneous parabolic reaction-diffusion equation with spatially localized, time-varying power source terms and variable convective cooling subject to nonhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. We employ a discretization of the continuous state PDE via a Crank-Nicolson finite difference scheme with a 5-point discrete Laplacian operator on a uniform spatial mesh, which preserves unconditional numerical stability and $O(\Delta x^2 + \Delta y^2 + \Delta t^2)$ second-order temporal and spatial accuracy. To efficiently compute exact gradients, we construct and implement a continuous backward-in-time adjoint state method with L-BFGS as our optimization algorithm of choice. The accuracy and second-order convergence rates of both forward state and backward adjoint solvers are quantitatively verified via the Method of Manufactured Solutions (MMS), and gradient accuracy is validated using directional derivative Taylor tests. Numerical experiments demonstrate that ADACT dynamically throttles software power workloads and modulates hardware cooling efforts to strictly uphold physical thermal thresholds while maintaining operational throughput.

papers.title: Gradient estimates and Liouville theorems for exponentially harmonic functions
papers.abstract: We study exponentially harmonic functions on complete Riemannian manifolds. Under a lower Ricci curvature bound \(\Ric_g\geq-Kg\), we first establish a local gradient estimate in terms of the oscillation. We then prove a pointwise gradient estimate for solutions bounded from one side. As an application, when \(\Ric_g\geq0\), we obtain a Liouville theorem under a one-sided sublinear growth condition. In particular, every exponentially harmonic function bounded above or below is constant.

papers.title: Grothendieck rings of near-Tambara--Yamagami fusion categories
papers.authors: Jingcheng Dong, S\'ebastien Palcoux, Kai Wang
papers.abstract: We determine the Grothendieck rings of fusion categories over $\mathcal{C}$ containing a nonpointed Tambara--Yamagami fusion subcategory and exactly one further simple object. The subcategory necessarily has rank five, its invertible objects form the Klein four-group, and the coefficient $\kappa$ of the additional simple object in its tensor square belongs to $\{0,2,7\}$. Each of these three based rings is categorifiable. For $\kappa=0$, every category belongs, up to tensor equivalence, to the rank-one odd-component extension list of Choi--Lu--Sun. For $\kappa=2$ we construct an explicit unitary group-theoretical realization, and for $\kappa=7$ a realization is $\rm{Rep}(\rm{PSU}(3,2))$.

papers.title: Sharp Norm Approximation of Covering Markov Operators
papers.abstract:
We study the operator-norm approximation of Markov operators associated with finite graph coverings. Let $q:Y\to X$ be a connected covering of degree $d\geq 2$ between finite connected graphs, and let $A_q:C(Y)\to C(X)$ be its fiber-averaging operator. We show that $A_q$ is not a finite convex combination of extreme Markov operators, although such combinations approximate $A_q$ arbitrarily well in operator norm.
  We determine the exact distances from $A_q$ to convex combinations of at most $m$ extreme Markov operators, with arbitrary or equal convex weights. If $m=kd+r$, where $k\geq 0$ and $1\leq r\leq d$, these distances are
  $2(d-r+1)/[d(k(d-r+1)+1)]$
  and
  $2r(d-r+1)/(dm)$,
  respectively. Both distances are attained and depend only on the covering degree $d$ and the number of terms $m$. We also determine when equal weights are optimal and quantify the additional approximation error when they are not. Our proofs use total-variation estimates and continuous rearrangements of labelled weighted atoms. In particular, the unrestricted errors have a common scaled limit, while the equal-weight errors exhibit residue-dependent asymptotic behavior.

papers.title: Computing ${}_{q+1}{F}_q$ via rational conformal maps
papers.abstract: It is well-known that certain M\"obius (linear fractional) transformations provide analytic continuation of the Gauss hypergeometric function. These transformations work by exchanging the roles of the three regular singular points and $0$, $1$, and $\infty$ of the Gauss hypergeometric differential equation. Not one of these transformations, however, brings the points $e^{\pm{\rm i}\pi/3}$ closer to the origin, and convergence in a neighbourhood of these is also troublesome. In this work, we produce a Maclaurin series in optimal complexity after rational conformal mapping that induces pointwise convergence to any ${}_{q+1}F_q$ throughout the cut complex plane $\mathbb{C}\setminus[1,\infty)$. We show that for the optimal parameter values this series converges faster than an approximate mapped Chebyshev series obtained by the ultraspherical spectral method.

papers.title: Finite-step projective dynamics of Schr\"odinger cocycles: non-degeneracy, regularity, and rigidity
papers.abstract:
We study the no deterministic images condition (NDI) for Schr\"odinger cocycles, which excludes a common image of a fixed probability measure under almost all projective transfer transformations. We prove two-step NDI at every energy for nonconstant measurable potentials over mixing systems and ergodic potentials with infinite essential range, and classify persistence for finite-state locally constant potentials. For bounded Markov and hidden Markov potentials on general state spaces under a one-step $L^2$ norm gap condition on the Markov operator, we prove H\"older bounds for solution-direction distributions above an exponential cutoff and H\"older conditional stationary measures. Counterexamples show the essential sharpness of both assumptions.
  For nonconstant real trigonometric potentials, including the almost Mathieu operator, we prove NDI and H\"older bounds for distributions of solution directions at all steps $k\ge2$ and all frequencies (rational or irrational). The exponent depends on the step, while the constant is uniform in steps, frequency and energy on compact intervals. For every irrational frequency and every energy with positive Lyapunov exponent, we prove non-atomicity of both Oseledets direction distributions and convergence to the unstable distribution from every phase-independent initial probability. This gives a new criterion for a zero Lyapunov exponent: a subsequential limit with an atom for one fixed initial direction suffices. All these results extend to an analytic class, with step-dependent regularity bounds.

papers.title: Boundedness and continuity of phase-corrected gradients on Sobolev spaces
papers.authors: Lars Eric Hientzsch, Raffaele Scandone, Robert Wegner
papers.abstract:
For a function $\psi: \mathbb{R}^d ightarrow \mathbb{C}$, we define the phase-corrected gradient $
abla_{\!\circ} \psi = |\psi|^{-1} \overline{\psi}\,
abla\psi$ and study the regularity of the map $\psi \mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} \psi$ on Sobolev spaces. Since $\mathrm{Re}[
abla_{\!\circ} \psi] = 
abla |\psi|$, the phase-corrected gradient fits naturally into the framework of nonlinear composition operators. Its imaginary part $\Lambda = \mathrm{Im}[
abla_{\!\circ} \psi]$, on the other hand, plays a key role in quantum hydrodynamic models. We prove that $\psi \mapsto 
abla_{\!\circ} \psi$ is bounded and continuous from $W^{s,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $W^{s-1,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1 \leq s <  rac32$, and we show that the threshold $s =  rac32$ is sharp. In particular, this answers an open question concerning the continuity of the map $\psi \mapsto |\psi|$ on Sobolev spaces. We also show that our results remain valid for functions that do not necessarily decay at infinity, a relevant setting in the context of Ginzburg--Landau theory. Finally, we extend our analysis to more general phase-corrected gradients of the form $f(|\psi|^{-1} \psi) 
abla \psi$, where $f: \mathbb{S}^1 ightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is Lipschitz, and discuss implications for certain parabolic PDEs.

papers.title: Positivity of Relative Pluricanonical Direct Images via Fixed-Point Metrics
papers.abstract: We develop a direct analytic approach to positivity of relative pluricanonical direct images through a fixed-point Hermitian metric by direct differential curvature calculations. The curvature resolvent formula from fixed-point equation leads to two-sided estimates of entire Nakano curvature by determinant curvature. In this way, we identify generic rank of determinant curvature with birational variation dimension for a projective algebraic fibration between smooth connected projective varieties with general fiber of general type and maximal birational variation, assuming $mK_F$ is globally generated or the $m$-canonical map is birational for general fiber $F$. In the global generation case, Green--Griffiths Conjecture asks for the tautological bigness of the ordinary symmetric powers $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}f_*\omega_{X/Y}^{\otimes m}$, without passing to reflexive hulls, for $\ell\geq P_m(F)=h^0(F,mK_F)$ whenever $m\geq 1$. We prove it for all $\ell\geq1$ at levels $m\geq 2$, also in the case of birational $m$-canonical map, but construct a counterexample at level $m=1$. Over curves, curvature and boundary estimates give a direct analytic proof of Viehweg's ampleness theorem requested by Fujino. For smooth projective families, we also establish numerical dimension and vanishing results related to the birational variation dimension.

papers.title: Curvature-induced fracture mode coupling in doubly curved shells
papers.authors: Riccardo Brambilla, Siddhant Kumar, Bianca Giovanardi
papers.abstract: Classical shell fracture theories predominantly consider cracks aligned with principal curvature directions in cylindrical and spherical shells under tensile mode or pressure loading, leaving the fracture behavior of arbitrarily oriented cracks in doubly curved shells under general loading poorly understood. Here, we introduce a semi-analytical framework based on Reissner shallow-shell theory to investigate isotropic shells with positive, zero, and negative Gaussian curvature. The formulation computes stress intensity factors, energy release rates, and crack-lip displacements for arbitrarily inclined through-thickness cracks in spheres, ellipsoids, cylinders, hyperboloids, and minimal surfaces under general mechanical loading. We show that shell curvature couples opening, sliding, and tearing, allowing a single loading component to activate multiple fracture modes, unlike in flat plates. This coupling depends strongly on crack orientation and the normal, parallel, and torsional components of the shell curvature. Ellipsoids exhibit weak coupling, hyperboloids generally exhibit the strongest coupling, and cylinders display the most complex orientation-dependent responses. Moreover, in-plane shear can induce crack closure in hyperboloidal shells, suggesting a potential geometric mechanism for enhanced damage resistance. These findings elucidate the role of local curvature in fracture-mode coupling and provide a mechanistic foundation for the analysis of shellular (meta-)structures with engineered curvature distributions.

papers.title: Extending the V-sequence reduction to arbitrary independent distributions
papers.abstract: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent random variables with arbitrary known distributions, where $n\ge2$. The optimal probability $V_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ of choosing an overall maximum satisfies $V_n(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\ge(1-1/n)^{n-1}$, and this bound is attained. We obtain this known sharp bound by extending the reduction lemma of Allaart and Islas (2016) from continuous to arbitrary distributions. We construct a $V$-sequence whose optimal win probability does not exceed that of the original sequence, and then apply the bound for $V$-sequences. The construction first replaces atoms by uniform observations on strictly ordered intervals and applies the original continuous reduction lemma. The reduced distributions are determined by a common critical level and a common probability for splitting a possible atom at that level.

papers.title: Modular representations of metabelian groups
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a module over a commutative ring with unity $R$, and let $\phi:M \to R$ be an $R$-linear map. Then the product $mn = m + (1+\phi(m))n$ defines a monoid $Mon(\phi)$ on $M$. We show that if $G$ is a group, then $G$ arises as the group of invertible elements of some such monoid $Mon(\phi)$ if and only if $G$ is metabelian.

papers.title: Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves II: Smooth bounded domains
papers.abstract: Continuing \cite{NWX} and Part I \cite{AOSI}, we further investigate symmetry for spacetime observability of wave equations. Building on asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) introduced in \cite{AOSI}, we study symmetry under glancing propagation and caustics. We prove that, on every smooth bounded domain in $\R^2$ and for every positive observation time, there is a fixed measurable set satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition. However, the observability inequality fails on this set.

papers.title: Counting transversals in Latin squares over groups of even order
papers.authors: James A. Davis, Jonathan Jedwab, Ian M. Wanless, Amy Wiebe
papers.abstract: The number of transversals in a Latin square $L(G)$ whose rows and columns are indexed by a finite group $G$ has been determined computationally for all $G$ of order at most $23$ and for $C_{25}$. However, computation of the number of transversals of $L(G)$ has until now been considered intractable for all non-cyclic groups $G$ of order $32$. We show, for a group $G$ containing an order $2$ normal subgroup $N$, that the image of a transversal in $L(G)$ under the quotient mapping from $G$ to $G/N$ is a $2$-plex in $L(G/N)$. We then derive linear algebraic conditions that determine the number of transversals in $L(G)$ whose image under the quotient mapping is a given $2$-plex in $L(G/N)$. This allows us to count transversals in $L(G)$ by examining all $2$-plexes in $L(G/N)$. Although we can simplify the counting of $2$-plexes in $L(G/N)$ by taking advantage of their symmetry group, the linear algebraic conditions can vary over a symmetry class of $2$-plexes. However, in the case that $G$ takes the splitting form $C_2 \times H$, the linear algebraic conditions become invariant over each symmetry class and so the counting of transversals in $L(C_2 \times H)$ reduces to counting the $2$-plexes in $L(H)$ under the action of their symmetry group. We illustrate the power of these techniques by computing the exact number of transversals in $L(C_2^5)$.

papers.title: On Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges of compact adjoint orbits
papers.abstract: We settle Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges associated with compact adjoint orbits of complex reductive Lie algebras, including its original formulation in terms of the inner product $B_\theta$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let $K$ be a connected compact Lie group whose Lie algebra is a compact real form of $\mathfrak{g}$. For any $x\in\mathfrak{g}$ and any complex linear functional $f\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, we prove that $\{ f( \operatorname{Ad} (k) x): k \in K \}$ is star-shaped about zero. In the reductive case, the star center is given by the value of $f$ on the central component of $x$, which coincides with the $B_\theta$-pairing of the central components in Tam's original formulation. Our proof is uniform for all complex semisimple Lie algebras. Indeed, using the adjoint Casimir operator, we show that all coordinate functions of the orbit map share a common Laplace eigenvalue; we then use a nodal-hypersurface argument to prove star-shapedness for complex-valued functions in a single eigenspace. The geometric argument relies on a two-sided hypersurface-separation property, which holds whenever the first real cohomology group vanishes. In particular, we do not need simple connectivity or real analyticity. More generally, for finite-dimensional representations of compact connected semisimple Lie groups, we establish star-shapedness whenever the nonfixed component of the orbit vector belongs to a single positive Casimir eigenspace.

papers.title: Graph-Convolutional Reinforcement Learning for Finite-Time Stabilization of a Chaotic Chua Circuit via Unified Flexible Terminal Sliding-Mode Control
papers.authors: Hooman Fatoorehchi, Majid Roohi, Rasmus Kold, Matthias Ehrhardt, Andreas Basse-O'Connor, Sebastian Nis Bay Villadsen, Philip L. Fosb{\o}l
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a graph convolutional reinforcement learning framework for the finite-time stabilization of chaotic dynamics in a physical Chua circuit. The circuit is modeled directly in terms of capacitor voltages, inductor current, and physical component parameters. This preserves the connection between the mathematical model and the underlying electrical system. A unified, flexible terminal sliding-mode controller is developed to achieve stabilization within a finite time in the presence of uncertainties in the lumped model, external disturbances, and bounded control inputs. The controller incorporates state-dependent nonlinear exponents to provide flexible convergence characteristics while avoiding singular terms near equilibrium. To minimize dependence on manual controller tuning, the admissible controller parameters are optimized using an actor-critic reinforcement learning scheme with a graph convolutional network that leverages the circuit dynamics' coupling structure. The learned parameters are constrained to the ranges required by the theoretical stability conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the rapid suppression of chaotic oscillations and the finite-time convergence of the state and sliding variables while respecting the prescribed input-saturation limits. Compared to a reference control method, the proposed approach reduces the IAE, ISE, ITAE, and ITSE by 56.27\,\%, 56.40\,\%, 61.69\,\%, and 64.70\,\%, respectively. These results suggest that graph-based reinforcement learning can effectively tune parameters while retaining the robustness and analytical structure of the underlying sliding-mode controller.

papers.title: Generalizing Praeger--Xu graphs
papers.abstract:
We uniformly study directed Praeger--Xu graphs and Praeger's generalized family $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(\Gamma,r,s)$, without requiring that $s\mid r$ and $\Gamma$ is an undirected graph. Assuming that $\Gamma\times\overrightarrow{K}_2$ is connected, we determine the full automorphism group of $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(\Gamma,r,s)$ for every $r$ and $s$, prove connectivity, characterize vertex-transitivity, and give an equivalent criterion for $t$-arc-transitivity. We also study when $\overrightarrow{\operatorname{PX}}(\Gamma,r,s)$ is a Cayley graph.
  We also give two applications. First, we give a new family of twin-free connected arc-transitive digraphs of valency $4$ whose vertex stabilizers have exponential growth. We also give a connected regular digraph that is not vertex-transitive but whose direct product with a directed cycle is Cayley.

papers.title: Local Koopman modes of saddle-point diffusions: exact singular functions and a data-driven estimator
papers.abstract: Coherent sets-regions of phase space that resist mixing-organize transport in stochastic dynamical systems and are encoded in the leading singular functions of the stochastic Koopman operator. These are typically computed numerically and globally; a local, analytic theory near a fixed point has been missing, although fixed points and the transitions between them organize the flow. We supply the local theory for a saddle, the transition state through which probability flows between basins. Naively the construction fails-probability escapes along unstable directions, the invariant measure is non-normalizable, the singular functions leave $L^2$, and singular values exceed one. We show that conditioning on non-escape (a Doob's $h$-transform) repairs this; that the required $h$ is the unique stabilizing solution of an algebraic Riccati equation; and that the resulting slow modes decay at the escape rate along the unstable manifold. We obtain these modes in closed form-products of Hermite polynomials in canonical coordinates times the $h$-function-and use their unitary structure to derive a data-driven estimator: canonical correlation analysis on conditioned trajectories. When a single unstable direction dominates, the leading mode is the reaction coordinate, locally recovering the stable manifold and committor of transition-path theory. The construction connects coherent sets to transition-path theory, to the stabilizing Riccati solution of linear control, and to the time-reversed dynamics of generative diffusion models.

papers.title: Efficient ADMM for Soft-Constrained Quadratic Programs via Generalized Slack Projections
papers.authors: Roland Schwan, Thomas Lew, Brian Plancher
papers.abstract: Quadratic programs (QPs) are a core building block in many applications. In practice, constraints are often softened with slack variables to guarantee feasibility. The standard approach tackles this by introducing additional decision variables, growing the resulting optimization problem. In this paper, we propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) scheme for a broad class of convex slack penalty functions, including all $\ell_k$-norms, without increasing the problem size. The only change to the ADMM scheme is a modified slack projection function, while the remaining algorithm stays the same. We demonstrate our approach on numerical examples, showing significant speedups, and show its flexibility on an energy optimization problem.

papers.title: On the Hasse principle for a block-diagonal form and a form of lower degree
papers.abstract: We investigate the Hasse principle for systems consisting of one form of degree $k$ which decomposes as a sum of $n$-ary forms, and one general form of degree $d < k$. By exploiting the block structure of the first form before applying Weyl differencing, we refine the method of Brandes and Parsell (arXiv:2003.04350) in this setting; in particular, for a sum of binary quartic forms and a quadratic form, the requirement $s > 516$ is relaxed to $s > 96$, which also improves on the bound $s > 100$ available for general forms.

papers.title: Finite groups with exactly 2p + 1 subgroups of order p
papers.abstract: Let m_p(G) be the number of elements of order p in a finite group G, p prime. We prove that there is no finite simple group G with m_p(G) = 2p^2-p-1, and that a finite group with this property exists if and only if 2p+1 is prime or 3^f with f an odd prime. This concerns an open problem and extends the classification of finite groups with few elements of prime order.

papers.title: Relative norm averaging property and selflessness of almost periodic actions
papers.abstract:
Let $D$ be a unital separable $C^*$-algebra with a faithful state $\sigma$ and $G$ be a discrete group. We introduce a property called relative norm averaging property (RNA) for almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving actions by $G$ on $(D,\sigma)$.
  We prove that if an almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action $\alpha$ satisfies that $\overline{\alpha(G)} \subseteq \text{Aut}(D,\sigma)$ is connected and nontrivial, then $\alpha$ satisfies (RNA). As an application, we prove that if $G$ has property PHP of Ozawa and $\alpha:G\curvearrowright (D,\sigma)$ is an ergodic (i.e. $D^G=\mathbb{C}$) almost periodic $\sigma$-preserving action with $\overline{\alpha(G)}$ being connected, then $D\rtimes_r G$ is selfless. This includes certain paradoxical isometric actions of $\mathbb{F}_2$ on the sphere.
  In non-ergodic case, we prove that the relative norm averaging property implies that $D\rtimes_r G$ satisfies the $D^G$-valued selfless, if $G$ satisfies PHP.

papers.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
papers.abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As a consequence, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$.

papers.title: The Riesz representation in submetric spaces and its probabilistic aspects
papers.abstract:
A submetric space is a topological space equipped with a continuous metric that generates a metric topology (usually) weaker than the original one (e.g., a~separable Hilbert space with the weak topology). We show that a positive linear functional on the space of bounded continuous functions on a submetric space is given as an integral with respect to a tight measure if, and only if, it is continuous in the strict topology. Neither local compactness nor complete regularity is required.
  We link the equicontinuity of a family of functionals in the strict topology to the uniform tightness of the underlying measures, and we provide a probabilistic representation (Skorokhod's parametrization) for such families. Finally, we identify the finest topology on the space of probability measures on a submetric space in which uniform tightness implies relative compactness. In non-metric spaces this topology is strictly stronger than the topology of weak convergence of probability measures.

papers.title: Singularity Analysis of Laplace Boundary Integral Equations on Three-Dimensional Domains with Corners
papers.authors: Wenmao Hua, Jun Lai, Baoling Xie, Lu Zhang
papers.abstract: Solutions to elliptic boundary value problems on three-dimensional nonsmooth domains exhibit singular behavior near edges and vertices. Using layer potential theory, we investigate boundary integral equations for the Laplace equation and characterize the leading singular exponents of the surface density on conical domains. For two canonical geometries, we derive explicit formulas for the two families of edge singular exponents on a dihedral wedge, and characterize the modewise vertex singular exponents on an axisymmetric circular cone through the zeros of associated Legendre functions and their derivatives. Building on these two prototypes and the dilation-invariance property, we formulate the associated operator pencil for general conical domains and develop a nonlinear eigenvalue solver. This solver employs the Nystr\"om method with graded meshes, logarithmically corrected trapezoidal rules, and Brent's method to compute these singular exponents accurately and efficiently. Numerical examples for trihedral cones, regular m-hedral cones, and droplet-type cones verify the effectiveness of our approach and illustrate the interactions between edge and vertex singularities.

papers.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
papers.abstract: A string couples to a two-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For global phases, topological and index invariants, and twisted-sheaf moduli, established equivalences give alternative descriptions through cocycles, bundles, operators, or modules, with the required global compatibility data. For three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation expresses the partition function as a sum of partition functions of ordinary finite-group gauge theories. An invertible local substitution reduces invariant classical actions for a class of 2-bundle connections represented by finite-dimensional crossed modules to ordinary gauge and tensor dynamics. These finite and local reductions explicitly eliminate field variables. A four-dimensional quadratic example instead admits a direct cochain evaluation even when an ordinary gauge-theory reduction fails. These results therefore do not require the additional 2-bundle presentation.

papers.title: Projections in reduced group C*-algebras with prescribed trace values in (0,1)
papers.abstract: Building on OpenAI's preprint, we construct, for every real number $r\in(0,1)$, a finitely generated discrete group $G_r$ and a projection $e_r\in C_r^*(G_r)$ whose canonical trace is $r$. The construction encodes the geometry of expanders in the dynamics of a semidirect product of groups. For irrational $r$, the $K$-theory class $[e_r]$ is not in the image of the reduced Baum--Connes map. The groups $G_r$ have torsion and satisfy the maximal strong Novikov conjecture.

papers.title: Supply Chain Information Sharing among Competitors: Profit-Based Participation under Market Shocks
papers.authors: Batuhan Celik, Bahar Cavdar, Jennifer Pazour
papers.abstract: Sharing information can help coordinate supply chain decisions in response to market shocks. Yet, firms must weigh these benefits against the risk of strengthening competitors. We study when competing firms voluntarily join an information-sharing platform to exchange information about market shocks while retaining operational autonomy. Firms differ in information capabilities and decide whether to participate before private signals are realized, creating stochastic information asymmetry. We model participation and quantity decisions as a two-stage dynamic game with incomplete information. For two horizontal competitors, we derive closed-form equilibrium participation strategies that reveal how information power and production efficiency shape participation. Numerical analysis examines more complex supply chain networks. We find that supply chain characteristics impact participation and the level of information asymmetry is a key factor in the equilibrium platform profiles. Firms with similar information power may benefit from joining forces to reduce their competitive disadvantage against higher information power competitors. Cost-inefficient firms may be less willing to participate because their competitors can exploit shared information, and uncertainty can serve as a competitive shield by restricting the actions of more efficient competitors. However, when several competitors join the platform, a cost-inefficient firm may also choose to participate to avoid an informational disadvantage.

papers.title: Sharp volume tests and entropy thresholds for quasilinear elliptic inequalities with gradient reactions
papers.authors: Yongheng Qin, Yuhua Sun, Jie Xiao
papers.abstract: We investigate positive weak solutions of $-\Delta_m u\ge u^p|\nabla u|^q$ on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds without curvature, volume doubling, or Poincar\'e assumptions. For the superhomogeneous mixed reaction we derive a curvature-free integral volume test by combining two first-order estimates with a recurrence for the mass of a \emph{fixed} density. The same approach organizes the pure-gradient and capacity criteria and yields sharp finite hierarchies of iterated-logarithmic growth bounds, with counterexamples on smooth model manifolds. In the subhomogeneous region, vanishing lower growth of $\log V(R)/R^{m-q}$ forces the Liouville property. On the homogeneous line $p+q=m-1$, we obtain the optimal strict lower-volume-entropy threshold $(p+1)((m-1)/p)^{p/(p+1)}$ for $p>0$ (and $1$ for $p=0$), together with examples at equality. The existing six-region classification is not claimed as new; the advances concern refined volume hypotheses and their model sharpness. The tests remain valid for smooth weighted measures and for locally bounded positive Sobolev solutions. Sharpness is understood within the stated model families; no characterization from volume alone on an individual manifold is asserted.

papers.title: Computing Data-Aware Diagonal Frame Decompositions
papers.authors: Andrea Ebner, Dirk Lorenz, Mathias Staudigl
papers.abstract: We present a method for computing a specific type of matrix decomposition that combines a structured framework with data-driven adaptation. This framework allows for an efficient and stable representation of signals or images using frames by identifying sets of vectors that naturally capture the essential features of the given data. The resulting decomposition enables the development of regularization techniques that enhance the quality of reconstruction by preserving important signal characteristics while suppressing noise. We develop an optimization-based algorithm to compute the decomposition and establish convergence properties of the resulting iterates. Numerical experiments on synthetic data and tomographic image reconstruction illustrate the behavior of the proposed method and its performance compared to conventional spectral regularization methods.

papers.title: Unconditional scattering below the ground state for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation
papers.abstract: Unconditional global existence and scattering are established for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical generalized Hartree equation with $0<\alpha<3$, below the ground-state energy and kinetic thresholds. The initial data lie in $\dot H^1$, with no radial symmetry, finite-mass, or finite-variance assumption. Annular frequency estimates and Gaussian interaction estimates rule out a compact critical trajectory by first controlling its nonlinear forcing and then recovering its conserved mass.

papers.title: Degree-list Kempe equivalence for 3-connected graphs
papers.abstract: In a proper coloring, a Kempe change interchanges two colors on a connected component of the subgraph they induce. For a fixed list assignment $L$, a Kempe change is $L$-valid if it transforms an $L$-coloring into another $L$-coloring. We prove that if $G$ is a $3$-connected graph other than a complete graph or the triangular prism, and $L$ is a list assignment with $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)$ for every vertex $v$, then $G$ has a proper $L$-coloring and any two such colorings can be transformed into one another by a finite sequence of $L$-valid Kempe changes. This proves a conjecture of Chakraborty, Feghali and Mahmoud.

papers.title: Curvature quotient flows and Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in hyperbolic space
papers.authors: Tianci Luo, Yong Wei, Ruijia Zhang, Rong Zhou
papers.abstract: We study quermassintegral-preserving curvature flows in $\mathbb H^{n+1}$, $n\geq3$, driven by the curvature quotient $(E_k/E_\ell)^{1/(k-\ell)}$. For $1\leq\ell<k$ with $k+\ell\leq n$, we prove that positive sectional curvature is preserved. Starting from a smooth closed strictly convex hypersurface with positive sectional curvature, the flow exists for all time and converges smoothly and exponentially to a geodesic sphere. As an application, we establish sharp Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities between $W_k$ and $W_\ell$ for smooth bounded convex domains whose boundaries have nonnegative sectional curvature, whenever $0\leq\ell<k\leq n$ and $k+\ell\leq n$. Equality holds if and only if the domain is a geodesic ball. Together with previously known cases, these inequalities give the full family of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for this class of domains in $\mathbb H^6$. We also construct counterexamples showing that $k+\ell\leq n$ is the optimal range for preservation of positive sectional curvature by these flows.

papers.title: Positivity for a $t$-analogue of refined Littlewood-Richardson rules
papers.authors: Jiaming Du, Emma Yu Jin, Xiaowei Lin
papers.abstract:
In 2010, Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg proved that the product of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a Demazure atom $A_{\gamma}$ expands positively in terms of Demazure atoms, and interpreted the coefficients as the number of Littlewood-Richardson skew skyline tableaux of a given shape and a filling type. Extending this approach, they further established the positive expansion for the product of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a quasisymmetric Schur function $S_{\alpha}$, or of a Schur function $s_{\lambda}$ and a Demazure character $\kappa_{\gamma}$. In particular, the latter provides a refinement of the classical Littlewood-Richardson rule.
  We present a natural $t$-analogue of these positive expansions by deriving the expansion for a product of a Hall-Littlewood polynomial $P_{\lambda}(t)$ and a $t$-Demazure atom $E_{\gamma}(t)$ in terms of $t$-Demazure atoms. The corresponding coefficients are $\mathbb{N}\,[t,1-t]$-positive; that is, they are polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients in $t$ and $1-t$, and they are interpreted in terms of standard Young tableaux. We take the approach of connecting the multiplication coefficients with the LLT polynomials, which differs from the combinatorial insertion arguments of Haglund, Luoto, Mason and van Willigenburg.

papers.title: Learning Behavioral Parameters of Network Equilibrium Models from Aggregate Mobility Data
papers.abstract: Estimating travel behavior parameters is essential for understanding current travel patterns and for forecasting how travelers may respond to future changes in transportation systems. However, reliable estimation remains difficult when behavior must be inferred from sparse and aggregate observations, especially when jointly recovering several behavioral components. In this paper, we develop a bi-level estimation program for a combined destination, mode and route choice model with congestion. The inner level is a convex program at given scale parameters, and returns the taste coefficients as its dual variables together with the equilibrium travel pattern. The outer level selects the scale parameters by out-of-sample prediction, measured by how well the modeled travel pattern predicts observations withheld from estimation. To solve the bi-level problem at scale, we propose a matrix-free Hierarchical Lagrangian Dual algorithm as the inner solver and an outer search by implicit differentiation, which uses the sensitivities of the inner solution to enable efficient search over the scale parameters and reaches the calibrated scales in a handful of iterations. We validate the approach on Los Angeles County using public origin-destination, mode-share and traffic-count data. Our approach scales to a county-level problem with 2.7 million variables and substantially improves computational efficiency over a general-purpose conic solver. Compared with the fixed-scale benchmark, the calibrated model improves predictive performance at the destination and mode levels, with consistent gains across complementary goodness-of-fit measures.

papers.title: Characterizations of the unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$ among minimal systems
papers.authors: Miguel Berasategui, Pablo M. Bern\'a, Stephen J. Dilworth, Denka Kutzarova, Timur Oikhberg
papers.abstract: Given a minimal system E for a Banach space X, Casazza, Dilworth, Kutzarova and Motakis introduced a multiplication $\otimes$ on span(E) and studied the Schauder bases for which $\|x \otimes y\|\approx \|x\|\|y\|$ asking whether every such basis is equivalent to the canonical unit vector basis of $c_0$ or $\ell_p$. We continue this study in the more general setting of minimal systems that are not assumed to be Schauder bases, and we obtain positive answers under hypotheses that are formally weaker than the ones considered so far: partial democracy instead of democracy or bidemocracy, and truncation quasi-greediness instead of quasi-greediness. Along the way we show that the above multiplicative estimate forces invariance under translations, we characterize when such a minimal system is a Schauder basis, and we give examples showing that the one-sided variants of the estimate behave very differently.

papers.title: Whittle--Mat\'ern metrics and isotropic Gaussian processes on compact metric graphs
papers.abstract: Isotropic Gaussian processes on networks have a covariance that is a function of a distance between locations, but valid constructions have so far required graphs with Euclidean edges and the resistance metric.
