The high-dimensional model is written in mixed primal-dual form with projection-based complementarity conditions, leading to nonlinear nonsmooth algebraic systems solved by a semi-smooth Newton method. On this basis, reduced models are constructed by proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of both primal and dual solution snapshots.
  To address cases where low-dimensional linear spaces provide limited approximation efficiency, we introduce a neural-network-augmented reduced model. Two feedforward networks learn corrections in the truncated POD coordinates of the primal and dual variables from solutions of enlarged Galerkin ROMs. The learned reconstructions enter the coupled equilibrium and constraint equations directly, defining a nonlinear reduced system solved by approximate semi-smooth Newton iterations. The online cost associated with high-dimensional residual evaluations is reduced through hyper-reduction, using a sparse cubature approach based on greedy nonnegative least squares.
  The proposed methodology is assessed on two nonlinear variational inequalities with distinct sources of nonlinearity: a two-dimensional obstacle problem with a cubic nonlinearity in the state equation, and a three-dimensional frictional contact problem in which the Coulomb law induces a nonlinear projection in the constraint equation. Numerical results compare the high-dimensional model, the linear reduced model, the neural-network-augmented reduced model, and their hyper-reduced variants, demonstrating accurate approximations with substantial reductions in online computational cost. The performance study also evaluates feasibility over the complete constraint set and measures how errors in the reconstructed obstacle and contact forces affect the primal response.

papers.title: A note on the cohomology of pullback Lie algebroids
papers.abstract: We give a direct differential-geometric proof of a result of Crainic on the cohomology of pullbacks of Lie algebroids under surjective submersions: If the fibers are connected and have vanishing cohomology through degree $n$, pullback with coefficients in any representation is an isomorphism through degree $n$ and is injective in degree $n+1$. The proof reduces to a vanishing result for leafwise cohomology and uses an exhaustion-and-patching argument due to Buchdahl. No local triviality or finite-type assumption on the fibers is required. We also prove the analogous result for holomorphic Lie algebroids.

papers.title: A case for clubs
papers.abstract: We present several remarks on cardinal coefficients associated with the generalized Baire space for an inaccessible cardinal kappa. Our inquiry originates in the work of van der Vlugt arXiv:2307.14118 . We provide evidence that the appropriate coefficients to consider are those determined by binary relations restricted to a club. In other words, we make a case for the systematic use of clubs.

papers.title: Strong convergence of Euler-Maruyama schemes for additive fractional SDEs with Lipschitz drift
papers.abstract: We study the strong convergence rate of the Euler--Maruyama scheme for additive stochastic differential equations driven by a fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1)$. Assuming the drift coefficient to be Lipschitz continuous, we establish strong convergence bounds of order $1$ if $H\in(1/2,1)$, and $1/2+H-\varepsilon$, for any $\varepsilon>0$, if $H\in(0,1/2]$. The main ingredient is a shifted stochastic sewing argument, which exploits the conditional Gaussian structure of fractional Brownian motion to control the noise discretization error.

papers.title: A sharp almost sure upper bound for partial sums of random multiplicative functions
papers.abstract: We prove that, for either a Steinhaus random multiplicative function or a Rademacher random multiplicative function $f$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, almost surely $|\sum_{n\le x}f(n)|\ll_{\varepsilon,f}\sqrt{x}(\log\log x)^{1/4+\varepsilon}$. Together with Harper's almost sure lower bound, this determines the sharp logarithmic exponent in both models. This settles Harper's conjecture on the large fluctuations of random multiplicative functions.

papers.title: Bounds on Odd and Odd-Even Induced Subgraphs
papers.authors: Qiwen Guo, Gregory Gutin, Yiming Hao, Yongtang Shi, Yong Zhang, Yacong Zhou
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph and let $\ell:V(G)\to\mathbb{F}_2$ prescribe degree parities. A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is $\ell$-admissible if every $v\in S$ has degree congruent to $\ell(v)$ modulo $2$ in $G[S]$. Let $h_\ell(G)$ be the maximum order of an $\ell$-admissible set, set $f_{\mathrm{oe}}(G):=\min_\ell h_\ell(G)$, and write $f_o(G):=h_{\mathbf{1}}(G)$, where $\mathbf{1}(v)=1$ for every $v\in V(G).$
  We prove three main results for graphs without isolated vertices. First, by extending Zeng's odd-cut method to arbitrary parity prescriptions and introducing a one-sided completion lemma, we show that $h_\ell(G)\ge 2n/11$ for every $\ell$. Consequently, $f_{\mathrm{oe}}(G)\ge 2n/11$, improving the previous bound $2n/21$.
  Second, for bipartite graphs we derive lower bounds on $f_o(G)$ in terms of the $\mathbb{F}_2$-rank of the bipartite adjacency matrix and combine them to obtain
  \[
  f_o(G)\ge \left(\frac14+\frac1{256}\right)n=\frac{65}{256}n.
  \]
  Thus, in the bipartite case, the factor $2$ in Scott's bound $f_o(G)\ge n/(2\chi(G))$ can be replaced by $128/65<2$.
  Finally, a fourth-moment argument gives, for $\alpha=\alpha(G)\ge2$ and $\delta(G)\ge 1$,
  \[
  f_o(G)\ge \frac{\alpha}{2}+\frac{\log_3\alpha}{8}
  -\frac14\log_3\log_3\sqrt{\alpha}.
  \]
  We also construct bipartite graphs satisfying
  \[
  f_o(G)\le \frac{\alpha(G)}2+\log_2\!\bigl(\alpha(G)+1\bigr)+\frac12,
  \]
  showing that the logarithmic additive improvement over Scott's bound $f_o(G)\ge\alpha(G)/2$ has the optimal order of magnitude.

papers.title: Exchangeable Testing Against an Unknown Benchmark
papers.abstract: We generate infinite binary exchangeable sequences by sequential comparison of data points against a latent benchmark. Assuming a prior distribution of the benchmark rank \(R_0\) within an unobserved group of players, we set up the Bayesian machinery which determines the posterior distribution of the running rank \(R_n\) in purely combinatorial terms, by counting insertion slots in a uniformly random ranking. This yields an explicit predictive probability of winning against the benchmark, which is a rational function of the counts. We identify some cases where the predictive probability has particularly simple form, notably a tournament related to the Topp--Leone distribution. The running benchmark rank is a P\'olya urn with random initial composition, and its normalised value converges to a latent strength variable with polynomial density. In a projective time scale, the fluctuations of the normalised rank about this limit are Brownian, with the Wright--Fisher coefficient frozen at the limit, while the associated recurrent up-down Markov chain on a high level $n$ of the Pascal graph is approximated by a Wright--Fisher diffusion with a nonlinear drift expressed through the prior density.

papers.title: A point-free theory of quantitative homogenization
papers.authors: Thuyen Dang, Yuliya Gorb, Silvia Jim\'enez Bola\~nos
papers.abstract:
We introduce a purely operator-theoretic framework for quantitative
  homogenization that bypasses the traditional reliance on large-scale
  spatial regularity and probabilistic assumptions. Inspired by
  Tartar's vision of a point-free theory, we derive explicit norm
  resolvent estimates using only the algebraic structure of multiscale
  operators and the abstract geometry of Hilbert spaces. In this
  framework, the effective macroscopic dynamics and the abstract
  corrector emerge naturally from an orthogonal decomposition of the
  state space, governed algebraically by a Schur complement. To
  quantify the convergence rate, we introduce a frequency-splitting
  technique and a flux corrector obtained by inverting the microscopic
  derivative on the residual field; this controls the error for
  regular macroscopic data in terms of explicit,
  $\varepsilon$-independent operator norms.
  This abstract perspective places on one footing stationary,
  non-stationary, periodic, quasi-periodic, and stochastic
  homogenization. We demonstrate that the physical distinctions
  between these media---and their respective convergence rates---are
  captured by the behavior of the spectral measure of the microscopic
  derivative operator, evaluated on the residual field, near zero
  frequency; in the periodic case the rate $O(\varepsilon)$ is proved,
  while in the stochastic case the rates are conditional on a
  density-of-states hypothesis. Furthermore, our results apply for
  multiscale systems that do not uphold subadditivity of energy
  quantities or do not have a well-defined Brillouin zone.

papers.title: Rigidity of Averages over the Two Largest Prime Factors
papers.abstract: Let $P_1(n)$ and $P_2(n)$ be the largest and second-largest distinct prime factors of $n$. Alladi and Johnson asked whether there is a bounded function $f$ on the primes such that the averages $\frac{1}{x}\sum_{2\le n\le x}f(P_1(n))$ and $\frac{1}{x}\sum_{2\le n\le x}f(P_2(n))$ converge to different limits, where $f(P_2(n))=0$ when $n$ is a prime power. We show that this cannot happen. In fact, whenever the first average converges, the second also converges to the same limit.

papers.title: On graphs without cycles of length $0$ modulo $3$ or $4$ modulo $6$
papers.abstract: We study graphs containing no cycle whose length is divisible by $3$ or congruent to $4$ modulo $6$. We prove that every such $n$-vertex graph $G$, where $n \ge 2$, satisfies $e(G) \le (11/8)n-7/4$. Moreover, equality holds if and only if $n=8k+2$ for some nonnegative integer $k$ and $G$ is isomorphic to the explicitly constructed graph $H_k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq2$, an $n$-vertex graph with $\left\lfloor (11/8)n-7/4 \right\rfloor$ edges satisfying the same cycle restriction. Consequently, this is the exact maximum number of edges for every $n \ge 2$.

papers.title: New Bounds on Distributional Sectional Category and Applications to Distributional Homotopic Distance
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish several new bounds for the distributional sectional category ($\mathrm{dsecat}$). We first prove Jauhari's conjecture, thereby establishing a cohomological lower bound for $\mathrm{dsecat}$ with arbitrary coefficients. We then obtain an analogous lower bound with rational coefficients by constructing a natural graded $\mathbb{Q}$-linear section of the homomorphism induced in cohomology by the symmetric diagonal. As applications, we provide several computations of the distributional sectional category. We also establish multiplicative product and composition inequalities for $\mathrm{dsecat}$. Finally, we apply these results to distributional homotopic distance. A sequential version of this invariant was recently introduced by Jauhari and Oprea; we give an equivalent formulation in terms of distributed homotopies and derive new fibration and multiplicative triangle inequalities.

papers.title: Ultra-high-dimensional spot support screening in continuous-time regression
papers.abstract: We study variable screening for high-frequency continuous-time regression, targeting the support of the spot regression coefficient. Under coordinatewise truncation and finite-variation jumps, uniform entrywise bounds for local correlation estimates yield the rate $\{(\log p)/n\}^{\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}$ under a local averaged $\alpha$-H\"older condition, up to confidence and grid factors. These bounds imply sure screening for the marginal support. To retain the regression support under local dependence, we propose partial-residual spot iterative screening with pathwise Lepski adaptation. Under sparse eigenvalues and standardized beta-min, the procedure has the sure screening property and requires only correlation columns associated with the current active set. A list-size minimax lower bound applies to both support targets and matches the localization and multiplicity order of the marginal-screening bound when $\log(p/d)\asymp\log p$. Simulations and a high-frequency factor application illustrate the procedures.

papers.title: Line-filtered ACM bundles and Ulrich defects on abelian varieties of Picard rank one
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety with $\NS(A)=\Z[L]$, $L$ ample. We show that a vector bundle filtered by line bundles splits uniquely into unipotent blocks, determine when it is ACM with respect to $L$, and show that it is never Ulrich. For a rank-two Ulrich bundle we bound from below the degree of the defect of every saturated line subbundle, compute the Hilbert polynomial of the defect, and show that the bound is attained exactly when an explicit cohomological support locus is nonempty. On abelian surfaces this locus is an ample curve in $\Pic^0(A)$; as a consequence, every rank-two Ulrich bundle is a Serre extension of a fixed numerical type, which we characterize and construct for every ample $L$. For $g\ge3$, we reduce the equality case to the existence of subcanonical codimension-two subschemes with prescribed cohomology.

papers.title: Polyhedral Outer Approximation for MISOCP: Geometry and Progressive Integrality
papers.abstract: Polyhedral outer approximation (OA) is widely used to solve mixed-integer second-order cone programs (MISOCPs) by iteratively strengthening polyhedral relaxations of conic constraints. However, the accumulation of cutting planes can increase the difficulty of solving the resulting mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs), while repeatedly solving these MILPs can be computationally expensive. To address these challenges, we investigate the geometry of supporting cuts and the computational role of integrality in OA. First, we establish theoretical bounds showing that the marginal contribution of a new supporting cut decreases at least linearly as its supporting direction approaches an existing one. Motivated by this analysis, we develop a closed-form cut-generation strategy that balances separation depth and directional diversity. Second, we propose a progressive-integrality OA framework that strengthens the polyhedral approximation through linear programs and partially integral relaxations before solving full MILPs. We theoretically characterize the transfer of cut-induced bound improvements across integrality levels and provide a branch-and-bound interpretation of the framework. Computational experiments on CBLIB instances and large-scale AC unit-commitment models demonstrate substantial improvements over classical OA and direct MISOCP solution, with runtime reductions of up to 62\% relative to classical OA on the reported power-system instances.

papers.title: Entropy Scales in Topological Dynamical Systems
papers.authors: Yunxiang Xie, Ercai Chen, Xiaoyao Zhou
papers.abstract: In this paper, we define topological and measure-theoretic entropy scales in dynamical systems for the scaling introduced by Helfter. Firstly, we establish a variational principle between Bowen and lower entropy scales on compact subsets. Secondly, we prove factor inequalities for Bowen and upper capacity entropy scales on arbitrary subsets; unlike the classical additive case, the fiber contribution is described by a transfer function and need not be additive. We also study entropy scales and sequence entropy scales under the induced action. Under suitable conditions, zero values are preserved in both directions, while positive values become infinite; counterexamples show that additional assumptions are generally necessary. As an application, we use entropy scales to distinguish zero-entropy systems sharing the same entropy dimension but differ in finer orbit-growth rates.

papers.title: High-order $L^2$-Galerkin schemes for the decoupled potential integral equations
papers.abstract: We prove Sobolev space well-posedness of the decoupled potential integral equations. Using basic pseudo-differential techniques, discrete stability is obtained for the standard $L^2$-pairing, and we deduce spectral convergence for high-order schemes employing discontinuous basis functions, or with additional element-wise tangential continuity imposed in the vectorial part of the system. The schemes are shown to be much better conditioned than a mature commercial EFIE/CFIE solver. In many cases appearing almost independent of wavenumber, mesh density, and the order.

papers.title: On The Spectral Properties of Discrete Landscape Functions
papers.abstract: We study the landscape function on a discretized interval. The discrete landscape has an explicit closed form, and its spectral coefficients can be computed exactly. We show that these coefficients lie in explicit abelian extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ and obtain the bound $$[\mathbb{Q}(c_k(N)):\mathbb{Q}]\leq\varphi(N)$$ for every odd $k$. The Chandra--Jain conjecture, asserting that $[\mathbb{Q}(c_1(N)):\mathbb{Q}]=\varphi(N)$ for all $N\geq3$, has since been proved by Q. Zhou (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21935814). We then reduce higher modes to the coprime case. Exact computations for all 624 pairs with $3\leq N\leq50$ reveal only the degrees $\varphi(N/d)$ and $2\varphi(N/d)$ for non-coprime modes, where $d=\gcd(N,k)$. This motivates the Second Chandra--Jain Conjecture that this degree dichotomy holds generally. We also discuss connections with parity, the Arnold cat map, and Lefschetz numbers.

papers.title: Two improved Liouville-type theorems for the 3D stationary tropical climate model without temperature assumptions
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we establish two improved Liouville-type theorems for the three-dimensional stationary tropical climate model without imposing any temperature assumptions. Compared with previous results, we achieve significant improvements on the growth assumptions imposed on $u$, $v$ and $
abla v$. Owing to the special structure inherent to the equations, we fully exploit the $L^2$-estimate for the oscillation of the temperature, refined interpolation techniques and an iteration argument to establish a Liouville-type theorem under flexible and relaxed power-law growth conditions. As an interesting consequence, we obtain the triviality of solutions under the integrability conditions imposed only on $(u,
abla v)$ or $(
abla u,
abla v)$. Furthermore, by developing a systematic framework to handle the energy function associated with the non-trivial solutions and with the aid of delicate ODE analysis and a contradiction argument, we refine our Liouville-type theorem by introducing logarithmic corrections to the growth rates.

papers.title: Comparing positive Toeplitz operators on holomorphic and pluriharmonic Fock spaces
papers.abstract:
We prove sharp norm comparisons between positive Toeplitz operators associated with the same positive Borel measure, acting respectively on holomorphic functions and on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions, both equipped with the Gaussian-weighted $L^2$ norm. For every positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $0<p<\infty$, both operators are compact with summable $p$th powers of their singular values (i.e. Schatten) exactly when $z\mapsto\mu(B(z,r))$ belongs to $L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$ for some fixed radius $r>0$.
  For other weights, this agreement can fail dramatically. We construct a weight $e^{-2\phi}$ and a finite positive measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}$ for which the operator on holomorphic functions has the same singular values as with the Gaussian weight and the same measure $\mu$. These values have summable $p$th powers for every $p>0$, yet the quadratic form on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions is unbounded in weighted $L^2$. The example still satisfies $\Delta\phi=2$, as for the Gaussian choice $\phi(z)=|z|^2/2$.

papers.title: Reducibility of linear representations, free ideals, and Kippenhahn's conjecture
papers.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study of the characteristic polynomial of matrix tuples and finite dimensional group representations. Among other things, several key concepts are introduced, including the minimal polynomial, algebraic extension, spectral index and multiplicity, and characteristic graph. Notably, this framework leads to a complete resolution of Kippenhahn's conjecture by providing necessary and sufficient conditions for its validity.

papers.title: Nilpotency and Engel-Type Theorems for Lie Affgebras
papers.authors: Tarik Anowar, Ripan Saha, Sayan Thokdar
papers.abstract: We investigate structural properties of Lie affgebras, viewed as affine analogues of Lie algebras. We introduce the notion of an ideaf, the affine counterpart of an ideal, and establish characterizations of left and right ideafs. We further study centers, quotient structures, and product ideafs, proving, under suitable conditions, that the center of a Lie affgebra is an ideaf. We then develop the notion of affine nilpotency and establish connections between the nilpotency of Lie affgebras and that of their retracted Lie algebras. As an application, we prove an Engel-type theorem for Lie affgebras of the form $\mathfrak{a}(\mathfrak{g};\kappa=2\lambda,\lambda,s)$.

papers.title: Two averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. In 1965, Chowla gave a conjecture that the values of $\lambda(n+h_1),\dots, \lambda(n+h_k)$ are asymptotically unrelated for any distinct natural numbers $h_1, \dots, h_k$. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will show a dynamical generalization of Chowla's conjecture on average. In the proof, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. Moreover, we will use this approach to show an analogue of the dynamical Chowla's conjecture along the primes on average. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and a variant for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.

papers.title: Internal Reasoning and Consistency in Reflective Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract:
Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) is a paracomplete arithmetic allowing direct expression of any general-recursive computation. Every RGA term is a program and truth is grounded evaluation, with a proof certificate at each universal quantifier. This paper shows, in a machine-checked Isabelle/HOL development, that such a system is powerful enough to carry out its own metamathematics. A fuel-indexed decider of RGA's grounded semantics and checkers for RGA's proofs are compiled primitive-recursive RGA terms. RGA proves internally that its decider never affirms $0 = 1$, and that every well-formed term it affirms has an RGA proof accepted by a transparent test. RGA proves that, for each valid RGA proof, its conclusion is true. RGA proves that each grounded-true well-formed term is provable. RGA proves that no proof in either of two decided classes of RGA proofs derives $0 = 1$.
  G\"odel's incompleteness theorems hold for RGA, but their proofs must be adapted. In RGA an implication $A \rightarrow B$ is strictly stronger than an entailment $A \vdash B$: RGA discharges a hypothesis only when it can prove the hypothesis decided, a restriction needed to defuse Curry's paradox. RGA's implication is material and RGA has the disjunction property, so RGA proves no implication between ungrounded sentences. The implications that the textbook proof of G\"odel's second theorem uses are of this kind and fail, but the entailments and rules it uses hold: G\"odel's proof survives as entailments. RGA does not prove its consistency sentence $\mathit{Con}$: RGA carries out G\"odel's argument internally, with a decided proof predicate and explicit proof transformers, and only the last step, that RGA does not prove $0 = 1$, is left to HOL. RGA also proves its own second incompleteness theorem as an entailment from $\mathit{Con}$, and as a single sentence quantified over proofs.

papers.title: Exponential Growth of Mean Multiplicities in Length Spectra of Semi-Arithmetic Surfaces of Arbitrary Arithmetic Dimension
papers.abstract: For a semi-arithmetic Fuchsian group $\Gamma$ of arithmetic dimension $r$ with a generalized modular embedding, EGMM holds for $r\leq2$, and for $r\geq3$ under an explicit \emph{strong contraction condition}, via a multi-dimensional Schwarz-Pick bound and a geometry-of-numbers estimate. A covering construction turns every known example into an infinite explicit family with the same exponent via principal congruence towers. We add new $r\leq2$ examples (genus-$3$/$4$ Prym eigenform loci, a different commensurability class from the known triangle groups and McMullen genus-two family) and attempt a direct flat-geometric bound on the contraction constant $\delta$ for the latter via its Lyapunov exponents ($\delta=2/3$ on ergodic average, by Bainbridge exact computation), explaining why an average bound does not yet certify the pointwise one \eqref{eqstrong-contraction} needs.

papers.title: Two-sided coherent algebras over any field with $\mathcal{PGF}(R)\subsetneq\mathcal{GP}(R)$
papers.abstract: For a ring $R$, let $\mathcal{GP}(R)$, $\mathcal{GF}(R)$, and $\mathcal{PGF}(R)$ denote the classes of Gorenstein projective, Gorenstein flat, and projectively coresolved Gorenstein flat left $R$-modules, respectively. We answer negatively the question whether $\mathcal{GP}(R)=\mathcal{PGF}(R)$ for every ring. More precisely, over every field $k$ we construct a left and right coherent central $k$-algebra $T$ and a strongly Gorenstein projective left $T$-module which is not Gorenstein flat; hence $\mathcal{PGF}(T)\subsetneq\mathcal{GP}(T)$.

papers.title: Surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators: from the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to automatic transversality
papers.abstract: This paper relates the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to the surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators. We establish a conformally invariant $L^2$ criterion and an asymptotic slope criterion, which yield higher-rank automatic transversality criteria for pseudoholomorphic curves beyond the classical rank-one framework. Applications to pseudoholomorphic spheres in $S^6$ provide quantitative $L^2$ obstructions to the integrability of almost complex structures.

papers.title: Minimum attaining operators on reducing subspaces: Spectral structure and density
papers.abstract:
In this article, we introduce and study the class $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ of minimum attaining operators on a separable Hilbert space $H$ whose restrictions to every nonzero reducing subspace are minimum attaining. This class lies between the classes of absolutely minimum attaining operators and minimum attaining operators. We establish a spectral characterization of positive operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$: a positive operator $T$ belongs to $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ if and only if $T=\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\lambda P_\lambda$, where $\Lambda\subseteq[0,\|T\|]$ is a countable well-ordered set, $(P_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is a family of mutually orthogonal nonzero projections, and $\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}P_\lambda=I$ in the strong operator topology.
  We also establish a connection between $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ and the class of operators attaining their norm on every nonzero reducing subspace. Further, we obtain stability results under suitable finite-rank and compact perturbations, and prove that $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$ is norm dense in $\mathcal{B}(H)$. We also establish the norm density of operators in this class having a nontrivial invariant half-space. Finally, we characterize normal operators in $\mathcal{M}_r(H)$, obtain a corresponding characterization for multiplication operators on $L^2(\mathbb{T})$, and characterize the condition $\mathcal{R}_T=\mathcal{R}_{|T|}$ in terms of the von Neumann algebra generated by $|T|$, showing that this condition forces $T$ to be normal.

papers.title: A characterization of the reversibility of linear cellular automata
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group, let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field, and let $V$ be a $\mathbb{K}$-vector space. We prove that there exists a bijective linear cellular automaton $V^G\to V^G$ whose inverse is not a cellular automaton if and only if $G$ is not locally finite and $\dim_{\mathbb{K}}V \geq |\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$. In particular, $|\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$ is the exact dimension threshold for non-reversibility. This answers an open problem proposed by T. Ceccherini-Silberstein and M. Coornaert.

papers.title: Average-Radius List-Decodability of Random Linear Codes
papers.authors: Venkatesan Guruswami, Shilun Li, Mihir Singhal
papers.abstract: We prove that for every prime power $q$ and every $p \in (0, 1-1/q)$, a random $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear code of rate $1 - h_q(p) - \epsilon$ is $(p, C_{p,q}/\epsilon)$-average-radius list-decodable with probability at least $1 - q^{-\Omega(n)}$, i.e., for every center $y \in \mathbb{F}_q^n$, the $C_{p,q}/\epsilon$ codewords closest to $y$ have average fractional Hamming distance at least $p$ from $y$. This extends a similar result for (standard) list-decoding due to Guruswami, H\r{a}stad, and Kopparty (2010) to the stronger average-radius guarantee, with the same $O(1/\epsilon)$ list size. For average-radius list-decoding, such a result was previously known only for binary linear codes (Guruswami, Li, Mosheiff, Resch, Silas, and Wootters, 2021) and for general (non-linear) random codes over arbitrary alphabets (Elias, 1991).

papers.title: Mirror descent algorithms with logarithmic barriers
papers.authors: Alberto De Marchi, Yura Malitsky, Adrien B. Taylor
papers.abstract: We derive convergence guarantees for mirror descent and proximal mirror descent with a logarithmic barrier as the distance-generating function. When the solution lies on the boundary, the Bregman divergence blows up and classical guarantees become vacuous. While existing remedies recover $O(\log k/k)$ rates by adapting classical bounds, we propose a more direct route in which the Bregman distance to the solution never appears, and which achieves the same rate with constant stepsize. We also construct an example showing that this rate cannot be improved in general. Finally, we compare the proposed approach with interior-point methods.

papers.title: Tensor-Train Isogeometric Analysis for Large-Scale Three-Dimensional Linear Elasticity
papers.authors: Quoc Thai Tran, Duc P. Truong, William Dai, Kim {\O}. Rasmussen
papers.abstract: This work develops tensor-train (TT) formulations for solving large-scale three-dimensional linear elasticity problems discretized by isogeometric analysis. By exploiting the tensor-product structure of the basis functions and the low-rank structure of geometry-dependent coefficient fields, the stiffness operator, mass operator, force vector, and displacement solution are represented in TT format. Two solution strategies are investigated: a block-operator formulation, in which the coupled elasticity operator is stored as separated TT blocks, and a single-operator formulation, in which the full coupled system is stored as one monolithic TT operator. A matrix-free three-field TT conjugate-gradient solver is introduced for the block formulation, while AMEn is used for the single-operator formulation. Numerical examples demonstrate substantial compression of both operators and solutions compared with conventional sparse full-grid representations, showing that TT-based formulations provide an efficient and scalable approach for large-scale three-dimensional elasticity simulations.

papers.title: Self-similar stationary Navier--Stokes flows in a half-space with arbitrarily large swirl forcing
papers.authors: Yun Wang, Chunjing Xie, Shaoheng Zhang
papers.abstract: We study axisymmetric self-similar solutions of the stationary Navier--Stokes equations with $(-3)$-homogeneous forces and no-slip boundary conditions in a half-space. For a fixed force without swirl, we characterize the interval of amplitudes for which solutions exist and describe the velocity singularity at its finite endpoints. For each parameter in this interval, a solution exists after adding a swirl force of any size, and it is unique among solutions with bounded profiles when the swirl force is sufficiently small. The proof uses the nonnegative contribution of swirl to a Riccati equation and a comparison estimate. We also prove that, when the tangential curl of the force is sufficiently small, there exists a unique solution with small velocity profiles.

papers.title: The high dimensional monostable reaction-diffusion equation with free boundary and radial symmetry
papers.authors: Hongkai Cao, Jingyi Cui, Chengzhe Tang, Xiaoyan Zhang
papers.abstract: We consider the radially symmetric version of the reaction-diffusion equation $u_t-d\Delta u=f(u)$ with a monostable nonlinearity $f$, viewed as a model for the spreading of a species with population range $r<h(t)$ and density $u(t,r)$ ($r=|x|$), where the free boundary $r=h(t)$ is governed by $u(t,h(t))=\delta>0$ and $h'(t)=-d u_r(t,h(t))/\delta$. For the one-dimensional case ($N=1$), Du \cite{DN} proved that when $\delta\in(0,1)$, spreading occurs: $u\to1$ locally uniformly in $\mathbb{R}$, $h(t)\to\infty$, and $\lim_{t\to\infty}[h(t)-c_*t]=\tilde{h}\in\mathbb{R}$ with no logarithmic shift. In the present paper we consider $N\ge2$ and establish a complete trichotomy: spreading for $\delta\in(0,1)$; transition for $\delta=1$, where $u\to1$ uniformly on $[0,h(t)]$ and $h(t)\to h_\infty\in(0,\infty)$; and vanishing for $\delta>1$, where $h(t)\to0$ and $u\to\delta$ uniformly on $[0,h(t)]$. For the spreading regime, by constructing sharp upper and lower solutions, we prove that the solution converges globally to the semi-wave profile and reveal a logarithmic shift of the form $ \lim_{t\to\infty}\big[h(t)-c_*t+c_N(\delta)\log t\big]=\hat{h}\in\mathbb{R}$, with the coefficient $c_N(\delta)>0$ satisfying $ \lim_{\delta\to0}c_N(\delta)=d(N-1)/c_0$, where $d(N-1)/c_0$ is the shift coefficient for the high-dimensional radial pushed-case Cauchy problem. These results reveal the connection to the spreading behavior modeled by the corresponding Cauchy problem.

papers.title: Discrete dynamics of Eratosthenes sieve
papers.abstract:
We study Eratosthenes sieve as a discrete dynamic system. At each stage of the sieve there is a cycle of gaps ${\mathcal G}(p^\#)$ of length $\phi(p^\#)$ and span $p^\#$. There is a recursion ${\mathcal G}(p_k^\#)\longrightarrow {\mathcal G}(p_{k+1}^\#)$ that creates the next cycle from the current one.
  If we take initial conditions from the cycle ${\mathcal G}(p_0^\#)$, then for all constellations of span $|s| < 2p_1$, including gaps $g < 2p_1$, the driving terms of various lengths form Markov chains. These yield {\em exact} models for the populations $n_s(p_k^\#)$ for all further stages of the sieve.
  If $s$ is an admissible constellation of length $J$, then its population $n_{s,J}(p^\#)$ grows as $\Theta \left( \prod (q-J-1)\right)$. So we factor out the superexponential growth to obtain the exact model for the relative population $w_s(p_k^\#)$ of the constellation $s$ across all further stages of the sieve. $$ w_{s,J}(p_k^\#) \; = \; n_{s,J}(p_k^\#) \, / \, \prod_{J+1 < p \le p_k} (p-J-1) $$ The asymptotic value of the relative population is a constant ${w_{s,J}(\infty) \ge 1}$ that depends only on the odd prime factors that divide a span in $s$.
  Assuming that the instances of a constellation $s$ are approximately uniformly distributed in ${\mathcal G}(p_k^\#)$, we develop initial estimates of the number of instances $s$ that would occur in the interval of survival $\Delta H(p_k) = (p_k^2, p_{k+1}^2)$. We define a statistic $\eta_s(p_k)$, the quadratic density of the constellation $s$ over the interval $\Delta H(p_k)$. We show that the initial estimates $\widehat{\eta_g}(p)$ for prime gaps agree with samples up to $5.677\,E14$.

papers.title: Solvability of unimodular equations in groups and Lie algebras
papers.authors: Anton A. Klyachko, Mikhail A. Mikheenko, Alexander Yu. Olshanskii
papers.abstract: Our results imply, in particular, that a finitely generated solvable group $G$ is nilpotent if and only if it contains a solution to any unimodular equation, i.e., an equation of the form $\prod g_ix^{n_i}=1$, where $g_i\in G$ and $\sum n_i=\pm1$. A similar fact turns out to be true for Lie algebras. We also exhibit an example of a unimodular equation $w(x)=g$ over a finitely generated group $G$, which has a solution (in $G$) for any $g\in G$, but the solution is not unique for some $g\in G$. We show that, for nilpotent groups $G$, the set of unimodular mappings $G^n\to G^n$ (which are defined naturally) forms a group under the composition.

papers.title: A note on the center of the queer super Yangian ${\rm Y}(\mathfrak{q}_1)$
papers.abstract: We investigate two families of central elements of the queer super Yangian ${\rm Y}(\mathfrak{q}_1)$, arising from the constructions of Poletaeva-Serganova and from Nazarov's quantum Berezinian. We establish an explicit relation between their generating series, thereby giving an answer to the question raised by Nazarov in \cite{Na22}.

papers.title: Failure of the local decay formula for Arnold multiplicities under twisted K\"ahler--Ricci flow
papers.abstract: Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether local Arnold multiplicities under maximal weak twisted K\"ahler--Ricci flow with fixed cohomology class satisfy $\lambda(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{\lambda(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We construct counterexamples with analytic initial singularities in every dimension $n\ge2$. On the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$, $e\ge2$, the initial current $[S]+(e+1)[F]$ yields $\lambda(\varphi_t,x)=1/2-t/e$ for $x\in S\setminus F$ and $0<t<e/2$, where $S$ is the negative section and $F$ a fibre. Products with smooth stationary factors give higher-dimensional examples. The Zariski negative part of $\{S\}+\{F\}$, the reduced support class, forces extra divisor mass. For pure divisorial data with simple normal crossings support, a smooth semipositive representative of the reduced support class's positive part gives exact short-time formulas. On one surface we construct flows with identical initial current germs, background data and global initial Arnold multiplicity, but different local rates.

papers.title: Farey Structure in Modulo Krinkle Tilings: Mediant Splicing and Generation of Prototiles from a Single Edge
papers.abstract: The Modulo Krinkle tilings of Imura (arXiv:2506.07638) form a family of non-periodic, spiral monohedral tilings parametrized by a reduced fraction $m/k$ and an integer $t\ge 2$. We show that the Farey sum (mediant) $(m_1+m_2)/(k_1+k_2)$ of two Farey-adjacent parameters is realized by an exact geometric operation on prototiles: the lower boundary path of the $(m_1+m_2,k_1+k_2)$-prototile is obtained by concatenating the parents' lower paths after an edge-length-preserving progressive rotation (fan-twist) of their edges. Conversely, every prototile admits exactly one fan-twist splice decomposition -- no non-adjacent parameters ever splice -- the cut position being $k_1=m^{-1}\bmod k$, and the recursion descends the Stern-Brocot tree to a single unit edge. The combinatorial core of the operation is the classical standard factorization of Christoffel words; the contribution here is its exact edge-isometric realization on circular direction systems and the resulting structure theory for the Modulo Krinkle family, including the recently introduced variants: we prove a separation theorem stating that every variant prototile is the common recursively-generated core plus finitely many direction-invariant decoration edges. As a corollary of Imura's spiral-arm count formula, the two Farey parents are visible in the offset-free tiling itself: the numbers of counterclockwise and clockwise spiral arms are $tk_1$ and $tk_2$.

papers.title: Aperiodic random walks: uniform estimates, local limits and invariance principles
papers.abstract: We prove uniform endpoint estimates, killed local limits, and conditioned-bridge invariance principles for triangular arrays of centered, aperiodic, integer-valued random walks with uniform exponential tails. The endpoint estimates cover all nonnegative heights, while the local limits treat positive diffusive and zero endpoints. The increment law may vary with the scaling parameter.

papers.title: On the invariance of risk-sensitive LQR gain under input randomization
papers.abstract: This paper shows that the optimal gain of the risk-sensitive linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem is invariant under input randomization when the cost penalizes the realized noisy input. This may appear counterintuitive at first glance because certainty equivalence does not hold for risk-sensitive LQR and input randomization inflates the effective process noise. Nonetheless, the gain is preserved because the input noise enters not only the system dynamics but also the cost functional, and its total effect eventually vanishes. Consequently, the optimal gain and the Riccati recursion need not be recomputed, and the increment in the optimal cost can be readily evaluated in closed form. This result facilitates the use of risk-sensitive LQR in applications that employ input randomization for privacy or exploration, such as dynamic watermarking for replay attack detection.

papers.title: Finite Directional Coefficient Modules over Euler Fibers of $A$-Hypergeometric Systems
papers.abstract: Let A be a d-by-n integer matrix of rank d, let beta belong to the d-dimensional complex vector space, and consider the A-hypergeometric system defined by the ideal H_A(beta), with relation lattice L equal to the integer kernel of A. No homogeneity, pointedness, or positivity assumption is imposed on A. We study directed formal logarithmic solutions simultaneously over all exponent lattices in the Euler fiber over beta, which form an uncountable family when L has positive rank. For a fixed L-generic direction, negative-support strata are described by rational sign polyhedra, and their directional boundedness is characterized by recession cones. On each exponent lattice, normalization reduces the infinitely indexed coefficient equations to a finite system of Euler, transit, and directional vanishing relations, represented by a finitely presented directional coefficient module. We prove that only finitely many exponent lattices contribute nonzero directed solution spaces and that every contributing coefficient module has finite length. Macaulay inverse-system duality then identifies the dimension of the all-lattice directed formal logarithmic solution space with the length of the all-lattice coefficient module. We also give an explicit formal-series realization and a polynomial colon-ideal criterion for all realizable lowest exponents.

papers.title: Airy limit for the Jack process and topological expansion
papers.abstract: For every $\beta>0$, we establish multi-time soft-edge moment convergence for a class of Jack processes, including the Jack--Plancherel process, a discrete $\beta$-analogue of Dyson Brownian motion. The limiting moments admit an absolutely convergent expansion in terms of nonnegative Brownian bridges decorated by pairs of equal and opposite jumps. At equal times, we identify this limit with the joint Laplace statistics of the Airy$_\beta$ process for $\beta\geq1$. The same Brownian expansion yields an asymptotic $\beta$-topological expansion of the marginal $b$-conjecture and, at $\beta=2$, an explicit nonnegative formula for the Witten--Kontsevich intersection numbers.

papers.title: Central non-vanishing of Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every sufficiently large modulus $q\not\equiv2\bmod4$, at least $3/8-o(1)$ of the primitive Dirichlet characters $\chi$ modulo $q$ have $L(1/2,\chi)\ne0$. We also establish stronger proportions for moduli $q$ satisfying certain arithmetic conditions.

papers.title: Induced Size-Ramsey Numbers of Odd Cycles via Spread Measures
papers.abstract:
We prove that, for every $k\ge2$ and every sufficiently large odd $n$, the induced size--Ramsey number of $C_n$ satisfies \[ \widehat R_{\mathrm{ind}}(C_n;k)=e^{\Theta(k)}n. \] This improves the previous upper bound of $e^{O(k\log k)}n$ and resolves a conjecture of Brada\v{c}, Dragani\'c and Sudakov. We obtain this result by proving a stronger form of their odd-hole gadget conjecture: we construct a graph with $e^{O(k)}$ edges whose every $k$-edge-colouring contains a monochromatic induced odd cycle of length $O(\log k)$.
  Our proof develops a spread-based approach to finding induced cycles. The key idea is to place spread probability weights directly on families of candidate cycles and control their possible chords through a quadratic chord score. Combining this with random sparsification and hypergraph containers yields a sparse host graph that works for every $k$-edge-colouring.

papers.title: A quantitative convergence rate for torsional creep to the distance function as p tends to infinity
papers.authors: Farid Bozorgnia, Masoud Bayrami-Aminlouee, Khudoyor Mamayusupov
papers.abstract: We prove that the Dirichlet $p$-torsion function $u_p$ converges to the distance to the boundary $d$ at the rate $O(1/p)$ in the uniform norm, on every bounded domain and with a constant depending only on the dimension and the diameter. The upper bound comes from a radial barrier with its pole at a boundary point, which is an admissible comparison function for $p>n$ and needs no boundary regularity; the lower bound comes from an inscribed ball. On the ball the error equals $(1+\log n)/p+O(p^{-2})$, so the order $1/p$ cannot be improved in general. Under a uniform exterior ball condition an annular barrier gives $u_p\le K_\Omega^{1/(p-1)}d$ for every $p>1$, with $K_\Omega$ explicit in the dimension, the diameter and the exterior radius; on convex sets the constant is the diameter, and a multiple of $d$ is a supersolution whenever $-\Delta d$ has a positive distributional lower bound. On $C^2$ domains, the same barrier and the classical gradient maximum principle give $\norm{\nabla u_p}_{L^\infty}^{p-1}\le K_\Omega$. When $-\Delta d$ is a measure of finite total variation, which we prove for $C^1$ domains with a uniform exterior ball, the gradients converge in $L^q$ at the rate $O(p^{-1/2})$ for $q\le2$ and $O(p^{-1/q})$ for $q\ge2$; these exponents are not claimed to be sharp. The explicit ball profile shows that the gradients do not converge uniformly.

papers.title: Real-rooted Eulerian polynomials from permutations, words, and paths
papers.abstract:
We study seven Eulerian-type polynomial families. We prove that the
  descent polynomials of derangements are real-rooted, settling the
  derangement part of a conjecture of S.~Fu, Z.~Lin, and J.~Zeng. We also
  resolve the real-rootedness conjecture in OEIS
  A335340, strengthen the known rowwise real-rootedness of an even-top
  descent family to consecutive strict interlacing, and prove real-rootedness,
  consecutive interlacing, and real-rooted gamma-polynomials for U.~Shankar's
  super-Eulerian polynomials. A differential recurrence gives consecutive
  weak interlacing for ternary words counted by increasing runs.
  We prove stability of the peak-value refinement and consecutive
  interleaving of its positive weighted diagonals, settling a conjecture of
  P.~Alexandersson and O.~Nabawanda. Finally, we prove that the zig-zag Eulerian
  polynomials, which enumerate swaps in alternating permutations, have simple
  negative roots, settling the real-rootedness conjecture of T.~Kyle Petersen
  and Y.~Zhuang.

papers.title: Asymmetric Periodic Water Waves in Finite Depth
papers.authors: Yuchen Wang, Shusen Yan, Maolin Zhou
papers.abstract: We consider the full two-dimensional water-wave equations in finite depth, with and without surface tension. Water waves have been studied mathematically for more than two centuries. Reflection symmetry remains a common assumption in constructions of periodic steady waves, although asymmetric profiles have been observed in experiments and numerical computations. We construct families of periodic stationary solutions whose free surfaces have no axis of reflection, in both the pure-gravity and capillary--gravity cases. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous construction of asymmetric periodic pure-gravity waves for the full two-dimensional water-wave problem in finite depth. The proof combines localized vorticity laws with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. In the pure-gravity case, we introduce a small background shear flow to obtain an invertible boundary operator and couple the interior and free-surface approximations at leading order.

papers.title: Matchings and shape-Wilf-Equivalence of sets of patterns of length three I: Triples
papers.authors: Sucharita Biswas, Umesh Shankar, Sivaramakrishnan Sivasubramanian
papers.abstract: Permutation pattern avoidance on Ferrers boards has become a central topic in enumerative combinatorics with important connections to matchings, set partitions, and other combinatorial structures as it allows one to build families of Wilf-equivalent patterns. While shape-Wilf-equivalence classes have been completely determined for individual patterns and pairs of patterns of length three, the corresponding classification for larger pattern sets has remained open. In this paper, we provide a complete classification of the shape-Wilf-equivalence classes of triples of patterns of length three. Our proofs use a bijective encoding of pattern avoiding transversals to establish all equivalence classes. As an application, we enumerate matchings avoiding triples of patterns of length three for all, extending previous results of Bloom and Elizalde. These enumerative results identify additional families of combinatorial objects counted by the Fuss-Catalan numbers and by other integer sequences appearing in the OEIS.

papers.title: The maximum spectral radius of outerplanar and planar $k$-uniform hypergraphs
papers.abstract: For $k\ge3$, a $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected outerplane graph whose interior faces are bounded by $k$-cycles, and a closed $k$-angulation is a simple $2$-connected plane graph all of whose faces are bounded by $k$-cycles. Their face hypergraphs have the same vertices as the graphs; the hyperedges are the vertex sets of the interior faces, respectively all faces. For $k=3$, the extremal problems over these hypergraphs agree with those for the outerplanar and planar $3$-uniform hypergraphs of Ellingham, Lu and Wang, who determined the outerplanar maximizer for large $n$ and conjectured the planar one. In this paper, for each fixed $k$, we determine the hypergraphs of maximum spectral radius in both classes for all sufficiently large $n$ satisfying the corresponding face-count divisibility condition. In the outerplanar case, the unique extremal hypergraph is the face hypergraph of the fan, in which one vertex lies on every interior face. In the planar case with $k=3$, it is the face hypergraph of $K_2+P_{n-2}$, which confirms the conjecture of Ellingham, Lu and Wang. For $k\ge4$, the extremal hypergraphs are the face hypergraphs of balanced theta graphs, in which two vertices lie on every face. For $k=4$, the result holds for every $n\ge5$, with extremal hypergraph ${\mathcal H}(K_{2,n-2})$. For $k\ge6$ and an even number of faces, there are exactly $\lfloor(k-2)/2\rfloor$ extremal hypergraphs up to isomorphism.

papers.title: Internal congruences modulo powers of 2 for $k$-colored overpartitions into odd parts
papers.authors: Manjil P. Saikia, Prabal Talukdar, Dazhao Tang
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{po}_k(n)$ denote the number of $k$-colored overpartitions of $n$ into odd parts. For every odd number of colors, we establish infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $2$. The proof proceeds by expressing the relevant difference generating functions as a fixed theta quotient multiplied by polynomials in an auxiliary function. Uniform lower bounds for the $2$-adic valuations of the polynomial coefficients then yield the stated internal congruences. These results generalize an internal congruence of Saikia, Sarma and Sellers (J. Ramanujan Math. Soc.~2025) on overpartition triples into odd parts.

papers.title: Critical Schatten exponents for the Berger-Coburn endpoint problem
papers.abstract: Berger and Coburn showed that boundedness of a Toeplitz operator $T_g$ on the Fock space controls the heat transform $g^{(t)}$ for $1/4<t<1$, and conjectured that $T_g$ is bounded if and only if $g^{(1/4)}$ is bounded. Looi recently disproved the forward implication by constructing a bounded $T_g$ with unbounded $g^{(1/4)}$. We prove that the reverse implication also fails, even for a real-valued admissible symbol $g$ with $g^{(1/4)}\in C_0(\mathbb{C}^n)$, and that the forward implication fails even when $T_g\in S_p$ for every finite $p>1$. Our counterexamples come from Baire category and closed graph arguments, which yield no explicit symbols. Despite this two-sided failure, the forward implication has a sharp Schatten-class form: $\|g^{(1/4)}\|_\infty\le 2^n\|T_g\|_{S_1}$ for every admissible symbol $g$ with $T_g$ trace class. We show that the constant $2^n$ is optimal and that the same estimate holds with $S_p$ in place of $S_1$ for $T_g\in S_p$ when $0<p\le1$. For $p>1$, no corresponding uniform estimate holds, even for smooth compactly supported symbols. We also determine the optimal constants in the Berger--Coburn estimates for $1/4<t\le1$. Finally, for $1\le p<\infty$, we show that the equivalence $T_g\in S_p$ if and only if $g^{(1/4)}\in L^p$ holds exactly when $p=2$, answering a question of Bauer, Coburn, and Isralowitz.

papers.title: The norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator
papers.abstract: We determine the exact $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ norm of the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator for every $1<p<\infty$, proving that it equals $p/(p-1)$. This settles the sharp strong-type problem for the centered maximal operator on the real line. For every $p$ in this range, the norm is strictly larger than the constant associated with the critical power $|x|^{-1/p}$, thereby disproving the conjecture of Dror, Ganguli, and Strichartz that this profile determines the unrestricted norm.

papers.title: Hodge-Deligne and Poincar\'e polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$
papers.abstract: By studying wall crossings of Hassett moduli spaces of weighted pointed curves, we prove a recursive formula that reduces the computation of the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$ to that of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,(0^+)^n}$ of stable pointed curves of minimal weights. For $g=1$, we further prove an explicit formula for the Hodge-Deligne and Poincar\'e polynomials of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,(0^+)^n}$. Combining these, we prove formulas that enable us to compute the cohomology of $\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}$ efficiently.

papers.title: Free boundary minimal surfaces of genus zero
papers.abstract: We prove that any embedded genus zero free boundary minimal surface in the ball has first Steklov eigenvalue $1$. This implies the uniqueness of the critical catenoid.

papers.title: Averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the signs of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at any fixed collection of distinct shifts. In 2015, Matom\"aki, Radziwi\l\l and Tao proved an averaged form of Chowla's conjecture. In 2022, Lichtman proved a variant of this conjecture over primes on average. In the same year, Lichtman and Ter\"av\"ainen proved the Hardy-Littlewood-Chowla conjecture on average. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will first establish the analogous dynamical generalizations of these three results related to Chowla's conjecture. In the proofs, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we will also prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and some variants for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.

papers.title: Hankel-Koopman Finite-Horizon Energy Decomposition of Coupled Experimental Data: A Three-Phase Data-Driven Twin Forecasting Framework
papers.abstract: Finite-horizon prediction is challenging when observations are limited and a quantity of interest depends on several coupled nonlinear measurement channels. This paper develops a three-phase data-driven twin framework that integrates finite-horizon Hankel--Koopman energy decomposition, inverse-calibrated reconstruction using nonlinear autoregressive models with exogenous inputs, and forecast composition. Channel dynamics are identified and simulated in Hankel coefficient space, with candidate models assessed after reconstruction in physical measurement space. The resulting reduced-order model of the channel dynamics drives recursive prediction of the quantity of interest. Three theorems support the framework, establishing the energy decomposition and modal orthogonality; existence, uniqueness, and inverse stability of the auxiliary continuous inverse-calibration solution; and finite-horizon stability of the composed forecast for a fixed selected model under stated assumptions. A retrospective solar-power case study yields high correlations between predicted and reference trajectories across the considered forecast horizons, demonstrating reproduction of a constructed channels-dependent quantity of interest.

papers.title: Proximal-Linearized NEP Method for Composite Optimization with Set-Inclusion and Manifold Constraints
papers.authors: Hao He, Ruyu Liu, Shaohua Pan
papers.abstract: This paper focuses on difference-of-convex (DC) composite optimization problems with set-inclusion and manifold constraints. We develop an inexact proximal-linearized nonsmooth exact penalty (NEP) method that penalizes the conic constraint while retaining the manifold constraint explicitly. At each outer iteration, the method approximately solves a strongly convex proximal-linearized subproblem over the current tangent space, using computable inexactness criteria, adaptive parameters, and a retraction-based acceptance mechanism. Under boundedness of the iterates and penalty parameters, we establish an $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ worst-case outer iteration complexity for finding an $\epsilon$-approximate KKT point of the original problem. We further develop a complexity-transfer framework relating uniform primal objective-gap and KKT-residual decay, or dual objective-gap decay, to total inner-iteration complexity bounds. This yields an $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ overall oracle complexity with either accelerated semi-proximal ADMM or FISTA applied to the dual subproblem as the inner solver. Using semi-proximal ADMM as the inner solver improves the bound to $O(\epsilon^{-2}\log(1/\epsilon))$ under an additional uniform error-bound condition. We further establish convergence of the entire iterate sequence to a KKT point under the same boundedness assumption and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property of the associated potential function. Numerical experiments demonstrate the competitive performance of the proposed method on row-sparse PCA, clustering, robust SVMs, and nonconvex SOCPs.

papers.title: Matrix nearness problems: Do real inputs admit real solutions?
papers.abstract: Given a real square matrix $A$ and a nonempty closed target set of complex matrices $\mathcal{E}$, invariant by complex conjugation and containing real matrices, does the subset of $\mathcal{E}$ consisting of the matrices nearest to $A$ in the Frobenius distance always contain a real matrix? We give negative answers when $\mathcal{E}$ is either the set of normal matrices (solving a question posed by N. Higham) or the set of matrices whose eigenvalues lie in the closed left half-plane (solving a question posed by the first author and F. Poloni). For the latter problem, we also argue that the ratio between the real and complex distances is unbounded in every dimension $n\geq 3$, and this holds for every distance induced by a unitarily invariant norm. For both problems and $n \geq 3$, we show that a real input $A$ uniformly drawn from the unit sphere $\|A\|_F=1$ has no real minimizer over $\mathcal{E}$ with probability strictly between $0$ and $1$. Beyond these two cases, we prove for an arbitrary nonempty closed target sets $\mathcal{E}$ that, for almost every real input, either $\mathcal{E}$ contains a unique nearest matrix which is real, or every nearest matrix in $\mathcal{E}$ is nonreal.

papers.title: Variational properties of Perron's extremal solutions in the Bernoulli one-phase problem
papers.authors: Farhan Abedin, William M. Feldman, Kerrek Stinson
papers.abstract: We study the Perron extremal solutions of the stationary one-phase Bernoulli problem. These solutions are important in several applications, but not much is known about the regularity of their free boundaries due to their non-variational construction. We show that, in fact, Perron extremal solutions retain some variational features; specifically, they are solutions in the sense of inner variations. We establish this property by showing that extremal solutions arise as infinite-time limits of monotone solutions of the parabolic Bernoulli problem. As a consequence, we are able to describe the structure of singularities for Perron extremal solutions in two dimensions: largest subsolutions have smooth free boundaries, while smallest supersolutions have free boundary points that are either smooth, or whose blow-up limits are two-plane wedges with equal slope.

papers.title: On the arithmetic of Tate-Shafarevich groups via Kolyvagin's conjecture
papers.abstract: We investigate how Heegner points detect the finiteness of the $p$-primary part of Tate-Shafarevich groups of semi-stable elliptic curves over the rationals of \emph{arbitrary} rank with any good reduction prime $p \geq 5$ with irreducible mod $p$ representation and partially recover \c{C}iperiani--Wiles' theorem on solvable points on genus one curves. As a key ingredient of the proof of these results, we also give a concise proof of Kolyvagin's conjecture for semi-stable elliptic curves with supersingular reduction with a relevant choice of an imaginary quadratic field. Our approach is independent of the cyclotomic Iwasawa main conjecture for elliptic curves with supersingular reduction.

papers.title: Generating pairs in $\mathfrak g_2$ related by an involution
papers.authors: Santiago Pineda Montoya, Johan H. R\'ua Mu\~noz, Borut Jur\v{c}i\v{c} Zlobec
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb O$ be the real octonion division algebra, let $\mathfrak g_2=\operatorname{Der}(\mathbb O)$, and fix a quaternionic subalgebra $H\subset\mathbb O$. We ask when an element $Z$ preserving $H$ and its conjugate $TZT^{-1}$ generate $\mathfrak g_2$, where $T$ is a prescribed involutive octonion automorphism. We prove that such a $Z$ exists if and only if $T(H)\ne H$. Moreover, a fixed set of six derivations preserving $H$ contains a generating choice for every such $T$. For an arbitrary $Z\in\mathfrak g_2$, we construct a polynomial criterion with two factors: one detects reducibility on the imaginary octonions, and the other detects generated algebras of dimension at most three. An irreducible proper generated algebra must be a principal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. We characterize the elements admitting this case by their rotation frequencies and parametrize all corresponding involutions. For one specified involution and quaternionic subalgebra $H$, we describe the nongenerating set by four geometric families and six irredundant systems of scalar equations, and prove that it has real dimension four.

papers.title: On smooth and bundle structures on topological manifolds homotopy equivalent to $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$
papers.abstract: We first verify the expected calculations of the topological structure set, in the sense of surgery theory, for the total spaces of $S^{4k-1}$-bundles over $S^{4k}$ for $k\ge3$, in which manifolds homotopy equivalent to the total spaces are organized. Next, we investigate the question of which of the elements in these structure sets can be realized as such bundles. Moreover, we study the forgetful map from the smooth version to the topological version of the structure set; we determine its image. All elements in the image turn out to have the underlying manifold such a bundle.

papers.title: Strong laws, random monotone vector fields and gradient flows on metric spaces of nonpositive curvature
papers.abstract: We establish a probabilistic Lie-Trotter-Kato formula for the gradient flow generated by an integral function over suitable separable Hadamard spaces. This result leverages Stojkovi\'c's Lie-Trotter-Kato formula for gradient flows of sums of convex functions and Ba\v{c}\'ak's result relating resolvent and gradient flow convergence, along with a strong law of large numbers for normal convex integrands. For separable Hilbert spaces and locally compact Hadamard spaces, these strong laws follow from results of King and Wets and Artstein and Wets, respectively, but we crucially go beyond these examples by establishing a new such strong law for normal convex integrands on all Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones are isometric to Hilbert spaces, a class that includes non-Hilbertian, non-locally compact examples such as infinite-dimensional hyperbolic space. This new strong law arises as a combination of a strong law of large numbers for integrable random monotone vector fields on Hilbert-Hadamard spaces, that is, Hadamard spaces whose tangent cones all embed isometrically into Hilbert spaces, extending a result of Salim from Hilbert spaces, together with a new result on the interchangeability of the subdifferential and the integral, which we establish for $L^2$-Lipschitz integrands. This latter ingredient provides, to our knowledge, the first nonlinear version of (a particular case of) a previous result due variously to Ioffe and Tikhomirov, Levin, Hiriart-Urruty, Thibault as well as Rockafellar and Wets. On the way to this strong law for random monotone vector fields, we also establish a distribution-uniform generalization of Sturm's strong law of large numbers for inductive means of $L^1$-sequences of i.i.d. random variables on Hadamard spaces via a new effective non-asymptotic concentration inequality. Throughout the paper, we highlight various remaining open problems.

papers.title: Mixing time under monotone censoring
papers.abstract:
We prove the conjecture of Ding and Mossel~\cite{DM}: the lazy random walk on the discrete cube, censored to any increasing set of fixed positive density, mixes in time $O(n\log n)$. More precisely, for every nonempty increasing set $A\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$, with $a=\mu(A)$ and $\mu$ uniform on the cube, we prove $$
  t_{\mathrm{mix}}(P)\le C_a n\log(en), $$ where $C_a$ depends only on $a$. The proof uses hypercontractivity on the ambient cube to strengthen the Poincar\'e inequality on coordinate sections. An optimal stopping time occupation inequality for increasing sets converts the resulting local bound into a uniform bound on hitting times of large sets. An appendix by Y.~Peres improves the density dependence to $C_a=13a^{-1}\log(e/a)$, within a logarithmic factor of the conjectured $a^{-1}$ dependence.

papers.title: Graded Algebras of Modular Forms and Sign Changes of Fourier Coefficients for Eta Quotients
papers.abstract: In this paper, for $N=8,12,16,20,32$, we determine the explicit structure of the graded algebra of modular forms for $\varGamma_0(N)$ of both integral and half-integral weights, with all quadratic Dirichlet characters modulo $N$. We give explicit eta quotient generators and determine the relations among them. Using these structures, for a given weight, a level among those considered above, and a quadratic character, we obtain a basis for the corresponding space of modular forms consisting of eta quotients. Using these eta quotient bases, we obtain necessary and sufficient conditions for the periodicity of the signs of the Fourier coefficients of modular forms in three specific spaces. Finally, we determine all eta quotients in these spaces whose Fourier coefficient signs are periodic.

papers.title: Maximal Algebraic Ideals in Nonunital $C^*$-Algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of maximal algebraic two-sided ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras. We formulate singular-distribution estimates in terms of lower semicontinuous $2$-quasitraces and introduce a novel criterion, which we call an admissible compact quasitracial triple set. These tools allow us to control membership in algebraic ideals and to prove the nonexistence of maximal ideals in nonunital $C^*$-algebras under a closed finite-scale face condition. This nonexistence result applies to a broad class of simple $C^*$-algebras including simple separable stable AF algebras, and nonunital, simple, separable, stably finite, $\mathcal Z$-stable $C^*$-algebras $A$ that admit an approximate identity consisting of increasing projections $(p_n)$ and for which the simplex $\operatorname{QT}_2^1(A,p_1)$ of normalized traces at $p_1$ has finitely many extreme points. Moreover, we construct a simple AF algebra whose finite-scale face is dense but not closed and which nevertheless has a maximal dense algebraic ideal. This example yields a negative resolution to a question raised by Ozawa, asking whether every maximal algebraic two-sided ideal in a $C^*$-algebra must be closed.

papers.title: Wehrl-type entropy problem for compact connected semisimple Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected semisimple Lie group, and let $\pi:G\to U(V_\lambda)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation associated with the highest weight $\lambda$. We prove that coherent projectors are the unique minimizers of the Wehrl entropy over all density matrices on $V_\lambda$. Similar extremal properties hold for power functions in place of the entropy function. The proof uses a second variation at the extremizer by perturbation in directions associated with Killing fields, similar to the strategy of Frank and Lieb used in \cite{FrankLieb}. Then the problem reduces to the uncertainty principle characterizing coherent states. This solves the Wehrl-type entropy problem for arbitrary compact connected semisimple Lie groups.

papers.title: Biharmonic Conformal Immersions of Hypersurfaces: Dirac Rigidity and Mixed Clifford Geometry
papers.abstract:
A biharmonic conformal immersion asks whether a hypersurface can become a critical point of the bienergy after a conformal change of the domain metric. We study when this flexibility can produce compact nonconstant-mean-curvature geometry in space forms. For surfaces in three-dimensional space forms, with $U=\lambda^2H$, Ou's system is encoded exactly by a Laplace-type operator acting on a restricted ambient Killing spinor. We classify all monic scalar--chiral factorizations of this operator. In nonzero curvature such a factorization exists locally exactly when the principal curvatures are locally constant; the normalized Euclidean branch is equally rigid, and the remaining real spherical non-CMC branch is excluded by a finite-type Frobenius obstruction.
  For $m>2$, this scalar rigidity does not imply geometric nonexistence. The conformal tension has independent normal and tangential components. We prove that $\mathbb R\xi\oplus TM$ is the minimal natural $O(m)$-equivariant carrier, derive the corresponding strongly elliptic Jacobi block and its two-grade Clifford realization, and identify off-diagonal hybridization as the escape mechanism. Exact cohomogeneity-one reductions, combined with validated interval and Chebyshev/radii-polynomial arguments, yield embedded proper non-CMC, nowhere-umbilical examples in round spheres, including $$ S^1\times\mathbb S^n\times\mathbb S^n\hookrightarrow\mathbb S^{2n+2} \qquad(n\ge1). $$ Thus the scalar obstruction is sharp with respect to coefficient bundle: the smallest enlargement forced by conformal tension already supports compact non-CMC solutions.

papers.title: An improvement of the large sieve for square moduli under Hooley's hypothesis $R^*$ for short Sali\'e sums
papers.abstract: Let $S(Q,M,N,(a_n))=\sum_{q\le Q}\sum_{a\bmod q^2,(a,q)=1}|\sum_{M<n\le M+N}a_ne(an/q^2)|^2$ be Zhao's large sieve sum with square moduli. Zhao conjectured that $S\ll(QN)^\epsilon(Q^3+N)\sum|a_n|^2$. The bound of Baier and Zhao (2008) exceeds this conjecture by a factor which reaches $Q^{1/2}$ at the critical point $N=Q^3$, and there the exponent $1/2$ has not been lowered since. We prove that, under Hooley's Hypothesis $R^*$ for short Sali\'e sums, $S\ll(QN)^\epsilon(Q^3+N+Q^{4/3}N^{2/3})\sum|a_n|^2$. This replaces the excess over Zhao's conjecture by its $2/3$-th power throughout the range $Q^{5/2}<N<Q^4$; at $N=Q^3$ it gives $S\ll Q^{1/2-1/6+\epsilon}N\sum|a_n|^2$. The proof is short. Following Zhao's original treatment, we approximate the point under consideration by fractions $b/r$ with denominators up to $Q^{2/3}N^{1/3}$, which for $N<Q^4$ is beyond the customary $\sqrt{N}$. If the approximation is poor, an elementary count suffices. If it is good, the analytic part of the problem disappears: after Poisson summation in both variables the count is expressed through quadratic Gauss sums, and their exact evaluation at every modulus turns the sum over the dual variable into short Kloosterman and Sali\'e sums, to which Hypothesis $R^*$ applies and gives the square root of the elementary count. At odd moduli the hypothesis is needed only in the form of Conjecture (C*) of Friedlander and Iwaniec. The Gauss-sum evaluations, including even moduli and coefficients sharing a factor with the modulus, are proved in full. This version supersedes earlier versions, which obtained the exponent $1/2-1/28$ at $N=Q^3$ by a much longer route through sums of modular square roots. The paper was prepared in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic).

papers.title: Element-wise Convergence Behavior of Subspace Iteration
papers.abstract: This paper studies the element-wise convergence behavior of subspace iteration. All results are established for both \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R}\) and \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}\). For a diagonal matrix \(\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\) with \(|\lambda_1|>\cdots>|\lambda_n|>0\), we analyze the modulus of each entry of the iterative matrix sequence generated by subspace iteration, both without and with the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure. Under mild assumptions on the initial matrix \(X\in\mathbb{F}^{n\times m}\), we first derive exact asymptotic expressions for \(|Q_k(i,j)|\) in the subspace iteration without the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure: entries with \(i\neq j\) decay as \(|\lambda_{\max\{i,j\}}/\lambda_{\min\{i,j\}}|^k\), and the deviation of \(|Q_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \(\max\{|\lambda_j/\lambda_{j-1}|,|\lambda_{j+1}/\lambda_j|\}^{2k}\), with explicit coefficients determined by the LU factorization of \(X\). Similar conclusions could also be established for upper triangular matrices. For the Rayleigh--Ritz variant, we obtain element-wise bounds for the normalized Ritz vectors \(Z_k\). Specifically, for \(|Z_k(i,j)|\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\geq m+1\) decay as \((|\lambda_i|/|\lambda_j|)^k\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\leq m\) decay as \((|\lambda_{m+1}|^2/(|\lambda_i||\lambda_j|))^k\), and the deviation of \(|Z_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \((|\lambda_{m+1}|/|\lambda_j|)^{2k}\). These results give an element-wise description of the convergence behavior of subspace iteration. After an orthogonal or unitary change of basis, the results could be further generalized.

papers.title: Fourier Ratio and Restricted Isometry via Entropic Descent
papers.authors: Will Burstein, Alex Iosevich, Ben Krause
papers.abstract: In this second paper on descent methods as proof mechanisms in harmonic analysis (the first treated Bourgain's $\Lambda(p)$ selection theorem), entropic mirror descent gives an improved restricted isometry bound, improving sampling and recovery bounds in the Fourier Ratio program. Let $H$ be a complex $n\times n$ matrix with $H^*H=nI$ and $|H_{ij}|=1$. For fixed $0<\varepsilon<\frac14$ and $A_0>0$, independent Bernoulli row selection with expected cardinality $C_{\varepsilon,A_0}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log(2r)\leq m\leq n/2$ preserves, after normalization by $\sqrt m$, the squared norm of every complex vector $y$ with $\|y\|_1\leq\sqrt r\|y\|_2$ within a factor $1\pm\varepsilon$, with failure probability at most $Cn^{-A_0}$. This includes every $r$-sparse vector and also fully supported ones; support size enters only through this inequality. For $y=\widehat f$ the condition is exactly $\operatorname{FR}(f)^2\leq r$, where $\operatorname{FR}(f)=\|\widehat f\|_1/\|\widehat f\|_2$, giving uniform energy sampling and approximate recovery even for signals with full Fourier support. The same holds for a uniform subset of prescribed cardinality, and for discrete Fourier and real Hadamard matrices. At fixed accuracy the bound removes one sparsity logarithm from the earlier count and replaces $\log n$ by $\log\frac{2en}{r}$; for Walsh matrices it matches, up to constants, the lower bound of B\l asiok et al.\ in their range. One relative-entropy potential controls the corrections of an amplitude predictor at every scale; counting them on the symmetric difference of two samples gives the uniform estimate. We also prove the sufficient bound $C_{A_0}\varepsilon^{-5}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log\frac{2r}{\varepsilon}$, and stable sparse recovery from $Cs\log\frac{2en}{s}\log(2s)$ measurements, with error controlled by the noise and the best $s$-term approximation.

papers.title: Prime and Cohen-Macaulay ideals of 2-minors with linear resolution
papers.abstract: Prime and Cohen-Macaulay ideals of 2-minors of matrices of variables with linear resolution are classified.

papers.title: Non-maximal quasi-isometric $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$-representations via alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: For every admissible non-maximal Toledo invariant $t$, we construct a locus of irreducible representations of a closed genus-$g$ surface group into $\mathrm{PU}_{2,n+1}$ with Toledo invariant $t$ whose orbit maps are quasi-isometric embeddings. These loci have real codimension $10(g-1)$ or $10(g-1)+2(n-1)$ in the character variety depending on the Toledo value. Our construction uses $4$-cyclic Higgs bundles and their correspondence with $\partial$-alternating surfaces in complex pseudo-hyperbolic spaces.
