We then train the model dynamics under $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ and show that the model is indeed free of arbitrage while fitting the dynamics of the market well. We also propose a range of BHW-tests to test for absence of arbitrage.

papers.title: Union of Translates of a Convex Body
papers.abstract: Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a strictly convex body and let $Z\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ be a finite set of sites in general position. We consider the problem of calculating the volume $\mu_d$ of $\bigcup_{z\in Z}(z-K)$. Let $V_z$ be the Voronoi cell of $z\in Z$ with respect to the convex distance function induced by $K$, and let $N$ be the nerve of the Voronoi cells. When $K$ is a ball, a classical result reduces the inclusion-exclusion formula to a sum over $N$: $\mu_d(\bigcup_{z\in Z}(z-K))=\sum_{J\in N}(-1)^{|J|+1}\mu_d(\bigcap_{z\in J}(z-K))$. When may the hypothesis that $K$ is a ball be dropped? We show that for $d\leq 2$ the reduced formula holds for every strictly convex $K$, while for each $d\geq 3$ there is a strictly convex $K$ for which it fails. For $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, let $\chi_x$ be the Euler characteristic of the subcomplex of $N$ induced by the sites lying in $K+x$. A sufficient condition for the reduced formula to hold is $\chi_x\equiv 1$ on the union. When $d=3$ and $K$ is $C^4$, we show that $\chi_x\equiv 1$ on the union for all $Z$ in general position if and only if $K$ is an ellipsoid. The proof relies on the Fubini-Pick affine invariant.

papers.title: Automatic Differentiation with Constraints in Forward and Inverse Problems
papers.authors: Nikolay Yavich, Alexander Ryabov, Viacheslav Naumov, Sayan Ranu, N. M. Anoop Krishnan, Evgeny Burnaev, Vladimir Vanovskiy
papers.abstract: Approximate solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) on unstructured grids can be represented on a graph. Numerical optimization involving stiff evolutionary and static PDEs often requires solving a large system of equations, which can be treated as a constraint. In this work, we present a fully differentiable graph-based implicit solver that incorporates this constraint. We evaluate its performance across four key tasks: a) linear and nonlinear forward modeling of evolutionary and static problems, b) solving inverse problems to estimate equation coefficients, c) solving inverse problems to estimate the right-hand side, and d) learnable graph coarsening to accelerate forward modeling. The stability and differentiability of our solver enable significant reductions in the complexity of forward modeling while efficiently addressing related inverse problems. These capabilities make it a powerful tool for different physics and engineering applications, in particular for geophysics, where inverse problems are commonly solved in order to reduce the model uncertainty.

papers.title: Probabilistic Stability Transfer for One-Dimensional Euler Characteristic Transforms
papers.abstract: The Euler characteristic transform (ECT) is a computable topological signature for shapes embedded in Euclidean space. Existing ECT stability results control changes in the transform through deterministic geometric perturbation bounds, but many data-generating mechanisms produce perturbations that are random and unbounded in the worst case. In such settings a uniform deterministic bound may be unavailable or too pessimistic. This paper formulates a probabilistic stability-transfer principle for one-dimensional ECT stability: a deterministic stability estimate is combined with a tail bound for the induced geometric error to obtain a high-probability ECT error bound. We instantiate this principle using the stability theorem of Marsh and Beers for embeddings of finite one-dimensional CW complexes. The resulting consequences cover ambient displacement fields conditionally on admissibility and supremum-tail estimates, and finite landmark perturbations with reconstruction. For landmark perturbations, bounded, sub-Gaussian, sub-exponential, and polynomial-tail noise assumptions give explicit high-probability ECT stability bounds. The framework isolates a geometric stochastic component that arises in shape analysis pipelines across biological morphology, medical imaging, molecular structure analysis, and remote sensing.

papers.title: Metric dimension and maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of graph Laplacians
papers.authors: Monther Rashed Alfuraidan, Suliman Khan, Lorenzo Sauras Altuzarra
papers.abstract: We study equality between metric dimension and the maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of the Laplacian and signless Laplacian matrices. These quantities are not ordered in general. Using the standard decomposition associated with twin classes, we separate forced multiplicities from quotient-spectrum contributions. We give complete equality classifications for complete multipartite graphs and core--satellite graphs, and enumerate the multipartite equality graphs by order. For graphs formed by attaching at least two leaves to every vertex of a connected core, the metric dimension and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $ 1 $ are known; we show that this multiplicity is maximal for both matrices, and uniquely maximal except for $ P_3 $. We enumerate this core--leaf family up to isomorphism and obtain a uniform asymptotic formula by order and metric dimension, together with the quadratic exponential growth rate $ 1/18 $. An exact census of connected graphs of orders two through seven identifies the first separating examples and examples without twins. Finally, for every odd $ r \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 3} $, we study $ \Theta_{2, 2, r} $ and determine both maximum multiplicities: the two equality properties alternate with $ r $ modulo four, producing infinite separating families in both directions.

papers.title: A positivity conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton (2003) that $\frac{1-q}{(q^n;q)_m}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}$ has nonnegative power-series coefficients for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. We obtain a polynomial version by bounding a M\"obius correction by first differences of Gaussian coefficients. The proof uses partitions and quadratic and cubic semi-invariants of binary forms. An extension of this bound proves the Reiner--Stanton--White conjecture on positivity of orbit polynomials for flags of subspaces.

papers.title: Borel's computation of the ranks of $K$-theory revisited
papers.abstract: We reprove Borel's computation of the rank of the $K$-groups of rings of algebraic integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ for certain number fields, e.g., $F = \mathbb{Q}(\mu_{l^k})$ for $l$ an odd regular prime number. The idea is to recover a simple formula for $l$-adic {\'e}tale cohomology groups of $\mathcal{O}_F$ in terms of Iwasawa theoretic objects without using Borel's result as an input.

papers.title: Inscribed 4-polytopes of maximal volume with seven and eight vertices
papers.abstract: We prove, with sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic, that every cyclic $4$-polytope with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $2/5$. Hence no $4$-polytope of maximal volume with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ is cyclic, answering a question of Horv\'ath and L\'angi for $d = 4$, and with their theorem the maximal volume is $\sqrt{3}/4$. With eight vertices, the same method bounds the volume of every simplicial type other than the cross-polytope by $13/20$, so the regular cross-polytope, of volume $2/3$, is up to orthogonal transformations the unique maximiser.

papers.title: Disc-presheaves and normal invariants
papers.abstract: In this note, we elaborate on a result of Krannich--Kupers--Mehzer on Disc-presheaves. We show that equivalences of $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves of manifolds yields homotopy equivalences with trivial normal invariant. As an application, we show that two closed, simply connected manifolds are homeomorphic if and only if their $2$-truncated Disc-presheaves are equivalent.

papers.title: The Volume Exchange Metric
papers.authors: Enrique Alvarado, Joseph Jung, Jeremy Mason, Shrunal Pothagoni, Benjamin Schweinhart
papers.abstract: The volume exchange metric between cell structures embedded in Euclidean space is introduced. Intuitively, it measures the minimum amount of volume that must be swept out to continuously transform one cell structure into another. The main result is that the volume exchange metric coincides with a discrete analogue defined as a minimum over matchings between cells. Algorithms are described to compute the discrete volume exchange metric and illustrate its effectiveness at distinguishing polycrystalline microstructures in computational experiments.

papers.title: On the square of an isosimple module
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be an isosimple module, that is, a nonzero module isomorphic to every nonzero submodule of itself. In this paper, we investigate if the square $S^2 := S \oplus S$ is isoantian when $S$ is an isosimple module. If the base ring is commutative, then the answer is yes. However, for noncommutative rings this is no longer true even when $\mathrm{End}_R(S)$ is a discrete valuation ring. We also give some positive results coming from quasi-projectivity and Morita equivalence. Finally, we consider when every finite powers of an isosimple module are isoantian provided it holds for the square. Our related result says that if $S^2$ is isoantian and $E = \mathrm{End}_R(S)$ is either commutative Noetherian or right semihereditary, then every finite power of $S$ is isoantian.

papers.title: Reverse Module Categories of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.authors: Chongying Dong, Binghui Li, Li Ren, Yilong Wang
papers.abstract: We study the realization of the reverse braided category of the module category of a rational vertex operator algebra V. Using holomorphic extensions and commutant constructions, we prove that this realization property is preserved under suitable cosets, tensor products, extensions, and finite-group orbifolds. As applications, we establish the property for unitary Virasoro minimal models, affine vertex operator algebras of types ABCDE at positive integral levels, the corresponding principal W-algebras of type ADE, and related parafermion vertex operator algebras.

papers.title: Dynamic Regret and Tightened Constraint Violation for Communication-Efficient Distributed Online Bilevel Optimization
papers.authors: Fan Li, Xinlei Yi, Guanghui Wen, Yang Shi, Tao Yang
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the distributed online bilevel optimization problem with time-varying inequality constraints. In this setting, a multi-agent network is confronted with a hierarchical decision-making task characterized by coupling between the inner and outer optimization levels. We first propose a communication-efficient single-loop distributed online primal--dual algorithm based on communication compression, which tracks both the inner-level solution and the Hessian-inverse-vector product using only one update per-round. We show that this algorithm achieves a dynamic network regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{\max\{\theta_1,1-\theta_1\}}+T^{\theta_1 } P_T+H_{1,T}+E_{1,T})$, where~$\theta_1 \in (0,1)$, $P_T$ is the outer-level path variation, $H_{1,T}$ is the inner-level path variation, and $E_{1,T}$ is the gradient path variation alongside a network cumulative constraint violation bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{1-\theta_1/2})$, which is further reduced to $\mathcal{O}(T^{1-\theta_1})$ under Slater's condition. Furthermore, to eliminate the dependence of regret on the inner-level and gradient path variation, we propose a novel adaptive multi-loop distributed online algorithm to control the inner-level approximation accuracy at each round. By dynamically adjusting the number of inner-level updates based on a gradient-norm tolerance condition, this algorithm yields an improved dynamic network regret bound of $\mathcal{O}(T^{\max\{\theta_1,1-\theta_1\}}+T^{\theta_1 } P_T)$ which depends solely on the outer-level path variation while maintaining the same network cumulative constraint violation bound. Finally, numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Vertex Removal and Vertex-Edge Domination
papers.authors: Minhui Li, Shumin Zhang, Fengming Dong
papers.abstract: A vertex $v$ of a graph $G$ $ve$-dominates every edge incident with a vertex in its closed neighborhood $N_{G}[v]$. A set of vertices is a vertex-edge dominating set ($ve$-dominating set) if every edge of $G$ is $ve$-dominated by some vertex in the set. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the vertex-edge domination number $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, also known as the isolation number. In this paper, we study the effect of vertex removal on $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, establish sharp bounds on $\gamma_{ve}(G-v)$ and characterize the vertices whose removal decreases, preserves, or increases $\gamma_{ve}(G)$. Let $V^0(G)$ and $V^+(G)$ denote the sets of vertices whose removal preserves and increases $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, respectively, and let $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ consist of the vertices in $V^0(G)$ belonging to every minimum $ve$-dominating set. We prove that \[ |V^0(G)|\geq3|V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)|+\sum_{v\in V^+(G)} \bigl(\gamma_{ve}(G-v)-\gamma_{ve}(G)+1\bigr). \] In particular, $|V^0(G)|\geq 2|V^+(G)|$. We also prove that every vertex in $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ lies on a cycle and that $V^0(T)\neq\emptyset$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three.

papers.title: Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviations and precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with random step sizes
papers.authors: Xiequan Fan, Shuyuan Liang, Dongxue Ma
papers.abstract: In this paper, we focuses on how the distribution of random step sizes affects Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviations and precise large deviations for the elephant random walk with random step sizes. First, with sub-exponential moment condition of random step sizes, we establish Cram\'{e}r-type moderate deviation results. Consequently, moderate deviation principles are obtained. Secondly, for random step sizes with sub-exponential tails, we establish a large deviation principle on tail probabilities. Finally, for random step sizes with regularly varying tails, we obtain precise large deviations.

papers.title: Sharp Signed Mass and Rigidity for Critical Finsler--Liouville Equations
papers.authors: Yanjun Liu, Zhongwei Tang, Heming Wang
papers.abstract: We study bounded-above entire solutions of critical Finsler--Liouville equations with a possibly sign-changing prescribed function and finite absolute mass. Under a lower cone-growth condition, we establish a sharp signed-mass bound without upper growth or monotonicity assumptions. With an additional growth condition, annular compactness for a sequence of dilations yields Pohozaev boundary limits and rigidity for radially nonincreasing prescribed functions. Explicit examples show that the rigidity threshold is optimal. In the Euclidean plane, the mass estimate also gives a sharp obstruction to completeness.

papers.title: Littlewood's mutually touching cylinders: the maximum is seven
papers.authors: Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that eight congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ cannot touch pairwise. Since seven such cylinders exist, the maximum number of congruent mutually touching infinite cylinders is seven. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968.

papers.title: Lucas recurrences and Lambert series in coprime double sums
papers.abstract:
For the Lucas numbers $L_0=2$, $L_1=1$, and $L_n=L_{n-1}+L_{n-2}$, we obtain \[ \sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}}\frac{1}{L_{2n}L_{2m}L_{2(n+m)}}=\frac1{45}. \] This follows from the absolutely convergent identity \[ \sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}}\frac{q^{n+m}} {(1+q^n)(1+q^m)(1+q^{n+m})} =\frac{q^2}{(1-q^2)^2},\qquad |q|<1. \] We give a self-contained proof by local cancellation on the Calkin--Wilf tree, as a specialization of Hata's Farey-interval telescoping principle. Specializations yield a hyperbolic-cosine identity \[\sum_{\substack{n,m\ge1\\(n,m)=1}} \frac{1}{\cosh(nx)\cosh(mx)\cosh((n+m)x)} =\frac{2}{\sinh^2(2x)}, x>0\]
  and weighted sums for canonical second-order Lucas recurrences. Decomposing arbitrary positive pairs according to their greatest common divisor gives an unrestricted sum expressed by a Lambert series and the quasimodular Eisenstein series $E_2$. Conversely, M\"obius inversion recovers the primitive identity from a double Lambert-series result of Cui, Kumar, and Singh.

papers.title: Iterated Lavrentiev regularization under random noise: variational source conditions and rates in expectation
papers.authors: Ankit Singh, Hemant Sharma, Kiran Davuluri
papers.abstract: The convergence theory of iterated Lavrentiev regularization for nonlinear monotone ill-posed equations is deterministic: the data error is bounded by a known level that the discrepancy principle uses explicitly. Under Gaussian noise no such bound exists. For a discretized two-dimensional nonlinear inverse source problem for the Poisson equation, we analyse convergence in a finite-energy Gaussian noise model, keeping the linearized and nonlinear cases apart. For the linearized iteration the noisy and noise-free iterates differ by one resolvent applied to the noise; this gives an exact singular-value variance formula, a priori rates in expectation, and the main result: for a family of discretizations whose distance functions are bounded uniformly in the mesh, the rate is governed by that decay, which relaxes the classical range condition. The rate degrades gracefully, down to logarithmic, as the underlying continuum error loses smoothness, and a balancing rule attains it without knowing the smoothness. For the full nonlinear iteration under the order-one source condition, a truncated discrepancy principle fed only the noise level attains $\sigma_E^{1/2}$ in expectation, in the energy noise level $\sigma_E\asymp\sigma/h$, the rare event of large noise being controlled by concentration. The rough nonlinear regime and the general-exponent nonlinear rate are left open and supported numerically for kink and jump errors. We separate the deterministic worst-case, Gaussian, and white-noise settings, prove a worst-case lower bound, and describe where the method is statistically inefficient relative to spectral cut-off. Heterogeneous media and a cost comparison with an adjoint-based scheme are given as supplementary material.

papers.title: A noise-level-free parameter-choice rule for iterated Lavrentiev regularization of nonlinear potential monotone ill-posed problems
papers.abstract: We consider nonlinear ill-posed operator equations $F(x)=y$ in a Hilbert space, where $F$ is monotone with a Lipschitz continuous Fr\'echet derivative that is self-adjoint near the solution $x^\dg$ (a locally \emph{potential} operator), and only noisy data $y^\delta$ with unknown noise norm $\delta:=\|y-y^\delta\|$ is available. For the nonstationary iterated Lavrentiev regularization \[ x_{k+1}^\delta=x_k^\delta-\bigl(F'(x_k^\delta)+\alpha_kI\bigr)^{-1}\bigl(F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta+\alpha_k(x_k^\delta-x_0)\bigr), \] all classical stopping rules require $\delta$. We analyze a \emph{noise-level-free} parameter-choice rule of retrospective type, selecting a minimizer $k_*$ of $\theta(k,y^\delta)=\|F(x_k^\delta)-y^\delta\|^2/\alpha_k^2$ over a finite computed window. Under a standard noise condition (necessary in view of the Bakushinskii veto) the rule is well defined and $\alpha_{k_*}^2\ge c\,\delta/\|x_0-x^\dg\|$. If moreover $x_0-x^\dg\in\R(F'(x^\dg))$ and $k_*\ge1$, we prove $\|x_{k_*}^\delta-x^\dg\|=O(\sqrt{\delta_*}+\sqrt{\delta})$ with the computable $\delta_*=\|F(x_{k_*}^\delta)-y^\delta\|$ satisfying $\kappa\delta\le\delta_*\le C\sqrt\delta$, yielding the baseline rate $O(\delta^{1/4})$ along admissible growing-horizon families, and $O(\sqrt\delta)$ whenever $\delta_*=O(\delta)$; no range-invariance or tangential cone conditions are imposed. Rates under H\"older source conditions with $p\ge1$ (including saturation) follow; the case $p<1$, the removal of the self-adjointness assumption, and a full oracle inequality are identified as open problems.

papers.title: On $c$-Normal Maximal Chains of Sylow Subgroups in Finite Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be finite group. A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is said to be $c$-normal in $G$ if there exists a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ such that $G = HN$ and $H\cap N\leq H_G$, where $H_G$ is the core of $H$ in $G$. Let $P$ be a nontrivial $p$-group. A chain of subgroups $1=P_0 <P_1<\cdots P_{n-1}<P_n=P$ is called a maximal chain of $P$ provided that $|P_i:P_{i-1}|=p$ for $i=1,2,\ldots n-1$. In this paper, we determine the structure of finite groups having $c$-normal subgroups of of a maximal chain of Sylow subgroups. We obtain new characterizations of finite $p$-nilpotent and supersolvable groups.

papers.title: Gaussian Lower Bounds for Distinct Subset Sums in Higher Dimensions
papers.abstract: For sequences of $n$ nonnegative integer vectors in $\mathbb Z^k$ with distinct subset sums, we prove, for fixed $k$, the uniform lower bound $M\ge (C_k-o(1))2^{n/k}/\sqrt n$ for the largest coordinate, where \[ C_k=\sqrt{\frac{2k}{\pi}}\, \frac{(k+1)^{(k-1)/(2k)}}{\sqrt{\lfloor (k+1)^2/4\rfloor}}. \] The proof compares a Gaussian-kernel expectation with a sum over a translated lattice, uniformly over the vector sequence. We optimise the resulting quadratic-form constant using a vertex second-moment certificate. We show that $C_k$ also exceeds the variance constant obtained by optimising an ellipsoidal geometry.

papers.title: A 2X2 Matrix Approach to Hopf Fibrations:: Quaternionic Reduction of Octonionic Bi-unitary Matrices and an RLLR/LRRL Bracketing Rule
papers.abstract: We develop a common two-by-two matrix framework for the four classical Hopf fibrations associated with the real, complex, quaternionic and octonionic numbers. In all four cases the Hopf map is the image of the north pole of a sphere of trace-free Hermitian matrices under conjugation by a bi-unitary matrix, and it depends only on the first column of that matrix, without any bracketing convention, even for the non-associative octonions. Our main results concern general octonionic bi-unitary matrices, beyond the compatible matrices, with entries in a single complex subalgebra, on which earlier work on octonionic Lorentz transformations relies. We prove that every octonionic bi-unitary matrix is in fact quaternionic: its entries lie in a quaternion subalgebra depending on the matrix. We show that requiring Hermitian output leaves exactly four inequivalent ways of bracketing the octonionic triple products, among them an interlaced rule called RLLR/LRRL, and that each of them splits into an ordinary five-dimensional rotation and a four-dimensional scaling governed by a non-commutative determinant. This determines exactly when the evaluation preserves the geometry of the sphere, shows that it may contract or even collapse four dimensions, and explains why it cannot be compatible with matrix multiplication. We also recover in compact form, through the Clifford map, the known fact that suitable compatible matrices, which we interpret as transvections of the eight-sphere, generate the spin group Spin(9) by nested evaluations. Non-associativity thus does not prevent a two-by-two octonionic description of the full Spin(9) symmetry; it prevents that description from being realised through unrestricted multiplication of octonionic matrices.

papers.title: Polynomial Spectral Gap Estimates for Finitely Differentiable Quasi-Periodic Schr\"odinger Operators
papers.authors: Ao Cai, Yang Gao, Jiawei He
papers.abstract: We prove polynomial upper bounds on spectral gaps of quasi-periodic Schr\"odinger operators with small $C^{k}$ potentials and Diophantine frequencies. For sufficiently large $k$, the decay exponent is $k-34\tau$, where $\tau$ is the Diophantine exponent. We construct examples with lower bounds along infinitely many gap labels, showing that the leading coefficient $1$ of $k$ is asymptotically optimal. The proof uses quantitative reducibility and the Moser-P\"oschel argument.

papers.title: Convex-cyclic and super convex-cyclic weighted shifts
papers.abstract:
Convex-cyclic operators are considered by H. Rezaei \cite{R1}. However, there is a general lack of theoretical understanding of super convex-cyclic operators.
  In this paper, we analyze super convex-cyclic operators. In particular, Super Convex-cyclicity Criterion is described. Additionally, we characterize convex-cyclicity of (invertible) bilateral weighted shifts in terms of their weight sequences, which in turn correct \cite[H. Rezaei (2013) Theorem 4.2 ]{R1}. Meanwhile, we give super convex-cyclicity of (invertible) weighted shifts in the bilateral case.

papers.title: Uniqueness of twisted linear periods
papers.authors: Yufeng Li, Hengfei Lu, Junyan Xiao
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero, and let $\D$ be either $F$ or a quaternion division algebra over $F$. We prove that every irreducible smooth representation of $\GL_{p+q}(\D)$ has at most one linear period transforming under any prescribed character of $\GL_p(\D)\times\GL_q(\D)$.

papers.title: A Critical Case for the Near Field Refraction Problem in Negative Refractive Index Material
papers.authors: Yi He, Feida Jiang, Haokun Sui
papers.abstract: This paper studies the near field refraction problem for the critical case in negative refractive index material. Snell law in vector form is first reviewed, and the physical constraint governing refraction is discussed. We then define the refractor for the critical case and analyze several of its key properties. Building on these properties, we introduce the notion of a weak solution to this problem and prove the existence of the weak solution when the target measure is either discrete or a finite Radon measure. The proof relies on the Minkowski method, an iterative approach to refraction and reflection problems in geometric optics.

papers.title: Endpoint maximal estimates for the half-wave propagator
papers.authors: Bowen An, Wenjuan Li, Huiju Wang
papers.abstract:
We present a proof of the strong maximal estimate for the Euclidean half-wave propagator at the critical pair $s_d=d/(d+1)$ and $q_d=2(d+1)/(d-1)$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, i.e. \begin{equation*} \biggl\|\sup_{0<t<1}|e^{it\sqrt{-\Delta}}f(x)|\biggl\|_{L^{q_d}({\mathbb{R}}^d)}
  \le C_d\|f\|_{ H^{s_d}({\mathbb{R}}^d)}. \end{equation*}

papers.title: Least singular values of Gaussian matrices with deterministic shifts
papers.authors: Xuanang Hu, Zeyan Song, Xinglong Wu
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a deterministic real square matrix and $G$ a standard Gaussian matrix. We determine $\E\smin(A+G)$, up to universal constants, in terms of the singular values of $A$. The expectation is comparable to the square root of the smallest zero of the expected characteristic polynomial of $(A+G)^{\top}(A+G)$. This resolves Problem~3 in Tikhomirov's ICM 2022 survey. We also prove that the zeros of the expected characteristic polynomial are majorized by the expected ordered eigenvalues of $(A+G)^{\top}(A+G)$.

papers.title: On the Motivic K-Theories of Classifying Spaces of Cyclic 2-Groups
papers.abstract: We compute the $2$-completed integral motivic homology, effective algebraic $K$-theory, and very effective Hermitian $K$-theory of the geometric classifying spaces $B\mu_{2^n}$, $n\geq 2$, over algebraically closed and real closed fields. We first carry out the corresponding classical calculations and, then obtain the motivic results using motivic spectral sequences and comparison techniques. The results reveal the classical $2$-torsion together with motivic $\tau$-periodicity and $\rho$-torsion.

papers.title: Data-driven accelerated multigrid method for Riesz space fractional diffusion equations
papers.abstract: The multigrid method is one of the most efficient iterative methods for solving large structured linear systems, and its efficiency stems from the complementarity between the smoother and the coarse grid correction. In this paper, we consider the block Toeplitz linear system obtained by discretizing time dependent Riesz space fractional diffusion equations, and employ the weighted Jacobi iterative method as a smoother. The weighted Jacobi smoother features a simple structure and low computational cost, yet its smoothing property is highly dependent on the relaxation parameter. We adopt Gaussian process regression to select the relaxation parameter to accelerate the convergence of the multigrid method. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical analysis, which simultaneously verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the data-driven parameter selection strategy.

papers.title: Single commutators in Schatten ideals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that every operator in the Schatten $p$-class ($p>2$) can be realized as a single commutator of operators in the Schatten $2p$-class. This settles the Pearcy-Topping question for Schatten ideals. We also obtain simultaneous operator and Schatten norm bounds for the factors.

papers.title: On Diophantine tuples involving star numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss two related Diophantine tuple problems involving star numbers $S_n=6n(n-1)+1$. First, we investigate classical $D(k)$-tuples whose elements are star numbers. We construct infinitely many $D(k)$-pairs for several positive and negative admissible values of $k$, and we prove several nonexistence results for $D(k)$-triples and quadruples. Second, we introduce a modified notion of a star number $D(k)$-tuple, requiring $a_ia_j+k$ itself to be a star number. We construct several infinite families of $D(1)$-triples, and study their extensions to quadruples. In particular, we prove that $\{4,108,165\}$ has the unique extension $\{4,108,165,360\}$ to a star number $D(1)$-quadruple. The main tools used in this paper are generalized Pell equations, Nagell's theorem, lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms due to Matveev and Dujella-Peth\H{o} version of the Baker-Davenport reduction method in diophantine approximation.

papers.title: Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract:
A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function.
  A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs.
  Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.

papers.title: Boundary One-Point Functions in the Open XXZ Spin Chain with Generic Integrable Boundaries
papers.authors: Till Bargheer, Tengis Batmunkh, Paul Ryan
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.

papers.title: Partitionability is NP-complete
papers.abstract: We show that the problem of deciding whether a simplicial complex is partitionable is NP-complete in dimensions two and higher, answering a 1995 question of Kleinschmidt and Onn.

papers.title: Tree Lattices and the Neumann-Zagier conjecture
papers.authors: Joshua Evan Greene, Ahmad Issa, Duncan McCoy
papers.abstract: A tree with integer weights on its vertices presents an integral lattice called a tree lattice. We prove that if a tree lattice is positive definite, then one of the vertex elements is irreducible, i.e. determines a facet of its Voronoi polyhedron. As a corollary, we settle a 1985 conjecture of Neumann and Zagier: if a tree lattice is isometric to the lattice of integer points in Euclidean space, then the tree contains a vertex of weight one.

papers.title: Subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs
papers.abstract: Since their introduction by Karo\'nski, Scheinerman, and Singer-Cohen in 90's, random intersection graphs have attracted much attention, mostly due to their various applications. In this article, we establish a general result for the probability that a given small subgraph is present in a random intersection graph. Our theorem applies to a broad range of parameters, including regimes that have not previously been considered in the literature. Moreover, it extends known results and situates them within a broader framework, making this approach a convenient tool for comparing the probabilities of graphs in the random intersection graph model. To prove our main result, we develop new proof techniques that, to the best of our knowledge, have not previously been employed in the study of small subgraphs in random intersection graphs. Many special cases and examples are presented as well.

papers.title: A note on the hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral in Douglis analysis
papers.authors: Isidro Paulino-Basurto, Jean Marie Vilaire, Jos\'e Oscar Gonz\'alez-Cervantes, Juan Bory-Reyes
papers.abstract: Hypercomplex analysis extends classical complex analysis to Douglis algebras, replacing holomorphic functions with hyperanalytic functions, i.e., null solutions of the Douglis operator in $\mathbb R^2$ (identifying $\mathbb R^2$ with $\mathbb C$). The hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral, is one of the main actors in the hypercomplex analysis and many properties have been studied in recently decades. This paper aims to present local estimates of the hypercomplex singular Cauchy-like integral.

papers.title: Orthogonal group sections via light bulb systems
papers.abstract: For any oriented, smooth $4$--manifold $X$ diffeomorphic to $(S^2\times S^2)^{\# n}\# D^4$, this paper shows that the natural group homomorphism $$\mathrm{Mod}(X,\partial X)\to \mathrm{O}(H_2(X;\mathbb{Z}))$$ admits a section. In fact, every light bulb system in $X$ gives rise to a section, which can be characterized uniquely in terms of implanted barbell twists and implanted crossbell involutions. Moreover, all sections arising from different light bulb systems become identical after a single $S^2\times S^2$--stabilization of $X$.

papers.title: Normal approximation for subgraph counts in random intersection graphs: the case of cliques
papers.abstract: Let $X^{(r)}_n$ denote the number of copies of a complete graph $K_r$ in the random intersection graph model on $n$ vertices. We derive upper bounds on the distance between the standardized version of $X^{(r)}_n$ and the standard normal distribution, measured in both the Kolmogorov and Wasserstein metrics. We complement these results with necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality. As a byproduct, we provide precise estimates for the variance of $X^{(r)}_n$. In the process, we develop new general techniques for analysing so--called clique covers, which play a crucial role in the study of subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs.

papers.title: Supercritical Branching Random Walks on Nested Lattices
papers.abstract:
In classical models of supercritical continuous-time branching random
  walks (BRWs) on a $d$-dimensional lattice, the dimension $d$ is typically
  assumed to be fixed. When comparing the exponential growth rate
  $\lambda_0$ of a particle population in a BRW with a single branching
  source across lattices of different dimensions, a question arises whether
  it is possible to construct a family of random walks on $d$-dimensional
  lattices such that the model for a $(d+1)$-dimensional lattice
  ``inherits'' the properties of the model for a $d$-dimensional lattice in
  a meaningful sense. To address this question, the paper introduces the
  concept of a ``random walk on nested lattices'' and investigates the
  effect of the dimension $d$ on particle population growth using the
  ``inheritance'' condition. For an arbitrary symmetric random walk, a
  limit theorem is proved on the representation of the positive eigenvalue
  of the evolution operator for the mean particle numbers in terms of the
  process parameters and the dimension $d$, as the branching source
  intensity $\beta \to \infty$. The theorem shows that the influence of
  dimension persists even for very strong branching.

papers.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture and improved bounds for bipanchromatic colorings
papers.abstract: We study the bipanchromatic number $\chi_B$, introduced by Lalou et al. (Discrete Appl. Math. 391 (2026), 511-522) as the maximum number of colors in a panchromatic hypergraph coloring where every color appears at least twice. They show that merging uniquely occurring colors in a maximum panchromatic coloring gives the lower bound $\beta=\chi_P-\lceil\alpha/2\rceil \leq \chi_B$, where $\chi_P$ is the panchromatic number and $\alpha$ is the minimum number of such colors among maximum panchromatic colorings. They conjectured that $\chi_B=\beta$ and subsequently disproved it (arXiv:2610.08042). We identify the smallest counterexample, with six vertices and three hyperedges, both minimum possible. We show that the ratio bound $\chi_B/\beta<2$ is asymptotically sharp and prove minimality results for the order and hyperedge count. For $3\le\alpha<\chi_P$ we show that every integer from $\beta$ to $\chi_P-1$ occurs as $\chi_B$ while $\chi_P$ and $\alpha$ are held fixed. Furthermore, we discover that the values $|V|,\chi_P,\alpha$ directly decide whether the conjectured equality holds except when $\alpha=4$, where a matching reduction resolves the ambiguity. We derive the optimal universal lower bound $L$ depending only on $|V|,\chi_P,\alpha$ in the nontrivial regime $0<2\alpha<|V|$. Finally, we prove $\chi_B/L\le5/4$ and $\chi_B/L\le6/5+1/(5L)$, with $5/4$ sharp and $6/5$ asymptotically sharp as $L\to\infty$.

papers.title: BIBO stability in infinite dimensions: extensions and limitations of finite-dimensional theory
papers.abstract: The study of bounded-input bounded-output (BIBO) stability of infinite-dimensional systems gives rise to difficulties that do not occur in the classical finite-dimensional setting. In this paper, we resolve several questions concerning the definition and characterisation of BIBO stability in the framework of system nodes. In particular, we show that $\mathrm C^\infty$-BIBO stability need not imply $L^\infty$-BIBO stability in general, but that the two notions are equivalent when the output space is reflexive. Furthermore, we investigate to what extent classical results extend to the infinite-dimensional setting, including the relation between BIBO stability and exponential stability under controllability and observability assumptions.

papers.title: Class polynomial obstructions to canonical congruences for the smallest parts function
papers.abstract: We resolve an open conjecture by proving that the only "canonical'' Ramanujan congruence primes for the Andrews' smallest parts function, $\operatorname{spt}(n)$, are $\ell= 5, 7, 13$. Building on work of Ahlgren and Kim, we show that any such congruence forces square-index coefficients of certain weakly holomorphic forms of weight $1/2$ to vanish modulo the congruence prime. A normalized Borcherds product converts this into the vanishing of the derivative of a quotient of two oriented CM polynomials on $X_0(6)$. A quaternionic volume estimate in an Eichler order of level $6$ prevents that vanishing when a suitable inert discriminant is small. Trevi\~no's character estimate supplies such a discriminant for every prime at least $10^{11}$. The remaining range is covered by the previous calculations of Ahlgren and Kim. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

papers.title: A periodic Anderson--Bernoulli model with infinitely many spectral gaps
papers.abstract: We prove that the (almost-sure) spectrum of a periodic Anderson--Bernoulli model may enjoy infinitely many gaps. In particular, this shows that Schr\"odinger operators associated with transitive subshifts of finite type do not necessarily have finite-gap spectra. This resolves a pair of open problems posed by Damanik and the first named author. The main mechanism is the construction of a transverse heteroclinic connection within the class of Schr\"odinger transfer matrices, together with a scale-matching argument to produce a sequence of invariant multicones.

papers.title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
papers.abstract: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $\theta=\beta/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $N\theta\to\gamma>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/\theta$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $\gamma$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $\beta$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $\gamma\to\infty$.

papers.title: Sionna Bench: Towards Benchmarks in Wireless Communications
papers.authors: Gian Marti, Jakob Hoydis, Fay\c{c}al A\"it Aoudia, Sebastian Cammerer, Alexander Keller
papers.abstract: Academic research in wireless communications has no tradition of benchmarks so far. Remarkable progress in benchmark-oriented fields like machine learning suggests that the adoption of benchmarks could benefit our field. In the absence of benchmarks, however, a scientific debt has accumulated: since the academic community has not canonized specific problem setups, methods that address essentially the same problem were often developed for slightly different setups and lack a common framework for comparison. Any attempt to establish a new benchmark is faced with the challenge of resolving this debt. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) create an opportunity to do so by leveraging AI-assisted coding. This makes it possible to implement the state-of-the art at scale and to adapt it to a common framework for comparison. We present Sionna Bench to initiate benchmarks in academic wireless communications research. As a pilot study, we use the problem of MIMO-OFDM channel estimation. At the time of writing, Sionna Bench's channel estimation benchmark features twenty channel estimation methods that were implemented from ten different papers. The ability to compare methods against the state-of-the-art will be crucial for navigating the research landscape in an era where AI-generated methods coexist with human-developed algorithms.

papers.title: Recent progress in the construction of Hadamard matrices
papers.authors: Ronan Egan, Ilias Kotsireas, Stephen London, P\'adraig \'O Cath\'ain
papers.abstract:
A Hadamard matrix is a square matrix with entries $\pm 1$ whose rows are mutually orthogonal. Hadamard matrices are conjectured to exist at every order divisible by $4$; for approximately the last twenty years, the smallest open case of this conjecture was order 668.
  In August 2026, Alp\"oge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle announced Hadamard matrices at the twelve orders below $2000$ at which none was known. In this paper we verify and analyse the claimed matrices. We survey results on the existence of Hadamard matrices and list the $95$ orders up to $10\,000$ at which no Hadamard matrix is currently known. In pursuing this work we constructed Hadamard matrices at sixteen orders that were open in the published literature. We conclude with a list of open problems.

papers.title: Total $\{k\}$-domination in caterpillars: Structural properties and exact results
papers.authors: Mariana Escalante, Paola Tolomei, Mar\'ia In\'es Lopez Pujato
papers.abstract: The total $\{k\}$-domination problem ($T\{k\}DP$) seeks a minimum-weight function such that the sum of weights in every open neighborhood is at least $k$. While this problem is known to be NP-hard for general graphs, we demonstrate that for the family of caterpillars, it simplifies to the classical total domination number ($k=1$) via the identity $\gamma^{\{k\}}_t(G) = k\gamma_t(G)$. This reduction is supported by a general upper bound established for all graphs, which we prove to be tight specifically for caterpillars. The central tool for our analysis is the introduction of a $(T,R)$-representation, a one-to-one mapping that abstracts caterpillar structure into discrete vectors based on support vertex distribution and central path segment lengths. By characterizing these segments through congruence modulo 4, we derive an exact closed-form expression for the total $\{k\}$-domination number of any caterpillar graph.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Monotone Completeness Conjecture
papers.abstract: Combining a modification of the recent counterexample to the quasitrace conjecture with model-theoretic reductions due to the first author, we exhibit a counterexample to the monotone completeness conjecture. We fully reproduce the disproof of the quasitrace conjecture by a modified construction and arguments.

papers.title: Euler Time-Discretization of Funnel-Controlled Dynamics
papers.authors: Thomas Berger, Hannes Gernandt, Pushya Mitra
papers.abstract: We analyze explicit and implicit Euler discretizations of the continuous-time closed-loop dynamics generated by a funnel controller for a fully actuated nonlinear full-state system of relative degree one with scalar positive input gain. A quantitative continuous-time funnel margin provides the compactness and regularity bounds needed for the error analysis. For explicit Euler, a computable upper step-size threshold guarantees a global nodewise distance from the funnel boundary. We show that first-order convergence holds on finite time horizons and, under a~dissipativity condition (a~one-sided Lipschitz bound on the plant dominated by the funnel damping), uniformly in time. For implicit Euler, an admissible update exists for every step size and every trajectory initialized in the funnel retains a step-size-independent nodal margin. Under dissipativity, the admissible root is unique for every step size, the discrete flow is contractive, and the first-order error bound is uniform in time.

papers.title: Geometry of a class of $\varphi$-minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2\times \mathbb{R}$
papers.authors: Katianny Rosa Freitas, Jo\~ao Paulo dos Santos, Ant\'onio Mart\'inez
papers.abstract: We study a class of $\varphi$-minimal surfaces in the product space $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$, that is, weighted minimal surfaces whose corresponding weight is determined by a smooth potential function $\varphi$ that depends only on the height coordinate relative to the factor $\mathbb{R}$. Under monotonicity, concavity, and asymptotic conditions on $\varphi$, we obtain a complete classification of connected, properly embedded $\varphi$-minimal surfaces that are invariant under isometries of $\mathbb{H}^2\times\mathbb{R}$ acting trivially on $\mathbb{R}$ and by rotations or parabolic translations on $\mathbb{H}^2$. Finally, we establish several non-existence results for $\varphi$-minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{H}^2 \times \mathbb{R}$, either by using properties of the height function or by applying the tangency principle together with suitable invariant surfaces as barriers.

papers.title: Canard points in planar mass-action networks: a flux criterion, a duality, and a complete classification
papers.abstract: We determine which mass-action reaction networks on two species, one fast and one slow, admit a canard point: a singular Hopf bifurcation at a fold of the critical manifold, followed by a canard explosion. In flux coordinates, existence reduces to three linear equations, one linear inequation and a sign condition on the product of two linear forms, and the criticality of the explosion is the sign of an explicit cubic form. For four reactions with a balance matrix of full rank, both become integer polynomial conditions on the stoichiometry. A vacancy duality, which exchanges the activator-inhibitor and substrate-depletion mechanisms, preserves canard points together with their criticality. The central structural result is a mode criterion: a network has a canard point if and only if its elementary flux modes contain a sign-meeting pair and a mode carrying a fold. Hence every canard network contains a minimal one carried by at most three modes, and so by at most twelve reactions, whatever the molecularity. For complexes of molecularity at most three we enumerate all 138,754 minimal canard networks and label each exactly by the criticalities it admits. None has more than six reactions; 32 have canard points of codimension zero and no explosion; and most six-reaction networks admit both criticalities, separated by degenerate canard points. All labels rest on exact certificates.

papers.title: Low Residuals, Wrong Value: Learning the Viscosity Solution of Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs Equations with PINNs
papers.authors: Raul Jimenez, Pablo Tejerina-P\'erez, Leonid Sarieddine, Pedro Taranc\'on-\'Alvarez, Marisol Traforetti, Pau Sol\'e-Vilar\'o, Oleksii Ignatenko, Nazar Tkach, Pavlos Protopapas
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and other residual-trained solvers judge a candidate solution by the size of its sampled PDE residual. For first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations this is not sufficient: the same equation and boundary data admit Lipschitz almost-everywhere solutions that differ from the viscosity solution by $O(1)$ while violating the equation only on sets of measure zero. We study whether residual minimization selects such solutions in a fixed-horizon pursuit-evasion game whose Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs value function is known in closed form on the circle $S^1$ and on the flat tori $\mathbb{T}^{2}$ and $\mathbb{T}^{4}$. We train four neural parameterizations with ten seeds on each geometry, 120 runs in total. A standard network with periodic Fourier features converges to folded almost-everywhere solutions in all 30 runs: small residuals and the expected capture-layer gradient, yet values that are wrong over most of the domain. A network with periodicity imposed through the loss recovers the viscosity solution in one and two dimensions but becomes unreliable in four. Two parameterizations that receive the geodesic distance do substantially better: a single network fed the wrapped displacement and its distance recovers the viscosity solution in all 30 runs, while a minimum over periodic image charts succeeds in 27 of 30 and introduces a wrong-image failure mode. Finally, for the convex Hamiltonian considered here, we use the semiconcavity of the viscosity solution to build a mesh-free finite-difference test that needs only forward network evaluations; it detects the folded solutions and the harmful min-of-charts failures without access to the exact value function. A small sampled residual thus does not by itself validate a learned Hamilton-Jacobi solution; the parameterization and independent structural diagnostics can be essential for selecting the viscosity solution.

papers.title: A Brezis--Merle inequality for the biharmonic operator with Dirichlet boundary conditions in four-dimensional balls
papers.authors: Jo\~ao Marcos do \'O, Federica Sani, Victor Rafael Silva
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a Brezis-Merle type inequality for very weak solutions of the biharmonic Dirichlet problem in the four-dimensional unit ball. By combining this inequality with moving-plane arguments, we obtain uniform a priori estimates for positive solutions of semilinear biharmonic equations with exponential nonlinearities in both the subcritical and critical regimes. As an application of these estimates, we prove the existence of a positive solution by means of topological methods. We also extend the analysis to a class of non-variational cooperative systems.

papers.title: A functional central limit theorem for the KPZ equation with narrow wedge initial data
papers.authors: Raluca M. Balan, Le Chen, Jinxin Wang
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation with narrow wedge initial data. We prove a functional central limit theorem for the spatial average of the solution, which solves an open problem from Gu and Pu (2025). Our main tool is Clark-Ocone formula from Malliavin calculus, combined with an in-depth analysis of the increments of the solution. The main step is a moment bound for time increments of the normalized spatial integral. For this, we introduce a new technique, called a ``common-ray'' change of variables. Using the fact that Malliavin derivative of the solution satisfies a Chapman-Kolmogorov relation, we reduce the kernel differences at two times to spatial increments at one common time.

papers.title: Connected $\omega$-limit sets of Cournot maps: periodic orbits, realization and almost every point
papers.abstract: Let $F(x,y)=(f_2(y),f_1(x))$ be a Cournot map of the unit square, $\varphi=f_2\circ f_1$ and $\chi=f_1\circ f_2$. Linero Bas and Mu\~noz Guillermo proved that an $\omega$-limit set of $F$ with nonempty interior is connected if and only if \textup{(C1)} its two projections are connected and \textup{(C2)} $\omega_{F^2}(z)\cap\omega_{F^2}(F(z))\neq\emptyset$, and conjectured that this holds for every $\omega$-limit set. We prove the conjecture for every point $z=(x,y)$ such that $\omega_\varphi(x)$ or $\omega_\chi(y)$ is finite, and for Lebesgue almost every point $z$ of the square whenever $\varphi$ is metrically regular (every metric attractor is a periodic orbit, a solenoid, or a cycle of intervals carrying a well-behaved absolutely continuous invariant measure). Over a periodic orbit the $\omega$-limit set is a \emph{comb}, whose sections are rigid; when one projection is connected it is a point, a \emph{lattice} $(P\times J)\cup(K\times Q)$ with $P\subset K$, $Q\subset J$ and $\#P=\#Q$, or an \emph{alternating comb} of $2m$ disjoint segments. Conversely, every lattice and every alternating comb is an $\omega$-limit set of a Cournot map with piecewise linear reaction functions; the construction rests on a lemma producing exact compositions of piecewise linear maps with prescribed values. This answers, for this class, the question of Balibrea, Linero and C\'anovas of which nowhere dense sets are $\omega$-limit sets of Cournot maps. For instance, the letter H is not an $\omega$-limit set at any such point, and for metrically regular $\varphi$ the points whose $\omega$-limit set is connected, infinite, nowhere dense and not a lattice form a Lebesgue null set.

papers.title: Small sums of roots of unity: polylogarithmic exceptional sets and conditional separation
papers.abstract: We prove a polylogarithmic exceptional-set estimate for symmetric five-term sums of roots of unity of arbitrary order. More precisely, at most $O((\log(2N))^{11})$ points of the $N$-grid satisfy $|1+2\cos(2\pi x)+2\cos(2\pi y)|<\exp(-C(\log(2N))^{13})$. This implies the corresponding bound for small conjugates at the reduced conductor: outside polylogarithmically many real embeddings, every such sum is at least quasipolynomially large. The proof is unconditional and combines a polynomial-vector-field multiplicity estimate, arithmetic jet determinants, analytic propagation, and interpolation determinants for nearby grid points. As a companion result, assuming a uniform number-field $abc$ conjecture, we prove that every sum of a fixed number of distinct prime-order roots of unity has modulus at least $\exp(-\varepsilon p)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, uniformly in the exponents. That proof uses simultaneous compression of the exponents, discriminant estimates, and cyclic resultants.

papers.title: Combining Exponential and Polynomial Convergence Rates for Accelerated Extremum Seeking: A High-Order Lie Bracket Approach
papers.abstract: In this paper, we leverage the recently developed general higher-order Lie bracket approximation theory and framework for control-affine systems to show that we can design extremum seeking (ES) systems that combine flows based on: (i) first-order Lie bracket approximation, which provide an exponential convergence rate for quadratic objective functions and polynomial convergence rate for non-quadratic objective functions; and (ii) higher-order Lie bracket approximation, which provide exponential convergence rate near the minimizer even if the objective function is non-quadratic (i.e., flatter and possesses vanishing Hessian at the minimizer). Such combination provides an accelerated ES design that benefits from the polynomial decay rate farther away from the minimizer and exponential decay rate near the minimizer even for complicated nature of objective functions. We provide numerical simulations to demonstrate the results, including multi-variable and nonpolynomial flat-bottomed objective functions.

papers.title: On counterexamples to the unification of free entropy
papers.abstract: It has been a long-standing open problem to determine when two versions of Voiculescu's free entropy, $\chi$ and $\chi^*$, agree. OpenAI recently generated the first example with $-\infty < \chi < \chi^*$. We give a detailed presentation of a similar example, and explicitly show the separation between free Fisher information and the large-$n$ limit of classical Fisher information through the relationship with Wasserstein distance. We thus situate the example in the context of probability theory and information geometry.

papers.title: Quantum polynomial-time conjugacy in metabelian groups
papers.abstract:
We prove that the conjugacy problem in finitely presented metabelian groups with a fixed number of generators is solvable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time, uniformly in the defining relations of the group. Both the group presentation and the words representing the elements are part of the input.
  The main ingredient is a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for computing all multiplicative relations among a fixed number of units in a commutative affine $\mathbb Z$-algebra presented with a fixed number of variables. The algorithm reduces the problem to computations in finite-dimensional algebras over $\mathbb Q$ and finite rings by identifying the lattice of exponent vectors whose corresponding products are algebraic over the coefficient field. An effective arithmetic splitting combines the rational and finite-ring computations. The proof uses effective bounds for polynomial equations, algorithms for finite-dimensional commutative algebras, quantum integer factorization, and finite abelian hidden-subgroup algorithms.

papers.title: From Hermite Chaos to an Attractive Log-Gas: Explicit High-Rank Limits of Iterated-Logarithm and Tail Constants
papers.abstract:
Let $Z$ be a standard Hermite process of order $m\ge2$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$. For $d<H-1/2$, let $Y$ be the variance-normalized version of the weighted integral $\int_0^1 x^{-d}\,\mathrm dZ(x)$. Its right tail satisfies $
  \log\Pr\{Y>t\}\sim
  -\frac12\left(\frac{t}{\Lambda_m}\right)^{2/m}, t\to\infty, $ where the positive constant $\Lambda_m$ admits an infinite-dimensional variational representation. The same constant governs the sharp law of the iterated logarithm for weighted sums of nonlinear functions of long-memory Gaussian sequences. A general closed-form evaluation at finite order is not known.
  As $m\to\infty$ with $H$ and $d$ fixed, the normalized constants $\sqrt{m!}\,\Lambda_m$ decrease to an explicit positive function of $H$ and $d$, with relative error $O(m^{-1})$. This function also gives a lower bound for the normalized constant at every finite order. An exact R\'enyi variational representation at each order yields, in the high-rank limit, the entropy--energy variational problem of an attractive logarithmic gas. The limiting free energy is evaluated through the Selberg integral and the Barnes $G$ function.
  For $d\le0$, convergence remains uniform up to the memory boundary $H=1/2$. After division by the square-root boundary factor $\sqrt{2H-1}$, the high-rank and boundary limits commute. Their common value is explicit; for constant weights it equals $2^{3/2}\pi^3G(1/2)^8=2^{11/6}\pi e\,\mathsf A^{-12}$, where $\mathsf A$ is the Glaisher--Kinkelin constant. The quadratic and cubic coefficients of the fixed-order expansion of the normalized constant as $H\uparrow1$ converge, as $m\to\infty$, to those of the explicit limiting function. Global finite-order bounds and a concentrating-weight limit complement the main result.

papers.title: Convolution Quadrature with Adaptive History Compression for Variable-Order Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a fully implicit fast method for semilinear variable-order fractional reaction--diffusion equations with periodic fractional diffusion and exponential-transition Scarpi memory. A Volterra-resolvent analysis establishes local well-posedness and temporal regularity estimates that describe the weak initial singularity. Backward Euler convolution quadrature combined with Fourier pseudospectral discretization achieves mesh-uniform stability and positive-time first-order convergence. To accelerate the scheme, we utilize Cauchy--FFT weight recovery and adaptive blockwise sum-of-exponentials compression, which significantly reduces the cost of history evaluation under local error control. A logarithmic perturbation bound quantifies the effects of weight recovery, history compression, and inexact nonlinear solves, giving tolerance conditions that preserve the convergence order. Numerical experiments confirm the first-order accuracy and demonstrate that the accelerated method efficiently resolves long-time spatial patterns at a substantially reduced computational cost.

papers.title: The integral $K_0$-ring of the stack of smooth hyperelliptic curves
papers.abstract: We compute the integral $K_0$-ring of the moduli stack $\mathscr H_g$ of smooth hyperelliptic curves of genus $g\ge2$ over a field of characteristic zero. We show that it is a free abelian group of rank $8g+2$ for even $g$ and $8g+4$ for odd $g$. We use the isotypic decomposition of the $K_0$ of a related $\mu_{g+1}$-gerbe to obtain presentations for both even and odd $g$'s from the standard quotient presentation of $\mathscr H_g$. Thus, our technique differs from the $CH^\bullet(\mathscr H_g)$ computations of Edidin--Fulghesu, Fulghesu--Viviani, Di Lorenzo, and the $K_0(\mathscr M_2)$ computation of Edidin--Hu. Using Pagani's description of the inertia stack of $\mathscr H_g$, we apply Riemann--Roch to interpret the rank of $K_0(\mathscr H_g)$ as the number of inertia components. Finally, we compare the $K_0$ and Chow rings of $\mathscr H_g$ through the gamma-filtration and give presentations to the associated graded rings $\operatorname{gr}_{\gamma}K_0(\mathscr H_g)\otimes\mathbb F_p$ for every prime $p$.

papers.title: Ordered frequency in relatively hyperbolic groups
papers.abstract: We study word frequencies along infinite strings whose finite prefixes lie in a regular language of geodesic representatives of group elements. Let \((G,\mathcal H)\) be a non-elementary relatively hyperbolic pair, and suppose that, over a finite symmetric generating set, there is a prefix-closed regular language containing exactly one shortest word representing each element of \(G\). Modeling this language using a finite-state Markov chain, we define a probability measure on the space of infinite strings whose finite prefixes are words belonging to this language. Each such string labels a geodesic ray emanating from the identity. We show there is a continuous surjection from this space onto the Bowditch boundary, and the pushforward of the probability measure under this map is a Patterson--Sullivan probability obtained as a weak limit of weighted counts of group elements. For a word \(w\), the ordered frequency of \(w\) along a given labeled ray is the limiting proportion of consecutive nonoverlapping tuples of length \(|w|\) that exactly spell \(w\). For almost every infinite string under the constructed measure, these frequencies exist simultaneously for all nonempty geodesic words, with no restriction on their lengths. Consequently, almost every boundary point with respect to this Patterson--Sullivan probability is the endpoint of at least one such ray along which all these frequencies exist. In particular, after possibly enlarging the generating set, these results apply when the peripheral subgroups are virtually abelian.

papers.title: Analytical solution of electromagnetic heating in a stratified absorbing medium
papers.abstract: We consider the temperature evolution in a skin tissue when it is exposed to an electromagnetic wave. The heating is caused by the absorbed power as the electromagnetic wave attenuates inside the skin. In many applications, the characteristic depth of attenuation is small in comparison with the lateral size of the electromagnetic beam. Because of this separation of length scales, the lateral heat conduction is negligible at leading order. Previously, we studied electromagnetic heating in a skin of a single homogeneous layer. We derived the leading-term analytical solution and the asymptotic corrections up to the second order for lateral heat conduction and for oblique incidence. In this study, we derive the analytical solution in the case of perpendicular incidence on a stratified skin tissue with a layer-specific profile for electromagnetic attenuation. It should be emphasized that in the current study, the heat capacity and conductivity are still uniform over the entire skin tissue; only the electromagnetic attenuation is stratified resulting in a layer-specific heating profile.

papers.title: A Pittel-type limit law for the largest component of random $d$-uniform hypergraphs: enumeration and excursions
papers.abstract:
Let $H_d(n,M)$ be a $d$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ vertices and $M$ hyperedges. In the critical window $M=\frac{n}{d(d-1)}(1+\lambda n^{-1/3})+O(1)$, its largest component $L_n$ satisfies $$n^{-2/3}L_n\xrightarrow{\mathcal L} \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}\bigl((d-1)^{1/3}a,\lambda(d-1)^{-2/3}\bigr).$$ (Here $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}(x,\mu)$ denotes the limiting law of the largest component of the critical random graph established by Pittel (2001).) The proof rests on two pillars.
  First, a bivariate exponential formula gives the exact finite-size law of $L_n$. Subsequently, cancellation of the orders $n,n^{2/3},n^{1/3}$ in the tree normalization determines the series of rooted hypertrees, then that of unicyclic components and its singular expansions at the radius of convergence $\rho_d$. These calculations are exact; they serve the fixed-excess identities and the cancellation mechanism, and nothing more: no unproved uniformity in the excess enters the proof of the limit law.
  Next, by exploration and martingale approximation, the ordered sizes converge unconditionally to the excursion lengths of a Brownian motion with parabolic drift. A monotone coupling transfers the law to $H_d(n,M)$. The limit law is then identified with Pittel's law by a Brownian rescaling: if $h=d-1$, it suffices to multiply lengths by $h^{-1/3}$ and evaluate at parameter $\lambda h^{-2/3}$. The exact Poisson representation dispenses with any separate deconditioning.
  We also formulate a two-regime $d$-uniform Bollobas bound (Wright for fixed $\ell$, global combinatorial beyond that), and explicitly indicate why neither regime alone suffices to close the analytic route.

papers.title: Explicit sharp gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincar\'e inequality and fundamental gaps for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian operator
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the gradient stability of the $L^{p}$-Poincar\'e inequality with explicit constants on bounded convex domains for any $1<p<\infty$. These estimates control the distance to the optimizers in the strongest possible norm with the optimal stability exponent $\max\{2,p\}$, exhibiting the same phenomenon initially observed by Figalli and Zhang [FZ22a] for the $L^p$-Sobolev inequality. As a result, we also confirm the conjecture posed by Fleckinger-Pell\'e and Tak\'a\v{c} [FPT02, Section 8]. We then apply the inequality to obtain positive fundamental gap estimates in terms of the inradius for the Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian.

papers.title: PL standardness of the four-pentachoron census sphere Q
papers.abstract: We prove that the four-pentachoron homotopy \(4\)-sphere \(Q\) singled out in the census of Burke, Burton and Spreer is PL homeomorphic to the standard \(4\)-sphere. The key construction identifies the compact exterior of an explicit locally flat \(2\)-sphere in an auxiliary 39-vertex model of \(Q\) with the exterior of Budney, Burton and Hillman, then certifies its fibration by a normal cut followed by a relative collapse. The exterior identification uses finite checked moves, an exact regular-neighbourhood construction and a PL lemma controlling the passage through an ideal triangulation. Cutting the compact exterior along the specified normal hypersurface gives a manifold that collapses onto one boundary copy of the punctured \(3\)-torus in 209,144 elementary pairs; a marked product lemma identifies the cut as a product. The resulting integral monodromy realizes \(Q\) as a Cappell--Shaneson filling whose two surgery framings are standard by Gompf's results. The fibration certificate is independent of Issa's earlier PL-compatible constructions. Combined with the published census, the result establishes standardness for every homotopy \(4\)-sphere triangulated with at most four pentachora.

papers.title: Graphexon Mean Field Games on Large Network Limits
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes graphexon mean field games (GXMFG) on large network limits. By considering edge distributions of a sequence of finite graphs, we define the empirical graphexon measures and study their subsequential weak limits in a graphexon space consisting of all symmetric probability measures on $[0,1]^{2d}$. This concept of network limits extends graphon theory to general, not necessarily dense, networks. To formulate the game using the graphexon limit, we exploit a useful property that a probability measure on a product space is the product of a probability kernel and a marginal distribution. Based on such graph limits and the probability kernel of the associated graphexon measure, we derive the GXMFG equations, and present a detailed analysis for the linear-quadratic case. For linear-quadratic models with finite populations residing over large networks, we use the GXMFG equations to construct decentralized strategies, for which an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium property is established.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture
papers.abstract: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture asserts that the ground-state particle density and total current determine the scalar potential up to an additive constant and the vector potential up to a gauge transformation. We give three counterexamples for two spinless fermions in the physically relevant setting of three spatial dimensions. In each, a Hamiltonian $H^{v,\mathbf{A}}$ has a nondegenerate ground state with identically zero total current but nonzero magnetic field. Complex conjugation then yields a second Hamiltonian $H^{v,-\mathbf{A}}$, with the same scalar potential and interaction, whose ground state has the same density and the same zero current, while the magnetic field is reversed. The first two examples are noninteracting. One is explicit, with a smooth bounded vector potential and a Gaussian density. The other has smooth bounded scalar and vector potentials in the standard potential spaces. The third example has Coulomb repulsion with unit coupling, an isotropic harmonic scalar potential, and Dirac monopole fields of magnetic charge $\pm 1/2$. The monopole example uses vector potentials defined on separate spatial patches, since these fields are not curls of globally defined smooth vector potentials.

papers.title: Chaotic CLT using Poisson Fourth Moment Theorem and Graph Theory
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider the parabolic Anderson model and the hyperbolic Anderson model in dimension 1, driven by a time-independent L\'evy noise, which is either white, or colored with integrable coloration kernel $\kappa$. Using a Poisson version of the Fourth Moment Theorem due to D\"obler, Vidotto and Zheng (2018), we prove that the spatial integral of the solution satisfies a central limit theorem. We prove that this result also holds for the hyperbolic Anderson model in dimension $d=2$, if in addition $\kappa$ is bounded. To estimate the fourth cumulant of the projection of the spatial integral on a fixed chaos, we develop a novel technique using graph theory, which allows us to handle some intricate integrals involving the modified contractions.

papers.title: $L^{p}$-parabolicity of Riemannian manifolds
papers.authors: Alexander Grigor'yan, Leandro F. Pessoa, Alberto G. Setti
papers.abstract: We describe the $L^p$-parabolicity of a Riemannian manifold in terms of a unified theory of nonlinear $L^p$-capacities, for the whole range $1\leq p\leq \infty$. For example, the \(L^{1}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to the usual notion of parabolicity/recurrence, while \(L^{2}\)-parabolicity is equivalent to biparabolicity. For any $1\leq p\leq \infty,$ the $L^p$-parabolicity turns out to be equivalent to the $L^q$-Liouville property for positive superharmonic functions, where $p$ and $q$ are H\"older conjugate exponents. We also provide a new capacitary characterization of the $L^1$-Liouville property. Finally we obtain an almost optimal volume growth condition for the $L^p$-parabolicity for $1<p\leq 2$ as well as a sharp volume condition for all $1<p<\infty$ for manifolds of non-negative Ricci curvature and for model manifolds.

papers.title: Michael Rabin's fingerprints across the theory of computation
papers.abstract: Michael O. Rabin was a major founder and leader of theoretical computer science. He died on April 14, 2026, at the age of 94. This paper aims to survey the wide scope and lasting impact of his research.

papers.title: Monomial Moving Zeros for the Heat Semigroup: An Explicit Finite-Order Differential Hierarchy
papers.abstract:
Let $P_t=\exp(t\D^2/2)$ be the heat semigroup. For every integer $k\geq2$ and parameter $\rho\in\C$, we construct an entire function $\Gamma_{\rho,k}$ whose heat evolution has the prescribed moving zero $x=\rho t^k$ and constant spatial flux there: \[
  (P_t\Gamma_{\rho,k})(\rho t^k)=0,
  \qquad
  \partial_x(P_t\Gamma_{\rho,k})(\rho t^k)=1. \] The initial function is explicit, \[
  \Gamma_{\rho,k}(x)
  =x\sum_{q\geq0}\frac{(-2^k\rho x^{2k-1})^q}{q!}
  \frac{(kq)!}{((2k-1)q+1)!}, \] and is a generalized hypergeometric function whose entire-function order is strictly below two. Most importantly, it is annihilated by an explicit polynomial-coefficient differential operator of order $2k-1$. Thus every monomial moving boundary admits a finite-order stationary realization after a natural boundary-flux selection, even though the naive order-$k$ family $\D^k+a x^{k-1}$ already fails to produce the exact boundary at $k=4$. No minimality claim is made: the result gives a universal finite-order hierarchy, while the least possible differential order remains open and depends on the choice made inside the inverse kernel.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
papers.authors: Ricardo Freire, Cristian Gonz\'alez-Riquelme, Claudio Mu\~noz, Felipe Poblete, Vicente Salinas
papers.abstract:
Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function
  \[
  H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, \Phi_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du,
  \]
  where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density
  \[
  \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds.
  \]
  The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$.
  We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates.
