  Building on the PhiBE approximation (Zhu, 2024; Zhu et al., 2025), we propose iterative algorithms to approximate the optimal $Q$-function in both model-based and model-free settings using only discrete-time off-policy data. Under linear function approximation, we establish error bounds and explicit convergence rates for the algorithm in the popoluation level. The finite-data algorithm is evaluated numerically.

papers.title: Why Hadamard states?
papers.abstract: In QFT on curved spacetime, the Hadamard condition is often presented as a necessary condition on 'physically reasonable' states of the quantum field, and plays a central role in many theoretical and foundational applications - ranging from proofs of the renormalizability of Wick polynomials to derivations of the Hawking temperature. Yet despite this, the philosophical and foundational underpinnings of the Hadamard condition remain murky. I critically discuss existing motivations for the Hadamard condition in the literature, before arguing in favour of an alternative motivation for the Hadamard condition, according to which it is best understood as a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a well-defined operator product of a certain form on a sufficiently large space of observables of the quantum field, satisfying a variety of further conditions. This clarifies the role and status of the Hadamard condition, including its relationship to the equivalence principle, to well-definedness of physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator, and the sense in which Hadamard states are 'vacuum-like'.

papers.title: A mass-type invariant for smooth metric measure spaces and its relation with the fractional Yamabe problem
papers.authors: Sergio Almaraz, Levi Lopes de Lima, Shaodong Wang
papers.abstract: On asymptotically Schwarzschild smooth metric measure spaces modeled on the Euclidean half-space, we define a new mass-type invariant analogous to the ADM mass of an asymptotically flat manifold. We prove that this invariant is independent of the choice of admissible asymptotic coordinates. We further show that it fits into a very general framework for mass-type invariants and we also isolate static equations for smooth metric measure spaces under natural boundary conditions. For smooth metric measure spaces obtained through a generalized stereographic projection using the Green's function associated with the fractional Yamabe problem, we identify the mass with the constant term in the asymptotic expansion of the Green's function. This identification gives a geometric interpretation of the constant appearing in the fractional Yamabe problem and recasts its conjectured positivity as a positive-mass-type question.

papers.title: Beyond Mutual Information: Extension Profiles and Shape Functions of Random Variable Pairs
papers.abstract:
We study the extension profile of a pair of jointly distributed finite-valued random variables $(X,Y)$, defined as the set of all triples of numbers \[ ( H(X|W), H(Y|W), I(X:Y|W) ) \] obtained by extending the pair with an auxiliary random variable $W$. This object captures structural properties of a joint distribution that are not determined by the entropies of $X$ and $Y$ and their mutual information.
  We associate with the extension profile its \emph{shape function} defined in terms of the Legendre--Fenchel transform of the profile's lower boundary. We establish upper and lower bounds on the shape function in terms of classical information-theoretic quantities. For random pairs $(X,Y)$ whose joint distribution is uniform on its support, we relate the shape function to combinatorial and spectral properties of the associated bipartite support graph. We show that for random pairs uniformly distributed on the edges of balanced expander graphs, the shape function is within $O(\log H(XY))$ of the pointwise infimum over all pairs, which proves the conjecture stated in [MR26].
  These results connect the extension profile with non-Shannon-type information inequalities, G\'acs--K\"orner common information, and spectral graph theory. We apply these techniques to study an approximate version of a question posed by Zhen Zhang ([Zha03]) concerning the characterization of pairs with maximally non-extractable mutual information.

papers.title: A Littlewood-Richardson Rule for Forest Polynomials
papers.abstract: The forest polynomials $\mathfrak{P}_a$ of Nadeau-Tewari form a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of $\mathbb{Z}[x_1,x_2,\ldots]$ whose role for the cohomology of the quasisymmetric flag variety parallels that of Schubert polynomials for the classical flag variety. Nonnegativity of the structure constants $\beta_{a,b}^c$ in $\mathfrak{P}_a \mathfrak{P}_b = \sum_c \beta_{a,b}^c \mathfrak{P}_c$ is known, but no Littlewood-Richardson-style enumerative rule has been available. We give such a rule: $\beta_{a,b}^c$ counts pairs of forest RC graphs of forest-codes $a$ and $b$ whose lift product lands on a forest RC graph of forest-code and weight both equal to $c$. The same rule descends to the cup product on $H^\bullet(\mathrm{QFl}_n)$. The proof introduces a squash product $\boxtimes$ on RC graphs, which on full Grassmannian RC graphs of a fixed height recovers the plactic monoid, a multiplactic algebra $\mathcal{M}_n$ that models Schubert polynomial multiplication, and a lift product $*$ on RC graphs whose quasi-crystal structure, in the framework of Cain-Guilherme-Malheiro, transports the Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence through the computation. The row-decomposition machinery on RC graphs that underlies these constructions is developed in a companion paper.

papers.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the computation of transform pairs
papers.authors: Kaitlynn Lilly (Department of Applied Mathematics, University of Washington), Thomas Trogdon (Department of Applied Mathematics, University of Washington)
papers.abstract: We develop a unified methodology that integrates spectral theory, Riemann-Hilbert problems, and inverse scattering theory for the construction and numerical evaluation of transform pairs associated with linear variable-coefficient partial differential equations. The approach combines analytical formulae with numerical methods for ordinary differential equations and Riemann-Hilbert problems, yielding a hybrid analytical-numerical strategy for working with these transforms. Results are presented for transforms arising in the Dirac equation, demonstrating accurate computations, even in the presence of discontinuous coefficients.

papers.title: Noise Sensitivity Governed by Continuous-Time Random Walks on the Symmetric Group
papers.abstract: We study the noise sensitivity of Boolean functions on the symmetric group $S_n$, where noise is induced by running a continuous-time Markov chain on $S_n$. We investigate the noise sensitivity of several fundamental functions, including the parity function and analogues of the dictator function. We focus, in particular, on the case where the underlying Markov chain is an interchange process on the complete graph. We establish comparison results between noise sensitivity with respect to the interchange process on the complete graph and the weighted interchange process on any connected graph. We also show that the indicator function of long cycles is noise sensitive under the interchange process on each of these graphs. Finally, using the fact that the interchange process on the complete graph $K_n$ is the continuous-time random walk generated by all transpositions, we prove that noise sensitivity is preserved when the noise source is changed to the continuous-time random walk generated by all $s$-cycles, where $s$ is even and $2<s\ll n$.

papers.title: Debiased parametric inference for regime-switching jump diffusions with infinite variation jumps
papers.abstract: We study high-frequency inference for an ergodic regime-switching jump diffusion with locally stable infinite-variation jumps. The state and the finite-state regime are observed on the same grid. The mesh satisfies \(h_n\to0\), while the horizon satisfies \(T_n=nh_n\to\infty\). We estimate structural drift and diffusion parameters in the presence of unknown regime-specific L\'evy measures. For a common activity index \(1<\beta<8/5\), we remove two leading jump biases from each regime's truncated variation. We then combine the diffusion estimator with estimated signed tail means in an adaptive drift contrast. We prove joint asymptotic normality at rates \(\sqrt{T_n}\) and \(\sqrt n\), together with feasible studentization. The growing horizon requires uniform control of the debiasing remainders and random denominators over increasing regime exposures. It also produces an explicit L\'evy-measure term in the drift covariance. A fixed-grid median stabilizes the two-step correction without changing its first-order limit. We study finite-sample behavior by simulation and apply the method to 127.5 hours of cattle sensor data. In the application, jaw-activity labels are recorded by a device separate from the sensor that measures the state process.

papers.title: On the range of competing random walks
papers.abstract: We consider $N$ independent random walks $X^1,\dots,X^N$ in the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and prove limit theorems for the competitive range $\mathcal{R}_n^k$ of the $k$-th random walk $X^k$, which corresponds to the number of distinct sites that it has discovered before any of the other $X^\ell$, $\ell\ne k$, up to time $n$. This is a natural object to study foraging mechanisms in population ecology, in which context it is also natural to ask how the effect of competition for the access to resources affects the number of resources consumed by each individual. We work with random walks in the domain of attraction of a $\beta$-stable law and focus on the regime $d/\beta\in[1,3/2)$, in which classical results for the range show that the fluctuations are described by the renormalized self-intersection local time of the limiting process. We establish a central limit theorem in which a competition term emerges, thus answering the two previous questions we asked. We end the paper with a brief discussion on the remaining regimes $d/\beta\ge3/2$, in which the fluctuations are Gaussian and are not affected by the competition, and $d/\beta<1$ in which no strong law of large numbers holds and we expect the effect of the competition to strongly affect the first-order asymptotics.

papers.title: On algebraic and arithmetic properties of monoids of product-$K$ sequences
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and $K$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. A sequence over $G$ is a finite collection of terms from $G$, where repetition is allowed, and the order is disregarded. A product-$K$ sequence is a sequence whose terms can be ordered such that their product in $G$ belongs to $K$. The set $\mathcal B_K (G)$ of all product-$K$ sequences over $G$ forms a monoid, called the monoid of product-$K$ sequences, under the operation of sequence concatenation. In this paper, we investigate the algebraic and arithmetic properties of the monoid $\mathcal B_K (G)$. Among our main results, we provide precise characterizations of when $\mathcal B_K (G)$ satisfies key properties, namely being (transfer) Krull, a (seminormal) C-monoid, or (half-)factorial. After that, we study the Isomorphism Problem for monoids of product-$K$ sequences. Our results generalize existing frameworks, making them applicable to both the classical abelian and the more recently developed non-abelian settings.

papers.title: A category of locally convex Lie algebroids
papers.abstract: We study first-order locally convex Lie algebroids in the setting of Bastiani calculus. The first-order condition is automatic in finite rank, but is an additional regularity hypothesis for general locally convex vector bundles. We define sheaves of scalar-valued and vector-valued Lie algebroid forms as fiberwise continuous alternating maps with smooth local representatives. Morphisms are defined by requiring the induced pullback on inverse-image sheaves of scalar-valued forms to commute with the Lie algebroid differentials. We prove that these algebroids form a category, study representations and cohomology sheaves, and show that the Lie algebroids and morphisms of locally convex Lie groupoids belong to this category. We also give two applications. For a compact manifold $K$, the current algebroid $C^\infty(K,A)\to C^\infty(K,M)$ of a first-order Banach Lie algebroid $A\to M$ is a first-order Fr\'echet Lie algebroid, provided $M$ admits local addition. Finally, we prove a Banach Lie II theorem: a morphism from the Lie algebroid of a locally convex Lie groupoid to that of a Banach-Lie groupoid, both with Hausdorff source fibers, integrates uniquely to a groupoid morphism when the source groupoid is source-connected and source-simply connected.

papers.title: Isometries between C$^*$-algebras with finite corank
papers.abstract: We give a characterization of linear isometries with finite corank between two arbitrary unital C$^*$-algebras in terms of Jordan $^*$-homomorphisms and ``finite-dimensional remainders''. Also, the corresponding results are given for linear isometries and linear order embeddings between self-adjoint parts of C$^*$-algebras. In the finite-dimensional case, we give new examples of linear isometries between matrix algebras.

papers.title: A complete curve of genus 5 in the moduli space of curves of genus 3 and related questions
papers.abstract: Let M_3 be the coarse moduli space of smooth complex projective curves of genus 3. Through a general point of M_3, we construct a smooth complete curve of genus 21 and gonality 7, and a singular complete curve whose normalization has genus 19 and gonality 6. We also construct a Hodge-generic complete trigonal curve of geometric genus 5 in M_3.

papers.title: Sharp Riesz and reverse Riesz inequalities for degenerate elliptic operators of Grushin type
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp $L^p$ ranges of the Riesz transform and the reverse Riesz inequality for a class of power-degenerate elliptic operators of Grushin type. When the degenerate variable has dimension at least two, the Riesz transform is bounded throughout the reflexive range. In dimension one, a capacity-driven transition occurs: weak degeneracy produces a sharp finite upper endpoint, whereas strong degeneracy separates the two half-lines and restores the full range. The reverse inequality displays a different sharp phenomenon. In the weakly degenerate one-dimensional regime it holds throughout the reflexive range except at a single Hardy-critical exponent, while in all remaining regimes it holds for every $1<p<\infty$.

papers.title: Finite Group Reduction of the DR/DZ Hierarchies
papers.authors: Si-Qi Liu, Youjin Zhang, Tianwen Zhong
papers.abstract: We show that the finite group reduction of the Dubrovin-Zhang/Double Ramification hierarchy associated with a semisimple CohFT preserves its bihamiltonian structure and its tau structure. By applying this result to the orbifold Gromov-Witten theory with the target $\mathbb{P}^1_{2,2,2,2}$, we obtain two non-equivalent integrable hierarchies which can be associated with the Frobenius manifold structure on the Hurwitz space $M_{1;1}$, and we show that one of them is equivalent to the genus one topological recursion.

papers.title: $H^2(\Omega)$ A Priori Error Bounds for Boundary-Adapted PINNs Solving Elliptic Dirichlet Problems
papers.authors: Nathanael Tepakbong, Jun Fan, Xiang Zhou, Ding-Xuan Zhou
papers.abstract: We study the numerical resolution of uniformly elliptic Dirichlet boundary value problems (BVPs) by minimization of the PDE residual over a hypothesis space of Neural Networks made to satisfy exactly the boundary conditions through multiplication by a user-defined \emph{distance-to-boundary approximation} $\rho$. While an $L^2(\partial\Omega)$ boundary penalty cannot generally guarantee $H^2(\Omega)$ error control, we show that exact enforcement can, provided $\rho$ is chosen appropriately. More precisely, we identify a sharp sufficient condition on $\rho$ preserving the regularity needed for $H^2(\Omega)$ error control, provide practical constructions of such $\rho$ for general smooth domains $\Omega$, and refer to the resulting networks as \emph{boundary-adapted}. For boundary-adapted Rectified Quadratic Unit (ReQU) and hyperbolic tangent (tanh) networks, we then derive explicit high-probability $H^2(\Omega)$ convergence rates by combining approximation-theoretic and statistical-learning arguments, making explicit the dependence on $\rho$. Numerical experiments support our theoretical results, showing that appropriate choices of $\rho$ improve accuracy and convergence, while poorly chosen distance functions can substantially degrade the solution. Our proof also yields new VC-dimension bounds for hypothesis spaces of higher-order derivatives of ReQU and tanh networks, together with new approximation bounds for shallow ReQU networks in higher-order Sobolev norms, all of which are of important independent interest.

papers.title: Self-Similar Solutions of the Two-Dimensional Incompressible Euler Equation from Large Initial Data
papers.abstract: Given $0<a<1$ and any $C^1$, divergence-free, $(-a)$-homogeneous vector field $u_0$ on the punctured plane, we construct a forward self-similar solution of the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on the plane with initial datum $u_0$. No smallness or sign condition is required. The solution is obtained as a vanishing-dissipation limit of hypodissipative self-similar profiles. The key estimate is a uniform vorticity profile bound in the critical Lorentz space $L^{\frac{2}{1+a},\infty}$. The resulting velocity has locally finite energy and converges strongly to $u_0$ locally in $L^2$ as time approaches zero. The vorticity preserves its distribution function and converges strongly to the initial vorticity locally in $L^{\frac{2}{1+a}-}$ as time approaches zero.

papers.title: Skeleton Chordalities
papers.abstract:
We study new higher-dimensional analogs of graph chordality and review the existing ones. Our main results for simplicial complexes are:
  (1) $\Delta$ skeleton-E-chordal $\Rightarrow$ $\Delta^\vee$ vertex-decomposable $\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$ skeleton-clique-chordal. Moreover, for subflag complexes, $\Delta$ skeleton-E-chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ $\Delta^\vee$ vertex-decomposable. (For $d=1$ this boils down to ``$G$ chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ $G^\vee$ vertex-decomposable'', a result closely related to Fr\"oberg's theorem.)
  (2) For subflag complexes, $\Delta$ is skeleton-E-chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ it splits as $\Delta = \Delta_1 \cup \Delta_2$, with each $\Delta_i$ a skeleton-E-chordal induced subcomplex of $\Delta$, and with $\Delta_1 \cap \Delta_2$ a complex whose $1$-skeleton is a clique. (This generalizes ``$G$ chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ $G$ splits as a union of chordal graphs that intersect in a common clique'').
  (3) $\Delta$ skeleton-E-chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ every nonempty induced subcomplex of $\Delta$ has a skeleton-E-simplicial vertex. (Generalizes ``$G$ chordal $\Leftrightarrow$ every nonempty induced subgraph has a simplicial vertex''.)
  (4) $\Delta$ underclosed $\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$ skeleton-weakly-chordal and weakly-closed. (Generalizes ``$G$ interval $\Rightarrow$ $G$ chordal and co-comparability''.)
  (5) All pure E-chordal complexes are vertex-chordal; all pure mid-chordal complexes are weakly-vertex-chordal; all pure very-weakly-chordal complexes are weakly-ridge-chordal. (This expands Bigdeli, Yazdan-Pour and Zaare-Nahandi's work on ridge-chordality.)

papers.title: An infinite family of counterexamples to the Polycirculant Conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove the Polycirculant Conjecture, which states that every transitive 2-closed permutation group is non-elusive, i.e. contains a derangement of prime order. In fact, we prove a stronger result, answering a long-standing question of Maru\v{s}i\v{c} and Jordan: there exists a vertex-transitive graph admitting no semiregular automorphism. To do so, we employ recently developed methods of Chen et al. for constructing elusive groups via non-split extensions, allowing us to construct an elusive group $7^6.\mathrm{PSU}_3(3)$ of degree 16,464. We show that this group is the full automorphism group of seven of its orbital graphs and hence is 2-closed. Our example extends to infinitely many counterexamples of the Polycirculant Conjecture, and infinitely many vertex-transitive graphs admitting no semiregular automorphism.

papers.title: Computable Quantification in Reflective Grounded Arithmetic
papers.abstract: Informal statements of G\"odel's incompleteness theorems often run: "any consistent formal system with arithmetic has true but unprovable statements." That reading assumes a classical notion of truth, under which a universal statement is true as soon as each of its numeral instances is. This paper presents reflective grounded arithmetic (RGA), in which truth is grounded in computation and universal quantification is grounded reflectively: a universal statement is true when the system's own proof search certifies its schematic instance, and false when the system refutes one numeral instance. RGA allows recursive definitions without restriction and proves addition, multiplication and Ackermann's function total as theorems quantified inside the system. RGA is consistent, and it is complete for its own, grounded notion of truth: every well-formed statement that evaluates to true is provable. G\"odel's theorems still hold for RGA, as a companion paper shows. The statements that classical reasoning calls true but unprovable have every numeral instance provable but no certified schematic instance, so they are ungrounded in RGA; read instance by instance, in an $\omega$-semantics for which RGA is also sound, they are true. All results are machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL: soundness and consistency; completeness for grounded truth, open statements included; $\omega$-soundness and $\omega$-consistency; that grounded truth is recursively enumerable and RGA represents exactly the recursively enumerable sets; and $\omega$-incompleteness. The logic is neither classical nor intuitionistic: double negation is eliminable as an entailment, excluded middle fails wherever a statement has no boolean value, RGA has the disjunction and witness properties, and the deduction theorem holds exactly at provably decided hypotheses.

papers.title: Jacobi polynomials on the simplex of Hermitian matrices and zonal spherical functions on partial flag manifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce the radial part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on partial flag manifolds and study its eigenfunctions, the elementary zonal spherical functions. These eigenfunctions can be related to orthogonal polynomials on the simplex of Hermitian matrices invariant under simultaneous conjugation by unitary matrices with respect to the complex matrix-variate Dirichlet distribution. Using a matrix-variate version of Koornwinder's method for constructing orthogonal polynomials in multiple variables from orthogonal polynomials in one variable, we construct a family of pairwise orthogonal polynomials in terms of Hermitian Jacobi polynomials and conjecture that some of these are elementary zonal spherical functions. Furthermore, we recall the definition of multivariate Schur polynomials and show how they can be used to obtain information about elementary zonal spherical functions. In particular, we give some partial results in the direction that the radial part of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on partial flag manifolds is strongly triangular with respect to the multivariate Schur polynomials. The elementary zonal spherical functions can then be constructed by applying the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation process to the multivariate Schur functions.

papers.title: Near full groups of bounded type, II
papers.abstract: We study when a finitely generated group of bounded type contains the AF alternating group of the tail groupoid of its defining Bratteli diagram. This containment is an input to the full group completion theorem of Part I. We give sufficient conditions for this containment, in which selectors separate inherited diagonal actions, and an exact criterion for finite regular coverings. In the covering case, the intersection with the AF alternating group is the centralizer of the deck transformations commuting with the adjoined AF permutations. The formula classifies all subgroups between the canonical lift of the base AF alternating group and the AF alternating group of the covering. In particular, the lift is maximal exactly when the deck group has prime order, and cyclic coverings yield finitely generated groups whose intersections with the AF alternating group of the covering realize these subgroups. We identify fragmentations that produce the required selectors. For periodic fragmentations of the directed generator in the modified Fabrykowski--Gupta group, surjectivity of the activity subspace onto each pair of consecutive coordinates gives containment with absorption delay at most two. A five-periodic example also satisfies this condition, although its activity subspace has dual distance two. The original four-periodic fragmentation group has index four in its topological full group.

papers.title: Geometric Methods for Stochastic Dynamical Systems: A Concise Introduction
papers.authors: Jinqiao Duan, Ting Gao, Qiao Huang, Yuanfei Huang
papers.abstract:
There is growing interest in stochastic dynamics in the applied mathematics, interdis-ciplinary science, and artificial intelligence communities. This book is written primarilyfor applied mathematicians and scientists who may not have the necessary backgroundto go directly to advanced reference books or research literature in geometric methodsfor stochastic dynamics.
  Our goal is to present a few selected geometric methods for understanding solutionsof stochastic differential equations. Some necessary background is reviewed, while moreadvanced materials are referred to relevant literature. It is our hope that this book willprovide a guide to the reader in accessing advanced monographs and research literaturein stochastic dynamics. We have tried to strike a balance between mathematical precisionand accessibility for the readers of this book. For example, some proofs are presented,whereas some are outlined and others are directed to references. Some definitions arepresented in separate paragraphs starting with Definition, but others are introduced lessformally as they occur in the body of the text.
  This book may be used as a textbook or a reference for advanced doctoral students, postdoctoral fellows, researchers and practitioners in applied mathematics, machinelearning, artificial intelligence, engineering and applied science.

papers.title: Kalton-Peck space is not isomorphic to its hyperplanes
papers.authors: A. Das, V. Ferenczi, Ch. Rosendal
papers.abstract: Let $Z_2$ denote the real Kalton-Peck space. No hyperplane of $Z_2$ admits a complex structure, and $Z_2$ is even in the sense of Ferenczi-Galego. Therefore, $Z_2$ is not linearly isomorphic to its hyperplanes, solving a long-standing conjecture in Banach space theory. The argument uses the Kalton-Swanson symplectic form on $Z_2$, the Castillo-Gonz\'alez-Pino Fredholm theorem in $Z_2$, and a special case of a mod-$2$ theorem of Li-Zhu on skew-adjoint Fredholm relations in symplectic spaces, for which a self-contained proof is included.

papers.title: Two-Sided Dimension Bounds for the Peterson Hit Problem via Projections and Matrix Minors
papers.authors: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal P_k=\mathbb F_2[x_1,\ldots,x_k]$ be the polynomial algebra over the prime field $\mathbb F_2$, viewed as an unstable module over the mod-$2$ Steenrod algebra $\mathcal A$. The well-known Peterson hit problem asks for a minimal set of generators for the $\mathcal A$-module $\mathcal P_k$. This is equivalent to determining the dimension of the cohit space $(Q\mathcal P_k)_d=(\mathcal P_k/\mathcal A^{+}\mathcal P_k)_d$, where $\mathcal A^{+}$ denotes the augmentation ideal of $\mathcal A$, for every $k\geq1$ and positive degree $d$. Although solved in every degree for at most four variables, it remains a difficult open problem in general. Furthermore, given the limitations of current tools, explicitly determining the dimension of $(Q\mathcal P_k)_d$ in the general case appears out of reach. Motivated by these limitations, we establish explicit upper and lower bounds for this dimension for arbitrary positive integers $k$ and $d.$ Our method combines binary combinatorics, linear algebra, and graph and simplicial structures associated with the generating Steenrod squares. We characterize zero rows, count zero columns, and refine rank estimates using Adem relations. Minors and zero rows of the resulting smaller matrix yield further two-sided cohit bounds without determining a complete basis or computing the full hit rank.

papers.title: Finite-Rank Lie Algebroids for Singular Foliations of Prescribed Vanishing Order
papers.authors: Austin Davis, Cheng-Yi Hung, Sangjun Ko, Kaichuan Qi
papers.abstract: We construct a family of finite-rank Lie algebroids realizing, through their anchor maps, the singular foliations of vector fields vanishing to a prescribed order at the origin. The construction is obtained from the sub-adjacent Lie algebroids of a class of left-symmetric algebroids.

papers.title: Electrostatics as a Stress Theory in $\mathbb R^3$ : Free and Bound Charge, Gauge Invariance, and Mechanical Interactions
papers.authors: Vladimir Gol'dshtein, Wolfgang H. M\"uller, Reuven Segev
papers.abstract:
We formulate electrostatics in three as the simplest instance of the theory of stresses: the virtual velocity field of continuum mechanics is simply replaced by a scalar potential field. A charge distribution is then a linear functional on potential fields whose value is the potential energy, and it is represented by a volume charge density and by surface charge densities on the boundaries of subbodies. Cauchy's theorem gives a vector field $ oldsymbol P$, the analog of the traction stress, and a scalar field $r$, so that the energy is $\int(r\varphi+ oldsymbol P\cdot
abla\varphi)dV$. The pair $(r, oldsymbol P)$, the analog of a variational stress, splits every charge distribution uniquely into free charge, with density $r$, and a dipole distribution, with density $ oldsymbol P$, which carries the bound charges $-
abla\cdot oldsymbol P$ and $ oldsymbol P\cdot oldsymbol{
u}$; the fields $r$ and $ oldsymbol P$ are the densities of charge and of dipole moment. We do not impose gauge invariance of the energy. Instead, we show that it is the analog of the balance of forces on every subbody, and that it singles out the neutral charge distributions. For charges embedded in matter, the forces exerted by the electric field are derived. They are shown to be gauge invariant for every charge distribution, and they include an asymmetric active stress $ oldsymbol E oldsymbol\otimes oldsymbol P$ whose skew-symmetric part is the couple density $ oldsymbol P	imes oldsymbol E$.

papers.title: The distribution of $k$-free ideals in ray class groups
papers.authors: Adrian Barquero-Sanchez, Jack Heimrath, Bernd Sing, Nicol\'as Sirolli, Caylee Spivey, Michael Wijaya
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the classical problem of studying the distribution of $k$-free integers in arithmetic progressions to the setting of arbitrary number fields. Using the language of ray class groups, we establish asymptotic formulas, together with error terms, for the number of $k$-free ideals of bounded norm lying in a given ray class. In particular, our results show that $k$-free ideals are equidistributed among ray classes. We also obtain improved error estimates in the cases of ideal class groups and narrow class groups by using sharper ideal counting asymptotics due to Landau. Our results recover the classical formulas of Gegenbauer and Cohen--Robinson over $\mathbb{Q}$ and extend previous work of Benkowski, Nymann, and Sittinger to the setting of ray class groups. We also present explicit computational examples that illustrate the asymptotic formulas and the equidistribution of $k$-free ideals among ray classes.

papers.title: Shimura curves of discriminant 14 and 15 and associated Heun Functions
papers.abstract:
We study the Shimura curves $X_D^*(1)$ of discriminant $D$ for $D=14, 15$ relating specific weight $4$ modular forms on these Shimura curves to the associated Heun functions for the quadrilateral group. We also discuss how the Picard-Fuchs equation of the associated family of abelian surfaces has solutions coming from modular forms on $X^*_{D}(1)$. We determine the rational exceptional sets of the associated Heun functions, and the algebraic values attained by the Heun function at these points. For example,
  $${\rm He}\left( 81, \frac{1}{2}; \frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2};-\frac{729}{112}\right)= \left( \frac{2^2 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^3}{7^5} \right)^{\frac{1}{6}} $$.

papers.title: Scaled boundary cubature scheme in higher dimensions: integration over polytopes and curved regions
papers.abstract: We extend the scaled boundary cubature (SBC) scheme from planar regions to higher-dimensional regions described by oriented boundary patches. The resulting parametrization transforms integrals over compact regions in $\mathbb{R}^d$ into sums of integrals over the boundary-patch parameter domains and a radial coordinate. In three dimensions, this yields a direct volume-integration rule for solids bounded by affine faces, triangular or tensor-product surface patches, B-spline patches, NURBS patches, and combinations of curved and affine boundary representations. For affine polytopes, recursive application of the scaled boundary map yields nested tensor-product rules over simplex sectors; in three dimensions, these reduce to tetrahedral-sector rules that apply equally to convex and nonconvex oriented polyhedra. We also develop transformations for weakly singular integrands. Placing the scaling center at a point singularity exposes the radial power cancelled by the Jacobian, while generalized radial scalings and Gauss--Jacobi quadrature handle fractional powers. A transverse scaled-boundary map provides the analogous construction for affine singular sets, with straight-line examples in three dimensions. Numerical examples verify polynomial exactness on affine polyhedra and a four-dimensional tesseract, rapid convergence on curved B-spline and NURBS solids, and the expected convergence improvements for point and line singularities. Near-boundary singularity tests also identify when additional patch subdivision or patch-parameter transformations are required.

papers.title: The Geometric Function Atlas: Using What We Know About Radius Problems to Solve New Ones
papers.authors: Prasanna Devadiga, Kishan Gurumurthy, Arya Suneesh, Pushparaj Devadiga, Asha Sebastian
papers.abstract: Usually, radius problems between Ma--Minda classes are solved one pair at a time, by fitting a disk inside the target region, providing a sufficient but not always the sharp radius. The same class appearing under different names makes comparison of results harder, with mistakes and duplication eluding detection. The Geometric Function Atlas catalogs radius problems using exact generators and a direction (source $\to$ target), ensuring unique identification. For each problem, we then compute the radius numerically, together with the point where the image first meets the target boundary. This helps us identify the sharp estimate which guides the proof we write. With this system, we were able to refine two earlier stated estimates, the disk radius for the sine $\to$ modified sigmoid and sine $\to$ rational cases from $\operatorname{arsinh} c$ to $\arcsin c$, and correct earlier stated values for the crescent and exponential classes: the sharp radius is $\sin 1$ from crescent to exponential, and $\log(1+\sqrt2)$ from exponential to crescent. All four proofs follow a common strategy: an estimate that is exact at the contact point, followed by the standard extremal function. Applying the method, we derive fifteen further sharp radii, four of them known.

papers.title: An alternating Mizuno formula, modified gamma functions, and double sine special values
papers.abstract:
For $n\ge1$ and $\operatorname{Re}(x_j)>0$, we prove an alternating analogue of Mizuno's product formula: \begin{equation*} \prod\nolimits_{m=0}^{\infty} \left(\prod_{j=1}^{n}(m+x_j)\right)^{(-1)^m} = \frac{(\sqrt{\pi/2})^n} {\prod_{j=1}^{n}\widetilde{\Gamma}(x_j)}, \end{equation*} where $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ is the modified gamma function associated with the alternating Hurwitz zeta function. The polynomial factors are regularized using factorwise logarithms, and the formula establishes compatibility between this regularization and polynomial factorization. Applications include Gaussian and cyclotomic (Kurokawa--Wakayama type) evaluations; the single-factor case recovers the alternating Lerch formula, and a normalized ratio yields Wallis' product.
  A second group of results concerns an alternating double sine-type function. At nonexceptional positive periods, its positive-integer special values admit finite tangent-product representations. These products define locally meromorphic continuations $F_m$ in the period parameter. For $m\ge2$ and nonzero algebraic parameters, the continued values belong to $\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ at rational parameters and are finite, nonzero, and transcendental at nonrational parameters. We determine their orders at rational parameters and distinguish parameter continuation from fixed-period specialization at exceptional parameters.
  Additional results include Barnes factorizations of multiple alternating gamma functions, a Glaisher--Kinkelin special value, finite-product Stirling-type asymptotics, a symmetric two-parameter form of the known odd-integer multiplication formula, and an odd-scaling distribution relation for the alternating double sine-type function.

papers.title: Levine Equivalence in Aura Topological Spaces: Reachability, Alexandrov Structure, and Quotient Frames
papers.authors: S. M. Elsayed, Tareq M. Al-shami
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Levine equivalence in aura topological spaces. We show that the aura topology is determined by the reachability preorder induced by the scope function and is therefore an Alexandrov topology. We prove that the aura-Levine hull has the explicit representation $K_{\mathfrak a}(A)=\uparrow_{\mathfrak a}A=S_{\mathfrak a}^{\infty}(A)$, and hence two subsets are aura-Levine equivalent if and only if they have the same eventual forward spread. We also describe the quotient structure of the equivalence classes, characterize separation properties through the reachability preorder, classify scope functions that induce the same Levine equivalence, and examine preservation under aura-continuous mappings. For finite aura spaces, we provide an explicit procedure for deciding aura-Levine equivalence using the reflexive-transitive closure of the scope relation.

papers.title: The Parafree Conjecture for Lie rings and associative algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a finitely generated parafree Lie ring with nonzero second homology and, over every nonzero commutative ring, a finitely generated parafree augmented associative algebra with nonzero second homology. These examples disprove the analogues of the Parafree Conjecture for Lie rings and for augmented associative algebras. Our constructions also provide finitely generated parafree examples that are not finitely presented, both in the Lie-ring and augmented-algebra settings.

papers.title: Ramification ideals for products of pure subgroups
papers.abstract: We study ramification ideals of finite Galois extensions of henselian valued fields whose Galois groups are products of pure subgroups. We give a criterion showing that the ideals supplied by the factors need not exhaust all subgroup ideals, and construct $C_p^2$-counterexamples of rank one with each defect $1,p,p^2$. For ramification-adapted families, whose intersections generate each ramification group, every subgroup ideal is represented by a cyclic subgroup of one member; when the members are pure, this gives a description in terms of distance sets. Such adapted decompositions always exist for elementary abelian groups. We also characterize principality of ramification ideals through defectlessness of the pure adapted factors. Kuhlmann's example shows that these conditions do not imply defectlessness of the full extension.

papers.title: Optimal Selling of Defaultable Assets using the Distribution Builder
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of when it is best to sell a risky asset in the \textit{distribution builder} framework under the consideration of potential ruin. This approach allows investors to express their preferences directly as a desired target distribution without first specifying a risk aversion or utility function. Mathematically, the problem is closely related to the Skorokhod embedding problem of attaining a given distribution by stopping a diffusion process. We work in a general framework of one-dimensional diffusion processes and extend existing results to include the possibility of ruin. We first provide a full characterization of the set of distributions that can be attained before ruin occurs. Then, we formulate two optimization problems that tackle the issue of what to do if the originally specified distribution is either not attainable or not optimal: finding the attainable distribution closest to an unattainable distribution and selecting an optimal attainable distribution under first-order stochastic dominance constraints if the originally specified distribution is attainable, but not optimal. We provide sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of solutions to these constrained convex optimization problems in an extended \(f\)-divergence framework, provide an analytic characterization of the solutions, and present numerical examples.

papers.title: Point Counts of Cluster Varieties of Marked Surfaces Over Finite Fields
papers.abstract: We establish formulae for point counts of cluster varieties of cluster algebras of marked surfaces, possibly with punctures. We then establish formulae for the number of non-deep points in these cluster varieties over $\mathbb{F}_2$, which gives us the number of algebraic tori necessary to cover the cluster manifold over $\mathbb{F}_2$. We also show that these formulae satisfy certain recurrence relations.

papers.title: Sign Propagation of Principal Minors in Fully Semimonotone Matrices and Stone's Conjecture
papers.abstract: Stone conjectured in 1981 that every fully semimonotone $\mathbf{Q}_0$-matrix is a $\mathbf{P}_0$-matrix; Murthy and Parthasarathy (1995) proved this for orders up to $4$ and for several special classes. We study the principal minors of fully semimonotone matrices $A\in\Ezerof$ without using $\Qzero$. Let $\G(A)$ be the graph whose vertices are the index sets $\alpha$ with $\det A_{\alpha\alpha}\neq 0$ (including $\alpha=\emptyset$), two vertices being adjacent when they differ in exactly one index. We prove that the sign of the principal minor is constant on every connected component of $\G(A)$, and positive on the component of $\emptyset$. Consequences: an $\Ezerof$-matrix with no vanishing principal minor is a $\mathbf{P}$-matrix, and any $\Ezerof$-matrix satisfying a simple ``descending'' condition on its nonvanishing minors is a $\mathbf{P}_0$-matrix. We show that a sign change across two steps through vanishing minors forces strictly positive coupling in the corresponding principal pivotal transform, and that a principal submatrix of minimal order with negative determinant is an almost-$\mathbf{P}_0$ matrix whose inverse lies in $\Ezerof\cap\Nzero$ and has zero diagonal. Explicit examples show that the component structure can contain negative components, that $\det A>0$ does not force $A\in\Pzero$ in $\Ezerof$, that $\Ezerof$ is not invariant under $A\mapsto A+\varepsilon I$, and that $\Ezerof\cap\Pzero$ contains matrices with $\det A>0$ outside $\Qzero$. Stone's conjecture itself remains open.

papers.title: Serial Depth of Adaptive Parallel Sampling: Lower Bounds and Schedules for Masked Diffusion Models
papers.authors: Chuling Wen, Weijie Liang, Jian Lu, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models generate sequences in rounds, predicting several masked positions at once. Fewer rounds can accelerate decoding, but sampling positions independently can lose their dependence and bias the output. How few rounds suffice for a prescribed error budget? Beyond error bounds for individual decoding rules, we study sharp lower bounds on the number of rounds required for a given target distribution. We introduce serial depth: the minimum number of rounds, averaged over target sequences, needed to meet a forward Kullback-Leibler error budget. With exact conditional probabilities, we prove these bounds for all deterministic rules that may adapt to generated values and construct matching schedules for several distribution families, with depths ranging from $\log\log n$ to linear in sequence length $n$. To narrow the gap to trained models, we show that these lower bounds remain valid for learned predictors and give sufficient accuracy conditions on visited contexts for schedules to retain their error guarantees. On two pretrained models across five text domains, a schedule suggested by the theory achieves higher average log-likelihood on held-out text in five rounds than random selection in eight. A preregistered confirmation study certifies a relative improvement on independent dialogue data.

papers.title: Dilator-based analysis of KP
papers.abstract: Proof theorists developed various frameworks to analyze impredicative systems like $\Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{CA}_0$ or $\mathsf{KP}$; One is an operator-controlled derivation system, and the other is Girard's dilator-based $\beta$-logic. In this paper, we provide a functorial formulation of operator-controlled analysis of $\mathsf{KP}$, thereby unifying the two approaches into a single framework. As an application, a new proof of Girard's boundedness theorem is also provided, which states that every $\Sigma_1$-over-$L_{\omega_1^{\mathsf{CK}}}$-definable function $\omega_1^\mathsf{CK}\to \omega_1^\mathsf{CK}$ is bounded by a recursive dilator.

papers.title: Macroscopic scalar curvature bounds on surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized Geroch conjecture, and the corresponding hyperbolic conjecture, in dimension two.

papers.title: A counterexample to the stable forking conjecture
papers.abstract: Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture. This answers a long-standing open question of Hart, Kim and Pillay (1996).

papers.title: Sharp Threshold for Universality of Rational Canonical Forms over a Finite Field
papers.abstract:
We study the rational canonical form of sparse random matrices over a finite field. Suppose $A_n\in\mathrm{Mat}_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$ has independent and $\alpha_n$-balanced entries. We prove that if $n\alpha_n-\log n\to+\infty$, then, for every fixed collection of distinct monic irreducible polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the corresponding primary partitions of $A_n$ converge jointly to the same asymptotically independent Cohen-Lenstra distributions as in the uniform random matrix model. This strengthens the finite-field cokernel universality theorem of Lee (arXiv:2511.13070), which assumes $\alpha_n=c\log n/n$ for a fixed $c>1$, by resolving the additive endpoint case explicitly left open in his work. Moreover, our result extends universality from ordinary cokernels to the full rational canonical form. The condition is optimal for universality uniformly over fixed irreducible polynomials.
  Our proof uses the surjection moment method developed by Sawin and Wood (arXiv:2210.06279) over $\mathbb{F}_p[t]$, together with a refinement of Lee's Fourier estimates that retains the full leading-order decay. We also construct degree-$d$ critical sparse obstructions, suggesting a polynomial-dependent threshold of $1/d$ for irreducible polynomials of minimal degree $d$.

papers.title: On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes C_m$
papers.abstract: For a prime $p$, a pair $(s,m)\in\mathbb{N}^2$ with $m$ relatively prime to $p$, a homomorphism $\chi:C_m\rightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(C_{p^s})$, and an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$, we consider the semidirect product $G=C_{p^s}\rtimes_{\chi} C_m$, the $p$-Sylow subgroup $H\cong C_{p^s}$ of $G$, and a $k[G]$-module $V$. Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of residue field $k$ and mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ that contains a primitive $p^s$-th root of unity. If $\chi$ is injective, we present two necessary and sufficient criteria for lifting $V$ to an $R[G]$-module $\widetilde{V}$ which is a free $R$-module: (i) when no extra requirement is made on $\widetilde{V}$ and (ii) when we require $\widetilde{V}^H=\{0\}$. The criteria correct several results in the literature and we use them to prove that, if $\chi$ is injective and $G$ acts faithfully on a connected smooth projective curve $X$ over $k$, then, under mild hypotheses satisfied if $X\rightarrow X/G$ is a Harbater--Katz--Gabber cover, the $k[G]$-module $H^0(X,\Omega_X)$ has a lift $\widetilde{V}$ to $R$ with $\widetilde{V}^H=\{0\}$. Also, with $B:=R[\frac{1}{p}]$, we prove the following obstruction when $p$ is odd, $m$ is even, $\chi$ is injective, and $X/C_{p^s}\cong\mathbb{P}^1_k$: if no such lift $\widetilde{V}$ exists with the $B[H]$-module $\widetilde{V}\otimes_R B$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, then the action of $G$ on $X$ does not lift to $R$.

papers.title: Symmetries and Causality: Causal Effect Identification Beyond IID Data
papers.abstract: We develop theory for the identification of complex causal queries from non-IID data. We propose a formal description of stochastic systems based on symmetries in data leaving causal mechanisms invariant. These symmetries become the source of statistical repetition for identification and mandate knowledge-transfer from observations to queries. The result is an abstract, simple and very general language for causal reasoning. We give descriptions of models and queries, and the formal infrastructure for their mathematically rigorous identification. The proposed structure enables a number of simplifying principles: A shared description of mechanisms and interventions, a duality of observed and queried structure, and the sub-division of the identification task into three steps - extraction, computation and query-expression. Our approach reproduces and matches standard theoretical results on IID data and transport of experimental and non-experimental data. By design, it additionally applies beyond IID data and captures complex causal queries not expressible via do- or soft-interventions.

papers.title: Lifting curved Kakeya sets to linear Kakeya sets
papers.abstract:
We prove that many curved Kakeya problems, originally motivated by H\"ormander's oscillatory integral problem, lift to the classical Kakeya problem in higher dimensions.
  As a consequence, if the classical Kakeya set conjecture were true in all dimensions, the families of curves whose curved Kakeya sets have full dimension are dense among H\"ormander-type families. This is in contrast to the nowhere dense Bourgain's condition, which is a necessary condition for best-case curved Kakeya maximal function estimates. Furthermore the linear Kakeya set conjecture would imply a fairly complete understanding of Kakeya sets of quadratic curves, as first studied systematically by Wisewell. These results give a better understanding of a question posed by Guo--Guth--Nadjimzadah--Shen--Zhang, and they more generally show that the classical Kakeya conjecture in high dimensions rests on a broad range of curved Kakeya problems in lower dimensions.

papers.title: A polynomial criterion for Jordan elements in a free associative algebra
papers.abstract: Let $J$ be the Jordan subalgebra of the free associative algebra $\Q\langle X\rangle$ generated by $X$ and $1$ under $a\cdot b=\tfrac12(ab+ba)$. We give a polynomial criterion for an associative polynomial to belong to $J$. For every $n\ge1$, Robbins' recursion gives a family of operators $T_\alpha\in\Q[S_n]$, indexed by compositions of $n$ into parts $1$ and $2$. We prove that right multiplication by $U_n=\sum_\alpha T_\alpha^\dagger T_\alpha$ has image $\SJ(n)$, the space of multilinear Jordan elements. If its characteristic polynomial is $t^{e_n}q_n(t)$, where $q_n(0)\ne0$, then $\Pi_n=I-q_n(U_n)/q_n(0)$ is an idempotent and $f\in\SJ(n)$ if and only if $fq_n(U_n)=0$, or equivalently $f\Pi_n=f$. The same operators give the criterion for arbitrary homogeneous polynomials of degree $n$. We also prove $\SJ(n)\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n}r_\lambda S^\lambda$, where $r_\lambda=\rank\rho_\lambda(U_n)$. Thus $\dim\SJ(n)=\sum_\lambda d_\lambda r_\lambda$ and $e_n=\sum_\lambda d_\lambda(d_\lambda-r_\lambda)$, with $d_\lambda=\dim S^\lambda$. We give a recursion for the corresponding row spaces and use it to compute the multiplicities over $\Q$ through degree $12$. Exact block characteristic polynomials through degree $7$ and direct computations in small degrees illustrate the criterion.

papers.title: Positive solutions for an indefinite-weight Minkowski mean curvature Neumann problem: multiplicity and asymptotic behaviour
Vanishing boundary geometry and critical pressure compactness for the three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We prove boundary partial regularity for the three-dimensional nonstationary Navier--Stokes equations in bounded domains with fractional Sobolev boundary graphs whose integrability exponent is greater than three. Within the fractional Sobolev graph setting, this lowers the boundary threshold from fifteen quarters to three. We work in Breit's boundary suitable weak-solution framework, with the mixed maximal-regularity pair $(5/3,15/14)$ explicitly included in the solution assumptions. The main difficulty is to recover pressure compactness without imposing higher regularity on the rough boundary coefficients. After a rigid rotation to the tangent plane and parabolic rescaling, we show that each boundary graph becomes small in both Sobolev multiplier classes needed for the local energy inequality and the critical Stokes estimate. Geometry and fluid excess enter a contradiction argument as independent small parameters, so the limiting problem is the standard flat Stokes system. A localized pressure decomposition separates the vanishing nonlinear and coefficient errors from the forced and homogeneous flat pressures. The error pressure converges strongly at the critical mixed integrability pair, whereas higher spatial integrability is used only for the flat problems. These estimates yield a one-step excess decay bound with a constant independent of the contraction radius. A physical-scale iteration, followed by interior--boundary Campanato patching, gives local parabolic H\"older continuity of the velocity at every regular boundary point when the force has integrability exponent greater than five halves. The boundary singular set is relatively closed and has zero parabolic Hausdorff measure in dimension five thirds. The geometric decay determines a uniform starting scale and does not restrict the final regularity exponent.

papers.title: Shape calculus and automatic differentiation for multi-phase level-set topology optimisation with unfitted finite elements
papers.authors: Zachary J. Wegert, Martin Berggren, Vivien J. Challis
papers.abstract: We present shape calculus techniques and a scalable automatic shape differentiation framework for multi-phase topology optimisation on unfitted discretisations defined by several level-set functions. First we establish general, exact shape calculus expressions in the discrete case for multi-phase systems by leveraging concepts from convex geometry. To complement this theoretical foundation, we introduce an open-source multi-phase automatic shape differentiation framework based on polytopal cutting. This computational framework is validated against both finite differences and our established exact expressions, matching the latter to near machine precision. Furthermore, the proposed automatic shape differentiation is scalable across distributed computing environments, demonstrating near ideal weak scaling up to 1.65 billion finite elements across 13,824 computer cores. We demonstrate our implementation by solving unfitted multi-phase topology optimisation problems for anisotropic diffusion, linear elasticity, and fluid--structure interaction. Together, these theoretical and computational contributions provide a robust and accessible foundation for advancing multi-phase topology optimisation using unfitted finite element methods. In particular, the methods enable the solution of topology optimisation problems involving multi-phase and multi-physics systems with non-trivial boundary conditions. The open-source software is available at https://github.com/zjwegert/GridapTopOpt.jl.

papers.title: Global Sobolev Convergence of Howard Iteration for Finite-Horizon Controlled Diffusions
papers.abstract: We study Howard policy iteration for finite-horizon stochastic control problems in which the control enters the diffusion coefficient. Each iteration selects a policy by maximizing the Hamiltonian and evaluates it through a linear parabolic equation. Since the improvement depends on the Hessian, even smooth data can produce discontinuous evaluation coefficients. We prove global convergence in the full parabolic Sobolev space under assumptions that allow this loss of regularity. In one space dimension, bounded measurable coefficients and uniform ellipticity suffice, without a large discount, a short horizon, small diffusion variation, or regularity assumptions on the improving policies. Multidimensional extensions hold under structural conditions on the diffusion matrix. The proof combines monotonicity with a parabolic growth estimate to show that the Bellman residual vanishes in measure. Uniform higher integrability then yields strong convergence of the values, gradients, Hessians, and time derivatives, and constructs the unique strong solution. We also establish residual error bounds, extend the argument to entropy regularization and zero-temperature limits, and obtain quadratic convergence for special one-dimensional models.

papers.title: Monodromy Eigenvectors for Difference Equations with Root-of-Unity Step
papers.abstract: A qKZ-type discrete flat connection with multiplicative step $p$ has monodromy operators when $p$ is a root of unity. The monodromy operators are commuting endomorphisms of the connection. We construct their eigensections and eigenvalues. The construction is based on the presentation of the discrete flat connection as a discrete Gauss-Manin connection.

papers.title: A parity obstruction to completeness of object cotorsion pairs
papers.abstract: Fu, Guil Asensio, Herzog and Torrecillas asked whether a complete ideal cotorsion pair of object ideals in an exact category always induces a complete cotorsion pair of objects. We show that it need not, even in a Hom-finite, weakly idempotent complete Frobenius exact category. Our example consists of bounded complexes of finite-dimensional vector spaces with even total cohomology dimension. We characterize special object approximations by parity and identify the obstruction as a non-split idempotent in the stable category. For cohereditary pairs, a criterion of Saor\'{\i}n and \v{S}\v{t}ov\'{\i}\v{c}ek gives an affirmative answer when the stable category is idempotent complete.

papers.title: A Universal Law of Large Numbers for Extreme Cycles in Random \v{C}ech Complexes
papers.abstract: We study the maximal multiplicative persistence of $k$-cycles in random \v{C}ech complexes. Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a probability density function, let ${P}_n$ be a Poisson process with intensity $nf$, and let $\Pi_{k,n}$ denote the largest death-to-birth ratio among all non-essential $k$-cycles ($1\le k \le d-1$). For the uniform distribution in the unit hypercube, it was proved in [9] that $\Pi_{k,n} = \Theta\left( \left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/k}\right)$. In this paper we sharpen and extend this result to a law of large numbers, for a broad class of distributions. Most significantly, we show that the limiting constant depends only on $d$ and $k$, and not on the probability density $f$. Thus the extreme value of multiplicative persistence exhibits a universality phenomenon. We show that the limiting constant is determined by the asymptotic covering density of the $k$-dimensional sphere. Our proof identifies the geometric mechanism underlying maximal cycles, a persistent isoperimetric inequality, which gives sharp bounds on the number of points needed to generate a highly persistent cycle. By combining covering-density estimates with isoperimetric inequalities, we show that this minimum is asymptotically attained by efficient coverings of a $k$-sphere. A key ingredient is a geometric measure theory argument that uses compactness to relate discrete covering counts to the volume of a limiting cycle.

papers.title: Peeling sequences: a directional method for the three-block construction
papers.abstract:
A peeling sequence of a finite planar point set is an ordering of its points, such that when the points get removed in this order,
  each removed point is a vertex of the current convex hull of the set. Write $g(S)$ for the number of such sequences, and $g(n)$ for the minimum of $g(S)$ over $n$-point sets in general position. We present a method which can be used to prove better upper bounds on the previously analysed recursive 3-block constructions $S_n$. In fact, we prove $g(n)\leq g(S_n)=O(6.57^n)$, using directional restrictions and a weighted prefix-tree form of the Kraft--McMillan inequality. From the other direction, we show that the same construction cannot attain the current best known lower bound of $c\cdot3^n$. In fact, $g(S_n)\geq 5.22^n$ when $n$ is a large enough power of $3$. Improving the general lower bound on $g(n)$ is still an open question.

papers.title: Sharp spectral norm concentration and regularization of sparse random tensors
papers.abstract: We prove sharp spectral-norm bounds and construct a mean-fitting regularization procedure for sparse random tensors of fixed order $k$. For an $n\times\cdots\times n$ tensor with independentBernoulli$(p)$ entries, the centered norm is $O(\sqrt{np})$ with polynomially high probability whenever $np\ge c\log n$. This removes the logarithmic loss in Zhou and Zhu (2021). We also determine the expected centered norm at every sparsity level: for every $0<p\le1/2$, it has order $\min\{n^kp,\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{eff}}}\}$, where $d_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is an effective degree accounting for unusually large fiber counts. The upper bounds extend to tensors with deterministic entrywise weights and unequal sampling probabilities. Analogous two-sided bounds hold for the Friedman--Wigderson model at every degree; its expected centered norm has order $\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{eff}}}$. We also give an all-sparsity regularization procedure for independent Bernoulli tensors with unknown, possibly unequal means in $[0,p]$. Our light-fitting regularization estimates the original mean with minimax expected spectral-norm error of order $\min\{\sqrt{np},pn^{k/2}\}$ for every known $0\le p\le1$. The procedure fits light multilinear residuals under an entrywise constraint on the candidate mean, rather than deleting high-degree fibers.

papers.title: Extremal numbers of acyclic matrices
papers.abstract:
For a zero-one matrix $P$, let $\operatorname{Ex}(n,P)$ denote the maximum number of ones in an $n\times n$ zero-one matrix avoiding $P$. We prove that
  $$\operatorname{Ex}(n,P) \leq n^{1+O_P(1/\log\log n)}$$ for every acyclic $P$, settling the weak form of the Pach-Tardos conjecture.

papers.title: Eigenvectors of $p$-Curvature for Geometric Difference Equations
papers.abstract: A qKZ-type additive discrete flat connection in characteristic $p$ has $p$-curvature operators. They are commuting automorphisms of the connection. We present a Bethe-ansatz-type construction of eigensections and eigenvalues of the $p$-curvature operators. An eigensection of $p$-curvature operators is a discrete hypergeometric sum over the finite lattice $\mathbb{Z}^r/p\mathbb{Z}^r$. Thus, the $p$-curvature eigensections are constructed by a finite, discrete analogue of a hypergeometric integral.

papers.title: Continuous sonic-supersonic flows in two-dimensional infinitely long divergent nozzles
papers.authors: Lili Qian, Chunpeng Wang, Zihao Zhang
papers.abstract: This paper concerns continuous sonic-supersonic flows in a two-dimensional infinitely long divergent nozzle with straight solid walls. For a given inlet that is a small perturbation of an arc centered at the vertex of the nozzle, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of a continuous sonic-supersonic potential flow which is close to the radially symmetric sonic-supersonic flow. The flow is sonic at the inlet, with its velocity along the normal direction, and becomes supersonic in the nozzle. Such a sonic-supersonic model is governed by a quasilinear nonstrictly hyperbolic equation with degeneracy at the inlet, and the degeneracy is weak in the sense that there exist exactly two distinct characteristics from each sonic point, except for those at the walls, pointing into the supersonic region. One of the crucial ingredients of the analysis is to obtain the precise asymptotic behavior near the sonic inlet by the method of characteristics, which is essential for establishing the local existence of continuous sonic-supersonic flows. Another one is to extend the local solution globally and derive uniform estimates in the supersonic region.

papers.title: Eigenvectors and Eigenvalues of $p$-Curvature Operators for KZ--type Differential Connections
papers.abstract: A KZ-type connection in characteristic $p$ has $p$-curvature operators. These operators are commuting endomorphisms of the connection. We present a Bethe-ansatz-type construction of their eigenvectors and eigenvalues. The eigenvector is constructed as the value of a characteristic $p$ hypergeometric integral and extends to a flat eigensection over the Frobenius neighborhood of the corresponding Bethe point.

papers.title: Light rays of Lorentzian graphs and the Born-Infeld model
papers.abstract: Following a program outlined by Bartnik, and also employing nonlinear potential techniques we developed in the last years, we study lightlike singularities of variational solutions to the prescribed Lorentzian mean curvature equation with possibly unbounded (rough) curvature. This corresponds to allowing for unbounded charges in the Born-Infeld model.

papers.title: A minimization problem for a cooperative system with a degenerate Bernoulli weight
papers.authors: Lili Du, Chunlei Yang, Jing Yang
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study local minimizers of the energy functional$J(\mathbf{u}) = \int_D (|\nabla \mathbf{u}|^2 + Q^2(x)\chi_{\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}})\,dx$ which give rise to a singular cooperative system. Here \(\mathbf{u}=(u_1,\dots,u_m): D\to\R_+^m\) is a vector-valued unknown function, \(\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}:=\{|\mathbf{u}|>0\}\) is the positive set, \(\chi_{\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}}\) is the characteristic function of the positive set \(\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}\), and \(Q(x)\) is the Bernoulli weight function. This problem was first introduced by Caffarelli, Shahgholian, and Yeressian in the poineer work ({\it Duke Math. J.} \textbf{167}(10), 2018), where the regularity theory for minimizers and for the free boundary \(\partial\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}\) was established for nondegenerate Bernoulli weights, i.e., \(Q(x)\ge Q_{\rm min}>0\). The present paper studies the same free boundary problem but for a degenerate Bernoulli weight. The main difficulty lies in the coupling between the degeneracy of \(Q(x)\) and the vector-valued nature of the problem.
  We show that the the free boundary set \(\partial\Omega_{\mathbf{u}}\cap\{Q(x)=0\}\) decomposes into a nondegenerate part and a degenerate part. Nondegenerate points admit nontrivial blow-up limits; degenerate points have zero weighted density. We classify nondegenerate points into single-phase, multi-phase non-branching, and multi-phase branching points, analyzing their geometric structure. The branching-point singular structure for multi-phase points is purely vectorial and new in this setting.
  Finally, following Naber--Valtorta (Ann. Math. 185, 2017) and Edelen--Engelstein (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 371, 2019), we prove the nondegenerate set has locally finite $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-measure and is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable.

papers.title: Exact Ehrhart Series of Birkhoff Polytopes via Constant Terms and Finite-Field Evaluation
papers.authors: Xinru Jiang, Guoce Xin, Chen Zhang, Yueming Zhong
papers.abstract: The Ehrhart series of the $n$th Birkhoff polytope is $\sum_{r\geq0}H_n(r)z^r$, where $H_n(r)$ counts nonnegative integer $n\times n$ matrices whose row and column sums all equal $r$. We present an exact method for computing this series using constant terms and finite fields. A root filter expresses $H_n(r)$ as a weighted sum of the values $h_r(M)^n$, where $h_r$ is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial and $M$ ranges over multisets of $m$th roots of unity with $m=r+1$. Constant-term cancellation reduces the evaluation of $h_r(M)$ to a sum over repeated elements $a$ of $M$. For a particular $a$ of multiplicity $\mu_a$, the computation uses a generalized Todd coefficient of degree $\mu_a-2$. Sums of $h_r(M)^n$ over selected multiplicity classes are handled using symmetric function techniques. Together with the remaining individual evaluations, this gives $O_n(m^{n-5}+m^4)$ field operations for each admissible prime and fixed $n\geq5$. An explicit bound and the Chinese remainder theorem recover the integer counts, and Ehrhart symmetry determines the full series. The same method applies to the World Cup problem, which counts the same matrices with diagonal entries required to be $0$. We prove correctness and compute complete series for both families through order $13$. The Birkhoff series for orders $10$--$13$ and the World Cup series for orders $9$--$13$ are tabulated in the appendices.

papers.title: Coarse rigidity in von Neumann algebras via derivations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the interaction between amenability and first cohomology into tempered representations of groups, we propose a notion of relative coarse rigidity for $\sigma$-finite von Neumann algebras through modular derivations and their associated GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups. This extends Peterson's framework of $L^2$-rigidity to the nontracial setting. Our main result shows that the absence of relatively amenable summands forces the associated deformations to converge on relative commutants in ultrapowers. For diffuse von Neumann algebras with separable predual, this yields a dichotomy between the presence of an amenable summand and rigidity in terms of central sequences. Combining this principle with mixing and compactness, we provide a novel unified approach for proving indecomposability properties such as fullness, primeness and stable solidity. Applications yield new examples of relatively $\omega$-solid and relatively stably solid type III von Neumann algebras arising from amalgamated free products, operator-valued free Araki-Woods constructions, cocycle crossed products, and twisted nonsingular discrete measured groupoids.

papers.title: Matching Upper and Lower Bounds for Higher-Order Nonconvex Finite-Sum Optimization
papers.authors: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We establish tight randomized higher-order oracle complexity for finding first-order stationary points of nonconvex finite sums. Let $n$ be the number of components, $\Delta>0$ the initial objective-gap bound, $L_p>0$ an individual $p$-th derivative Lipschitz bound, and $\epsilon>0$ the target gradient norm. For every fixed integer $p\ge 2$, the minimax number of exact component queries returning the value and all derivatives through order $p$, with success probability at least $2/3$, is \[ \Theta_p\!\left( n+\Delta L_p^{1/p}n^{1-1/(2p)} \epsilon^{-(p+1)/p} \right), \] where the constants depend only on $p$ and the worst case ranges over all finite dimensions. The lower bound holds for unrestricted randomized adaptive algorithms and closes the $\sqrt{n}$ gap between the previously known general-order upper and lower bounds in their dependence on $n$. We extend dense weak hiding to complete higher-order replies while keeping each component's regularity independent of the chain length. The matching upper bound retains the known finite-sum exponent, requires only mean-squared $p$-th derivative increments, and removes the fixed-confidence logarithmic loss by verifying entire recursive-estimation epochs with exact function values. The characterization includes the additive $n$ term for every positive parameter regime; it counts oracle calls with unrestricted internal computation.

papers.title: Localization near the edge for the lattice Anderson-Bernoulli model on general dimension
papers.authors: Linjun Li, Shihe Liu, Lingfu Zhang
papers.abstract: The Anderson tight-binding model is a fundamental model of quantum transport and localization in disordered media. Solving a problem left open by Bourgain and Kenig, this paper proves Anderson localization near the bottom of the spectrum for the lattice Anderson model with Bernoulli potential, in any dimension $d\ge 2$. The proof uses the multiscale framework of Fr\"ohlich-Spencer and Bourgain-Kenig, and the main new ingredient is a probabilistic discrete unique continuation principle (PDUC) for the discrete Schr\"odinger equation. This PDUC is established via a bootstrap argument and a key probabilistic lemma proved by adaptively revealing the random potential.

papers.title: A classification of zero $p$-rank curves with large automorphism groups in odd characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $\cX$ be a curve of genus $g\ge2$ and $p$-rank zero over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $G\le\Aut(\cX)$ satisfy $|G|>24g(g-1)$. We prove that $G$ fixes a point unless $(\cX,G)$ belongs to an explicit list. For $g\ge4$, the curve is a cyclic quotient of a Hermitian curve, of a Giulietti--Korchm\'aros curve, or of Skabelund's cover of a Ree curve. We determine the equations and all the groups $G$ that occur, including their central kernels. The exceptional $A_7$ action in characteristic $5$ is on the Hermitian curve of degree $6$; genera $2$ and $3$ are treated separately. The equations are recovered from the group action by two rigidity lemmas for equivariant one-point $p$-group covers of the affine line. If $G$ has no common fixed point and its Sylow $p$-subgroups are noncyclic, then, unless $G$ induces ${}^2G_2(3)$ on the orbit of Sylow fixed points, the bound $|G|>\max\{84(g-1),2g^2\}$ gives a rational quotient with exactly one wild and one tame short orbit, and a rational Sylow quotient.

papers.title: Satellites and invariants of links
papers.abstract:
An invariant $v$ of $m$-component links is called "cableable" if there exists a $k$ such that whenever a link $L'$ is obtained from a link $L=(K_1,\dots,K_m)$ by replacing each knot $K_i$ with its $(p_i,q_i)$-cable for some $p_i$ and $q_i$, we have $v(L')=(p_1\cdots p_m)^kv(L)$.
  The following problem is implicit in a number of papers by P. M. Akhmetiev and originates from the Arnold-Moffatt program for finding topological lower bounds for the energy of a magnetic field: Does there exist a cableable finite type invariant of links in $S^3$ which is not a function of the pairwise linking numbers? According to Akhmetiev, he solved this problem himself, with the desired invariant being defined for $3$-component links as an analytic expression involving a magnetic field modeled on the given link. We offer a different solution, with the desired invariant for $m$-component links, $m\ge 3$, being a function of the coefficients of the Conway polynomial of the link and its sublinks; the function is given explicitly when $m=3$. Moreover, we show that the cables can be replaced by arbitrary satellites. Much of the proof is a study of low degree coefficients of the Conway potential function $\Omega_L(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ expanded as a formal power series in Conway's variables $z_i=x_i-x_i^{-1}$.
  We also discuss type $n$ invariants which are "cableable up to an invariant of type $n-1$", some cableable invariants which are not of finite type (particularly a certain modification of Milnor's $\bar\mu$-invariants), and applications to links of solenoids.

papers.title: Jackson and Bernstein Inequalities with Explicit Weight Dependence for Band-Limited Wavelet Approximation in Weighted Besov Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove direct and inverse estimates for band-limited biorthogonal wavelet systems in weighted Besov spaces with Muckenhoupt weights. On functions recovered from their wavelet expansion along the dyadic tree of the unit cube, the error of approximation by a prescribed number of terms decays at a rate set by the smoothness-to-dimension ratio, and this exponent cannot be increased. Under a multiresolution condition, Bernstein inequalities hold at a single scale and on every multiresolution subspace, and the linear approximation spaces are identified with weighted Lebesgue--Besov intersections. All constants are explicit; the weight enters only through displayed powers of the Muckenhoupt characteristic.

papers.title: There is no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph
papers.authors: Artem Hak, Sergiy Kozerenko, Andrii Serdiuk
papers.abstract: A graph is $K_3$-irregular if its vertices belong to pairwise distinct numbers of triangles. We prove that no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists, settling the last unresolved case. Following the initial discovery of such graphs for regularities $r \in \{10,11,12\}$ (Stevanovi\'c et al., 2024), our previous work (Hak et al., 2025) showed that no such graphs exist for $r \le 7$, provided the first example for $r=9$, and proved that any $8$-regular candidate must have between $17$ and $22$ vertices. We exclude these possible orders for $r=8$ by combining careful analysis of triangle degrees with integer linear programming techniques. Meanwhile, a recent construction (Zhang, 2026) established that regular $K_3$-irregular graphs do exist for all $r \ge 9$. Together with our results, this establishes that an $r$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists if and only if $r\geq 9$.

papers.title: Supersingular Tate conjecture for irreducible symplectic varieties of known types: I
papers.authors: Lie Fu, Xuanlin Huang, Zhiyuan Li
papers.abstract:
We prove that for a supersingular irreducible symplectic variety admitting suitable lifting to characteristic zero has Tate Chow motive if it is of deformation type $K3^{[n]}$, OG6 (with Artin invariant $
eq$ 4), or OG10 (with Artin invariant $
