papers.title: The Sharp Generalized Bogomolov Inequality
papers.abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Gauduchon and astheno-K\"ahler manifold. Using $L^p$-approximate critical Hermitian structures, we establish a sharp generalized Bogomolov inequality for holomorphic vector bundles on $X$, without any semistability assumption. We further characterize the equality case by studying the Hermitian-Yang-Mills flow. If equality holds, every Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration is by holomorphic subbundles, and its stable quotients admit projectively flat Hermitian metrics. If, in addition, the bundle is not $\omega$-semistable, then $X$ is projective.

papers.title: Pseudodifferential structure, rigidity, and sharpness for the Steklov problem on differential forms
papers.authors: Daguang Chen, Guotao Huang, Tingyu Liao
papers.abstract: We resolve four questions concerning Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential forms. First, for $0\leq p\leq n-2$, we prove that the operator is classical pseudodifferential of order one and compute its principal symbol, which is elliptic on the coclosed symbol space. This answers Open Question 7.19 in the survey of Colbois, Girouard, Gordon, and Sher [7]. Second, the symbol calculation yields a Weyl law with remainder $O(\tau^{n-2})$, resolving the smooth case of their Open Question 7.23 in [7]. Third, in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$, we show that conformal deformations of the Euclidean ball fixing the boundary metric preserve the full operator. Nonisometric metrics therefore retain all equalities in Karpukhin's initial equality range, disproving the isometry-rigidity assertion of Conjecture 2.12 in [19](the rigidity assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]). Fourth, we establish the all-index sharpness asserted in Conjecture 2.13 in [19](the sharpness assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]) in the class of smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian manifolds with boundary. For $p\geq1$, a shrinking-core construction inspired by the collapsing models of Ann\'e and Takahashi produces manifolds with fixed spherical boundary and explicit two-sided bounds for an initial eigenvalue cluster.

papers.title: Local Nevanlinna embedding for Hardy space of Dirichlet series below critical exponent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate a problem posed by Saksman and Seip [ Contemp. Math., 2016] on whether functions in the Hardy space of Dirichlet series $\mathcal{H}^p$, \(0<p<2\), are locally in the Nevanlinna class of the critical half-plane \(\mathbb C_{1/2}\). We show that the local Nevanlinna embedding fails below critical exponent \(p=2\) by constructing $\mathcal{H}^p$-functions whose local logarithmic mass becomes unbounded as \(\real s\to 1/2^+\). This also clarifies the distinction between global Jessen-type logarithmic control and local boundary Nevanlinna behavior for Dirichlet series.

papers.title: Classification of twisted Yangians as coideal subalgebras of Yangians
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an involution $\omega$. We classify the homogeneous right coideal subalgebras of the Yangian of $\mathfrak g$ whose classical limit is the enveloping algebra of the twisted current algebra, embedded in the standard way, without assuming any formula for the coaction. For nontrivial $\omega$, they form a family parametrized by a spectral parameter and an element of the center of the fixed-point subalgebra; for $\omega=\mathrm{id}$, only a spectral parameter occurs. All members of the family are isomorphic as graded algebras, through explicit isomorphisms. In particular, the twisted Yangians with a central correction introduced by Huang and Lu are coideal quantizations, and the $\imath$Yangian of quasi-split type $\mathsf A_{2n}$ is isomorphic to the traditional twisted Yangian studied by MacKay and by Belliard and Regelskis. The PBW property is proved uniformly from the classical affine Serre relations, without quantum defining relations. We also recover finite presentations in split and quasi-split types and verify the technical hypotheses of the quantum duality principle used by Lu, Wang, and Weekes.

papers.title: Thoughts on Quantum Events, Quantizing Gravity and von Neumann Algebras
papers.abstract: This short document presents no new results. It is a collection of related ideas that may lead to a way of quantizing gravity. To achieve this it may be relevant to use my recent new approach to quantum theory, which is based on quantum events. Given that most standard quantum texts do not define a mathematical object which corresponds to a physical event, the definition of a quantum event is motivated and discussed in detail. This in turn leads to the idea that the mathematical object that contains enough quantum events for describing a quantum system is a von Neumann algebra. The next idea is that the kinematics of special relativity (as embodied in flat Minkowski space) should be quantized as a first step in the program of the quantization of general relativity, that is, quantizing Einstein's equation. It must be emphasized that the events of special relativity are viewed as part of the kinematics, rather than of the dynamics of that theory. The same holds for general relativity. Similarly, I am viewing quantum events as part of the kinematics of quantum theory, even though some find this to be counterintuitive. An Appendix shows how ``collapse'' is easily understood in this new approach to quantum theory.

papers.title: The locally quaternion group is a countable $B$-group
papers.abstract: A group $G$ is a $B$-group if every primitive permutation group containing a regular subgroup isomorphic to $G$ is doubly transitive. We prove that the locally quaternion group $\mathrm{Dic}(C_{2^\infty},c)$, the extension of the Pr\"ufer $2$-group by an element squaring to its involution and inverting it, is a $B$-group. This gives an example of a countably infinite $B$-group. This answers Problem 13.30 of the Kourovka Notebook. The proof analyses the automorphism group of an orbital Cayley graph through the central involution. In the main case two half-flip automorphisms generate, with their conjugates, an elementary abelian normal subgroup whose orbits form a nontrivial block system; in the remaining case, where the pointwise stabilizers of the two cosets of the Pr\"ufer group have order two, the conjugates of the central translation generate an elementary abelian normal subgroup, which would be regular if the automorphism group were primitive; an affine lemma for the Pr\"ufer group excludes this. The proof does not depend on computer verification: its two finite case analyses are written out in full, and programs that re-check them are provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: Integrable building blocks for symplectic neural networks: learned-type layers, fiber-preserving layers, and what a single layer can do
papers.abstract: Exactly symplectic neural networks are built almost exclusively from shear maps and gain expressivity only through depth. We ask what else a single explicit symplectic layer can be. Observing that every layer in use is the exact flow of a Hamiltonian that is a function of commuting integrals, we obtain three families of layers: a learned-type layer, in which every conjugate pair is rotated, squeezed or sheared by a state-dependent amount and the type is found by training; moving-plane shears, residual symplectic maps outside the known ridge-function class; and fiber-preserving layers, which combine an unconstrained point transformation with a fiber translation at the cost of one linear solve. We characterize residual symplectic layers $x \mapsto x + J\nabla H(x)$: in one degree of freedom they are exactly the shears along a line, while from two degrees of freedom on a strictly larger class exists. Conjugating a learned-type layer by a symplectic network yields an exact one-parameter group with an exactly conserved learned Hamiltonian. In experiments on sixteen systems with one to forty degrees of freedom, against SympNets, H\'enonNets and learned-plane shear networks, layers built on nonlinear integrals are far more accurate when the Hamiltonian contains functions of those integrals. On nonlinear Schr\"odinger lattices with six to forty sites, twist layers alternating with linear symplectic maps are over a hundred times more accurate than every shear-based network, and with an on-site potential of learned form three to four orders of magnitude more accurate. On chains of Tao oscillators with the step size as an input, stretch layers are 45 to 70 times more accurate than learned-plane shears and recover the Hamiltonian to 1%. On generic non-separable systems, fiber layers improve on learned-plane shears by at most a factor of two, and widening the networks does not help any architecture.

papers.title: Moreau-Yosida Penalization of McKean-Vlasov Dynamics: Full-Flux Limits and Boundary Reaction Measures
papers.authors: Geuntaek Seo, Beomjun Choi, Yeoneung Kim
papers.abstract: We study McKean-Vlasov Fokker-Planck dynamics on a compact convex set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ through the whole-space Moreau-Yosida penalization $U_\lambda=\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,K)^2/(2\lambda)$, keeping the external and interaction potentials fixed. At finite times, the penalized densities converge to the unique variational solution of the reflected no-flux equation, strongly in space-time $L^2$ on $K$ and in whole-space $L^1$, and narrowly, uniformly in time. We prove that the singular penalty-force measures converge weakly-$*$ to the purely normal boundary reaction $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)n\,\mathcal{H}^{d-1}|_{\partial K}\,\mathrm{d}t$. This measure cancels exactly the surface singularity in the distributional gradient of the zero-extended density, explaining the emergent no-flux condition at the flux level. At equilibrium, we establish sharp $\sqrt\lambda$ rates in $L^1$ and Wasserstein distances for kernel-free Gibbs states, and in $L^1$ and quadratic Wasserstein distance for interacting fixed points under Dobrushin smallness or positive semidefiniteness, including maximum mean discrepancy interactions. The proof combines a tilted Gaussian supersolution, nonautonomous weighted energy estimates, and normal factorization with a Green-formula identification. We also identify the limit with a nonlinear reflecting diffusion, obtain path-space convergence and $\lambda$-uniform propagation of chaos through monotone synchronous coupling, and derive all-time Gibbs domination in the reversible case. Numerical experiments illustrate the boundary reaction and stationary scalings on a constrained maximum mean discrepancy flow.

papers.title: Lambda number of the reduced power graph of finite groups
papers.authors: Siddharth Malviy, Keerttiranjan Sahoo, Vipul Kakkar
papers.abstract: The reduced power graph $\Gamma_{RP}(G)$ of a group $G$ is a simple graph with vertex set $G$, where two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent if and only if $\langle u \rangle \subset \langle v \rangle$ or $\langle v \rangle \subset \langle u \rangle$. An $L(2,1)$-labeling of a graph $\Gamma$ is a mapping from the vertex set of $\Gamma$ to the set of non-negative integers such that the labels of adjacent vertices differ by at least $2$ and the labels of vertices at distance two are distinct. The lambda number of $\Gamma$, denoted by $\lambda(\Gamma)$, is defined as the minimum possible span of labels among all $L(2,1)$-labelings of $\Gamma$. In this paper, we establish upper and lower bounds for $\lambda(\Gamma_{RP}(G))$ and characterize the conditions under which these bounds are achieved. As an application, we determine the exact value of $\lambda(\Gamma_{RP}(G))$ for certain classes of finite groups.

papers.title: A characterization of finite modular 2-groups via magnitude homology
papers.abstract: Finite quasihamiltonian groups - that is, finite groups in which every pair of subgroups commutes - admit several characterizations. In this work, after introducing the notion of sectional contractibility graph, we provide a new characterization in terms of (a suitable subgroup of) magnitude homology. Our approach especially focuses on the subgroup lattices of finite groups and on the related notion of modularity. We present a detailed study for finite 2-groups, and, in particular, in the case of extraspecial 2-groups and Pauli groups. These groups, of interest because of their diverse applications in both mathematics and physics, already describe the wealth of information that one can obtain in restricting the study to the case of 2-groups.

papers.title: Saddle Codazzi tensor on spheres and hemisphere rigidity
papers.authors: Jian Ge, Mijia Lai, Yuntian Zhu
papers.abstract:
Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\geq 3$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. We ask whether $M$ must be isometric to the standard hemisphere if $\sec_g\geq 1$, $\partial M $ is isometric to the standard unit sphere, and its second fundamental form is Codazzi.
  Our approach centers on saddle Codazzi tensors on round spheres, where the saddle condition requires the restriction to every tangent two-plane to have nonpositive determinant. By analyzing the associated support maps, we prove that every smooth saddle Codazzi tensor on $\mathbb S^m$ vanishes identically for $m\geq 3$. Together with Panina's examples on $\mathbb S^2$, this shows that, among unit spheres of dimension at least two, nontrivial smooth saddle Codazzi tensors exist precisely in dimension two. The vanishing theorem yields an affirmative answer to the hemisphere rigidity question for $n\geq 4$.
  In dimension three, we realize the nontrivial saddle Codazzi tensors provided by Panina's construction, after scaling, as the second fundamental forms of smooth perturbations of the standard hemisphere, preserving the round boundary metric and the sectional curvature lower bound. This produces counterexamples to rigidity in dimension three. Nevertheless, under the same curvature and boundary assumptions, we prove the sharp inradius estimate $r_{\mathrm{in}}(M)\leq \pi/2$, with equality if and only if $M$ is isometric to the standard hemisphere.

papers.title: Schur-Positve Symmetric Functions from Products: Log-Majorization, Total-Positivity, and PSD Matrices
papers.abstract: For a polynomial $F(t) = 1 + a_1 t + a_2 t^2 +\dots + a_d t^d$ with coefficients in a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra $\mathcal{R}$, we consider Schur-positivity of the symmetric function $\Omega_F(\mathbf{x}) = \prod_{i \geq 1} F(x_i)$. Using work of Lindstr\"om and Gessel--Viennot, we give sufficient conditions for Schur-positivity in terms of directed networks. In the case when $F(t)$ is the multivariate independence polynomial of the incomparability graph $inc(P)$ of a natural unit interval order, we apply these ideas to give a new proof of Schur-positivity of the chromatic symmetric function $X_{inc(P)}(\mathbf{x})$. Additionally, we prove Schur-positivity of certain sums of chromatic symmetric functions, refining recent work of Amdeberhan--Shareshian--Stanley. In the case when $\mathcal{R} = \mathbb{Q}[z_1,z_2,\dots,z_n]$, we prove necessary and sufficient conditions for Schur-positivity in terms of symmetric function evaluations. In particular, we show for $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^n$, $s_\lambda(\mathbf{u}) \geq s_\lambda(\mathbf{v})$ for all partitions $\lambda$ if and only if $m_\lambda(\mathbf{u}) \geq m_\lambda(\mathbf{v})$ for all partitions $\lambda$, and these inequalities are equivalent to $\mathbf{u}$ log-majorizing $\mathbf{v}$. Using representation theory of $GL(\mathbb{C}^n)$, we prove Schur-positivity of $\Omega_F(\mathbf{x})$ when $F(t) = \det(I + t\sum_{i = 1}^m z_i \mathbf{v}_i \mathbf{v}_i^*)$ for a collection of vectors $\mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2,\dots, \mathbf{v}_m \in \mathbb{C}^n$. As an application for this result, we introduce the Kirchhoff symmetric function $K_G(\mathbf{x})$ of a loopless graph $G$ and show that it it always Schur-positive.

papers.title: Exponential loss of memory for random Lasota--Yorke convex maps with local average expansion
papers.abstract: We study i.i.d. random compositions of piecewise convex interval maps whose first branch is full. Uniform expansion is not required, and the maps may have contracting branches. Under a local average expansion condition at the origin, we prove both quenched and annealed exponential loss of memory for initial densities of bounded variation. The proof is based on a coupling argument. As applications, we obtain the quenched almost sure invariance principle and a rate of convergence in the quenched central limit theorem.

papers.title: Globally Optimal Estimation of Nested Logit Models
papers.abstract: Nested logit is widely used in operational demand models, yet jointly estimating its utility coefficients and nest dissimilarity parameters requires nonconvex optimization. Standard estimation routines offer no certificate of global optimality, leaving a gap between globally optimizing decisions under nested-logit demand and reliably estimating that demand model. We develop, to our knowledge, the first globally convergent optimization framework with an explicit global-accuracy guarantee for joint nested-logit estimation. Our central complexity result confines all exponential dependence to the number of free nest dissimilarity parameters: computation is polynomial in the numbers of observations, alternatives, and utility coefficients. Consequently, under the stated compact-domain and relaxation-error conditions, fixing the number of nests yields an additive polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS). The framework exploits an exact exponential-cone formulation for fixed dissimilarities and a spatial branch-and-bound algorithm that searches only over the free dissimilarities. Valid likelihood bounds provide an anytime certificate and finite termination at any prescribed additive average-log-likelihood tolerance. Across eight benchmark datasets and 240 estimation instances, the method certifies every reported solution and exposes inferior local estimates despite normal solver termination. These results establish a computational foundation for globally certified nested-logit estimation.

papers.title: A Self-Coupling Gaussian Extremal Inequality for Information-Constrained Optimal Transport with Applications to Rate-Distortion-Perception
papers.authors: Jiayang Zou, Jun Chen, Ayfer \"{O}zg\"{u}r, Jia Wang
papers.abstract: How much mutual information is needed to achieve a target correlation between two copies of a prescribed distribution? We prove a sharp Gaussian extremal inequality for this self-coupling problem: among distributions with a fixed mean and covariance, the Gaussian has the greatest minimum information cost for meeting a positive semidefinite cross-covariance target. The inequality is strict for non-Gaussian distributions when the target is positive definite. The proof uses a midpoint gluing construction. Two Ornstein--Uhlenbeck half-bridges, each started from the prescribed endpoint law, meet at a common intermediate distribution and are joined by conditional gluing. Changing the Gaussian reference then turns the resulting relative-entropy bound into the desired extremal inequality. As a first application, scaling one endpoint of the self-coupling establishes Gaussian extremality for rate-distortion-perception with unlimited common randomness, under quadratic distortion and squared Wasserstein-2 perception measures. We also establish an analogous result for finite common randomness, where the problem involves two mutual information constraints associated with an auxiliary random variable. In that setting, we retain an intermediate observation on one half-bridge and balance the two information budgets simultaneously using the Poincar\'{e}-Miranda theorem.

papers.title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
papers.abstract: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.

papers.title: Proving the optimality of the product construction for the intersection--union problem
papers.authors: Fan Chang, Peter Frankl, Jian Wang
papers.abstract: Let $m(n,p,q)$ be the largest size of a family of subsets of $[n]$ whose members pairwise intersect in at least $p$ vertices and omit at least $q$ common vertices. We prove that a product on disjoint sets attains this maximum whenever $p,q\ge2$ and $n\ge2^{15}(p+q-2)^3$. Together with the second author's result for $p=1$ or $q=1$, this establishes Frankl's Intersection--Union Product Conjecture in a wide range.

papers.title: Probabilistic Powerdomains of Pointed FS-Domains are FS-Domains
papers.authors: Xiaoyong Xi, Chong Shen, Dongsheng Zhao
papers.abstract: The Jung-Tix problem concerns the compatibility of probabilistic powerdomains with Cartesian closed categories of domains. We prove that both the subprobability and probability valuation powerdomains of every pointed FS-domain are FS-domains.

papers.title: The 3-adic Steinberg block and a categorical 3-adic local Langlands correspondence for $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$
papers.abstract: We extend the work of Johansson-Newton-Wang-Erickson on a categorical $p$-adic Langlands correspondence over $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ to $p = 3$ by recontextualizing their construction in the Steinberg case. We produce a novel, more categorical method of analyzing the properties of this construction without requiring an explicit algebraic presentation. As input to this argument, we also perform some new analysis of the representation theory of the $3$-adic Steinberg block of $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$, obtaining results complementing those of Pa\v{s}k\={u}nas.

papers.title: Classification of Hom--Lie structures on finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras
papers.authors: Jiacheng Sun, Chi Zhang, Haoran Zhu
papers.abstract: We classify the Hom--Lie structures on finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from \(2\) and \(3\). Except for the three-dimensional simple Lie algebra and the Zassenhaus algebras, every such structure is a scalar multiple of the identity. In the two exceptional cases, we determine the full Hom--Lie space: it has dimension six for the three-dimensional algebra, while for a Zassenhaus algebra it consists precisely of the multiplication operators arising from the corresponding divided-power algebra. This proves a conjecture of Makhlouf and Zusmanovich.

papers.title: Graded Structures of $v$-adic Carlitz Multiple Polylogarithms and $v$-adic Multiple Zeta Values
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms and $v$-adic multiple zeta values. We prove that, for every finite place $v$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(\theta)$, the natural weight gives a graded structure on the algebras generated by these values. Moreover, we show that every $\overline{\mathbb{F}_q(\theta)}$-linear relation among these values arises from an $\mathbb{F}_q(\theta)$-linear relation. In particular, our results establish a function field analogue of the Furusho-Yamashita direct sum conjecture and extend Chen's work from finite places of degree one to arbitrary finite places.

papers.title: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
papers.authors: Vincenzo Di Gennaro, Antonio Rapagnetta, Pietro Sabatino
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the N\'eron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$.

papers.title: Dimension-free comparison inequalities between $f$-divergences for Gaussian location mixtures
papers.abstract: We establish dimension-free comparison inequalities between the Kullback-Leibler (KL) and $\chi^2$-divergences and the squared Hellinger distance for Gaussian location mixtures with compactly supported mixing distributions. We show that both divergences are bounded by the squared Hellinger distance up to constants depending only on the radius of the support, independently of the ambient dimension and the number of mixture components. These results resolve an open question raised by \cite{jia2023entropic} and strengthen existing comparison inequalities. Our proof relies on a Gaussian interpolation argument that relates the derivatives of these divergences to differences between posterior means.

papers.title: A sharp lower bound for $h$-fold restricted sumsets of integers
papers.abstract:
Let $A\subseteq[0, L]$ be a set of $k\geqslant 9$ integers such that $0, L\in A$ and $\gcd(A)=1$. Define the $h$-fold restricted sumset $$h^{\wedge}A=\{a_1+\cdots+a_h: a_i\in A,\ 1\leqslant i\leqslant h, \ \ a_i\neq a_j\ {\rm for}\ i\neq j\}. $$ In this paper, we prove that, for every $1\leqslant h\leqslant k-1$, we have $$|h^{\wedge}A|\geqslant h(k-h)-k+2+\min\{L, h(k-h)-\mathbf{1}_h\}, $$ where $\mathbf{1}_h=1$ for $h\in\{2, k-2\}$ and $\mathbf{1}_h=0$ otherwise. The bound is sharp for every $1\leqslant h\leqslant k-1$ and the cardinality threshold $k\geqslant 9$ cannot be decreased.
  We also give a lower bound for the union of two consecutive restricted sumsets in a cyclic group and characterize equality.

papers.title: On an open question about the equivalence of monotone maximality and surjectivity condition in $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ spaces: Negative and partially positive answers
papers.abstract:
In a Hilbert space, it is known that a monotone operator is maximal if and only if the \emph{surjectivity condition}, \ie its resolvent has a full domain, holds.
  This equivalence is an open question in a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space, knowing only that the surjectivity condition implies the monotone maximality.
  In fact, there have been three approaches to generalize the monotonicity from a Hilbert space into a $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ space $X$ --- \textbf{A:} the ones of dual space $X^{\ast}$, \textbf{B:} of linear dual space $X^{\diamond}$, and \textbf{C:} of tangent bundle $TX$.
  In this paper, we answer \emph{negatively} on the first two approaches by constructing counterexamples on an $\mathbb{R}$-tree.
  We then go on proving that the equivalence is \emph{affirmative} on the same $\mathbb{R}$-tree, without any assumption on the domain.
  Moreover, we show that the answer is still \emph{positive} in some other cases, through a flat slice principle that transfers Minty's principle from Hilbert spaces to flat convex subsets, and through Minty's principle on proper Hilbert-Hadamard spaces satisfying a convex half-space condition.
  The question of equivalence \emph{remains open} under the general setting with the tangential approach.

papers.title: $\varepsilon$-$\mathcal{VU}$ spaces and approximate leaves\\ for sublinear composite functions
papers.abstract: Let \(h\) be proper, closed and sublinear, and let \(F\) be of class \(C^1\). The exact \(\mathcal{VU}\) calculus of the composite \(f=h\circ F\) is taken as known. This paper studies enlargements \(\bar\partial_\varepsilon h\subset\partial_\varepsilon h\) and the resulting \(\varepsilon\)-spaces of \(f\). Nested inclusions give one-sided Painlev\'e--Kuratowski limits of \(\mathcal{V}_\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon\) at points of the lineality space \(\mathcal{U}h(0)\). An additional transversality transfers those limits through \(F\); without it only the exact chain rule is available. Approximate leaves \(\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(x)=F^{-1}\bigl(F(x)+\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon h(F(x))\bigr)\) are inner semicontinuous under the nesting \(\mathcal{U}h(F(\bar x))\subset\mathcal{U}_\varepsilon h(F(x))\). For a polyhedral outer function the activity set freezes along the exact leaf for small \(\varepsilon\), so the dimension identity holds on that leaf and not necessarily in a full neighbourhood of \((\bar x,0)\). Partial smoothness of \(h\) relative to \(\mathcal{U}h(0)\) extends a known result from the origin to the lineality space; it is not used by the transfer theorems.

papers.title: A sound pure type system with ranks as sorts and Type-in-Type
papers.abstract: We present a dependently typed pure type system that contains a circular axiom $s : s$ for a certain sort $s$ and is nonetheless strongly normalizing. Girard's paradox is avoided because our sorts are not closed under a $\Pi$-former: function types are placed in sorts according to their rank. Turns out that this system has a unique set of characteristics: it has similar normalization behaviour as STLC (so complexity of normalization is TOWER-complete) while at the same time allowing non-uniform representation of arbitrary elementary recursive functions; furthermore, it has a nontrivial set-theoretical model in ZF+GCH and allows to carry out nontrivial proof developments. Base normalization proof is surprisingly simple (modulo general metatheoretical properties of pure type systems) and has been fully formalized in vanilla Rocq (formerly Coq) without additional axioms.

papers.title: On the isoperimetric profile in infinite dimensional pro-Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nontrivial compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric. On the compact pro-Lie group $K^{\N}$ we define a weighted variation by summing the distributional variations in its Lie group coordinates. We prove that all sublevel sets with bounded $L^1$-norm and weighted variation are compact in $L^1$ if and only if the coordinate weights tend to infinity. The proof gives a quantitative estimate for approximation by Haar averages over normal subgroups, illustrating that it is possible to apply a methodology which is typical of the geometric measure theory in a specific area of the topological group theory. The resulting perimeter is invariant under left and right translations and is preserved under pullback by quotient homomorphisms equipped with quotient metrics. Isoperimetric minimizers exist at every prescribed Haar probability. For the infinite torus, the compactness condition is equivalent to properness of a weighted length on its character group and to compactness of a Fourier multiplier's resolvent. Finally, we show that locally compact noncompact groups require an additional condition of tightness, in order to be treated as an appropriate generalization of the compact case.

papers.title: Refined proper descent for left completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces
papers.abstract: We refine the proper descent of Postnikov completed sheaves on locally compact Hausdorff spaces to the dualizable world.

papers.title: Pre-Query Retention with Bounded Bit and Word Retrieval
papers.abstract: An agent can retain information before receiving a future question and later retrieve evidence from an archive. Evaluating this arrangement requires accounting for both retained information and the width of each retrieval response. Decision-tree capacity bounds describe individual sets of distinguishable records, but a memory writer must encode every possible record before the query is known. We study fixed-length retention beside an immutable binary archive, with a worst-case limit on raw bit or word reads. We characterize feasible one-bit-read memory cells and construct encoders that partition the complete record space. Supporting pairwise exclusive disjunction and conjunction with one bit read is equivalent to supporting every Boolean query. For multiple reads, we combine explicit encoders with decision-tree counting and an entropy converse. The word-read bounds differ by at most two retained bits when the read budget is at most half the archive length. Under an explicit condition on word width and archive length, raw-word caching attains the exact optimum among all writers. A related condition preserves this optimum under positive average error. Exhaustive checks validate the implementations. In a matched dialogue-agent study, a categorical sufficient statistic preserves source decisions with less storage and lower decoding latency than the universal encoder. A catalogue-specific index reduces private state further and requires additional shared storage. The results characterize how response width and future query structure determine retention requirements.

papers.title: Identity crisis on tightly $C^{(2)}$-compact cardinals
papers.abstract: Bagaria and Goldberg asked if $\kappa$ being tightly $C^{(n)}$-compact implies $\kappa\in C^{(n+1)}$ for natural numbers $n\ge 1$? Usuba gave a negative answer for $n=1$. In this paper we give a negative answer for $n=2$.

papers.title: The center conjecture for cyclotomic Hecke algebras and cohomology of quiver varieties
papers.authors: Jun Hu, Andrew Mathas, Lei Shi, Ben Webster
papers.abstract:
For a quiver without edge loops, we construct an isomorphism from the cohomology of a Nakajima quiver variety with coefficients in an arbitrary field to the Jucys--Murphy center of the corresponding cyclotomic KLR algebra over that field. In affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, combining this with a dimension count shows that this Jucys--Murphy center coincides with the full center in characteristic $0$, when the characteristic does not divide $e$, and when the characteristic equals $e$. This follows from a geometric theorem showing that the sum of these cohomology rings is cocyclic as a module over an integral form of a loop algebra.
  As a consequence, we prove that the center of a cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type $G(r,1,n)$ with $q\neq 1$ over any field is generated by symmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements, and the same holds over any commutative domain in which $q-1$ is invertible. We also prove a generalization to the integral case of the conjecture of Krylov, Paegelow and Shlykov identifying the equivariant $K$-theory of the core of a Gieseker variety with the cocenter of the generic cyclotomic Hecke algebra, including the natural extension of this conjecture to positive characteristic.

papers.title: Non-Acceleration of the Heavy-Ball Method in 1D
papers.authors: Konstantinos Fotopoulos, Michael Helcig, Karl Deck, Jannis Alsbach
papers.abstract: Despite having an asymptotically optimal rate of convergence on convex quadratics, the acceleration of Polyak's heavy-ball method and a characterization of its dynamics within more general settings have remained long standing open problems. Recently, the work of Goujaud et al. [Math. Program. (2025)] made progress regarding acceleration in the context of smooth, strongly convex minimization: for a small enough inverse condition number, either the method does not accelerate on quadratics, or there exists a smooth strongly convex function such that heavy-ball cycles over the roots of unity. The constructed functions have two variables, thus leaving the question of acceleration over univariate functions open. In this work, we use a Fourier-based analysis to i) provide a proof for the non-acceleration of the heavy-ball method over the class of univariate smooth strongly convex functions. We also ii) provide a strict enlargement of the previous root-of-unity cycling region, with insights regarding the "fractional" sets of Goujaud et al. [arXiv:2502.19916], and iii) give a higher dimensional cycling instance which is not covered by root-of-unity cycling.

papers.title: Sharp Pointwise Error Estimates of Finite Element Methods for the Biharmonic Equation
papers.authors: Buyang Li, Zhenglei Li, Qigang Liang, Xuejun Xu
papers.abstract: We prove sharp pointwise error estimates for finite element approximations of the clamped biharmonic equation on convex polygonal domains. For $C^1$-conforming elements, we establish $W^{2,p}$-stability for all $2\le p\le \infty$, together with best-approximation type estimates in $W^{1,\infty}$ and $L^\infty$. For the nonconforming Morley element, we derive optimal estimates in $W^{2,p}$, $W^{1,\infty}$, and $L^\infty$; in particular, the $L^\infty$-error is of order $O(h^2)$ without an additional logarithmic factor. The analysis is based on three ingredients: local energy estimates for conforming and nonconforming plate elements, a removal of the local $L^2$-error term in these estimates, and H\"older estimates for derivatives of the Green's function. These tools are combined with a dyadic decomposition argument for regularized Green's functions. The results remove logarithmic losses present in earlier pointwise estimates for fourth-order problems and yield sharp rates for classical plate elements such as the Argyris, Bogner--Fox--Schmit (BFS), Hsieh--Clough--Tocher (HCT), and Morley elements.

papers.title: Directional Fineness for Radiant and Co-Radiant Sets: Separation and Quantitative Approximation
papers.abstract:
A prescribed directionally fine family of cones yields separation and primal bipolar identities for closed radiant and co-radiant sets in real normed spaces. Positive levels of adapted positively homogeneous functions separate points from closed radiant sets, while a correction by the norm provides bounded radiant neighbourhoods for co-radiant separation. The resulting classes also calibrate radial thresholds and represent gauges and cogauges through strict separators. For convex directionally fine families, the separating generators can be chosen Lipschitz and superlinear, yielding convex separating superlevels.
  Closed co-radiant sets with compact direction sets admit finite relative outer approximations by positive superlevels of selected generators, with separation preservation and directional and bounded-section error estimates, without requiring continuity or boundedness of the radial profile. Superlinear generators yield a global residual error bound, exact penalization for Lipschitz objectives, recovery estimates, and convergence of bounded approximate minimizers.
  An explicit convex directionally fine axial family is available in every real normed space. Its norm-corrected functions realize separation and bipolarity without rotundity assumptions, while an axial recovery map improves the relative distance factor from $\eta/(1-\eta)$ to $\eta$. A three-ray production model illustrates the quantitative recovery estimates.

papers.title: Prekosmic Grothendieck/Galois Categories
papers.abstract: We develop a theory on duality between groups and the categories of their representations, by providing an abstract characterization of such categories. The theory has two parallel formulations, each presenting a duality analogous to one of the two that were originally proposed by Grothendieck: the one between profinite groups and the abstract categories of their continuous representations on finite sets, and the other between affine group schemes over a field and the abstract categories of their finite-dimensional linear representations. In the present theory, groups and their representations are internal to a symmetric monoidal base category, with no finiteness condition imposed. The role of a fiber functor is played by a fiber point, an abstraction of the forgetful functor with its chosen adjoint. Over each base, a group determines the category of its representations equipped with the canonical fiber point, and a pointed abstract category determines the group that represents the presheaf of automorphisms of its chosen fiber point. These constructions yield mutually quasi-inverse equivalences of $(2,1)$-categories. By introducing change of base, we gather the dualities over individual bases into a single duality in each formulation. For a pointed abstract category, fiber points of the category are in perfect correspondence with torsors under the group associated to the chosen point. As an illustration of the theory, we reformulate the Galois theory of covering spaces for nonempty, path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected spaces.

papers.title: A counterexample to Reich's fixed point problem
papers.abstract: This note provides a negative answer to the well-known Reich's problem in fixed point theory.

papers.title: Non-canonical Oscillator Representations of Orthogonal Lie Algebras and Pfaffian Varieties
papers.abstract: Associated varieties are fundamental geometric invariants in the study of infinite-dimensional representations of semisimple Lie algebras. Luo and Xu (2013) constructed a large family of infinite-dimensional irreducible representations of orthogonal Lie algebras by applying Fourier transforms to the natural oscillator representations. In this paper, we prove that the associated varieties of these irreducible representations are isomorphic to explicitly described coordinate linear sections of Pfaffian varieties. The modules are realized as spaces of polynomial solutions of transformed Laplace equations. We construct filtrations from weighted polynomial degrees and determine the annihilator ideals of the corresponding associated graded modules. The defining equations consist of linear coordinate equations, minors and quadratic Pfaffian relations. The even and odd orthogonal Lie algebras are treated separately. The associated varieties are viewed as reduced affine schemes over a field of characteristic zero. In each irreducible family with fixed Fourier parameters, the associated variety is independent of the grading parameter. When the two Fourier parameters coincide, the projectivizations in the even case are Grassmannians.

papers.title: An optimal inequality between nonlinear eigenvalues in convex sets
papers.abstract: Let $\lambda_p(\Omega)$ be the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the $p$-Laplacian in a bounded convex open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge2$. We prove that $p\mapsto\lambda_p(\Omega)^{1/p}/\pi_p$ is strictly decreasing, where $\pi_p^p$ is the first eigenvalue on the unit interval. Consequently, for $1<q<p<\infty$, the sharp upper bound for $\lambda_p(\Omega)^{1/p}/\lambda_q(\Omega)^{1/q}$ is $\pi_p/\pi_q$. This bound is not attained and is approached by slabs, resolving the conjecture on the supremum formulated in the plane by Parini (J. Convex Anal. 2017). The proof combines log-concavity of the first eigenfunction with a vector field constructed from the one-dimensional eigenfunctions. The endpoint limits recover the Hersch--Protter and reverse Cheeger (or Buser) inequalities.

papers.title: The minimum number of vertices of a triangulation of $\mathbb{RP}^5$
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that every finite simplicial triangulation of real projective five-space has at least twenty-four vertices. Together with the construction of Guyer, Steinerberger, and Yang, this determines the minimum. A cup-product argument produces an induced subcomplex on sixteen or seventeen vertices. Transfer to the spherical double cover then imposes a covering condition on its lifted faces. In the sixteen-vertex case, a direct capacity bound excludes twenty-two vertices. For twenty-three vertices, a cochain extension argument reduces every relevant completion to one of 115 critical signed complexes; integer weights and exact covering certificates exclude all of them. The argument requires no assumption that the triangulation is combinatorial.

papers.title: Non-existence of Negative Weight Derivations of the Moduli Algebras of Isolated Weighted Homogeneous Hypersurface Singularities
papers.abstract: Mather and Yau proved that the analytic isomorphism class of an isolated complex hypersurface singularity is determined by its dimension and its moduli algebra. Yau's conjecture asserts that the moduli algebra of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity over $\mathbb{C}$ has no nonzero derivation of negative degree. We prove this conjecture. The proof uses Varchenko\textquotesingle s theorem on the $\mu$-constant stratum of an isolated weighted homogeneous singularity, also stated by M. Saito.

papers.title: Sharp quantum logarithmic Sobolev inequalities via semigroup interpolation
papers.abstract: We develop a semigroup interpolation method for sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequalities using spectral calculus and estimates of $\mathrm{Re}\langle\,Lx,x^2\rangle_2$, where $L$ generates an auxiliary symmetric quantum Markov semigroup. We apply the method to free groups and to crossed products of a finite von Neumann algebra $\mathcal N$ by $\mathbb Z$ or $\mathbb Z_n$, for $n=2$ or $n\ge4$, when the action commutes with the semigroup on $\mathcal N$. In particular, the word-length generators on quantum tori and the Weyl word-length generators on $M_n(\mathbb C)$ satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with optimal constant $2$.

papers.title: Crossing numbers of complete bipartite graphs
papers.authors: J\'ozsef Balogh, Nicholas Layman, Bernard Lidick\'y, Florian Pfender, Gelasio Salazar, Sam Spiro, Jan Volec
papers.abstract:
Zarankiewicz's long standing conjecture states that the crossing number $cr(K_{m,n})$ of the complete bipartite graph is \[ Z(m,n):=\bigg\lfloor{\frac{m}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{m-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n}{2}}\bigg\rfloor \bigg\lfloor{\frac{n-1}{2}}\bigg\rfloor. \] Using flag algebras, we show that $cr(K_{n,n}) \geq 0.96936 \cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. We also show that the rectilinear crossing number $\overline{cr}(K_{n,n})$ of $K_{n,n}$ is at least $0.987\cdot Z(n,n) + o(n^4)$. Additionally, we prove the following for complete bipartite graphs: if a drawing of $K_{n,n}$ contains no induced subdrawing of $K_{3,4}$ with exactly two crossings whose endpoints intersect in exactly one vertex, then it has at least $Z(n,n)+o(n^4)$ crossings. This is a local restriction inspired by Tur\'an-type problems that gives an asymptotically tight result.
  A closely related conjecture is Hill's conjecture stating that the crossing number $cr(K_{n})$ of the complete graph $K_n$ is \[ H(n):= \frac14 \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor \] for all $n \geq 3$. By an averaging argument, the asymptotic Zarankiewicz conjecture implies the asymptotic Hill conjecture. We improve the lower bound on $cr(K_{n})$ from $(0.985+o(1)) H(n)$ to $(0.9899+o(1)) H(n)$.
  Both conjectures were claimed to be true in manuscripts by OpenAI dated Sep 23, 2026 and made public on Oct 6, 2026. This paper represents the state of knowledge before those publications and shows how far we can push the flag algebra method.

papers.title: A relationship between three-dimensional Bessel processes in terms of Pitman's transformation
Condensation and Non-condensation in the Quasilinear 4-wave Kinetic Equation
papers.abstract: We study finite-time condensation at zero frequency for the isotropic quasilinear 4-wave kinetic equation in three dimensions. With Schrodinger dispersion and a product interaction coefficient with exponent $\beta\in(0,3/4]$, we construct global measure solutions $(g_t)_{t\geq0}$ for every nonnegative initial measure $g_0$ with finite wave action and energy. We then establish the sharp threshold $\beta=1/4$ for finite-time condensation of the constructed solutions. For $\beta\in[1/4,3/4]$, the constructed solutions satisfy $g_t(\{0\})=g_0(\{0\})$ for all $t\geq0$. For $\beta\in(0,1/4)$, every constructed solution with $(g_0)_{\mathrm{ac}}\neq0$ satisfies $\|g_t-\mathcal{N}_0\delta_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq C\mathcal{N}_0(1+\mathcal{N}_0^2t)^{-(1-4\beta)/40}$ for all $t\geq0$, where $\mathcal{N}_0=g_0([0,\infty))$ and $C=C(\beta,g_0/\mathcal{N}_0)>0$. In particular, for every $\zeta\in(0,1)$, there exists $T_\zeta<\infty$ such that $g_t(\{0\})\geq(1-\zeta)\mathcal{N}_0$ for all $t\geq T_\zeta$.

papers.title: Complementary Cauchy Elasticity
papers.abstract: We develop a nonlinear theory of complementary Cauchy elasticity in which the right Cauchy-Green strain is prescribed as a function of the second Piola-Kirchhoff stress, without assuming constitutive invertibility or the existence of a complementary strain-energy function. We introduce the complementary stress-work 1-form and characterize the obstruction to complementary hyperelasticity through the failure of major symmetry of the tangent compliance tensor. For general implicit elasticity, we show that the simultaneous closure of the stress-work and complementary stress-work 1-forms is characterized by the Lagrangian structure of the constitutive manifold. Using the Darboux classification, we obtain local canonical representations of anisotropic and isotropic complementary Cauchy elastic solids, including explicit non-hyperelastic examples. We investigate kinematic and stress constraints, including applications to pentamode solids, and show that internally constrained constitutive relations are naturally formulated on equivalence classes of stresses modulo reactive stresses. We formulate the balance laws and thermodynamics covariantly and establish that covariance of the energy balance directly yields the balance of angular momentum in complementary Cauchy elasticity, unlike in conventional Cauchy elasticity. Finally, we linearize implicit, Cauchy, and complementary Cauchy elasticity about finitely deformed and prestressed configurations and show that nonlinear non-hyperelastic solids may possess hyperelastic linearized responses.

papers.title: Generalized symmetric pairs, Lie superalgebras, Dirac operators and Kostant constants
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we present a geometric construction of contragredient Lie superalgebras, with the exceptions of $A(m,n)$ $(m,n>0)$ and $G(3)$.
  Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an order 4 automorphism $\sigma$, the eigenspace decomposition being $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)+\mathfrak{g}(-1)$. When $\mathfrak{g}(i)$ admits a $\mathfrak{g}(1)$-invariant symplectic structure, $(\mathfrak{g},\sigma)$ is called a \emph{generalized symmetric pair with symplectic subspace}. In this paper, we classify all such pairs and construct a natural Lie superalgebra structure on $L= L_{\bar{0}}+L_{\bar{1}}$ with $L_{\bar{0}}=\mathfrak{g}(1)$ and $L_{\bar{1}}=\mathfrak{g}(i)$.
  Furthermore, we investigate the constants arising from the squares of two distinct Dirac operators: $D$ for $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{g}^{\sigma^2}+\mathfrak{g}^{-\sigma^2}$, and $D_s$ for $L=\mathfrak{g}(1)+\mathfrak{g}(i)$. We prove that the constant $C$ in $D^2$ admits a remarkable factorization \[C=J^*(\Omega_{L_{\bar{0}}})\cdot\dim L_{\bar{1}}\cdot h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}},\] where $h^\vee_{\mathrm{sign}}$ is the signed dual Coxeter number of $L$ and $J^*(\Omega_{L_{\bar{0}}})$ is a mapped Casimir constant of its even part. This formula reveals an unexpected unification of symmetric space geometry and Lie superalgebra invariants.
  Finally, we prove that the Kostant constant $\mathrm{K_s} = \left.\Omega_{L_{\bar{0}}}\right|_{L_{\bar{1}}}=\frac{1}{2}$ is universal for all contragredient Lie superalgebras with non-degenerate Killing form, which implies that the constant $C_s$ in $D_s^2$ satisfies $C_s=\frac{1}{16}\dim L_{\bar{0}}$. We then establish a bijection between such superalgebras and solutions of the superadmissibility index equations $E_s^{I\!I} =\frac{1}{2}, E_s^I = \frac{1}{2}$, recovering the classification from an invariant-theoretic perspective.

papers.title: An inclusion coupling of prefix laws and the Chan-Pak rank inequality for all finite posets
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a finite poset, let $x\in P$, and let $N_k$ count its linear extensions in which $x$ occupies position $k$. We prove Chan and Pak's conjecture that, for all integers $a,h\ge1$, \[ (a+h-1)N_{a+h-1}N_a\ \ge\ (a-1)N_{a-1}N_{a+h}+hN_aN_{a+h}. \] The key result is an inclusion coupling of the laws of the set of elements preceding $x$, conditional on consecutive positions of $x$. We construct reversible exchange chains on the corresponding layers of order ideals and couple their generators so that the two prefix sets remain nested. Fishburn's correlation inequality gives monotonicity of endpoint probabilities; their unit total masses provide the rate bounds needed for the coupling. A stationary distribution of the coupled chain then has the required marginals. Normalized cover observables yield a four-term nonnegative certificate for the case $h=1$, and the general case follows by telescoping. The argument applies at every width and gives a proof of Stanley's log-concavity inequality with Fishburn's inequality as its sole external inequality.

papers.title: Covering finite fields by translates of multiplicative subgroups
papers.abstract:
Let $G_d$ be the subgroup of index $d>1$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and put $G_d^0=G_d\cup\{0\}$. For a covering $A+G_d^0=\mathbb{F}_q$ with $\#A=s$, we prove $q\le d^{8s/d}$ by shifting the roots of a Bonferroni polynomial. Although a uniform bound in $s$ alone must allow exponential growth, our estimate confines such growth to bounded indices and gives polynomial bounds when $s/d$ is bounded. A cubic specialization gives bounds of degree at most eight for $s\le2d$. For shift sets of logarithmic size, higher moment estimates give a uniform covering-probability formula, including the critical window. Together with the index restriction, this determines the covering indices of almost every shift set of size $\lceil k\log q\rceil$ for each fixed integer $k\ge2$.
  A subfield construction attains the order of the uniform restriction on the index. We determine its covering number exactly and prove minimality under subgroup inclusion. We also characterize equality in the elementary counting bound by subfield cosets. Fixing a subfield as the shift set in a quadratic extension leads to a sharper projection bound, attained by an infinite family with unique representations outside the shift subfield.

papers.title: The Streets--Tian conjecture on compact homogeneous quotients
papers.abstract: A Hermitian-symplectic metric is a Hermitian metric whose K\"ahler form is given by the $(1,1)$-part of a closed $2$-form. Streets-Tian Conjecture states that a compact complex manifold admitting a Hermitian-symplectic metric must be K\"ahlerian (i.e., admitting a K\"ahler metric). We study Hermitian-symplectic metrics on homogeneous complex manifolds with compact isotropy, and on their compact discrete quotients. If the transitive group is connected and unimodular, we show that an invariant Hermitian-symplectic form gives an invariant K\"ahler metric, with no lattice assumption. By averaging, the same conclusion holds for compact quotients, even if the initial metric has no invariant lift. The proof uses the top exterior power of a Hermitian-symplectic form to bound the volume functional on an invariant Aeppli slice. Applying this bound to midpoint metrics gives a uniform trace estimate. From this, volume maximization produces a balanced metric in the slice, which is also pluriclosed and hence K\"ahler. We also describe the resulting K\"ahler representative and give examples showing the role of the closed lift.

papers.title: Local Approximation of $A$-Harmonic Functions and the Super-Localization Conjecture
papers.authors: Moritz Hauck, Chupeng Ma, Daniel Peterseim
papers.abstract: We consider the local energy approximation of $A$-harmonic functions on concentric cubes with a fixed size ratio in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, for bounded, symmetric, uniformly elliptic diffusion tensors~$A$. We give a short proof of the Kolmogorov $n$-width decay rate $\exp(-cn^{1/(d-1)})$ conjectured by Ma [Found.\ Comput.\ Math.\ 26 (2026), 1699--1758], where $n$ denotes the approximation dimension. We apply this result to numerical homogenization, improving local approximation estimates for multiscale spectral generalized finite element methods and proving the conjectured local super-localization rate of Hauck and Peterseim [Math.\ Comp.\ 92 (2023), 981--1003] for interior Cartesian patches.

papers.title: Classification of Isometric Immersions of Spherical and HCMU Footballs into $\E^{3}$
papers.abstract: We study global isometric immersions of rotational metrics with two conical ends into Euclidean three-space. For a metric $g=\mathrm{d}u^2+f(u)^2\mathrm{d}\theta^2$ of positive Gauss curvature, we prove that vanishing endpoint traces of the weighted mixed shape coefficient $f^2b$ force every smooth isometric immersion to be rotational. The resulting congruence classes are parametrized by an integer angular covering degree bounded below by the two cone-angle parameters. The proof combines a scalar elliptic equation derived from the Gauss--Codazzi system, the maximum principle, and a global angular closing condition. For spherical footballs, isolated-singularity theory and a direct estimate in coordinates conformal for the second fundamental form establish the trace condition for every smooth immersion of the regular part. We also classify all rotational isometric immersions of HCMU footballs, including those whose curvature changes sign. When the minimum curvature is nonnegative, this classification exhausts the immersions satisfying the trace condition, and hence all immersions admitting a $C^2$ polar extension at both tips.

papers.title: Boundedness of nonregular bilinear pseudodifferential operators on variable Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces
papers.authors: Tengfei Bai, Jingshi Xu, Jinlai Zhu
papers.abstract: In this article, we introduce two bilinear, non-regular symbol classes\linebreak $BS\mathcal B^m_\delta(r,\mu,v;N,\lambda)$ and $BS\mathcal F^m_\delta(r,\mu,v;N,\lambda)$, where $m\in\mathbb R$, $0\leq\delta<1$, $0<\mu,v\leq\infty$, $1\leq\lambda\leq2$, $r>n/\mu$, and $N>2n/\lambda$, with $\mu<\infty$ for the latter class. For $\mu\geq1$, $(1-\delta)r\geq n/\mu$, and sufficiently large $N$, we establish boundedness of the associated bilinear pseudodifferential operators on Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with variable smoothness, integrability and summation exponents. To the best of the authors' knowledge, these operator estimates are new even on the classical Besov and Triebel--Lizorkin spaces with constant exponents. As an application, we establish the multiplication algebra property for both variable exponent spaces.

papers.title: Conventional Inference under Nonstationary Heavy Tailed Fractional Processes & Arrays
papers.abstract: Existing regression inference methods for nonstationary heavy tailed data are largely limited to unit roots tests. Functional central limit theorems (FCLTs), which are commonly used for the asymptotic analysis of nonstationary models, are inapplicable to nonstationary data characterized by a memory parameter $d<1$ and a stability parameter $\alpha<2$. Furthermore, it is well known that inference under nonstationarity is often non-conventional, and this issue is exacerbated in the presence of heavy-tailed data. The interaction of long memory and heavy tails significantly enlarges the nonstationary region---i.e., the covariate model space---where conventional inference methods typically fail. To address these challenges, we propose a new limit theory and methods that facilitate both workable asymptotics and conventional inference in regressions involving general nonstationary heavy-tailed covariate processes. Specifically, our approach develops a limit theory for heavy-tailed weakly nonstationary processes (hereafter, HT-WNPs), which lie on the threshold of nonstationarity (cf. Duffy and Kasparis, 2021, Annals of Statistics). We demonstrate that the proposed methods---including IVX-based and related instrumental-variable procedures---facilitate conventional inference for a broad class of stationary and nonstationary heavy-tailed covariates. This class includes nearly and mildly integrated arrays, as well as nonstationary fractional processes with memory parameter $1-1/\alpha<d<2-1/\alpha$, where $\alpha\in(1,2]$. Our analysis is applicable to both parametric and kernel regression models. The finite-sample performance of the proposed methods is evaluated through a comprehensive simulation study. Additionally, we provide an empirical application to the predictability of stock returns using long-memory heavy-tailed predictors.

papers.title: An Exact Mass Threshold for Global Existence and Blow-up in Semilinear Anti-de Sitter Equations
papers.authors: Wanderley Nunes do Nascimento, Michael Reissig
papers.abstract:
We study the influence of the mass parameter on global existence and finite-time blow-up for the semilinear anti-de Sitter Klein--Gordon equation \[
  \phi_{tt}-e^{2t}\Delta\phi+n\phi_t+m^2\phi=|\phi|^p
  \qquad\text{in }[0,\infty)\times\R^d. \] After removing the damping term, we establish $L^2$ energy estimates for the resulting Klein--Gordon equation with constant coefficient in the potential. They imply global existence for arbitrary sufficiently small energy data, without spatial localization, whenever \(
  m^2>-\frac{d(2n+d)}{4}
  \quad\text{and}\quad p>1. \) In the remaining mass parameter interval above the structural threshold, an exact change to conformal time reduces the problem to a scale-invariant effective damped wave equation. Exponentially weighted energy estimates then extend global existence to \(
  -d(n+d)<m^2\le-\frac{d(2n+d)}4
  \quad\text{for every } \quad p>1. \) In the complementary regime $m^2\le-d(n+d)$, we prove finite-time blow-up for every $p>1$ and for weak solutions with finite speed of propagation arising from nonnegative, nontrivial initial data. We further obtain lifespan estimates that are polynomial at the threshold and logarithmic below it. Thus, $m^2=-d(n+d)$ is the exact structural mass parameter threshold separating the global-existence and blow-up regimes.

papers.title: Pre-Nichols algebras and generation of pointed Hopf algebras in positive characteristic
papers.abstract:
We study when a finite-dimensional pre-Nichols algebra $R$ of $V$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\nmid\dim R$, is necessarily isomorphic to the Nichols algebra $\B(V)$. A trace identity gives a rigidity criterion involving the twist on minimal defining relations. Using integral forms and Hochschild cohomology, we establish uniform rigidity for Yetter--Drinfeld modules of bounded dimension over fixed finite abelian groups, and obtain related results for certain modules over nonabelian groups.
  For every finite group $G$ of odd order, outside finitely many characteristics depending only on $G$, every finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $H$ with $G(H)\simeq G$ and dimension prime to the characteristic is generated by group-like and skew-primitive elements. If $G$ is abelian, then, outside a possibly larger finite set of characteristics, every such $H$ is a Hopf $2$-cocycle deformation of its associated graded Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Lucas' Theorem modulo $p^n$ via Harmonic sums
papers.abstract: Lucas' theorem states that for a prime $p$, integers $a,b\geq0$ and $0\leq r,s\leq p-1$, one has $\binom{pa+r}{pb+s}\equiv\binom{a}{b}\binom{r}{s}\bmod p$. Let $D(p^n)$ be the set of pairs $(r,s)$ with $s\leq r$ for which this congruence holds modulo $p^n$ for all $a,b\geq0$. Rowland characterized $D(p^2)$ in terms of harmonic sums and symmetries of Pascal's triangle. For $n<p$, we give a criterion for a point $(r,s)$ to lie in $D(p^n)$ in terms of generalized harmonic sums of order at most $n-1$. We show that $D(p^n)$ is invariant under the reflection $(r,s)\mapsto(r,r-s)$ and the rotation $(r,s)\mapsto(p-1-s,r-s)$, so that with every point it contains its full orbit under the dihedral group $D_3$. Applied to the vertices, our criterion gives a result of Jacobsthal-Ljunggren type modulo $p^n$. In particular, we recover Zhao's result $(0,0)\in D(p^4)$ if and only if $p$ is a Wolstenholme prime. We also study the centroid and the edge midpoints, whose membership in $D(p^3)$ and $D(p^4)$ is governed by Bernoulli numbers and polynomials, Wolstenholme primes and super Wieferich primes. In particular, for $p=205129$ the centroid lies in $D(p^3)$, answering a question of Rowland.

papers.title: Response theory at low temperature for weakly interacting quantum spin systems
papers.authors: Joscha Henheik, Marius Lemm, Tom Wessel
papers.abstract: Recent work by Greenblatt, Lange, Marcelli, and Porta (Commun. Math. Phys. 2024) provides the first rigorous justification of adiabatic theory for interacting quantum systems at positive temperature. Their analysis treats weakly interacting lattice fermions and combines a rigorous Wick rotation with fermionic cluster expansion techniques. Here, we study a class of weakly interacting quantum spin systems and derive response theory at positive temperature, thereby covering non-Fermi systems for the first time. Our proof identifies and exploits the locality property of local indistinguishability as a key ingredient in carrying out low-temperature adiabatic expansions. The fact that these systems satisfy local indistinguishability was recently established jointly with Adhikari (arXiv:2508.15907) using cluster expansion methods together with a probabilistic swapping trick.

papers.title: Finite Symplectic Automorphism Groups of K3 Surfaces in Characteristic Seven
papers.abstract: We classify all finite groups of order divisible by $7$ that admit a faithful symplectic action on a K3 surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic seven, together with the possible heights and Artin invariants. Combined with the known classification of tame actions, this gives the complete list of finite groups admitting such an action in characteristic seven.

papers.title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
papers.authors: Huagui Duan, Hui Liu, Wei Wang
papers.abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $\pi_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

papers.title: Semi-classical Szeg\H{o} kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $\Pi_{k,\leq k\mu_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, k\mu_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_k$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq k\delta)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.

papers.title: Upper Bound on the Correlation Energy of a Dense Fermi Gas in the Thermodynamic Limit
papers.authors: Niels Benedikter, Sascha Lill, Marcello Porta, Benjamin Schlein
papers.abstract: We prove that the random phase approximation provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density. More precisely, we consider a mean-field scaling regime where the kinetic and interaction Hamiltonian are scaled by $\rho^{-2/3}$ and $\rho^{-1}$, respectively. We use a correlated trial state constructed through a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle--hole excitations associated to patches on the Fermi surface. Key of the proof is to control the position-space localization of the collective excitations. Combined with an iterated Duhamel expansion of the expectation values of (localized) particle number operators we obtain extensive estimates, which justify the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian and its approximate diagonalization.

papers.title: Cellular bases of mirabolic Hecke algebras
papers.authors: Jian Chen, Yan Liu Jinkui Wan, Xirui Yu
papers.abstract: We prove that the mirabolic Hecke algebra $\mathscr{H}_{n,R}(q)$ over a commutative ring $R$ is cellular by constructing explicit cellular bases. When $R=\mathbb{K}$ is a field, we also establish a Morita equivalence between $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$ and a direct sum of Hecke algebras associated with symmetric groups. As applications, we classify the irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules and obtain a semisimplicity criterion. Finally, when $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{C}(q)$, we show that the cell modules arising from one of our cellular bases coincide with Siegel's irreducible $\mathscr{H}_{n,\mathbb{K}}(q)$-modules.

papers.title: The associated graded algebras of biserial fractional Brauer graph algebras
papers.authors: Jing Guo, Nengqun Li, Yuming Liu
papers.abstract: For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$, one can associate a graded algebra (denoted by $\mathrm{gr}(A)$) with the radical filtration of $A$. An interesting question is to compare the representation theories of $A$ and $\mathrm{gr}(A)$. When $A$ is a Brauer graph algebra with defining Brauer graph $\Gamma$, we have described the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ in terms of the information of $\Gamma$. In this paper, we describe the representation type of $\mathrm{gr}(A)$ when $A$ is a biserial fractional Brauer graph algebra - a notion that properly generalizes a Brauer graph algebra - in terms of the information of the defining biserial fractional Brauer graph $\Gamma$ of $A$.

papers.title: Maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity of finite element methods for stochastic parabolic equations in polygonal domains
papers.authors: Genming Bai, Jianbo Cui, Buyang Li
papers.abstract: We prove that a spatial semidiscrete finite element method preserves the stochastic maximal regularity of the heat equation on bounded convex polygonal and polyhedral domains in dimensions two and three. A main difficulty is to establish suitable Green-function estimates for stochastic convolutions, whose paths generally lack classical time derivatives. Besides, the failure of the Burkholder-Davis-Gundy (BDG) inequality at the endpoint $p=\infty$ creates additional difficulties. Our approach leverages a hidden symmetry structure of the discrete Green's function, which enables the use of a key integration-by-parts type formula. Then the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^p$ regularity with $p\in [2,\infty)$ is obtained from the discrete local energy estimates and interpolation inequalities. To extend further the discrete stochastic maximal $L^p$-$L^q$ regularity with the full range of integrability exponents, i.e., $p\in (2,\infty), q\in [2,\infty)$ or $p=q=2$, we also show that the discrete convolution kernel satisfies the stochastic H\"ormander's condition, allowing the application of a stochastic version of the Calder\'on-Zygmund theory.

papers.title: Noncommutative $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities
papers.authors: Li Gao, Marius Junge, Zhendong Xu, Hao Zhang
papers.abstract: We derive $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups on finite von Neumann algebras, from a spectral gap (PI) or from a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality (MLSI). For $p\ge2$, the corresponding coefficients have optimal order $O(p)$ and $O(\sqrt p)$, respectively. Both estimates follow from Beckner inequalities by integration along semigroups. We also establish a non-tracial extension to quantum Markov semigroups satisfying GNS detailed balance. As a direct byproduct, we apply $L_p$-Poincar\'{e} inequalities to Schatten-valued functions on graphs in order to obtain the Schatten distortion of expanders.

papers.title: New Bernstein functions and subordination representations for time-nonlocal evolution equations
papers.abstract: This paper establishes subordination representations from multi-term time-fractional differential equations to single-term ones, a direction complementary to the previously known subordination from single-term to multi-term equations; combining the two complementary directions also yields subordination representations between two multi-term equations. The crucial step is to prove that certain implicitly defined functions are Bernstein functions. We show that the quotient $\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\lambda^{\alpha_j}\big)/\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\alpha_j\lambda^{\alpha_j}\big)$ is a Stieltjes function whenever $0\leq\alpha_1-\alpha_m\leq 1$, and consequently that the inverse function of $\lambda=\big(\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\varphi^{\alpha_j}\big)^{1/\beta}$ is a Bernstein function for every $0<\beta\leq\alpha_m$. As applications, we obtain subordination representations with a clear probabilistic meaning: from multi-term to single-term time-fractional diffusion-wave equations, between abstract nonlocal-in-time equations with kernels of type $(\mathcal{PC})$ (including equations of tempered stable type), and between nonlocal-in-time telegraph equations. A necessary and sufficient condition for $[(\lambda+b)^\beta-b^\beta]^\gamma$ to be a Bernstein function also yields a negative result: in general, no such subordination exists from an $\alpha$-stable type dynamics to a tempered $\beta$-stable one when $\alpha<1$.

papers.title: De Finetti Structures in Networks of Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: Consider $N$ identical quantum systems at the vertices of a graph, interacting via pairwise edge couplings. We designate $K$ vertices as a system of interest $\mathrm S$ and the remaining $N-K$ as a reservoir $\mathrm R$. Under generic connectivity assumptions between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$, we show that for $N\to\infty$, the reduced state of $\mathrm S$ converges to a convex combination of symmetric product states of $K$ single-vertex density matrices -- called a de Finetti representation. Unlike in standard derivations for symmetric (exchangeable) systems, we establish de Finetti representations for quantum networks, which are inherently non-exchangeable. We construct the representations explicitly and quantify the convergence rate. We show that Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graphs exhibit the de Finetti structure: as the reservoir grows, the reduced state of any fixed finite subgraph converges almost surely to an explicit deterministic product state. As applications, we establish a general area law for the entanglement entropy of $\mathrm S$, analyze mean-field and fluctuation scalings of the $\mathrm S$-$\mathrm R$ interaction, and illustrate our results on qubit networks. We also derive quantitative convergence estimates for information-theoretic quantities, including von Neumann entropy, mutual information, and entanglement within $\mathrm S$ and between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$.

papers.title: A Common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph
papers.abstract: Let G be a simple connected graph with the vertex set V (G) and the edge set E(G) such that |V (G)| = n and |E(G)| = q. The common neighborhood graph con(G) of G has the same set of vertices as that of G and uv is an edge in con(G) if u and v have at least one common neighbor in G. By a signed graph S, we mean a graph G whose edges has been assigned sign plus or minus. In this paper, the concept of common neighborhood graph has been initiated in the realm of signed graphs, that is, we define a common neighborhood signed graph of a signed graph.

papers.title: Pseudoconvex Exhaustions of Hartogs Domains Associated with $L^2$-Optimal Pairs
papers.abstract: By constructing a smooth pseudoconvex exhaustion of the associated Hartogs domain, we give a new proof of the Deng-Ning-Wang's characterization of plurisubharmonic functions without the smoothness assumption.

papers.title: Discrete geometry and de-Rham cohomology of graphs
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of discrete spaces which are built by gluing coordinate patches together into an atlas, much as a manifold is built from charts. Graphs are the main examples, and an atlas on a graph gives it a geometric structure analogous to that of a manifold. This structure leads to a cohomology theory, which we show to be a discrete analogue of de Rham cohomology. We define a "discrete coordinatized space" as a cubical set equipped with the Alexandrov topology, on which differential forms become sheaves. When the atlas is regular, the de Rham cohomology agrees with the sheaf cohomology of the constant sheaf, just as in the smooth case. We compute it for several examples, including a torus graph and a graph resembling a sphere, and recover the cohomology of the corresponding surfaces.

papers.title: Variance Reduction Note 2: The Convergence of SPIDER
papers.abstract: The stochastic path-integrated differential estimator (SPIDER) tracks a gradient by accumulating small, shared-sample gradient differences and periodically refreshing the estimate. This second expository note on recursive variance reduction explains SPIDER-SFO and gives a self-contained proof of its expected first-order stationarity guarantee. The argument combines an epochwise mean-square error bound with descent under a clipped, normalized update. It yields $O(\epsilon^{-3})$ stochastic gradient evaluations in the online setting and $O(n+\sqrt n\,\epsilon^{-2})$ component gradient evaluations for a finite sum, with the remaining problem parameters fixed.
