papers.title: Approximation numbers of critical Besov embeddings
papers.abstract: We determine the approximation numbers of critical embeddings between isotropic Besov spaces on nonempty bounded Lipschitz domains in any dimension. For 0 < p_1 < 2 < p_2 <= infinity and s_1 - s_2 = d max{1/p_1, 1 - 1/p_2} > d(1/p_1 - 1/p_2), the approximation numbers have order N^{-1/2}(log(e+N))^Gamma for every 0 < q_1, q_2 <= infinity, with an explicit four-case formula for Gamma. This resolves the strictly compact critical Besov approximation-number problem identified in Vybiral's overview. For q_1 < q_2, the logarithmic exponent depends on the ordering of p_1' and p_2; it can vanish for one pair (p_1,p_2) and remain positive for another with the same fine indices. A row estimate for the approximation error gives lower bounds when the target fine index is below one. Gaussian finite-rank approximations acting on several levels give the sharp upper bounds when Gamma < 1/2. For q_1 < q_2, matching lower bounds for the two strict orderings of the inner indices follow from Malykhin's finite-window estimates and norm comparisons. The results include quasi-Banach indices and the full spaces of bounded coefficient sequences at infinite fine indices.

papers.title: Brauer and iquantum categorification
papers.authors: Jonathan Brundan, Alistair Savage, Ben Webster
papers.abstract: We show that locally finite Abelian module categories over the affine Brauer category are the same thing as locally finite Abelian 2-representations of a certain 2-iquantum group satisfying some additional nilpotency and finiteness properties. Our results are valid over algebraically closed fields of characteristic other than 2 and for arbitrary spectra. This extends recent work of Gao, Rui and Song, who treated characteristic 0 with half-integral spectrum. The relevant Satake diagrams are of quasi-split type AIII and of diagonal type A, including affine types in positive characteristic. The key step in our approach identifies the affine Brauer category with a topologically dense monoidal subcategory of a completion of the 2-iquantum group. As an application, we show that deformed cyclotomic quotients on the two sides are equivalent.

papers.title: Gaussian equivalence for CNN with non-Gaussian weights
papers.abstract: We study the infinite-width limit of convolutional neural networks with random weights and show that the Gaussian process limit does not require Gaussian priors. Assuming that the weights are i.i.d., centered, and have sufficiently many finite moments, converges weakly in the space of continuous functions on the compact input set to independent copies of a centered Gaussian process. Our framework accommodates activation functions of polynomial growth together with a broad class of patch-extraction operators, covering standard convolutions, padding, stride, and common pooling mechanisms.

papers.title: Structural Identifiability in Non-Gaussian Graphical Discrete Lyapunov Models
papers.abstract: This paper studies the problem of structural identifiability for graphical discrete Lyapunov models in the non-Gaussian setting from observational data. A graphical discrete Lyapunov model associated with a graph $G$ consists of the set of stationary distributions of stable first-order vector autoregressive models whose transition matrices have sparsity patterns determined by $G$. This model has a causal interpretation as $G$ can be viewed as encoding dynamic causal relationships between random variables of interest. It has been shown that generic parameter identifiability holds for reflexive directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). Structural identifiability for these models remains unstudied beyond certain restrictive cases. In this work, we prove a non-constructive structural identifiability result for reflexive DAGs in non-Gaussian graphical discrete Lyapunov models by leveraging the information contained in the entire collection of stationary cumulants. We also provide a concrete algorithm for learning reflexive directed trees from stationary cumulants of orders $\leq 5$.

papers.title: Single-level reformulations for network pricing under Wardrop equilibrium with separable affine costs
papers.abstract:
We consider the problem of setting tolls on a subset of the arcs of a congested network so as to maximize the revenue of a network authority, anticipating that users route according to a Wardrop equilibrium. This problem is naturally cast as a bilevel program in which the leader sets tolls while the followers respond by choosing an equilibrium routing.
  We focus on the important special case of separable affine arc cost functions. Under this assumption, Wardrop equilibria admit Beckmann's convex characterization, from which we derive three new single-level reformulations of the bilevel problem, exploiting both Beckmann's formulation and its dual: an arc-based formulation, which we solve exactly, and two path-based formulations, solved by column-and-constraint generation. Beyond the reformulations, we further derive from Beckmann's potential an upper bound on the optimal revenue that can be used to certify optimality gaps across all formulations.
  An extensive computational study on instances derived from the Sioux Falls and Eastern Massachusetts networks compares our formulations with the recent mixed-integer nonlinear formulation of Beck, Labb\'e and Schmidt. The arc-based formulation solves substantially more instances to proven optimality (within a time limit of 1800 s) than this formulation and, unlike it, returns a feasible solution on every instance. It remains effective on the largest, 74-node network, on which the formulation of Beck et al. solves none. The magnitude of the upper bounds on the tolls proves to be a major driver of tractability: the genuinely hard core of the benchmark emerges once the regulatory cap on tolls is removed. The two path-based formulations, used as heuristics, return a solution within one percent of the optimum on every instance whose optimal value is known, often in seconds where exact formulations reach the time limit.

papers.title: The asymptotic stability of the stable solitons of the generalized good Boussinesq equation
papers.authors: Junsik Bae, Scipio Cuccagna, Daniele Del Santo, Masaya Maeda
papers.abstract: This paper continues the series where we apply a synthesis of the virial inequalities in the tradition of Merle, Martel and their collaborators and of Kato smoothing, to close the virial inequalities. We prove absence of nonzero imaginary eigenvalues for the linearization in unweighted space and asymptotic stability for every velocity $\frac{\sqrt{p-1}}{2}<c<1$ and every $1<p<5$.

papers.title: The existence of symmetric cyclic Steiner quadruple systems
papers.abstract: A Steiner quadruple system of order $v$, denoted by $\operatorname{SQS}(v)$, is called cyclic if it admits $\mathbb Z_v$ as a group of automorphisms acting regularly on its point set. A cyclic system is called symmetric cyclic, or S-cyclic, if the multiplier $-1$ preserves each block orbit individually. Grannell and Griggs conjectured in 1983 that such a system of order $v$ exists if and only if $v\equiv2,4,10,20\pmod{24}$ and every odd prime divisor $p$ of $v$ satisfies $p\equiv1$ or $5\pmod{12}$. This paper proves the conjecture. The main step is to construct an $S$-cyclic Steiner quadruple system of order $2p$ for every prime $p\equiv1\pmod4$. Together with existing reduction theorems, these constructions determine which finite abelian groups admit a symmetric group-invariant Steiner quadruple system.

papers.title: On the Information Bottleneck for Ergodic Finite-State Markov Chains: Stationary Approximation and Asymptotic Optimality
papers.authors: Wael Tabbara, Jihad Fahs, Mohamad Assaad
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the information bottleneck problem for sources that follow discrete-time ergodic finite-state Markov chains. We propose treating observations generated by the time-varying Markov chain as if they were drawn from its unique stationary distribution, and we use the solution to the information bottleneck problem for the stationary process to compress samples from the time-varying process. The resulting error is upper bounded by several information gap terms. We establish sufficient conditions under which these gaps converge to zero and analyze the convergence rates of the different information gap terms. The proofs are based on intricate analysis using convergence of subsequences along with the derivation of properties of the optimization sets associated with the information bottleneck problem. In addition to the inequalities and convergence results we establish, our analysis offers insights into how simple properties of ergodic Markov chains give rise to results concerning the information bottleneck problem for such chains.

papers.title: Tur\'{a}n coefficients of signed graphs
papers.abstract: We use spectral methods to determine Tur\'an coefficients of signed graphs under containment that preserves negative edges and allows positive edges to be realized by either sign. For a fixed forbidden signed graph $\sF$ with at least one edge, the coefficient $\tht(\sF)$ is the supremum of the weights $\rho\ge1$ for which every $\sF$-free signed graph $\sG$ of order $n$ satisfies $e^+(\sG)+\rho e^-(\sG)\le\binom n2+o(n^2)$. We prove a variational characterization of the weighted extremal density and show that $\tht(\sF)=1+1/L(\sF)$, where $L(\sF)$ is the supremum of the adjacency spectral radii of $\sF$-admissible graphs. The coefficient is infinite exactly when the underlying graph $F$ is bipartite, and equals one exactly when $F$ has no independent set meeting every negative edge. When $\chi(F)=3$, the possible coefficients are exactly $1$, $3/2$, $1+1/\sqrt3$, $(1+\sqrt5)/2$, $1+1/\sqrt2$, and $2$, each of which is realized by a signed graph. In this case, if $\tht(\sF)>1$, then $L(\sF)$ is attained by an admissible graph on at most five vertices, and the order bound is sharp. More generally, when some path is inadmissible, we obtain explicit order bounds for connected admissible graphs with bounded maximum degree. We also derive restrictions on the algebraic degree and rational values of $\tht(\sF)$.

papers.title: Size Ramsey numbers of star forests with two components on one side
papers.abstract:
We determine the size Ramsey number of a two-component star forest versus an arbitrary star forest. Let $q,a,b,n_1,\ldots,n_q$ be positive integers with $a\ge b$ and $n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_q$. We prove that \[ \begin{split} \rhat\left(K_{1,a}\sq K_{1,b},
  \bigsqcup_{i=1}^{q}K_{1,n_i}\right) ={}&(a+n_1-1) +\sum_{i=1}^{q-1}\max\{a+n_{i+1}-1,b+n_i-1\}\\ &+(b+n_q-1). \end{split} \] This proves the conjecture of Burr, Erd\H{o}s, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp (Erd\H{o}s Problem~\#561) in the case where one of the two star forests has exactly two components. The formula holds without any restriction on the parity of the star sizes. The proof combines vertex deletion, iterated matching deletion, and Lov\'asz's factor theorem.

papers.title: When vector abundance constrains vector-borne transmission: inside epidemic dynamics within a prescribed population
papers.authors: Lise Isnel (BioSP), Julien Papa{\"i}x (BioSP), Olivier Bonnefon (BioSP), Samuel Soubeyrand (BioSP), Lionel Roques (BioSP)
papers.abstract: The global burden of vector-borne diseases continues to rise, presenting escalating challenges to public health and agricultural systems. Their expanding geographic range and associated impacts underscore the need for tools to project disease dynamics and evaluate interventions. Mechanistic compartmental host--vector models provide such a framework by explicitly representing transmission processes. However, while these models often couple vector population dynamics with infection spread, the inherent complexity of vector demographic processes calls for a more modular approach. In this study, we consider the setting in which the total vector abundance is an externally-prescribed input to a general vector-mediated transmission model. Our objectives are threefold: (i) to provide theoretical guarantees for ensuring consistency between the prescribed total vector abundance and the dynamics of the model compartments, (ii) to characterize model properties related to the local reproduction index (informing extinction or emergence near the time of introduction) and the inter-seasonal propagation, and (iii) to derive insights for diseases transmitted by Aedes albopictus in mainland France. We apply this framework by feeding the epidemiological model with vector-abundance data obtained either from entomological surveillance systems or from an external detailed population dynamic model. Moreover, epidemiological national surveillance data are used to estimate the transmission parameter. Based on this, we derive conditions for emergence and extinction, and show how the extent of the epidemic depends on introduction timing, transmission rate, and susceptible population density. Taken together, these results highlight the value of generating and leveraging entomological surveillance data as well as their model-based counterparts when observations are unavailable (which is particularly relevant in the context of global warming and for the evaluation of vector-control strategies). Overall, we establish a refined framework integrating such data or forecast into compartmental models, with strong potential for a wide range of applications in animal, human or plant health.

papers.title: Complex Analytic Structure of Hybrid Classes of Generalized Polynomial-like Mappings
papers.authors: Miaokeyan Lin, Weixiao Shen, Yimin Wang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study hybrid classes of generalized polynomial-like mappings. We show that locally they are complex analytic submanifolds with finite codimension equal to the total order of critical points in the filled Julia set (counting multiplicity).

papers.title: On the simultaneous zeroes of Bessel processes
papers.abstract: Given n independent squared Bessel processes, a priori with different dimensions, we investigate the first time $\zeta$ at which at least n -1 of them vanish simultaneously. We show that the tail asymptotics of $\zeta$ admits a power decay, with a persistence exponent given as the first positive pole of some explicit meromorphic function. This answers a question raised by Q. Berger, L. B{\'e}thencourt and C. Tardif in the case n = 3. We also provide along the way a closed-form expression for the Mellin transform of the position of the remaining process at time $\zeta$. The paper is concluded by a more detailed study of the case of identical dimensions.

papers.title: A note on the solution to the standard normal Stein equation
papers.abstract: For $z\in\mathbb{R}$ we reconsider the solution $f_z$ to the standard normal Stein equation, corresponding to the Kolmogorov distance for distributions on the real line. More precisely, we prove the Lipschitz continuity of the related function $x\mapsto \rho_z(x):=xf_z(x)$ and explain how this observation may help to remove some unnecessary technical conditions from recent Berry-Esseen bounds in the literature around the Malliavin-Stein method. We further show that the Lipschitz constants of the functions $\rho_z$ are yet not uniformly bounded in $z$ and discuss consequences of this negative result.

papers.title: Herzog Class of Codimension $3$ Licci Monomial Ideals
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be the polynomial ring in three variables with homogeneous maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$. Licci ideals are ideals that can be linked by a finite number of steps to a complete intersection. All licci ideals admit a rigid deformation, and two licci ideals are said to be in the same Herzog class if they have a common rigid deformation. Guerrieri-Ni-Weyman gave a parametrization for the Herzog classes of codimension $3$ licci ideals in terms of pairs of partitions associated to Schur functors. In this paper, we give an explicit formula that determines the Herzog class of a given $\mathfrak{m}$-primary licci monomial ideal.

papers.title: Quadratic growth rigidity for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation
papers.abstract: For the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, we prove the Liouville theorem for solutions with quadratic growth.

papers.title: Bernoulli property for skew products of exponentially mixing systems over Anosov bases
papers.abstract:
We study $C^{1+\beta}$ skew products over topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphisms, with fiber dynamics generated by a locally free $\mathbb{R}^k$-action. For a Gibbs measure on the base and a cocycle with a nonzero average, we establish a Bernoulli criterion for ergodic invariant product measures. The fiber hypotheses apply to actions that are exponentially mixing with respect to the SRB measure, as well as volume measures that are almost exponentially mixing with a limit SRB measure.
  As an application, when the fibers are generated by geodesic flows or Weyl chamber actions, our results reveal a statistical phase transition determined by the drift.

papers.title: Cutoff beyond non-negative curvature
papers.authors: Max Fathi, Arnaud Guillin, Cyril Labb\'e, Justin Salez
papers.abstract: We study how a relaxed gradient estimate is enough to prove cutoff for several new families of Markov processes, within the varentropy framework of [Sal25]. In particular, we show how certain regularization estimates from hypocoercivity theory allow one to prove cutoff for kinetic dynamics. Moreover, we prove cutoff for some families of diffusions with non-convex potentials and for mean-field dynamics, as well as for biased random walks on the symmetric group, giving a simple proof of a far-reaching extension of a result of [NY24].

papers.title: On the Adaptive Covering Complexity of Strings: Unifying Relative and Self-Referential Compression
papers.abstract: We introduce and study the adaptive covering complexity C adapt S (s), defined as the minimum number of contiguous factor blocks required to partition a string s when each block is either a factor of a fixed external dictionary S or a factor of the target's already decoded prefix. This hybrid admissibility model formalizes the structural interaction between static dictionary matching and dynamic nonoverlapping self-referencing.  Our main theoretical result is the exact logarithmic law  which is tight and proves that dynamic self-reference can reduce phrase count by at most an exponential factor over static dictionary covering alone. We establish structural equivalences showing that the measure bridges word-segmented Relative Lempel-Ziv and non-overlapping LZ77, and we prove exact preset-history LZ77 sandwich bounds. Furthermore, we establish the optimality of the longest-match greedy parse via an exchange lemma and present an optimal implementation based on dual suffix automata running in O(M + n) time and space for a constant alphabet. These analytical results are complemented by counting bounds, stationary-ergodic asymptotic invariance, a dictionaryselection NP-hardness result, and a concise empirical illustration.

papers.title: Twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes and the rational hit conjecture
papers.abstract: We study the top degree concentration property for the cohomology of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes of multiarrangements of hyperplanes. Our main tool is a short exact sequence of twisted logarithmic de Rham complexes based on the deletion-restriction exact sequences for logarithmic differential forms found recently by Abe and Denham. We prove a number of general results that can be used to establish the top degree cohomology concentration property, and also establish that property for some families of multiarrangements. As a consequence of our results, we prove the rational hit conjecture of R.~M.~W.~Wood about the coinvariants of the rational Steenrod algebra acting on the polynomial ring. We also make progress on the deformed version of that conjecture proposed by Hivert and Thi\'ery, prove generalizations of the rational hit conjecture for all complex reflection groups $G(m,p,n)$, thus answering questions of Bergeron, Borie and Thi\'ery, and generalize the rational hit conjecture to all standard subalgebras of the rational Steenrod algebra.

papers.title: MONODROMY AND BIG QUANTUM COHOMOLOGY OF HYPERPLANE SECTIONS OF (CO)ADJOINT VARIETIES
papers.authors: Vladimiro Benedetti (LJAD), Simone Billi (CMLS), Nicolas Perrin (CMLS)
papers.abstract: We study the monodromy representation of general hyperplane sections of (co)adjoint varieties. We apply this result to reduce the generic semisemplicity of the big quantum cohomology to its ambient part, and to prove that the big quantum cohomology of general hyperplane sections of IGr(2, 6) is generically semisimple and satisfies Dubrovin's conjecture.

papers.title: Half-sized gaps between zeros of the Riemann zeta function
papers.abstract: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we prove that the lower limit of the normalised gaps between consecutive zeros of the Riemann zeta function is at most $1/2$. Our methods utilise a more efficient method for detecting gaps with short Dirichlet polynomials. Specifically, we apply resonance to a quotient of shifted zeta functions, rather than to the number of zeros in a short interval, using a M\"obius resonator adapted to the symmetry between the shifts.

papers.title: Sharp thresholds and convergence for a nonlocal bistable equation
papers.abstract: We study $u_t=J*u-u+f(u)$ on $\R^d$ with a bistable reaction and radial nonincreasing probability kernels. Under the stated hypotheses, every solution from compactly supported data between zero and one converges to zero, locally to one, or to a single nonzero decaying stationary state. At every nonzero decaying stationary state between zero and one, we assume either nondegeneracy up to translations or analyticity of the reaction near the closure of the state's range. Decaying limits are strictly radially decreasing, with centers in the initial support's closed convex hull. For $u_0=\mathbf1_{B_R}$, we give explicit threshold bounds; analyticity near $[0,1]$ yields a unique critical radius with a nonzero stationary limit.

papers.title: Dual Reflection Groups from Solutions to the Yang--Baxter Equation
papers.abstract: Suppose that $r: X^2 \to X^2$ is a nondegenerate, involutive solution to the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation. To this data, we can associate an Artin--Schelter regular algebra $A$ and an infinite family of groups $G_k$, where $k \geqslant 1$. For each $k$, we show that $G_k$ is a dual reflection group for $A$, in the sense the component of $A$ graded by $1_{G_k}$ is again Artin--Schelter regular. We also show that, using the additional structure afforded by the underlying solution to the Yang--Baxter equation, one can determine the centre, Koszul complex, and associated twisted superpotential for $A$.

papers.title: Lagrangian invariant tori for completely resonant nonlinear Schr{\"o}dinger equations
papers.abstract: We study small solutions of the parameterless nonlinear Schr{\"o}dinger equations on the circle. In this regime, the nonlinearity is perturbative and the system is thus nearly integrable. We prove the persistence, in the presence of nonlinearity, of full-dimensional tori. We justify this denomination by proving that they are Lagrangian in the sense that, although they are not submanifolds (since they are compact), at every point their tangent cone is a Lagrangian subspace. This is the first result of this type for an equation without an infinity of external random parameters. We achieve this by establishing new fine decay and uniformity properties of the amplitude-to-frequency map. This is the main technical novelty of this paper. It allows us to modulate all the frequencies and thus obtain non-resonance conditions without any assumption on the choice of the tangential sites.

papers.title: Compactness and weak compactness of linearized Holomorphic-Lipschitz maps
papers.authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Bayart, Mathis Lemay, Colin Petitjean
papers.abstract:
Any holomorphic Lipschitz map $f$, defined on the open unit ball $B_X$ of a complex Banach space $X$ and taking values in a complex Banach space $Y$, can be uniquely and canonically associated with a bounded linear operator $\widehat f : \mathcal G_0(B_X) \longrightarrow \mathcal G_0(Y)$ between the corresponding holomorphic Lipschitz-free spaces. The aim of this paper is to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the compactness and weak compactness of such operators.
  In particular, we obtain a general characterisation of the compactness of $\widehat f$ in terms of metric properties of its symbol $f$. We then focus on the case where the target space is a subspace of $\ell_p$, $1\leq p<\infty$. When the target space is $\ell_1$, we show that compactness and weak compactness of $\widehat f$ are both equivalent to $\widehat f$ not fixing a copy of $\ell_1$. Finally, when the target space is $\ell_p$ with $1<p<\infty$, we obtain a metric characterisation of the weak compactness of $\widehat f$. As a consequence, we show that compactness and weak compactness need not coincide, even when the target space is $\ell_p$.

papers.title: New Maximum Hermitian $d$-Codes and New Invariants from Skew Polynomial Rings
papers.abstract: Maximum rank-distance codes were introduced independently by Delsarte (1978) and Gabidulin (1985) for unrestricted matrix spaces, and their study was subsequently extended to the classical form spaces of alternating, symmetric, and Hermitian matrices. For Hermitian $d$-codes, Schmidt (2018) established the upper bound and constructed optimal additive codes for all admissible parameters except when $n$ and $d$ are both even and $4\le d\le n-2$. We settle this final open existence case, more generally, construct additive maximum Hermitian rank-metric codes for every admissible length and minimum distance. Rather than working directly in the space of Hermitian matrices, we construct our objects within central simple algebras with unitary involution arising from quotients of skew polynomial rings. We also introduce scalar-field and Lyapunov operators in these algebras, leading to new invariants for the equivalence of additive Hermitian codes. Explicitly determining these invariants yields strong necessary conditions for Hermitian equivalence and demonstrates that our construction contains a large number of pairwise inequivalent codes.

papers.title: On Reduced Rank Regression
papers.abstract: We propose a decoupled solution to the Reduced Rank Regression (RRR) problem, i.e. a pair of matrices (A*, B*) whose product A*B* minimizes the least squares error under a rank constraint. Using our formalism, we rewrite two other solutions from the literature and compare them with ours. In particular, we prove that all these formulations are equivalent. We then analyze their time complexity, and compare their running time and numerical precision on synthetic data, from which we derive practical recommendations. An open-source implementation of the algorithms and experiments is available here: https://gitlab.inria.fr/trudkiew/reduced\_rank\_regression.

papers.title: A Non-linearizable Action of $S_3$ on Free Metabelian Lie and Associative Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be the free metabelian Lie algebra of rank $4$ over the field of complex numbers $\mathbb{C}$. We construct a non-linearizable action of the symmetric group $S_3$, the smallest nonabelian group, on $M$ by automorphisms. We also construct a non-linearizable action of $S_3$ on free metabelian associative algebras of rank $4$.

papers.title: Single-graph rational exponents in mixed multicolour Ramsey theory
papers.abstract: For every rational number $\gamma>1$, we construct a fixed bipartite graph $H_\gamma$ such that $r_k(H_\gamma;K_N)=\Theta_{\gamma,k}((N/\log N)^\gamma)$ for every fixed $k\ge 3$. Here $r_k(H;K_N)=r(H,\ldots,H,K_N)$, with $k$ copies of $H$. The lower bound uses a symmetric random algebraic graph which avoids a fixed rooted power and has sufficiently strong local density for the Alon-Rodl method. The main algebraic step establishes a nonzero obstruction within the full symmetric coefficient space; the upper bound uses the rooted graphs from the proof of the rational exponents conjecture. We also obtain induced even-cycle asymptotics in the same construction.

papers.title: On Carmichael Numbers Constructed from Consecutive Jacobsthal Numbers
papers.abstract: We prove that no Carmichael number has the form \[ N=(2^mJ_n+1)(2^mJ_{n+1}+1)(2^mJ_{n+2}+1), \] where \[ J_n=\frac{2^n-(-1)^n}{3} \] is the Jacobsthal sequence, \(m,n\ge1\), and all three factors are prime. Assuming that such an \(N\) is Carmichael, Korselt's criterion yields divisibility conditions relating consecutive Jacobsthal numbers to powers of two. Combining these conditions with the Binet formula and a finite case analysis for \(n\le4\), we obtain a contradiction. Consequently, this family contains no Carmichael numbers.

papers.title: Distributions of metric $n$-point invariants and applications to molecular evolution
papers.authors: Michael Bleher, Mario G\'omez, Facundo M\'emoli, Maximilian Neumann, Andreas Ott
papers.abstract: Datasets often arise as samples from a metric measure space whose geometry reflects the data-generating process. We introduce metric $n$-point invariants, defined as functions of the pairwise distances of $n$-point configurations, to study the geometry of such spaces. This provides a unified framework for existing concepts, such as the pairwise distance itself, the Gromov product, and Vietoris-Rips persistence diagrams. The distribution of a metric $n$-point invariant $F$ over random $n$-point configurations can be used to extract geometric information from the space and is obtained as the pushforward of Gromov's $n$-th curvature measure $\mu_n$ along $F$. Our main result is an explicit bound for the expected $p$-Wasserstein distance between $\mu_n$ and the empirical curvature measure $\hat{\mu}_{n}$ of finitely many sampled $n$-point configurations, and carries over to the associated distributions of Lipschitz metric $n$-point invariants. From this we derive the sample size needed to achieve a prescribed accuracy and level of confidence in the approximation of the curvature measure. As an application, we use metric $n$-point invariants to study molecular evolution. We describe how site-wise nucleotide frequencies shape the corresponding distributions in Jukes-Cantor and Halpern-Bruno substitution models, and analyse five million SARS-CoV-2 genomes, revealing increasingly common failures of the four-point condition, constrained nucleotide accessibility consistent with the biased mutation spectrum, and rare cycles in persistent homology reflecting recurrent mutations across lineages. These findings demonstrate the potential of our sampling-based approach to the geometry of data as a scalable, phylogeny-free tool for detecting and quantifying evolutionary structure in large genomic datasets.

papers.title: Solving Classes of Linear Programs with Strongly Polynomial Straight Line Complexity in Strongly Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Daniel Dadush, Zhuan Khye Koh, Bento Natura, Neil Olver, L\'aszl\'o A. V\'egh
papers.abstract:
Recently, Allamigeon, Dadush, Loho, Natura, and V\'egh (ADLNV, SICOMP 2025) introduced an interior point method for linear programs whose number of iterations is bounded by the so-called straight line complexity (SLC) of the instance. This yields a strongly polynomial bound on the number of iterations of the corresponding interior point algorithm for broad classes of linear programs. In particular, in the companion paper we give a strongly polynomial straight line complexity bound for two-variable-per-inequality linear programs. However, in order to obtain a strongly polynomial algorithm for these classes, one also needs to address two important technical issues: initialization and bit-complexity bounds. Standard IPM initialization techniques either require numerical estimates that cannot be obtained in the strongly polynomial model, or involve modifying the instance in ways that do not preserve the geometry of the original LP, potentially affecting the SLC.
  In this work, we present an initialization framework for interior point methods for linear programming, along with a rounding procedure that ensures the continued feasibility of the IPM. We develop a multistage scheme in which each stage can be initialized in strongly polynomial time given the output of the previous stage. Additionally, we address the challenge of controlling the bit complexity of each iterate throughout the algorithm. To this end, we show that it is possible to represent iterates as low-complexity convex combinations of vertices and extreme rays. Our combinatorial rounding step is independent of the algorithm in ADLNV 2025, and can be applied more broadly in the context of path-following methods.

papers.title: Gauss-Manin connection in disguise: limiting periods and quasi-Jacobi forms
papers.abstract: We construct a six-dimensional algebraic moduli space of elliptic curves equipped with two ordered marked points, an enhanced relative de Rham frame, and a nonzero tensor of endpoint tangents. Its normalized period map is a biholomorphism. On the classical period locus, the regular coordinates pull back under its inverse to Weierstrass, Eisenstein, and theta functions. The associated Gauss-Manin vector fields realize differential operators on quasi-Jacobi forms of integer index. To relate this elliptic space to the genus-two construction, we study a specified smoothing family over a five-dimensional space of limiting enhancements. For this family, we identify the regularized period matrix and the boundary pullback of the holomorphic part of the logarithmic connection with respect to the chosen plumbing parameter. We then compute the unit relating the algebraic smoothing parameter to the Siegel period parameter and the limits of the specified genus-two generators. Separately, we express classical Fourier-Jacobi coefficients in enhanced elliptic coordinates.

papers.title: Counting Irreducible Components of the Semistable Global Nilpotent Cone
papers.abstract: We discuss various methods for parametrizing and counting irreducible components of the global nilpotent cone of semistable $G$-Higgs bundles on a smooth complex curve. By restricting our study to the case of generically regular components following previous work of Faergeman and Raskin, we obtain explicit counts of semistable generically regular irreducible components for $G = \mathrm{SL}_n$, and give the first examples of such counts outside type A. These numbers are obtained by counting points in some natural polytopes associated to $G$, but our method requires a finer analysis in cases where the center of the group $G$ is disconnected.

papers.title: One bubble against a ring: new sign-changing solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem
papers.authors: Angela Pistoia, Giuseppe Mario Rago, Giusi Vaira
papers.abstract: We consider the Brezis--Nirenberg problem $-\Delta u=|u|^{2^*-2}u+\varepsilon u$ in the unit ball of $\mathbb R^N$, $N\ge5$, with Dirichlet boundary conditions, and we look for sign-changing solutions which, as $\varepsilon\to0^+$, blow up positively at the centre and negatively at the $k$ vertices of a regular polygon. The key observation is that, for this configuration, the gradient of the reduced energy factorises, so that the whole finite-dimensional problem is governed by the zeros of a single explicit function of the radius of the polygon. Its behaviour depends on the dimension: when $N=5$ such solutions exist for every $k\ge2$, and the ring of negative peaks approaches the boundary at distance $O(1/k)$; when $N\ge6$ there are two solutions for $2\le k\le6$, while no solution of this type exists for $k$ large. For $2\le k\le6$ the nodal set of every such solution reaches the boundary of the ball, in contrast with what happens for the almost critical problem. Nevertheless, the two solutions found for $N\ge6$ have very different nodal structures: numerically, for $3\le k\le6$ one of them has only two nodal domains, and its nodal set meets the plane of the peaks along a closed curve around the centre, while the other one can have as many as $k+1$ nodal domains. These results extend to higher dimensions a configuration previously found in dimension four.

papers.title: Depth based on translates of a convex body: geometry, floating bodies, and empirical theory
papers.abstract: For a fixed full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, we study the $K$-depth of a point $y$ with respect to a probability measure $\mu$ by comparing the masses of translates of $K$ that fail to contain $y$. Its upper level sets are intersections of high-mass translates of $K$, and hence are convex and admit an exact representation as Minkowski erosions. We distinguish the closed core determined by the maximisers of the translation-mass function from the effective support on which the depth exceeds its unavoidable baseline. We establish continuity, affine equivariance, comparison with halfspace (Tukey) depth, and normal-cone and smoothness criteria. For uniform measures on convex bodies, the regions coincide exactly with the ball floating bodies of Sch\"utt, Werner and Yalikun; for positive continuous densities they coincide with the weighted ball floating bodies of Werner and Yalikun. For dilates $tK$, the depth converges to a depth generated by the tangent cones of $K$ as $t \to \infty$; for smooth $K$ this limit is Tukey's halfspace depth, whereas nonsmooth testing bodies can produce a genuinely different limit. The worst-case maximal $K$-depth is exactly $1/h_T(K)$, where $h_T(K)$ is the Helly number of the family of translates of $K$. Under a uniform interior rolling-ball condition and compact support and having zero mass on hyperplanes, the convergence to halfspace depth is monotone and uniform with an explicit error bound. If the density is bounded by $L$, then this bound is of order $O(t^{-1})$ and this order is sharp. We also record that the dependence on the testing body is not monotone in general, while Hausdorff perturbations of $K$ give stable depth functions and regions at regular levels. Finally, we prove uniform consistency and pointwise weak limits for empirical $K$-depth, including the non-Gaussian limit caused by nonunique active translates.

papers.title: An $8+9$ gluing computation for the Ramsey number $R(F_3,F_4)$
papers.abstract: Let $F_t$ be the graph consisting of $t$ triangles with a common vertex and otherwise disjoint vertices. We prove that $R(F_3,F_4)=17$ using an $8+9$ gluing computation. Neighbourhood matching arguments give degree and clique restrictions that reduce the search on seventeen vertices to $88,294,674$ ordered seed pairs. The verified main computation excludes $88,294,634$ pairs. A cross-edge counting argument excludes thirty-four of the forty exceptional pairs, and independently checked finite-domain certificates exclude the remaining six. Together with the construction whose red graph is the complete bipartite graph $K_{8,8}$, these results establish $R(F_3,F_4)=17$.

papers.title: Full-horizon magnetic control of the Vlasov--Poisson system for plasma confinement
papers.authors: Giacomo Albi, Giacomo Dimarco, Federica Ferrarese, Lorenzo Pareschi
papers.abstract: We study the full-horizon control of a two-dimensional Vlasov--Poisson system through an externally imposed magnetic field. The control is represented by time-dependent coefficients associated with smooth, spatially localized basis functions, and is designed to steer selected position and velocity moments of the distribution function while limiting particle dispersion and the control effort. Starting from the kinetic constrained optimization problem, we derive the continuous first-order optimality conditions, including a backward Vlasov equation, an elliptic adjoint equation, and the variational inequality associated with bounded controls. We then project this system onto a particle--grid representation and identify the resulting particle adjoints and control gradient. The full-horizon field is then computed on a reduced particle ensemble, initialized by an instantaneous control, and subsequently applied to a larger set of particles. Numerical experiments indicate that the instantaneous control field already provides an effective baseline, while the full-horizon correction can further reduce the relative thermal energy near the boundaries and improve confinement over the prescribed time interval.

papers.title: Absence of non-threshold embedded eigenvalues for nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
papers.abstract:
We consider the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ \begin{equation*}
  i\partial_tu+\Delta u+|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation*} We prove the absence of non-threshold embedded eigenvalues for the linearized operator around the positive ground state when $d=1,2$ and $p>1$, or when $d\ge3$ and $1<p\le1+\frac4{d-2}$. Starting from the fluid variables of NLS, we derive a biharmonic wave equation for the phase gradient after linearization around the ground state. Seeking a virial identity for this equation, we identify a mechanism for establishing a repulsive structure, which guides the subsequent ODE analysis to exclude embedded eigenvalues.

papers.title: Dunnett's and Tukey's procedures under mixed model covariance structures: dimensional reduction of multivariate-t integrals
papers.abstract:
Dunnett's test compares several treatments with one control, and Tukey's test compares every pair for independent samples with a common variance. We investigate which designs and covariances for a linear mixed model remain on the ordinary Dunnett and Tukey integrals, and in which direction the constants move when the correlation changes. It is shown that for Dunnett's procedure AR(1), the Toeplitz band, alternating ante-dependence, and the random slope have roots below the ordinary analysis-of-variance value, while heterogeneous compound symmetry and heteroscedastic groups have roots above that value. For Tukey's procedure every computed non-spherical covariance lowers the root.
  The second goal is the dimensional reduction of these multivariate-t integrals: a normal probability mixed over one chi-square scale. Conditioning on the latent variables shared by the contrasts replaces that probability by a product of univariate normals, and the integral has the dimension of the conditioning vector plus one. Balanced compound symmetry leaves a double integral. The studentized range reduces to the Pearson-Hartley integral. The reduction stops for asymmetric overlap of four or more treatments, for four or more autoregressive or unstructured follow-up times, for pair-dependent variances or correlated disjoint pairs, and for a separate variance estimate in each group.

papers.title: Study of the finite element discretization of the iterated quasi-reversibility method -- The Laplacian data assimilation case
papers.abstract: We investigate the finite element discretization of the iterated quasi-reversibility method, in the context of the data assimilation problem for the Laplacian. We provide error estimates explicit in all the parameters appearing in the model and the method (i.e. the amplitude of noise, the size mesh, the regularization parameter and the number of iterations of the method). This allows to devise strategies to choose the aforementioned parameters, for example to guarantee convergence of the method when the level of noise goes to zero. Numerical experiments on a two-dimensional problem are provided, illustrating the relevance of the obtained estimates.

papers.title: Local structure of sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets
papers.abstract: We show that if $X$ and $Y$ are self-similar sets in $\mathbb{R}$ with multiplicatively independent contraction ratios, then the Assouad dimension of $X+Y$ is one. As an application, we show that for a large class of self-affine carpets, the Assouad dimension of any non-principal orthogonal projection is one. The latter result is new even for the simplest case of Bedford-McMullen carpets.

papers.title: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv theorem for finite groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$. The Gao constant $\mathsf{E}(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length $\ell$ contains a subsequence of length $|G|$ whose terms can be ordered to have product equal to the identity. In 1961, Erd\H{o}s, Ginzburg and Ziv proved that every sequence of $2n-1$ integers has an $n$-term subsequence whose sum is divisible by $n$; equivalently, $\mathsf{E}(C_n)\leq 2n-1$, where $C_n$ denotes the cyclic group of order $n$. In this paper, we prove that $\mathsf{E}(G)\leq |G|+|G|/p-1$ whenever $G$ contains no cyclic subgroup of index $p$. Consequently, every finite non-cyclic group satisfies $\mathsf{E}(G)\leq |G|+|G|/p+p-2$, with equality if and only if $G$ contains a cyclic subgroup of index $p$. This establishes the conjectured upper bound for the Gao constant and provides a complete characterization of the equality case.

papers.title: Unimodular defect and antipodal lattice points of smooth reflexive polytopes
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a smooth reflexive polytope and let $Q=P^{*}$ be the dual of smooth Fano polytope. Ewald's conjecture (1988) predicts that the lattice points of $P\cap (-P)$ contain a lattice basis. In general it is not even known whether $P\cap (-P)$ contains a nonzero lattice point; we call this weakest form of the conjecture the antipodal condition. We define the unimodular defect of a finite set of lattice vectors as the least number of vectors that must be removed to leave a unimodular set, and the unimodular defect of $Q$ as that of its vertex set. Defect zero gives the unimodular smooth Fano polytopes, for which Ewald's conjecture is known. Our main result is that every smooth Fano polytope of unimodular defect at most two has a \emph{flat ridge}, a ridge $W$ with $|\det(v,W)|\leq 1$ for all vertices $v$; consequently its dual satisfies the antipodal condition. We also consider removed sets of pairwise non-adjacent vertices. Using results of Nill on independent vertices, we show that every such set has at most two elements unless $Q$ is unimodular, so the antipodal condition holds whenever such a set exists.

papers.title: Smooth radial quantized Type II blow-up for the three-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract:
We consider the focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in three dimensions. In \cite{Schmid2026CVPDE}, Schmid constructed finite-time type II blow-up solutions with a continuum of blow-up rates, while the existence of smooth finite-time type II blow-up solutions remained open. We resolve this problem by constructing, for each integer $L\ge1$, smooth radial solutions concentrating a single ground state with the blow-up rate $\lambda(t)=(\ell+o(1))(T-t)^{2L}$ for some $\ell>0$.
  Our proof follows a forward construction based on modulation analysis with the energy method. The main obstacle is the lack of a repulsive structure that can be directly exploited to control the remainder. To overcome this obstacle, we adapt Kato's smoothing theory from asymptotic stability analysis to the forward construction. This yields a global spacetime Morawetz estimate for the linearized flow, providing the spacetime control needed to bound the higher-order energy in place of the monotonicity derived from repulsive structures in previous blow-up constructions.

papers.title: On the Peak Estimation of Scalar Polynomial Systems via Integrability
papers.abstract: We develop a convergent occupation measure framework for peak estimation of scalar polynomial dynamical systems with no a priori state bound. The key observation is that scalar trajectories satisfy a uniform weighted integrability bound whose exponent precisely compensates for the singularity introduced by polynomial compactification. This yields a finite measure formulation with polynomial data. We establish a superposition principle for the resulting weighted continuity equation, prove no relaxation gap and establish convergence of the associated moment-sum-of-squares hierarchy.

papers.title: Ampleness of non-symmetric line bundles on degenerations of abelian varieties
papers.abstract: Answering a 1985 question of Moret-Bailly, we prove by way of counterexample that if a line bundle $\mathscr{L}$ on a degeneration of abelian varieties $G \to \mathrm{Spec}(R)$ is not symmetric, then $\mathscr{L}$ being ample on $G$ is not necessarily equivalent to $\mathscr{L}$ being ample on the generic fiber of $G$. Our technique of proof is to use the Fourier expansion principle for sections of line bundles on degenerations, due to Faltings--Chai and Lan.

papers.title: A numerical study of radius update rules in trust-region algorithms
papers.abstract:
Part I [arXiv:2606.30202] and Part II establish which trust-region radius update mechanisms can fail and under which hypotheses they must succeed. Neither says where the thresholds sit once a rule runs with real constants, or how the rule interacts with the model Hessian and the subproblem solver. This paper turns them into nine falsifiable claims and settles what it can, on four designed problems where the theory's quantities are computable and on CUTEst, where only aggregate cost is visible. Every mechanism runs in one Julia package written for this study, so two runs differing in one component differ in nothing else.
  The rule is worth less than the model and more than nothing. Crossing the mechanisms with four model Hessians puts $96.5$ per cent of the variation on the model and $1.6$ on the rule, and the rules separate most under the most accurate model rather than least. Uncapped R-grad is the robust default among the criticality-anchored rules, though the retrospective rule is ahead of it on this collection. No constant escapes the side conditions. For every cap there is a minimiser at which the constraint stays active, and for every anchoring constant a flatness on which escape takes arbitrarily long. The second of these is proved here as well as measured, and the proof uses no property of the model or of the subproblem solution beyond $\|s_k\| \leq \Delta_k$.
  The radius rule governs the length of the step, and so the cost of a run. The model decides the search direction, and with it whether the run converges at all.

papers.title: Structural conditions on trust-region radius updates. Part II: second-order convergence and asymptotic radius behaviour
papers.abstract:
Continuing Part I (arXiv:2606.30202), we ask not which structural conditions on $\{\Delta_k\}$ suffice for global convergence but what the radius does; the answers separate the mechanisms by whether the radius is tied to a criticality measure.
  We identify three asymptotic regimes: the criticality-anchored rules give $\sum_k \Delta_k^2/M_k < +\infty$, hence $\liminf_k \Delta_k = 0$, and $\Delta_k \to 0$ once the model Hessians are bounded; the step-driven rules inherit the summability of the step series, hence $\sum_k \Delta_k < +\infty$; the fixed-factor rules keep $\Delta_k$ bounded away from zero. Near a critical point with positive definite Hessian, convergence of a subsequence forces convergence of the full sequence.
  We then extend the framework to second-order criticality through $\tau_k = \max\{\|g_k\|, -\lambda_k^-\}$, obtaining convergence to second-order critical points with the worst-case complexity $\mathcal{O}(\max\{\varepsilon_g^{-2}\varepsilon_H^{-1}, \varepsilon_H^{-3}\})$, which reduces to $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ for a common tolerance and is sharp for quadratic models.
  Finally we establish eventual inactivity of the constraint and superlinear convergence, isolating the two properties of the radius rule through which the mechanism enters; the rate itself is mechanism-independent. The criticality-anchored and capped gradient-scaled rules reach inactivity only under a side condition, $\zeta > \overline{\kappa}$ or $\overline{\mu} > \overline{\kappa}$, with $\overline{\kappa}$ a constant of the solution that cannot be checked in advance. These conditions are necessary, not artefacts: on $f(x) = \sin(x)/x$, $\overline{\kappa}$ is unbounded over the minimisers, so no parameter value meets the condition at all of them. Among the rules tied to a criticality measure, only those with an unbounded multiplier escape such a constant.

papers.title: Zero products of Toeplitz operators with harmonic symbols on the Bergman space of the unit ball
papers.abstract: In this paper, using local boundary factorizations of harmonic functions and singular-value estimates for Toeplitz products, we study the zero-product problem for Toeplitz operators on the Bergman space of the unit ball in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We prove that a finite product of such operators is zero only if one of the symbols is identically zero, provided that all the symbols are harmonic on the open unit ball and continuous on the closed unit ball.

papers.title: Dual Quaternion Discrete Linear Canonical Transforms: FFT-Based Fast Algorithms and Joint Rotation--Translation Pose Denoising
papers.authors: Yi Wu, Xuan Chen, Kit Ian Kou
papers.abstract: Rigid-body pose signals couple rotation and translation, yet most existing denoising pipelines treat them separately and analyse them only in the Fourier domain. We show that this separation is unnecessary and often suboptimal. We fuse dual quaternions, which encode rotation and translation in a single singularity-free algebra, with linear canonical transforms, which supply flexible quadratic-phase analysis, to develop one- and two-dimensional dual quaternion discrete linear canonical transforms (DQ-DLCTs) with an explicit kernel ordering. We establish inverse and energy-preservation properties, structured spatial and frequency convolution relations, and, crucially, fast algorithms built on complex FFTs. These algorithms make the DQ-DLCT practical: a two-stage chirp-adaptive scheme then performs joint rotation--translation denoising in a single transform domain. Numerical experiments confirm the accuracy and efficiency of the fast transform and demonstrate strong denoising performance on measured pose sequences and constructed two-dimensional pose fields. The DQ-DLCT thus turns a heavy algebraic construction into a deployable tool for pose signal processing.

papers.title: Singularities of Multidimensional Item Response Models and the Rank of the Fisher Information Matrix
papers.abstract: Statistical models in item response theory are known to be singular. This singularity manifests itself as a loss of rank in the Fisher information matrix, and the usual theories underlying AIC and BIC, which assume regularity, cannot be applied without further justification. Chen and colleagues analyzed this degeneracy and nonregular likelihood ratio tests, but their analysis does not identify all the directions that produce degeneracy or their dimensions. In this study, we analyze the entire kernel of the Fisher information matrix as a linear space for multidimensional item response models, separating the degeneracy due to rotations from that due to an over-specified latent dimension without double counting. We determine the dimension of each component and the exact rank of the information matrix, and prove a formula for computing, from the item parameters, the dimension of the degeneracy that remains after these components are removed. These results go beyond establishing the existence of singularity to identifying its causes and extent, providing a foundation for inference and model comparison in IRT.

papers.title: Prescribed Beurling densities in spectral eigen-subspaces
papers.abstract: Let $(q,D,L)$ be a one-dimensional Hadamard triple with $2\leq m:=\#D<q$, and let $\mu_{q,D}$ be the associated self-similar probability measure. Write $\mathcal T=\{t\in\mathbb Z:(q,D,tL)\text{ is a Hadamard triple}\}$. We prove that, for every $0<s<\log m/\log q$ and every $\zeta\in[0,+\infty]$, there are continuum many spectra $\Lambda$ of $\mu_{q,D}$ such that $t\Lambda$ is a spectrum for every $t\in\mathcal T$, $\dim_{\mathrm{Be}}\Lambda=s$, and $D_s^+(\Lambda)=\zeta$. The construction combines a nested family of finite digit sets with lacunary spectral extensions. A two-sided interval-counting estimate controls the density of the prescribed subset, while the added frequencies ensure completeness for every multiplier without changing that density. Binary choices in the extension yield continuum many distinct spectra. This refines Beurling dimension interpolation in spectral eigen-subspaces by prescribing the upper density at every strictly intermediate dimension.

papers.title: The Douglas--Rachford algorithm for normal cones converges only weakly
papers.authors: Minh N. B\`{u}i, Honglin Luo, Xianfu Wang
papers.abstract: We show that the Douglas--Rachford algorithm applied to two normal cone operators associated with closed convex sets can fail to converge strongly, even when one set is a closed vector subspace, the other is a closed convex cone, and their intersection is a singleton.

papers.title: Bayesian Geometric Inversion for Wave Equation: Well-Posedness and Multiscale Multimodal Posterior Approximation
papers.authors: Xiong-Bin Yan, Ming-Jia Pei, Guang-Hui Zheng, Ting Wei
papers.abstract: Geometric full-waveform inversion aims to recover sharp subsurface interfaces from noisy waveform observations. We formulate this problem within a Bayesian level-set framework, where the unknown interface is represented as zero level set of a latent function endowed with a Gaussian prior. Although the level-set-to-medium-parameter map is discontinuous, we establish that the level-set-to-observation map is continuous almost surely with respect to the prior, thereby guaranteeing that the posterior measure is well-posed and locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the data in the Hellinger metric. To enable tractable posterior computation under the severe nonlinearity of the inverse problem and the resulting multimodality, we develop a multiscale multimodal Laplace approximation. A frequency-continuation strategy incorporates waveform data progressively from low to high frequencies, identifying and propagating multiple candidate modes across successive scales. At the final frequency level, local Gaussian approximations are constructed around the retained modes and combined into a Gaussian mixture, whose weights are determined by least-squares fitting to the unnormalized posterior density. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the method accurately reconstructs anomalous interfaces while effectively capturing posterior multimodality and the local uncertainty associated with distinct plausible geometries.

papers.title: $L^p$-Khinchin sequences and transference principles
papers.authors: Aihua Fan, Shilei Fan, Tongjin Li
papers.abstract:
A sequence \((\lambda_n)_{n\ge1}\) of distinct positive integers is called an \(L^p\)-Khinchin sequence, where $1\le p\le\infty$, if $
  n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n f(\lambda_k x)
  \longrightarrow
  \int_{\mathbb T}f\,d\mathfrak m $
  a.e. $x\in\mathbb T$ for every \(f\in L^p(\mathbb T)\). When $1\le p<\infty$, we characterize the \(L^p\)-Khinchin sequences by a weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequality for the associated averaging operators. We also establish a transference principle reducing the weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequality to weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequalities for three model systems: translation along a lattice path in the infinite direct sum of the semigroup $\mathbb{N}_0$, translation along a lattice path in the infinite direct sum of the group $\mathbb{Z}$ and translation on the circle $\mathbb{T}$. As consequences, we prove that $(2^n+1)_{n\ge1}$, the Fibonacci sequence, sequences of distinct primes and their partial products are \emph{not} $L^p$-Khinchin for any $1\le p<\infty$. We study the special class of multiplicative sequences generated by infinite words and we show that balanced infinite words generate $L^1$-Khinchin sequences, while typical random multiplicative sequences over at least two coprime integers are almost surely not $L^p$-Khinchin for any $1\le p<\infty$. We also obtain a {Conze-type principle} for countably generated semigroup actions on a probability space.

papers.title: A unified Carleman approach to inverse problems for coupled parabolic and hyperbolic-ODE equations
papers.authors: Jone Apraiz, Rodrigo Lecaros, Sebasti\'an Zamorano
papers.abstract:
We study inverse coefficient problems for two evolution equations with relaxation: a Kelvin--Voigt viscoelastic equation and the Moore--Gibson--Thompson (MGT) equation arising in nonlinear acoustics. In both cases, we establish the Lipschitz stability for recovering a space-dependent coefficient from a single measurement.
  Our approach exploits an exact factorization of each operator into a classical evolution operator (the heat operator for the viscoelastic system, or the wave operator for the MGT equation) coupled with a first-order differential operator in time. This makes it possible to combine global Carleman estimates with weighted ODE inequalities. For the Kelvin--Voigt model, the data consist of an interior dynamic observation and a Cauchy snapshot at a prescribed positive time. For the MGT equation, a single boundary trace is sufficient under a standard geometric condition. The resulting argument provides a common framework for coefficient inverse problems in evolution equations with relaxation effects.

papers.title: Critical functions and asymptotics for fractional Hartree Brezis--Nirenberg problems in low dimensions
papers.authors: Giusi Vaira, Yue Wu, Minbo Yang
papers.abstract: We study the Brezis--Nirenberg problem for the fractional Laplacian with an upper critical Hartree nonlinearity on a bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N$, in the low-dimensional range $2s<N<4s$. For a continuous potential $a$, we prove that the following properties are equivalent: the Robin function of $(-\Delta)^s+a$ is negative somewhere in $\Omega$; the associated Hartree--Sobolev quotient ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}(a)$ lies strictly below the best constant ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}$; and ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}(a)$ is attained. This leads to the notion of a critical potential, for which ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}(a)={\mathcal S_{H,s}}$ and every nontrivial decrease of $a$ lowers the infimum. For a critical potential $a$ and $V\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, we determine the leading term in the asymptotics of ${\mathcal S_{H,s}}(a+\varepsilon V)$ as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ and describe the blow-up of almost-minimizers, including the concentration speed and the location of the concentration point. Compared with the Sobolev case, the nonlocal nonlinearity produces several new interaction terms; a key ingredient is a proof of non-attainment at the threshold based on the sharp Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality on the sphere.

papers.title: A Matlab/Octave package for photometric stereo 3D reconstruction
papers.authors: Alessandro Buccini, Elisa Crabu, Federica Pes, Giuseppe Rodriguez
papers.abstract: The photometric stereo model allows the construction of 3D virtual replicas of real objects from images acquired under different light conditions. The assumptions of this model are strongly restrictive and are seldom fully satisfied in applications. Indeed, the surface of the observed objects may deviate from ideal conditions, and the geometry of the scene is often only an approximation of the one assumed by the model. Additionally, real-world surfaces may present reflection phenomena, which introduce distortions in reconstructions. In this paper, we present a revised version of the Matlab package \ttt{\small ps3d}~\cite{cdfrv21}, developed to implement the photometric stereo model under various conditions. The new package contains various extensions, the most notable one is the presence of an alternative model to address the presence of a reflective object surface. In addition, it implements particular metrics to analyze the compliance of a dataset to model assumptions, and it is compatible with GNU Octave. The tool allows users to test the model under different observation configurations, also in presence of reflection, using either synthetic or experimental data.

papers.title: Ramsey expansions of $S$-metric spaces
papers.authors: Jan Hubi\v{c}ka, Mat\v{e}j Kone\v{c}n\'{y}, Jaroslav Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il, Norbert Sauer
papers.abstract: Let $S\subseteq \mathbb R^+$ be a subset of positive reals. We say that a metric space is an $S$-metric space if the range of the metric is a subset of $S\cup \{0\}$. In 2007, Delhomm\'{e}, Laflamme, Pouzet, and Sauer characterized those sets $S$ for which the class of all finite $S$-metric spaces has the amalgamation property. Given an amalgamation class, a natural question is what its Ramsey expansion is. Ramsey expansions are known for classes of $S$-metric spaces for which $S\cup\{0\}$ carries a natural distance monoid structure, for example for $S=\mathbb Q^+$ or when $S$ is topologically closed. In this paper, we extend this result to all amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces, thereby completing the Ramsey-theoretic classification of amalgamation classes of finite $S$-metric spaces.

papers.title: Sign-changing bubbling solutions on polygons for the Brezis-Nirenberg problem in high dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider the Brezis--Nirenberg problem $-\Delta u = |u|^{2^{*}-2}u + \varepsilon u$ in a smooth bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{N}$, $N \geq 5$, with Dirichlet boundary conditions, where $\varepsilon > 0$ is small. Two multi-peak configurations found in dimension four in \cite{PRV2} persist. In an annulus, for every even $k \geq 2$, we construct solutions blowing up at the vertices of a regular $k$-gon with alternating signs. In the ball, we construct solutions blowing up positively at the vertices of a regular $k$-gon in a coordinate plane and negatively at those of a regular $k$-gon in an orthogonal plane, for $2 \leq k \leq 5$ if $N = 5,6$ and $2 \leq k \leq 4$ if $N \geq 7$. This range is sharp: for larger $k$ no such solution exists with parameters in a compact set, while otherwise the reduced energy has a unique, non-degenerate critical point.

papers.title: On the hyperplane conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the hyperplane conjecture, proposed by Hosono, Lian, and Yau in arXiv:alg-geom/9511001 and its generalization to orbifolds. Consequently, this establishes the expected equivalence between the \(A\) model (genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants with ambient insertions) of \(X\) and the \(B\) model (period integrals corresponding to vanishing cohomology) of \(X^{\vee}\) for Batyrev's mirror pair of Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces. As an application of our method, we also identify the residue of the Gauss--Manin connection and the cup product morphism on the \(A\)-side.

papers.title: Pellarin Values from Cauchy Coordinates on Arbitrary Curves
papers.authors: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be the ring of functions regular outside a closed point of degree $\mathrm{N}$ on a smooth projective curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. We express the normalized weight-one ideal Pellarin value of a rank-one Drinfeld $A$-module as an ordinary Hilbert-class trace of rational Cauchy differentials. A pairing on projective period lattices identifies the differential associated with each ideal class and computes its coefficients by finite torsion traces. For a nonfree lattice, the formula uses an isogeny with arbitrary nonzero derivative to a module with free period lattice. Each ideal-class subseries extends regularly to the characteristic point with value one, so the full series takes the value $|\operatorname{Cl}(A)|$. For every rank-one module, the quotient of the Anderson generating differential by the Drinfeld exponential is a meromorphic lattice sum whose value at zero is the Cauchy differential. Its Taylor coefficients give the higher-weight lattice differentials. For sign-normalized Hayes modules with free period lattice, an ordinary Hilbert-class trace after projection to powers divisible by $q^{\mathrm{N}}-1$ generates ideal values at $n\equiv1\pmod{q^{\mathrm{N}}-1}$. An algebraic parameter rescaling gives a trace formula for character-twisted values at $n\equiv1\pmod{q-1}$. The exact coefficient fields explain the difference between these weight ranges. For sign-normalized modules, decomposition by ideal classes also relates the element-type and ideal-type series at every positive weight. Explicit computations include the Hu--Huang--Yau module with nonprincipal period lattice and an elliptic curve with an infinite point of degree three, including the holomorphic term of its Cauchy differential. At rational infinity, the elliptic formula recovers the Green--Papanikolas identity.

papers.title: Geographic spread of vector borne diseases in periodic heterogeneous environments
papers.abstract: We consider a reaction-diffusion system that arises in epidemiology to describe the spatial spread of a vector borne disease. Our model is a coupled version of the classical SIR model of Kermack and McKendrick. We study the long-time behavior of the solutions, giving optimal criteria on the propagation or extinction of the disease, and compute the asymptotic speed of spread of solutions, which is given by a Freidlin-G{\"a}rtner type formula. We also give some qualitative properties of the model, which yield information on the influence of the parameters on the system's long-time behavior. In particular, we identify the limit of the spreading speed when the diffusions are very large, and we show that the system behaves in this case similarly to a homogenized system.

papers.title: A Hyperplane Bound and Ward's Divisibility Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $q=p^f$, where $p$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-ary linear code meeting the Griesmer bound, with positive dimension and minimum distance $d\ge1$, is $p^{\max\{0,\nu_p(d)-f+1\}}$-divisible, as asserted in Ward's conjecture. Arbitrary projective column multiplicities are allowed. The geometric ingredient is a bound independent of dimension: a nonzero scalar-invariant function $F:\mathbb{F}_q^k\to\mathbb{F}_p$, with $F(0)=0$ and prime-field algebraic degree at most $(f+s)(p-1)$, vanishes identically on at most $p^s(q-1)$ linear hyperplanes when $0\le s<f$. A truncated digit-sum inequality forces selected coefficient polynomials to be homogeneous of ordinary degree less than $q$. Weighted moments on a projective line then bound their linear factors, while a second-moment argument handles the complementary support configuration. An elementary finite-difference calculation supplies the degree bound for divided weight residues. Endpoint shortenings prove the basic divisibility layers; endpoint lifting, a surjective linear functional, and residual-code induction extend the argument to every valuation. We include the proofs of the classical ingredients, identify their sources, and distinguish the present argument from an earlier reported unpublished proof.

papers.title: Wave-Particle Complementarity in Quantum Walk from a Quantum Mechanical Perspective
papers.authors: Norio Konno, Shigeki Matsutani, Etsuo Segawa, Tomoyuki Terada
papers.abstract: A quantum walk is a mathematical model and a quantum version of a random walk. For the past two decades, it has been studied from mathematical and physical viewpoints. It has many desirable properties. This paper reevaluates quantum walk from a quantum mechanical perspective, as Feynman essentially proposed it as a toy model in his path integral method. Then we demonstrate that the quantum walk model exhibits both particle-like and wave-like properties by showing reflection and partial reflection as a particle and interference as a wave. In particular, for an initial state supported at two sites $\pm\ell$, we explicitly derive the weak limit distribution of the Hadamard walk and show that the Konno distribution is modulated by the interference factor $2\cos^2(\ell k(x))$. The resulting interference profile is reminiscent of far-field (Fraunhofer-type) diffraction.

papers.title: Flux-Based Time Bounds for Harmonically Degenerate Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: We study transfer-time estimates for finite-dimensional bilinear quantum control systems driven by an unbounded scalar control, in both the state-to-state setting (complex projective space) and the unitary synthesis setting (special unitary group). Lower bounds are recalled and refined via spectral and chordal methods. The main contribution is constructive upper bounds: we associate with the system a coupling graph whose edges correspond to non-resonant drift couplings, and construct transfer protocols along spanning trees. In contrast with earlier results requiring full rational independence of the spectrum of the control operator, our estimates allow rational resonances; they incorporate, via explicit correction factors derived from the arithmetic of the spectral gaps, the efficiency of the averaging procedure and of the phase adjustments. As an application, we consider finite-dimensional truncations of the planar quantum rotator under a dipolar electric field, and show that the transfer time between any two modes tends to zero as the truncation dimension grows.

papers.title: Input-to-Output Stability and Consensus Control of Opinion Dynamics on Graph State-Space
papers.authors: Arthur Doliveira (DIAPRO), Christophe Roman (DIAPRO), Guillaume Graton (DIAPRO), Mustapha Ouladsine
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a modeling of opinion dynamics in social systems with evolving structures on the Graph State-Space. It builds upon the Hegselmann-Krause (HK) model with variable influence weights, integrated into a hybrid dynamical systems framework where structural changes (agent addition/removal) are induced by inputs. We establish an Inputto-Output Stability (IOS) result under a strong connectivity assumption, using a nonsmooth Lyapunov function based on the opinion diameter; we show that the consensus expansion is then bounded by the maximal deviation of incoming agents relative to the existing convex hull. Assuming constant influence weights, we propose a consensus control result via agent injection in the social system. The results of this paper initiate, to the best of our knowledge, the analysis of resilience, stability, and control of dynamic systems on Graph State-Space.

papers.title: Entropy and periodic points in pseudo-Anosov isotopy classes
papers.authors: Pablo D. Carrasco, Federico Rodriguez-Hertz, Jana Rodriguez-Hertz, Ra\'ul Ures
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. We prove that, for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $g$ isotopic to $f$, the exponential growth rate of the number of nonempty Nielsen classes of its iterates equals $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)$ if and only if $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$. Thus Nielsen growth captures the full entropy precisely for representatives minimizing entropy in their isotopy class. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, $\alpha>0$, we identify this growth rate with the entropy of the global orbit quotient in Fathi's hyperbolic extension and establish Bowen's periodic-point formula for the quotient. We also prove that quotient entropy is upper semicontinuous in the $C^0$ topology throughout the isotopy class and continuous at every $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism, even under perturbations by arbitrary homeomorphisms in the class.

papers.title: A proof of the Baranov--Bessonov--Kapustin conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin: for a non-constant inner function $\theta$, every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on the model space $K_\theta$ has a bounded symbol if and only if $\theta$ is one-component

papers.title: Families that intersect in an arithmetic progression
papers.authors: Andrey Kupavskii, Fedor Noskov, Georgy Sokolov, Nikolai Terekhov
papers.abstract:
For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mu_n$ be the uniform measure on $2^{[n]}$. A family $\mathcal F \subseteq2^{[n]}$ is called $k$-AP-intersecting if $F_1\cap F_2$ contains a nonconstant $k$-term arithmetic progression for every $F_1, F_2\in\mathcal F$. Writing $m_k$ for the supremum of $\mu_n(\mathcal F)$ over all $n$ and all such families $\mathcal F$, we prove \[ 2^{-k}\le m_k\le32\cdot 2^{-k}\qquad(k\ge3). \]
  This greatly improves a recent result of Gillott, who proved that $m_k \leq k^{-1/3}$ for all sufficiently large $k$, and answers his question on $m_k$'s exponential decay. We also prove a similar bound for the corresponding cross-intersection problem.

papers.title: Corrections to ``The Method of Gaps: Exact Expressions for the Generalization Error of Supervised Learning Algorithms''
papers.abstract: In this paper, a counterexample to Lemma 5 of the paper referenced in the title is provided. Consequently, the formulation of the method of data-driven gaps presented in the referenced paper relies on an additional assumption, namely, that the conditional distribution of the training dataset given the learned model has identical data-point-specific marginals. To overcome this limitation, a generalized formulation of the method of data-driven gaps that does not rely on Lemma 5 and does not require the training samples to be independent or identically distributed is presented. Through this formulation, the applicability of the method of data-driven gaps is extended to a broader class of data distributions and randomized learning algorithms.

papers.title: Two pointwise estimates for singular integral operators over p-adic groups
papers.abstract: We establish some new pointwise boundedness properties for rough singular integral operators defined over p-adic groups. The properties of these operator rely essentially on the behavior of their rough kernels and we will present two different cases that fall outside the setting of the classical Calder{\'o}n-Zygmund setting.

papers.title: Two-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equations with critical long-range correlations
papers.abstract: We study a $(2+1)$-dimensional semilinear stochastic heat equation in which the noise is correlated like $f(\log |z|)/|z|^2$ as $|z|\to \infty$. Under an appropriate rescaling and logarithmic attenuation, we show that the limiting two-point statistics are given by the solution to a forward-backward stochastic differential equation. As shown in the work of Cosco, Cottini, and Donadini (2025), with whose results our study agrees in the linear case, the interesting feature of the two-dimensional, long-range problem is that one sees a varying influence on the limiting distribution from a range of spatial scales. We show that this phenomenon appears in the decoupling function for the limiting object and that the function $f$ modulates the weight of the contribution of each spatial scale.

papers.title: Structural aspects of $1$-limited domination in cubic graphs
papers.authors: Goran Radi\'c, Gordana Radi\'{c}, Aleksandra Tepeh
papers.abstract: A set $D\subseteq V(G)$ is a $1$-limited dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $D$ has a neighbor in $D$ and every vertex of $D$ has at most one neighbor outside $D$.
