For the Kraus-type free operations, we prove a necessary and sufficient criterion, Gram majorization, for converting pure states into targets with nonzero coefficients; it reduces to majorization for orthonormal reference states. It shows that golden states of these operations must be maximally coherent in the L\"{o}wdin basis, but that this does not ensure their existence: three reference states that are not orthonormal admit a golden state if and only if their overlaps have a common modulus $s$ and their Bargmann phase $\Phi$ obeys $s\geq2\cos[(\pi+|\Phi|)/3]$. Equal-overlap states also yield a complete family of superposition witnesses in the L\"{o}wdin basis, which show that white noise on the span of the reference states is a resource unless these states are orthonormal.

papers.title: Exact cost of the Euclidean Maximum Traveling Salesman Problem in one dimension
papers.abstract: We study the random Euclidean Maximum Traveling Salesman Problem: finding a Hamiltonian cycle of maximal total cost through any set of $N$ cities on a line, where each edge cost is a function of its Euclidean length. We characterize the maximizing cycles for convex increasing, concave increasing, and convex decreasing cost functions. For points sampled independently and uniformly from the unit interval, we derive explicit expressions for the average maximal cost for arbitrary $N$ and asymptotic expansions with power-law edge costs.

papers.title: Degree Bounds for Separating Polynomial and Neural Invariants for Point Clouds
papers.authors: Snir Hordan, Harm Derksen, Mircea Petrache, Nadav Dym
papers.abstract: Neural networks that respect the symmetries of point clouds commonly compute high-order representations of the rotation group to improve their expressivity. Such models are known to be universal, and thus able to separate any pair of point clouds, when using representations of sufficiently high order, yet no precise bound on this order, as a function of the number of points, was previously known. We establish the first quadratic lower and upper degree bounds for polynomials that separate point clouds of n points up to rotations and permutations. By showing Tensor Field Networks and MACE can express all invariant polynomials of a given degree with sufficient representation order, we additionally derive the first explicit, quadratic bound on the representation order sufficient for these architectures to be complete, replacing previous existence results with concrete guarantees. We further show that, under local regularity assumptions, point cloud separation can be achieved with a message-passing-based model using invariants whose degree depends only on the size of a local neighborhood, rather than on the size of the full point cloud. Finally, we provide counterexamples showing MACE must compute high order irreducible representations to separate locally regular point clouds.

papers.title: Statistical decision theory in thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce statistical decision theory in stochastic thermodynamic systems. Statistical decision theory integrates several statistical tasks, such as estimation, hypothesis testing, and classification. In this study, we consider statistical decision theory in stochastic thermodynamics, which unifies sensing, classification, and uncertainty relations. In particular, we focus on the minimax risk, the smallest achievable expected loss under the worst-case parameter choice, even with an optimal estimator. We derive lower bounds on the minimax risk using Le Cam's two-point method. The derived relationships can be used across a broader range of thermodynamic scenarios. To illustrate these relations, we study classification and distribution estimation problems in a Markov process. We demonstrate that the minimax risk provides lower bounds given by the dynamical activity in these problems. Furthermore, by examining particular dynamics, we establish that the resulting bounds simplify to uncertainty relations involving dynamical activity or entropy production.

papers.title: DM-RSA-OAEP: Formal Treatment of a Dual-Modulus Fault-Detection Countermeasure Based on Physical Diversity
papers.abstract: We revisit DM-RSA, an RSA variant that uses two independent moduli, whose original version was broken by H{\aa}stad's attack and contained an incorrect compromise-tolerance claim. We give a formal treatment of its repaired variant, DM-RSA-OAEP: (i) a complete IND-CCA2 security proof in the random-oracle model via a two-step hybrid argument, upper-bounding the security of the scheme by that of the weaker underlying RSA-OAEP instance, with an explicit simulation loss; (ii) a fault-detection theorem in an explicit adversary model that covers computation, key, and verification faults, including safe-error attacks, under a clearly stated physical-diversity assumption; (iii) an explicit analysis of why the countermeasure degrades to uselessness when the diversity assumption is violated (common-mode faults on a single chip). We position the scheme against the countermeasure landscape and against the broken dual-modulus literature. The contribution is deliberately framed as a fault countermeasure with a provable detection guarantee, not as a computationally stronger RSA. We conclude with a concrete instantiation and a detailed measurement protocol.

papers.title: On Integrable Deformations of CFTs and Integrable Two-Dimensional Sigma Models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze the systems of screening charges corresponding to $\eta$-deformed $O(N)$ and $OSp(N|2m)$ sigma models. These sigma models can be represented as integrable deformations of certain conformal field theories. Based on the case of $O(N)$ sigma models, which were conjectured in previous works by A.V. Litvinov and co-authors to be an integrable deformation of the conformal field theory corresponding to the algebras $W(D(n+1|n))$ and $W(D(n|n))$ for the cases $N=2n+2$ and $N=2n+1$ at $n \geq 1$, respectively, we formulate a hypothesis on how to write down the system of screening charges for the conformal field theory whose integrable deformation defines the $\eta$-deformed $OSp(N|2m)$ sigma model for the case of odd $N=2n+1$, asymptotically free models with $N-2m-2>0$ and $n \geq 2$, $m \geq 1$. This hypothesis is explicitly verified for the cases of $OSp(5|2)$, $OSp(7|2)$, and $OSp(7|4)$, which were separately investigated in the work of M.N. Alfimov and co-authors.

papers.title: Deep Pontryagin Learning for Continuous-Time Stochastic Control with Jumps
papers.abstract: We develop a deep Pontryagin learning framework for high-dimensional continuous-time stochastic control problems that naturally accommodates jump-diffusions. In contrast to direct policy optimization, which repeatedly differentiates the objective through the entire time-discretized dynamics, our method separates adjoint learning from policy improvement by explicitly incorporating state-sensitivity information from the Pontryagin stochastic maximum principle. For a fixed Markov control, we first compute pathwise adjoint labels by backpropagating the reward through time along simulated state trajectories, and project these labels onto the Markov state through a supervised regression step. The control is then updated by enforcing the pointwise Hamiltonian stationarity condition. We prove that the resulting projected adjoint process satisfies a discrete-time Pontryagin principle and converges, as the time step tends to zero, to the solution of the corresponding continuous-time adjoint backward stochastic differential equation. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy, stability, and scalability of the approach.

papers.title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
papers.authors: Shengyi Guan, Qiang Jia, Jiahua Tian, Yi-Nan Wang
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern--Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux--charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov--Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel--Watts theory.

papers.title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization
papers.abstract: Training a machine learning (ML) model is an optimization process that typically requires a set of examples with ground-truth labels beforehand. Obtaining these ground truths usually requires laborious human effort and can be costly. The scalability of human labeling becomes a concern when there are a large number of data points that need to be labeled. To address this practical issue, we consider an optimization setting where a subset of samples has ground-truth labels, while the remaining data points were labeled by an ML predictor, which could potentially assign incorrect labels to those points. We propose both first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods for training on datasets consisting of a mix of true-labeled and ML-labeled samples. We further conduct comprehensive empirical studies from training a linear regression model to fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for training with ML-labeled data.

papers.title: A simplified proof of the FPRAS for counting perfect matchings
papers.abstract: We give a simplified, self-contained proof of OpenAI's FPRAS for counting perfect matchings in general graphs. As in the original proof, we use a restricted Poincar\'e inequality for two matchings to sample weighted perfect matchings and estimate their total weight. We simplify the proof of this inequality by isolating parts of alternating cycles directly on the original vertex set and controlling the resulting error terms. This avoids the auxiliary vertices and tree constructions used in the original proof. The argument preserves the required parameter bounds and yields the same FPRAS guarantee.

papers.title: Data Center Oscillation Isolation and Grid Support: Fundamental Limits and Source-Selective Control
papers.abstract: The grid integration of large data centers poses a growing power-system stability challenge. Rapidly varying computing demand can induce oscillations, while the facilities must provide a prescribed response to grid disturbances. Existing controls address load fluctuations and grid support but do not establish their jointly achievable performance. This paper derives fundamental limits and develops a source-selective controller for simultaneous oscillation isolation and grid support. A coupled closed-loop model gives a condition for distinguishing disturbance sources and reveals a direct isolation-support conflict under grid-import-power feedback alone; additional electrical measurements can remove this pointwise conflict but leave a conditional cross-frequency sensitivity limit. Guided by these limits, we design a local residual-feedback storage controller through convex frequency-domain optimization with stability, isolation, and grid-response constraints across operating points. Tests on a single-generator interconnection and a modified nine-bus network show stronger oscillation isolation than equal-order optimized comparators while meeting the prescribed grid response across operating points.

papers.title: Next Best Action: Causal Constrained Offline RL for Business Action Targeting
papers.authors: Surya Ramachandiran, Yiming Li, Juan Mancilla-Caceres, Tao Ye, Jun Liu
papers.abstract: Next Best Action (NBA) systems must select among customer interventions (e.g., discounts, promotions, and lifecycle actions), maximize long-term economic value, satisfy complex operational constraints, and remain causally grounded. Existing approaches lack a rigorous framework for meeting these requirements jointly. We address this gap by formulating NBA as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). We then integrate off-policy causal correction of the estimated customer dynamics directly into the Linear Programming (LP) formulation of the CMDP. The resulting policy selects actions based on customer states to maximize long-term value while explicitly enforcing business guardrails. Furthermore, the LP formulation yields shadow prices that quantify the economic trade-offs of operational constraints (e.g., fairness and user welfare), enhancing policy interpretability. We validate our proposed offline Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework on an industry case study involving rideshare coupon targeting, where customer states are defined by Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) stages. We evaluate performance using model-based off-policy evaluation, with causal dynamics estimated from a temporal holdout. Under the observed coupon budget and RFM state representation, our optimized policy improves customer lifetime value (LTV) by 19% over the estimated behavior policy and 8% over a myopic baseline. Although the demonstrated action space is binary, the proposed framework is action-agnostic, yielding a general-purpose decision module for targeting systems that manage multiple interventions.

papers.title: Quantum algorithms for optimal control: large-scale finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulation
papers.authors: Xiajie Huang, Cristina \'Alvarez Yuste, Nikita Guseynov, Nana Liu, Javier Gonz\'alez-Conde
papers.abstract: We develop quantum algorithms for optimal control over a prescribed finite time interval (finite horizon), focusing on continuous-time linear-quadratic regulation (LQR). This foundational control problem often requires solving a nonlinear matrix Riccati equation, which can be costly for large systems and long control durations on conventional classical solvers. We instead work directly with the state-costate optimality equations, reformulating the LQR problem as a multiple-shooting linear system. Importantly, we prove a condition-number bound for the system that is independent of the horizon, under stabilizability and detectability assumptions. By incorporating the initial and final conditions into a single linear system, we can solve the subsequent linear system more efficiently with a quantum linear systems subroutine. For a given initial state, our quantum algorithms return classical estimates of the optimal cost and the optimal control inputs at a selected time, without constructing a Riccati solution operator. Given sparse-matrix block-encodings, an initial-state preparation oracle and a fixed number of control inputs, the query and gate complexities scale polylogarithmically with system size and control duration, provided that sparsity, relevant norms, and stability parameters are bounded. The dependence on the target error is inverse-linear up to logarithmic factors. We establish the required bounds uniformly in system size and duration for a family of damped mass-spring chains with two endpoint controls. Numerical experiments support the analysis.

papers.title: On The Acyclic MacPhersonian
papers.abstract:
The acyclic MacPhersonian $\AM_n^d$ is the poset of acyclic oriented matroids of rank $d+1$ on $n$ labelled elements, the combinatorial model of the space of configurations of $n$ points spanning $\R^d$ up to affine equivalence, which is the Grassmannian $G(d,n-1)$. We study it inside the larger poset $\Sep_n^d$ of \emph{spherical separoids}, those acyclic separoids whose Radon complex is a sphere of the dimension of the space of affine dependences.
  Our main unconditional results are as follows. Over every poset of spherical separoids that contains the realizable oriented matroids there is a tautological sphere fibration, and its Stiefel--Whitney classes show that the mod~$2$ cohomology ring of $G(d,n-1)$ is a ring retract of that of the poset, for all $n$ and $d$. For $d=n-2$ the poset of spherical separoids is homotopy equivalent to $G(n-2,n-1)$, and contains $\AM_n^{n-2}$ as a homotopy equivalent subposet. A fat model of $\AM_n^d$ made of piecewise geodesic antipodal spheres in the round sphere is weakly homotopy equivalent to its order complex. The chirotope of every such sphere is recovered from the degrees of its coordinate projections.
  We then analyse a strategy based on the mean curvature flow. Any argument that follows the combinatorial type of a sphere generically along the flow would connect every uniform oriented matroid to a realizable one by mutations. By a theorem of Gu and Knauer this is impossible in every rank $r\ge7$ on $n\ge r+17$ elements, so the flow must leave the oriented matroids. We show that the basin hypothesis of the flow, together with the property that $\|\AM_n^d\|$ is a homology manifold, implies $\|\AM_n^d\|\simeq G(d,n-1)$, without following types along the flow. We conclude with the open problems and conjectures that remain.

papers.title: Huneke's degree-computing problem
papers.abstract: In this short note, we deal with a problem posted by Huneke on a numerical invariant attached to symbolic powers of homogenous ideals.

papers.title: A few remarks on a Manin-Mumford conjecture in function field arithmetic and generalized Pila-Wilkie estimates
papers.abstract: We present here the natural extension of our Pila-Wilkie type estimates on the number of rational points of the trascendent part of a compact analytic subset of $\mathbb{F}_{q}((1/T))^{n}$ to analogous subsets of $K^{n}$, where $K$ is a general local field of any characteristic. That would integrate the analogous estimate provided by F. Loeser, G. Comte and R. Cluckers in characteristic 0.

papers.title: On the Rees, Dilworth and Matsumura number
papers.abstract: In this paper we study three numerical invariants of local rings: the Rees number, the Dilworth number, and the Matsumura number. These quantities measure, respectively, the minimal lengths of certain cyclic modules, the maximal numbers of generators of ideals, and a parameter-based analogue in higher dimension. We construct a non-exact local complete-intersection ring over $\mathbb{F}_2$, thereby providing a negative answer to a question of Matsumura on the exactness of zero-dimensional complete intersections. We also present a family of artinian Gorenstein local rings over a field of characteristic zero that are exact, making progress on a question of Watanabe. Finally, answering a further question of Matsumura, we introduce and study the Matsumura number and the class of homologically exact rings, which extend the notion of exactness beyond the one-dimensional case.

papers.title: Multi-pole extension for elliptic models of interacting integrable tops
papers.abstract: We review and give detailed description for ${\rm gl}_{NM}$ Gaudin models related to holomorphic vector bundles of rank $NM$ and degree $M$ over elliptic curve with $n$ punctures. Then we introduce their generalizations constructed by means of $R$-matrices satisfying the associative Yang-Baxter equation. A natural extension of the obtained models to the Schlesinger systems is given as well.

papers.title: Recovered-Coefficient Discontinuous Galerkin Approximation of an Averaged-State Credit-Rating Migration PDE
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze a discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method for an averaged-state regularization of a credit-rating migration equation, in which the volatility switch is smoothed at scale $\eps$ and evaluated at a mollified state of width $\ell$. The diffusion operator is written in conservative form and discretized by symmetric interior penalty, and the effective drift by upwinding. The nonlinear coefficients are evaluated from a recovered state obtained by Oswald averaging, the model mollifier, and an explicit norm cutoff calibrated by a data-computable maximum bound. The recovered coefficients are single-valued and uniformly $W^{2,\infty}$, so the standard upwind energy identity holds, and the recovery is Lipschitz from $L^2$ and compatible with the projected exact state at order $h^{p+1}$. For fixed $(\eps,\ell)$ we prove well-posedness and a maximum bound for the continuous problem, an $O(\ell^2)$ distance to the pointwise-regularized model, stability of the frozen-coefficient backward Euler DG scheme, and an $O(h^p+\Delta t)$ error estimate in the DG energy norm; an exact Nitsche--lifting identity covers nonhomogeneous Dirichlet data. Under local transversality, the regularized migration boundary is recovered at a proved, suboptimal rate. Computations with the analyzed scheme confirm the predicted rates and report the quantities on which the analysis rests.

papers.title: Prescribed Primitive Roots And The Least Primes
papers.abstract: Let $q\ne \pm1,v^2$ be a fixed integer. The least prime number $p \geq2 $ such that $q$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ is conjectured to be $p\ll (\log q)(\log \log q)),$ where $\gcd(p,q)=1$. This note proves the existence of a small subset of primes $p$ that satisfies the stated upper bound.

papers.title: Some Cubic and Quartic Inequalities of Four Variables
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{H} \subset \mathcal{H}_{n,d} := \mathbb{R}[x_1$,$\ldots$, $x_n]_d$ be a vector space, and $A$ be a compact semialgebraic subset of $\mathbb{P}_{\mathbb{R}}^{n-1}$. We shall study some PSD cones $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}(A$, $\mathcal{H}) := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}$ $\big|$ $f(a) \geq 0$ ($\forall a \in A$)$\big\}$. Our interests are (1) to determine the extremal elements of $\mathcal{P}$, (2) to determine discriminants of $\mathcal{P}$, (3) to describe $\mathcal{P}$ as a union of basic semialgebraic subsets, and (4) to find a nice test set when $\dim \mathcal{H}$ is low. In this article, we present (1), (2), (3) and (4) for $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,4}^{s0})$ and $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}_+^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,4}^{s0})$, where $\mathcal{H}_{n,d}^{s0} := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}_{n,d}$ $\big|$ $f$ is symmetric and $f(1,\ldots,1)=0 \big\}$. We also provide (1) -- (4) for $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}_+^4$, $\mathcal{H}_{4,3}^{c0})$, where $\mathcal{H}_{n,d}^{c0} := \big\{f \in \mathcal{H}_{n,d}$ $\big|$ $f$ is cyclic and $f(1,\ldots,1)=0 \big\}$.

papers.title: A characterization for the defect of rank one valued field extensions
papers.abstract: In this paper we present a characterization for the defect of a simple algebraic extension of rank one valued fields using the key polynomials that define the valuation. As a particular example, this gives the classification of defect extensions of degree $p$ as dependent or independent presented by Kuhlmann.

papers.title: Extensions of locally analytic generalized Steinberg representations
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a finite extension of $\mathrm{Q}_p$. We study locally $\mathrm{Q}_p$-analytic generalized Steinberg representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(L)$ associated with a general Zelevinsky segment and compute certain $\mathrm{Ext}^1$-groups involving these representations. These extension groups give rise to parabolic Breuil simple $\mathcal{L}$-invariants on the automorphic side of a conjectural $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for potentially semistable $p$-adic Galois representations in the non-trianguline case.

papers.title: Parabolic Simple $\mathscr{L}$-Invariants
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf{Q}_p$. Let $\rho_L$ be a potentially semi-stable non-crystalline $p$-adic Galois representation such that the associated $F$-semisimple Weil-Deligne representation is absolutely indecomposable. In this paper, we study Fontaine-Mazur parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants of $\rho_L$, which was previously only known in the trianguline case. Based on the previous work on Breuil's parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants, we attach to $\rho_L$ a locally $\mathbf{Q}_p$-analytic representation $\Pi(\rho_L)$ of $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(L)$, which carries the information of parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants of $\rho_L$. When $\rho_L$ comes from a patched automorphic representation of $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A}_{F^+})$ (for a define unitary group $\mathbf{G}$ over a totally real field $F^+$ which is compact at infinite places and $\mathrm{GL}_n$ at $p$-adic places), we prove under mild hypothesis that $\Pi(\rho_L)$ is a subrepresentation of the associated Hecke-isotypic subspace of the Banach spaces of (patched) $p$-adic automophic forms on $\mathbf{G}(\mathbb{A}_{F^+})$, this is equivalent to say that the Breuil's parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants are equal to Fontaine-Mazur parabolic simple $\mathscr{L}$-invariants.

papers.title: Lattice-based kernel approximation and serendipitous weights for parametric PDEs in very high dimensions
papers.authors: Vesa Kaarnioja, Frances Y. Kuo, Ian H. Sloan
papers.abstract: We describe a fast method for solving elliptic partial differential equations (PDEs) with uncertain coefficients using kernel interpolation at a lattice point set. By representing the input random field of the system using the model proposed by Kaarnioja, Kuo, and Sloan (SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 2020), in which a countable number of independent random variables enter the random field as periodic functions, it was shown by Kaarnioja, Kazashi, Kuo, Nobile, and Sloan (Numer. Math. 2022) that the lattice-based kernel interpolant can be constructed for the PDE solution as a function of the stochastic variables in a highly efficient manner using fast Fourier transform (FFT). In this work, we discuss the connection between our model and the popular "affine and uniform model" studied widely in the literature of uncertainty quantification for PDEs with uncertain coefficients. We also propose a new class of weights entering the construction of the kernel interpolant $-$ serendipitous weights $-$ which dramatically improve the computational performance of the kernel interpolant for PDE problems with uncertain coefficients, and allow us to tackle function approximation problems up to very high dimensionalities. Numerical experiments are presented to showcase the performance of the serendipitous weights.

papers.title: James reduced product schemes and double quasisymmetric functions
papers.abstract:
Symmetric function theory is a key ingredient in the Schubert calculus of Grassmannians. Quasisymmetric functions are analogues that are similarly central to algebraic combinatorics, but for which the associated geometry is poorly developed. Baker and Richter (2008) showed that $\operatorname{QSym}$ manifests topologically as the cohomology ring of the loop suspension of infinite projective space or equivalently of its combinatorial homotopy model, the James reduced product $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. In recent work, we used this viewpoint to develop topologically-motivated bases of $\operatorname{QSym}$ and initiate a Schubert calculus for $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$ in both cohomology and $K$-theory.
  Here, we study the torus-equivariant cohomology of $J\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^\infty$. We identify a cellular basis and introduce double monomial quasisymmetric functions as combinatorial representatives, analogous to the factorial Schur functions and double Schubert polynomials of classical Schubert calculus. We also provide a combinatorial Littlewood--Richardson-type rule for the structure coefficients of this basis.
  Furthermore, we introduce an algebro-geometric analogue of the James reduced product construction. In particular, we prove that the James reduced product of a complex (quasi-)projective variety also carries the structure of a (quasi-)projective variety.

papers.title: Weak solutions for weak turbulence models in electrostatic plasmas
papers.abstract: The weak turbulence model, also known as the quasilinear theory in plasma physics, has been a cornerstone in modeling resonant particle-wave interactions in plasmas. Stemming from the Vlasov-Poisson/Maxwell system under the weak turbulence assumption, incorporating the random phase approximation and ergodicity, it takes the form of a integro-differential system, which describes the time dynamics of particle distribution and wave spectrum. The interaction between particles and waves can be treated as a stochastic process, whose transition probability bridges the momentum space and the spectral space. To our knowledge, there is no preceding rigorous analytical work for the quasilinear theory addressed in this manuscript. In this paper, we establish the existence of global weak solutions to the one-dimensional electrostatic quasilinear model for nonnegative, smooth, rapidly decaying initial particle distributions and nonnegative, smooth wave spectra compactly supported in a positive wave-number band. The construction uses the resonance condition to reduce the coupled system to a scalar degenerate parabolic equation, together with uniform estimates and strong convergence of the gradients of regularized approximations. When the initial wave spectrum is positive throughout a single band, we further characterize the equilibrium selected by this approximation procedure. The equilibrium uniquely minimizes a quadratic functional over a nonnegative cone and admits a geometric construction through the least concave majorant of a primitive determined by the initial data. The limiting particle distribution is non-increasing on the corresponding resonant interval and forms plateaus wherever the equilibrium auxiliary function is positive. A relative-entropy argument establishes long-time convergence to this equilibrium.

papers.title: From vertex operator superalgebras to graded-local conformal nets and back
papers.authors: Sebastiano Carpi, Tiziano Gaudio, Robin Hillier
papers.abstract: We generalize the Carpi-Kawahigashi-Longo-Weiner correspondence between vertex operator algebras and conformal nets to the case of vertex operator superalgebras and graded-local conformal nets by introducing the notion of strongly graded-local vertex operator superalgebra. Then we apply our machinery to a number of well-known examples including superconformal field theory models. We also prove that all lattice VOSAs are strongly graded-local. Furthermore, we prove strong graded-locality of the super-Moonshine VOSA, whose group of automorphisms preserving the superconformal structure is isomorphic to Conway's largest sporadic simple group, and of the shorter Moonshine VOSA, whose automorphisms group is isomorphic to the direct product of the baby Monster with a cyclic group of order two.

papers.title: Equivalence of local weak and Benjamini--Schramm formulations of Berry's random wave model
papers.abstract: Berry's random wave model predicts that high-energy eigenfunctions of classically chaotic systems can be modeled locally, at the wavelength scale, by the Gaussian monochromatic random wave. Several rigorous formulations of this prediction have been proposed. We prove the equivalence of two such formulations on a closed manifold: local weak limits and Benjamini--Schramm convergence of manifolds decorated by eigenfunctions. The latter considers pointed manifolds equipped with a smooth function, up to isometry, without recording local orthonormal coordinates. The key step is to recover the unaveraged local function law from its orthogonal average using translation invariance and the ergodicity of the random wave. Finally, either formulation implies strong inverse localization, allowing high-energy eigenfunctions to approximate arbitrary solutions of the Euclidean Helmholtz equation, with applications to their nodal sets.

papers.title: The module of K\"ahler differentials for extensions of valuation rings
papers.abstract: The main goal of this paper is to describe the module of K\"ahler differentials for an extension of valuation rings. More precisely, we consider a simple algebraic valued field extension $(L/K,v)$ and the corresponding valuation ring extension $\VR_K\hookrightarrow\VR_L$. In the case when $e(L/K,v)=1$ (and under two additional conditions) we present a characterization of $\Omega_{\VR_L/\VR_K}$ in terms of a given sequence of key polynomials for the extension. We use our main result to present criteria for the equality $\Omega_{\VR_L/\VR_K}=(0)$ to hold.

papers.title: Improved Mixing Rates of Directed Cycles with Additional Sparse Interconnections
papers.abstract: We analyze the absolute spectral gap of Markov chains on graphs obtained from a cycle of $n$ vertices and perturbed only at approximately $n^{1/\rho}$ random locations with an appropriate, possibly sparse, interconnection structure. Together with a strong asymmetry along the cycle, the gap of the resulting chain can be bounded inversely proportionally by the longest arc length (up to logarithmic factors) with high probability, providing a significant mixing speedup compared to the reversible version.

papers.title: Categorical wall-crossing for higher-framed DT/PT quivers
papers.abstract: We study a framed three-loop quiver with $a+r$ incoming arrows and $a$ outgoing arrows. For a generic window parameter, we construct a semiorthogonal decomposition of the bounded derived category of the positive GIT quotient into products of unframed window categories and categories of the negative quotient. The arrow imbalance $r$ determines an interval of admissible slopes of length $r$. The proof separates a lower-convex-hull decomposition of dominant weights, Koszul induction, full faithfulness and semiorthogonality of Hall functors, and the two window equivalences. We extend the decomposition to trace potentials satisfying block additivity. Applications include a precisely specified open chart of the framed conifold quiver, an algebraically defined extended ADHM critical model, and the critical presentation of the Quot scheme of points on $\mathbb{A}^3$. We do not identify the extended ADHM model with moduli of higher-rank pairs having a generically rank-one reduced-curve sheaf. A formal MacMahon identity is proved separately, and the localized categorical rank formula is deduced using the localized strict-slope product formula of P\u{a}durariu--Toda.

papers.title: Semidefinite programming bounds for distance distribution of spherical codes
papers.abstract: Multipoint semidefinite programming bounds for spherical codes use polynomials in several variables. We show how to obtain bounds for the distance distribution using a polynomial of one variable on a prescribed interval. The multivariate SDP supplies the required positivity; the sign and size of the univariate polynomial reveal the geometric consequences. We prove three- and four-point reductions and explain how to choose the polynomial to bound the number of pairs in a prescribed interval. Three-point experiments in dimension four illustrate this procedure, including nearly antipodal pairs, intervals near inner product $1/2$, and a local approach to the kissing number bound. As a further application, we extract a degree-six polynomial from the exact four-point construction of de Laat, Leijenhorst, and de Muinck Keizer. Its sign and four zeros give a direct description of the distance restriction underlying uniqueness of the $24$-cell.

papers.title: An example of a reflexive Banach space with an uncomplemented isometric subspace
papers.abstract: We present an example of a reflexive Banach space $X$ with a basis $(e_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ 1-equivalent to its subsequence $(e_{2i})_{i=1}^\infty$. The closed subspace of $X$ spanned by the latter is not complemented in $X$, whereas the subsequence $(e_{2i-1})_{i=1}^\infty$ is unconditional.

papers.title: High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow in the Complex Projective Space
papers.abstract: We study the mean curvature flow of smooth, compact submanifolds of high codimension with quadratic pinching in $\mathbb{C}P^k$. We establish a codimension estimate, where in regions of high curvature, the submanifold becomes approximately codimension one, in a quantifiable way. Under a cylindrical type pinching, this limiting flow is weakly convex and moves by translation or is a self shrinker. These estimates allow us to analyse the behaviour of the flow near singularities and establish the existence of the limiting flow. With a decay estimate, the rescaling converges smoothly to a totally geodesic limit in infinite time, without using Stampacchia iteration or integral analysis.

papers.title: Generalizing Riemann curvature to Regge metrics
papers.authors: Jay Gopalakrishnan, Michael Neunteufel, Joachim Sch\"oberl, Max Wardetzky
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a generalization of the Riemann curvature tensor on manifolds (of dimension two or higher) endowed with a Regge metric. Specifically, while all components of the metric tensor are assumed to be smooth within elements of a triangulation of the manifold, they need not be smooth across element interfaces, where only continuity of the tangential components is assumed. While linear derivatives of the metric can be generalized to Schwartz distributions, similarly generalizing the classical Riemann curvature tensor, a nonlinear second-order derivative of the metric, requires more care. We propose a generalization that combines the classical angle defect and jumps in the second fundamental form across element interfaces and argue its correctness. Specifically, if a piecewise smooth metric approximates a globally smooth metric, then our generalized Riemann curvature tensor approximates the classical Riemann curvature tensor associated with the latter. Moreover, we show that if the metric approximation converges at some rate in a mesh-dependent norm equivalent to the $L^2$ norm, then the curvature approximation converges in the negative Sobolev space $H^{-2}$, the dual space of $H^2_0$, at the same rate, under additional assumptions. By appropriate contractions of the generalized Riemann curvature tensor, this work also provides generalizations of scalar curvature, the Ricci curvature tensor, and the Einstein tensor in any dimension.

papers.title: Minimal limit key polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the theory of minimal limit key polynomials of valuations on the polynomial ring $\kx$. Minimal key polynomials are useful to describe, for instance, the defect of an extension of valued fields. We use the theory of cuts on ordered abelian groups to show that the previous results on bounded sets of key polynomials of rank one valuations, extend to vertically bounded sets of key polynomials of valuations of an arbitrary rank. We discuss as well properties of minimal limit key polynomials in the vertically unbounded case.

papers.title: Generators for extensions of valuation rings
papers.abstract: For a finite valued field extension $(L/K,v)$ we describe the problem of finding sets of generators for the corresponding extension $\VR_L/\VR_K$ of valuation rings. The main tool to obtain such sets are complete sets of (key) polynomials. We show that when the initial index coincides with the ramification index, sequences of key polynomials naturally give rise to sets of generators. We use this to prove Knaf's conjecture for pure extensions.

papers.title: On the Girth of Graph Lifts
papers.abstract: The order of the smallest $k$-regular graph of girth at least $g$ is denoted by the well-studied function $n(k,g)$. We introduce an analogous function $n(H,g)$, defined as the smallest order of a graph of girth at least $g$ that is a lift (or cover) of the, possibly non-regular, graph $H$. We prove that the two main combinatorial bounds on $n(k,g)$, the Moore lower bound and the Erd\H{o}s-Sachs upper bound, carry over to the new lift setting. We also consider two other functions: i) The smallest order of a graph of girth at least $g$ sharing a universal cover with $H$. We prove that it is the same as $n(H,g)$ up to a multiplicative constant. ii) The smallest order of a graph of girth at least $g$ with a prescribed degree distribution. We discuss this known generalization and argue that the new suggested definitions are superior. We conclude with the best-known upper and lower bounds for covers of the diamond graph ($K_4 - e$) for girth up to $30$, obtained via a computerized search, and offer conjectures and open problems for future research.

papers.title: Strongly vertex-reinforced jump process on graphs with bounded degree
papers.abstract: We study asymptotic behaviours of a non-linear vertex-reinforced jump process defined on an arbitrary infinite graph with bounded degree. We prove that if the reinforcement function $w$ is reciprocally integrable and non-decreasing, then the process visits only a finite number of vertices. In the case where $w$ is regularly varying with index $\alpha>1$, we show that the process eventually gets stuck on a star-shaped subgraph and there is exactly one vertex with unbounded local time.

papers.title: Dynamical Coherence Measures
papers.abstract: We present three measures of the dynamical coherence of channels, which generalize several previous results. The measures are based on a generalized distance-like function between channels, such as a quantum divergence of channels, including the relative entropy and diamond distance. Free operations are considered to be detection-incoherent, creation-incoherent, and detection-creation incoherent. We consider free superchannels constructed from free pre- and post-processing channels. The new measures are monotone under free superchannels and convex.

papers.title: A Note on the Stability of Monotone Markov Chains
papers.abstract: This note studies monotone Markov chains, a subclass of Markov chains with extensive applications in operations research and economics. While the properties that ensure the global stability of these chains are well studied, their establishment often relies on the fulfillment of a certain splitting condition. We address the challenges of verifying the splitting condition by introducing simple, applicable conditions that ensure global stability. The simplicity of these conditions is demonstrated through various examples including autoregressive processes, portfolio allocation problems and resource allocation dynamics.

papers.title: A dimension bound towards the Casas-Alvero Conjecture
papers.abstract: The Casas-Alvero conjecture predicts that every univariate polynomial over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero sharing a common factor with each of its Hasse-Schmidt derivatives is a power of a linear polynomial. The conjecture for polynomials of a fixed degree $n$ is equivalent to the projective variety of such polynomials being one-dimensional. In this paper, we produce dimension bounds for this variety (in degree $n$) over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero using an arithmetic invariant $B(n)$ of $n$. Consequently for infintely many degrees $n$, we show that the associated arithmetic Casas-Alvero scheme has finitely many rational points over any characteristic zero field. Along the way, we prove several rigidity results towards the conjecture and study arithmetic properties of $B(n)$.

papers.title: On the solutions of the generalized Fermat equation over totally real number fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a totally real number field and $\mathcal{O}_K$ be the ring of integers of $K$. In this article, we study the asymptotic solutions of the generalized Fermat equation $Ax^p+By^p+Cz^p=0$ over $K$ with prime exponent $p$, where $A,B,C \in \mathcal{O}_K \setminus \{0\}$. For certain class of fields $K$, we prove that the equation $Ax^p+By^p+Cz^p=0$ has no asymptotic solution $(a,b,c) \in \mathcal{O}_K^3$ with $2|abc$. Then, under some assumptions on $A,B,C$, we also prove that $Ax^p+By^p+Cz^p=0$ has no asymptotic solution in $K^3$. Finally, we give several purely local criteria of $K$ such that $Ax^p+By^p+Cz^p=0$ has no asymptotic solutions in $K^3$, and calculate the density of such fields $K$ when $K$ is a real quadratic field.

papers.title: On extreme values of quadratic twists of Dirichlet-type $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In a recent work by Gun, Kohnen and Soundararajan, it has been shown that $L$-functions associated with arbitrary non-zero cusp forms take large values at the central critical point. The goal of this note is to derive analogous results for twists of Dirichlet-type functions. More precisely, for an odd integer $q >1$, let $F$ be a non-zero $\mathbb{C}$-linear combination of primitive, complex, even Dirichlet characters of conductor $q$. We show that for any $\epsilon>0$ and sufficiently large $X$, there are $\gg X^{1-\epsilon}$ fundamental discriminants $8d$ with $X < d \leq 2X$ and ${(d, 2q)=1}$ such that ${|L(1/2, F \otimes \chi_{8d})| }$ is large.

papers.title: Metric Lines in Engel-type Groups
papers.abstract: In the framework of sub-Riemannian manifolds, a natural question is: What are the ''metric lines'' (i.e., isometric embeddings of the real line)? This article presents a conjecture classifying metric lines in Carnot groups and investigates the question for Carnot groups of arbitrary rank. It focuses on metric lines in Engel-type groups, whose sub-Riemannian structure is defined on a distribution of rank $n+1$. The approach employs a novel technique, the sequence method, initially developed to study metric lines in jet space.

papers.title: Partial actions of inverse categories and their algebras
papers.authors: Marcelo M. Alves, Willian G. G. Velasco
papers.abstract: In this work we introduce partial and global actions of inverse categories on posets in two variants, fibred actions and actions by symmetries. We study in detail actions of an inverse category $\mathcal{C}$ on specific subposets of the poset of finite subsets of $\mathcal{C}$, the Bernoulli actions. We show that to each fibred action of an inverse category on a poset there corresponds another inverse category, the semidirect product associated to the action. The Bernoulli actions give rise to the Szendrei expansions of $\mathcal{C}$, which define an endofunctor of the category of inverse categories. We extend the concept of ''enlargement'' from inverse semigroup theory to inverse categories, and we show that if $\mathcal{D}$ is an enlargement of $\mathcal{C}$ then their Cauchy completions are equivalent categories; in particular, some pairs corresponding to partial and global Bernoulli actions are enlargements. We conclude by studying convolution algebras of finite inverse categories and showing that if $\mathcal{D}$ is an enlargement of $\mathcal{C}$ then their convolution algebras are Morita equivalent. Furthermore, using Kan extensions we also analyze the infinite case.

papers.title: Two Erdos-Hajnal-type theorems for forbidden order-size pairs
papers.authors: Fabian Arnold, Lior Gishboliner, Benny Sudakov
papers.abstract: The celebrated Erd\H{o}s-Hajnal conjecture says that any graph without a fixed induced subgraph $H$ contains a very large homogeneous set. A direct analog of this conjecture is not true for hypergraphs. In this paper we present two natural variants of this problem which do hold for hypergraphs. We show that for every $r \geq 3$, $m \geq m_0(r)$ and $0 \leq f \leq \binom{m}{r}$, if an $r$-graph $G$ does not contain $m$ vertices spanning exactly $f$ edges, then $G$ contains much larger homogeneous sets than what is guaranteed to exist in general $r$-graphs. We also prove that if a $3$-graph $G$ does not contain homogeneous sets of polynomial size, then for every $m \geq 3$ there are $\Omega(m^3)$ values of $f$ such that $G$ contains $m$ vertices spanning exactly $f$ edges. This makes progress on a problem of Axenovich, Brada\v{c}, Gishboliner, Mubayi and Weber.

papers.title: On an example of Aspinwall, Morrison, and Szendr\H{o}i
papers.abstract: We study the cohomology of a 1-parameter family Y_t of Calabi-Yau 3-folds introduced by Aspinwall and Morrison, related to the mirror quintic family. Szendr\H{o}i proved that Y_t, Y_{xi t}, ..., Y_{xi^4 t}, where xi is a fifth root of unity, have the same rational Hodge structure but are not isomorphic, and conjectured that they are not birational or even derived equivalent. We confirm this by proving that their integral Hodge structures are different, and discuss how this fits with known Torelli-type theorems and counterexamples.

papers.title: Sharp Quartic Pinching for the Mean Curvature Flow in the Sphere
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp quartic curvature pinching for the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{S}^{n+m}$, $m\ge2$, which generalises Pu's work on the convergence of submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^{n+m}$ to a round point. Using a blow up argument, we prove a codimension and a cylindrical estimate, where in regions of high curvature, the submanifold becomes approximately codimension one, quantitatively, and is weakly convex and moves by translation or is a self shrinker. With a decay estimate, the rescaling converges smoothly to a totally geodesic limit in infinite time, without using Stampacchia iteration or integral analysis.

papers.title: Suszko's Thesis and Many-valued Logical Structures
papers.authors: Sayantan Roy, Sankha S. Basu, Mihir K. Chakraborty
papers.abstract: In this article, we try to formulate a definition of ''many-valued logical structure''. For this, we embark on a deeper study of Suszko's Thesis ($\mathbf{ST}$) and show that the truth or falsity of $\mathbf{ST}$ depends, at least, on the precise notion of semantics. We propose two different notions of semantics and three different notions of entailment. The first one helps us formulate a precise definition of inferentially many-valued logical structures. The second and the third help us to generalise Suszko Reduction and provide adequate bivalent semantics for monotonic and a couple of nonmonotonic logical structures. All these lead us to a closer examination of the played by language/metalanguage hierarchy vis-\'a-vis $\mathbf{ST}$. We conclude that many-valued logical structures can be obtained if the bivalence of all the higher-order metalogics of the logic under consideration is discarded, building formal bridges between the theory of graded consequence and the theory of many-valued logical structures, culminating in generalisations of Suszko's Thesis.

papers.title: Singular semilinear elliptic equations in half-spaces
papers.abstract: We prove the monotonicity of positive solutions to the problem $-\Delta u = f(u)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N_+ := \{(x',x_N)\in\mathbb{R}^N \mid x_N>0 \}$ under zero Dirichlet boundary condition with a possible singular nonlinearity $f$. In some situations, we can derive a precise estimate on the blow-up rate of $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\eta}$ as $x_N \to 0^+$, where $(\eta,e_N)>0$, and obtain a classification result. The main tools we use are the method of moving planes and the sliding method.

papers.title: Backbone coloring for graphs with degree 4
papers.abstract: The $\lambda$-backbone coloring of the graph $G$ with backbone $H$ is a graph-coloring problem in which we are given a graph $G$ and a subgraph $H$, and we want to assign colors to vertices in such a way that the endpoints of every edge from $G$ have different colors, and the endpoints of every edge from $H$ are assigned colors which differ by at least $\lambda$. In this paper we pursue research on backbone coloring of bounded-degree graphs with well-known classes of backbones. Our result is an almost complete classification of the complexity of deciding whether $BBC_{\lambda}(G, H) \le k$ for graphs with maximum degree at most $4$ and matching, galaxy, Hamiltonian path, and spanning tree backbones. We also determine the effect of allowing isolated vertices in matching and galaxy backbones.

papers.title: On the quasi-isometric classification of permutational wreath products
papers.abstract: In this article, we initiate the study of the large-scale geometry of permutational wreath products of the form $F\wr_{H/N}H$, where $H$ is finitely presented and where $N$ is a normal subgroup of $H$ satisfying a certain assumption of non coarse separation. The main result is a complete classification of such permutational wreath products up to quasi-isometry, building up on previous works from Genevois and Tessera. For instance, we show that, for $d\ge k\ge 2$, $\mathbb{Z}_{n}\wr_{\mathbb{Z}^{k}} \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{m}\wr_{\mathbb{Z}^{k}}\mathbb{Z}^d$ are quasi-isometric if and only if $n$ and $m$ are powers of a common number. We also discuss biLipschitz equivalences between permutational wreath products, their scaling groups, as well as the quasi-isometric classification of other halo products built out of such permutational lamplighters.

papers.title: Non-vanishing for cubic Hecke $L$-functions
papers.authors: Chantal David, Alexandre de Faveri, Alexander Dunn, Joshua Stucky
papers.abstract:
Let $\omega$ be a primitive cubic root of unity. We study the non-vanishing problem for the family of Hecke $L$-functions associated to primitive cubic characters defined over the Eisenstein quadratic number field $\mathbb{Q}(\omega)$. We prove unconditionally that a positive proportion of Hecke $L$-functions associated to the cubic residue symbols $\chi_q$ with $q \in \mathbb{Z}[\omega]$ squarefree and $q \equiv 1 \pmod{9}$ do not vanish at the central point.
  Our proof goes through the method of first and second mollified moments. The principal new contribution of this paper is the asymptotic evaluation of the mollified second moment with power saving error term. No asymptotic formula for the mollified second moment of a cubic family was known (even over function fields) prior to the writing of this paper. Our new approach makes crucial use of Patterson's evaluation of the Fourier coefficients of the cubic metaplectic theta function, Heath-Brown's cubic large sieve, and a Lindel\"{o}f-on-average upper bound for the second moment of cubic Dirichlet series that we establish.
  The significance of our result is that the (unitary) family considered does not satisfy a perfectly orthogonal large sieve bound. This is quite unlike other families of Dirichlet $L$-functions in the literature for which unconditional results are known: the symplectic family of quadratic characters and the unitary family of all Dirichlet characters $\chi \pmod{q}$. Consequently, our proof has fundamentally different features from the corresponding works of Soundararajan and of Iwaniec and Sarnak.

papers.title: No new Goormaghtigh primes up to $10^{700}$
papers.abstract: The Goormaghtigh conjecture states that the only two numbers which have two non-trivial representations as repunits are $31$ and $8191$. We call such a prime number a {\it Goormaghtigh prime}. We show that there are no other Goormaghtigh primes less than $10^{700}$.

papers.title: Forcing ramification in the relative deformation method
papers.abstract: In this paper we generalize the forcing ramification argument of Khare-Ramakrishna to the setting of the lifting result by Fakhruddin-Khare-Patrikis. In particular, we show that in the relative deformation method the finite set of primes can be chosen so that the geometric characteristic 0 lift will be ramified at each of those primes. Moreover, we show that the restrictions of this lift to the local absolute Galois groups will correspond to formally smooth points in the generic fibers of the local universal lifting rings at each prime. Eventually, we prove that the local formal smoothness at each of the primes implies the vanishing of the geometric Bloch-Kato Selmer group associated to the adjoint representation of that characteristic 0 lift.

papers.title: Units of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant $K$-theory and bundles of UHF-algebras
papers.abstract: We consider infinite tensor product actions of a finite cyclic group $G$ on the UHF-algebra $D = \text{End}(V)^{\otimes \infty}$ for a finite-dimensional projectively faithful unitary $G$-representation $V$ and determine the equivariant homotopy type of the group $\text{Aut}(D \otimes \mathbb{K})$, where $\mathbb{K}$ are the compact operators on $\ell^2(G) \otimes H_0$ for a separable Hilbert space $H_0$ with $\dim(H_0) = \infty$. We show that this group carries an equivariant infinite loop space structure revealing it as the first space of a naive $G$-spectrum. We identify this spectrum with the positive units $gl_1(KU^D)_+$ of equivariant $KU^D$-theory, which was not possible in the case of circle actions considered by Evans and the second author. Here, $KU^D$ is a $G$-spectrum representing $X \mapsto K_*^G(C(X) \otimes D)$. As a consequence the first group of the cohomology theory associated to $gl_1(KU^D)_+$ classifies equivariant $D \otimes \mathbb{K}$-bundles over finite $G$-CW-complexes.

papers.title: A Table Theorem for Surfaces with Odd Euler Characteristic
papers.abstract: We use the square peg problem for smooth curves to prove a generalized table Theorem for real valued functions on Riemannian surfaces with odd Euler characteristic. We then use this result to prove the table conjecture for even functions on the two sphere.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of invariants of syzygies of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules
papers.abstract: $(A,\mathfrak{m})$ be a complete intersection ring of codimension $c\geq 2$ and dimension $d\geq 1$. Let $M$ be a finitely generated maximal Cohen-Macaulay $A$-module and $M_i=\text{Syz}^A_{i}(M)$ be the $i$-th syzygy of $M$. Let $e^{I}_i(M)$ be the $i$-th Hilbert coefficient of $M$ with respect to an $\mathfrak{m}$-primary ideal $I$. In \cite{Quasipolynomial}, it is proved that the function $i\mapsto e^I_1(M)$ is of quasi-polynomial type with period $2$ and degree $\leq \text{cx}_A(M)-1$, where $\text{cx}_A(M)$ is the complexity of $M.$ We prove that for $I=\mathfrak{m}$, the associated polynomials have the same degree equal to $\text{cx}_A(M)-1$. For $\text{cx}_A(M)=2$ and $j=0,1$, we prove $$\lim_{i\to \infty}\dfrac{e^{\mathfrak{m}}_1(M_{2i+j})}{i}\geq \lim_{i\to \infty}\dfrac{e^{\mathfrak{m}}_0(M_{2i+j})}{i}-\lim_{i\to \infty}\dfrac{\mu(M_{2i+j})}{i}.$$ When equality holds, we prove that the set $\{\text{reg }G_{\mathfrak{m}}(M_i)\,|\, i\geq 0\}$ is bounded, where reg $G_{\mathfrak{m}}(M_i)$ is the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of $G_{\mathfrak{m}}(M_i).$

papers.title: Affine highest weight structures on module categories over quiver Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that the category of finitely generated graded modules over the quiver Hecke algebra of arbitrary type admits numerous stratifications in the sense of Kleshchev. A direct consequence is that the full subcategory corresponding to the quantum unipotent subgroup associated with any Weyl group element is an affine highest weight category. Our results significantly generalize earlier works by Kato, Brundan, Kleshchev, McNamara and Muth. The key ingredient is a realization of standard modules via determinantial modules. We utilize the technique of R-matrices to study these standard modules.

papers.title: A new look at unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction for toric manifolds
papers.authors: Jos\'e M. Mour\~ao, Jo\~ao P. Nunes, Augusto Pereira, Dan Wang
papers.abstract:
For a symplectic manifold $M$ with the Hamiltonian action of a compact Lie group $G$, we give a new perspective on the problem of unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence. We argue that this correspondence leads naturally to the introduction of what we call Fourier polarizations, whose real directions include the Hamiltonian vector fields of all invariant functions of the moment map.
  For a Fourier polarization, quantization commutes with reduction unitarily. For a general $G$-invariant polarization, $\mathcal{P}$, unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence can then be formulated in terms of the existence of a Fourier polarization, $\mathcal{P}_F$, such that the quantizations with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ and to $\mathcal{P}_F$ are unitarily equivalent.
  We describe this perspective in detail for symplectic toric manifolds, by considering symplectic reductions associated to the action of a subtorus $T^p\subset T^n$. We consider half-form quantization in Fourier (mixed) polarizations $\mathcal{P}_\infty$, whose real directions are generated by(the Hamiltonian vector fields of the)components of the $T^p$ moment map. We show that Fourier mixed polarizations of this type can be obtained by Mabuchi geodesic rays of toric K\"ahler structures, starting at a given initial structure and with velocity given by the norm square of the moment map of the torus subgroup.
  We lift these geodesic rays to the quantum bundle via generalized coherent state transforms, which define equivariant isomorphisms between quantum Hilbert spaces for the K\"ahler and Fourier polarizations, where the later are obtained at infinite geodesic time. Unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction in these cases then becomes equivalent to the unitarity of these isomorphisms. In general, however, in the toric case, these isomorphisms are not unitary.

papers.title: $P$-trivial MMP, Zariski decompositions and minimal models for generalised pairs
papers.abstract:
We develop $P$-trivial MMPs whose steps are trivial with respect to a given nef divisor $P$, and an inductive method for generalised pairs without the NQC assumption. For such an MMP, rational approximation with fixed nef data controls extremal intersection numbers and scaling numbers. Under a rationality hypothesis on $K_X+B+M-P$, we establish finiteness of adjunction coefficients under divisorial adjunctions, yielding a special termination theorem. This includes the case $P=0$.
  As applications, we prove that a projective lc g-pair $(X,B+M)$ of dimension $3$ has a minimal model if $K_X+B+M$ birationally admits a Nakayama--Zariski decomposition with nef positive part and either $K_X+B+M\equiv D\geq0$ or $M\equiv D\geq0$. The same conclusion holds for klt g-pairs in arbitrary dimension under these hypotheses, and for projective lc g-pairs of dimension $4$ with a birational Nakayama--Zariski decomposition with nef positive part and log abundant nef data. These results extend a theorem of Birkar and Hu to generalised pairs under the above hypotheses.

papers.title: Ceresa Cycles of $X_{0}(N)$
papers.abstract: The Ceresa cycle is an algebraic 1-cycle on the Jacobian of an algebraic curve. Although it is homologically trivial, Ceresa famously proved that for a very general complex curve of genus at least 3, it is non-trivial in the Chow group. In this paper we study the Ceresa cycle attached to the complete modular curve $X_{0}(N)$ modulo rational equivalence. For prime level $p$ we give a complete description, namely we prove that if $X_{0}(p)$ is not hyperelliptic, then its Ceresa cycle is non-torsion. For general level $N$, we prove that there are finitely many $X_{0}(N)$ with torsion Ceresa cycle. Our method relies on the relationship between the vanishing of the Ceresa cycle and Chow-Heegner points on the Jacobian. We use the geometry and arithmetic of modular Jacobians to prove that such points are of infinite order and therefore deduce non-vanishing of the Ceresa cycle.

papers.title: Notes on the Divisibility of Divisor Sums of Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract:
We investigate divisibility questions for the sum-of-divisors function $\sigma(C_n)$ of the Catalan numbers $C_n=(n+1)^{-1}\binom{2n}{n}$. Using the prime factors occurring to exponent one in $C_n$, we give explicit divisors of $\sigma(C_n)$ and obtain, for each fixed integer $m\geq 2$, a power $m^{R_m(n)}$ dividing $\sigma(C_n)$, with
  $R_m(n)\sim\frac{2\log 2}{\varphi(m)}\frac{n}{\log n}$.
  We further prove uniform divisibility for all moduli up to fixed powers of $\log n$ and, with the same leading constant $2\log 2$, for almost all moduli up to $\sqrt{n}$ apart from logarithmic factors. We also establish a complete classification of the integers $m\geq 2$ for which $m\mid\sigma(mk-1)$ for every $k\geq 1$, identify precisely the exceptional coprimality relations among the associated linear forms, and record a twin-prime product divisor of $\sigma(C_n)$. The arguments use standard prime-distribution results and do not assume any conjecture concerning twin primes.

papers.title: On a specialization of Toda eigenfunctions
papers.abstract: This paper studies rational functions $\mathfrak{J}_\alpha(q)$, which depend on a positive element $\alpha$ of the root lattice of a root system. These functions arise as Shapovalov pairings of Whittaker vectors in Verma modules of highest weight $-\rho$ for quantum groups and as Hilbert series of Zastava spaces, and are related to the Toda system. They are specializations of multivariate functions more commonly studied in the literature. We investigate the denominator of these rational functions and give an explicit combinatorial formula for the numerator in type A. We also propose a conjectural realization of the numerator as the Poincar\'e polynomial of a smooth variety in type A.

papers.title: Discrete $N$-particle systems at high temperature through Jack generating functions
papers.abstract: We find necessary and sufficient conditions for the Law of Large Numbers for random discrete $N$-particle systems with the deformation (inverse temperature) parameter $\theta$, as their size $N$ tends to infinity simultaneously with the inverse temperature going to zero. Our conditions are expressed in terms of the Jack generating functions, and our analysis is based on the asymptotics of the action of Cherednik operators obtained via Hecke relations. We apply the general framework to obtain the LLN for a large class of Markov chains of $N$ nonintersecting particles with interaction of log-gas type, and the LLN for the multiplication of Jack polynomials, as the inverse temperature tends to zero. We express the answer in terms of novel one-parameter deformations of cumulants and their description provided by us recovers previous work by Bufetov--Gorin [Geom. Funct. Anal. 25 (2015), no. 3, 763-814] on quantized free cumulants when $\theta=1$, and by Benaych-Georges--Cuenca--Gorin [Comm. Math. Phys. 394 (2022), no. 2, 735-795] after a deformation to continuous space of random matrix eigenvalues. Our methods are robust enough to be applied to the fixed temperature regime, where we recover the LLN of Huang [Adv. Math. 380 (2021), Paper No. 107545, 91].

papers.title: Periodic Inscription of Isosceles Trapezoids
papers.abstract: We prove that a pair of continuous disjoint periodic curves in $\mathbb{C}$ inscribes an isosceles trapezoid with any similarity type. The case of smooth curves can be identified with a Lagrangian intersection problem for a pair of Lagrangian cylinders in $\mathbb{R}\times S^1\times\mathbb{C}$, and the continuous case follows from the smooth one by a standard convergence argument.

papers.title: Derived derivations govern contraderived deformations of dg algebras over dg (pr)operads
papers.abstract: We show that Hinich's simplicial nerve of the differential graded Lie algebra (DGLA) of derived derivations of a dg algebra $A$ over a dg properad $\mathcal{P}$ is equivalent to the space of deformations of $A$ as a $\mathcal{P}_{\infty}$-algebra in Positselski's contraderived dg category. This resolves Hinich's counterexamples to the general existence of derived deformations. It also generalises his results when $A$ is homologically bounded below, since contraderived deformations are then precisely derived deformations.

papers.title: Valuation rings in simple algebraic extensions of valued fields
papers.abstract: Consider a simple algebraic valued field extension $(L/K,v)$ and denote by $\VR_L$ and $\VR_K$ the corresponding valuation rings. The main goal of this paper is to present, under certain assumptions, a description of $\VR_L$ in terms of generators and relations over $\VR_K$. The main tool used here are complete sequences of key polynomials. It is known that if the ramification index of $(L/K,v)$ is one, then every complete set gives rise to a set of generators of $\VR_L$ over $\VR_K$. We show that we can find a sequence of key polynomials for $(L/K,v)$ which satisfies good properties (called neat). Then we present explicit ``neat" relations that generate all the relations between the corresponding generators of $\VR_L$ over $\VR_K$.

papers.title: Hermitian adjacency matrices with at most three distinct eigenvalues
papers.authors: Saieed Akbari, Jonathan Aloni, Maxwell Levit, Bojan Mohar, Steven Xia
papers.abstract: We study oriented graphs whose Hermitian adjacency matrices of the second kind have few eigenvalues. We give a complete characterization of the oriented graphs with two distinct eigenvalues, showing that there are only four such graphs. We extend this result to mixed graphs. We show that there are infinitely many regular tournaments with three distinct eigenvalues. We extend our main results to Hermitian adjacency matrices defined over other roots of unity.

papers.title: High-dimensional sparse recovery from function samples - Decoders, guarantees and instance optimality
papers.authors: Moritz Moeller, Sebastian Neumayer, Kateryna Pozharska, Tizian Sommerfeld, Tino Ullrich
papers.abstract: We investigate the reconstruction of multivariate functions from samples using sparse recovery techniques. For Square Root Lasso, Orthogonal Matching Pursuit, and Compressive Sampling Matching Pursuit, we demonstrate both theoretically and empirically that they allow us to recover functions from a small number of random samples. In contrast to Basis Pursuit Denoising, the deployed decoders only require a search space $V_J$ spanned by dictionary elements indexed by $J$ and a sparsity parameter $n$ to guarantee an $L_2$-approximation error decaying no worse than a best $n$-term approximation error and the truncation error with respect to the search space $V_J$ and the uniform norm. We show that this happens simultaneously for all admissible functions if the number of samples scales as $n\log^2 n\log |J|$, coming from known bounds for the RIP for matrices built upon bounded orthonormal systems. As a consequence, we obtain bounds for sampling widths in function classes. In addition, we establish lower bounds on the required sample complexity, which show that the log-factor in $\vert J \vert$ is indeed necessary to obtain such {\em instance-optimal} error guarantees. Finally, we conduct several numerical experiments to show that our theoretical bounds are reasonable and compare the discussed decoders in practice.

papers.title: Depth of Artin-Schreier defect towers
papers.abstract: The depth of a simple algebraic extension $(L/K,v)$ of valued fields is the minimal length of the Mac Lane-Vaqui\'e chains of the valuations on $\kx$ determined by the choice of different generators of the extension. In \cite{NN25}, Nart and Novacoski characterized the defectless unibranched extensions of depth one. In this paper, we analyze this problem for towers of Artin-Schreier defect extensions. Under certain conditions on $(K,v)$, we prove that the towers obtained as the compositum of linearly disjoint defect Artin-Schreier extensions of $K$ have depth one. We conjecture that these are the only depth one Artin-Schreier defect towers and we present some examples supporting this conjecture.

papers.title: Martingale measure associated with the critical $2d$ stochastic heat flow
papers.abstract:
In [CSZ23], the authors proved the convergence of the finite dimensional time distribution of the rescaled random fields derived from the discrete stochastic heat equation of $2d$-directed polymers in random environment in the critical window. The scaling limit is called critical $2d$ stochastic heat flow (SHF).
  In this paper, we will show that the critical $2d$ SHF is a continuous semimartingale. Moreover, we will consider the martingale problem associated with the critical $2d$ SHF in a similar fashion to the super Brownian motion which is one of the well-known measure valued process. Also, we define the martingale measure associated with the critical $2d$ SHF in the sense of [Wal86, Chapter 2].
  The quadratic variation of the martingale measure gives information of the regularity of the critical $2d$ SHF.

papers.title: Uniform vector bundles over $\mathbb{P}^4$
papers.abstract: There is a long-standing conjecture which states that every uniform algebraic vector bundle of rank $r<2n$ on the $n$-dimensional projective space $\mathbb{P}^n$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$ is homogeneous. This conjecture is valid for $n\leq3$. In this paper, we classify all uniform vector bundles of rank $r<8$ over $\mathbb{P}^4$ and show that the conjecture holds for $n=4$.

papers.title: Complexity of measure-induced maps
papers.abstract: A classical result by Glasner and Weiss states that a map $f$ has zero topological entropy if and only if its measure-induced map $f_*$, defined as the push-forward of a measure, does. In this work, we use generalized entropy to distinguish the complexity of these maps and prove that the measure-induced map is strictly more complex whenever the generalized entropy of the original map is nonzero and is not an abstract order of growth. Moreover, we show that the complexity of the measure-induced map is of at most polynomial type when the nonwandering set of $f$ is finite. For homeomorphisms of infinite spaces, this bound is attained, so measure-induced maps of Morse--Smale diffeomorphisms cannot be distinguished from one another.

papers.title: A Geometric Framework for Stochastic Iterations
papers.authors: Patrick L. Combettes, Javier I. Madariaga
papers.abstract: This paper concerns models and convergence principles for dealing with stochasticity in a wide range of algorithms arising in nonlinear analysis and optimization in Hilbert spaces. It proposes a flexible geometric framework within which existing solution methods can be recast and improved, and new ones can be designed. Almost sure weak, strong, and linear convergence results are established in particular for stochastic fixed point iterations, the stochastic gradient descent method, and stochastic extrapolated parallel algorithms for feasibility problems. In these areas, the proposed algorithms exceed the features and convergence guarantees of the state of the art. Numerical applications to signal and image recovery are provided.

papers.title: On certain Lagrangian subvarieties in minimal resolutions of Kleinian singularities
papers.abstract: Kleinian singularities are quotients of $\mathbb{C}^2$ by finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$. They are in bijection with the simply-laced Dynkin diagrams via the McKay correspondence. Anti-Poisson involutions and their fixed point loci appear naturally in the classification of irreducible Harish-Chandra modules over Kleinian singularities. There are three goals of this paper. The first is to classify anti-Poisson involutions of Kleinian singularities up to conjugation by graded Poisson automorphisms. The second is to describe the scheme-theoretic fixed point loci of Kleinian singularities under anti-Poisson involutions. The third and main goal is to describe the scheme-theoretic preimages of the fixed point loci under minimal resolutions of Kleinian singularities. These preimages are singular Lagrangian subvarieties in the minimal resolutions whose irreducible components are $\mathbb{P}^1$'s and $\mathbb{A}^1$'s. Additionally, we discuss the connections between anti-Poisson involutions and Lie algebra involutions.

papers.title: Geometric conditions which imply $w^*$-normal structure
papers.authors: Deepak Gothwal, T. S. S. R. K. Rao
papers.abstract:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space. In their seminal work, Lau and Mah (\cite{LM}) study a geometric property called Lim's condition which, for separable $X$, implies that for any non-empty $w^*$-compact convex set $K \subset X^*$, any nonexpansive mapping $T: K \rightarrow K$ has a fixed point.
  In this paper, we study a weaker form of Lim's condition, which we call weak-Lim's condition. We prove that if $\ell_1 \not\hookrightarrow X$, then weak-Lim's condition on $X^*$ implies the fixed point property for non-expansive maps on weakly compact subsets of $X$. In the case of a commutative $C^\ast$-algebra, we prove that weak-Lim's condition is equivalent to Lim's condition. We show that Lim's condition characterizes $C^*$-algebras which are a $c_0$-direct sum of finite-dimensional operator spaces, while weak-Lim's condition characterizes $C^*$-algebras which are a $c_0$-direct sum of the spaces of compact operators on Hilbert spaces. For a uniform algebra, we extend a result of Lau and Mah to show that weak-Lim's condition implies that the space is finite-dimensional. In the case of an $L^1$-predual space, we show that this condition implies $k$-smoothness of the norm in the sense considered in \cite{LR}.

papers.title: Reeb orbits frequently intersecting a symplectic surface
papers.abstract: Consider a symplectic surface in a three-dimensional contact manifold with boundary on Reeb orbits (periodic orbits of the Reeb vector field). We assume that the rotation numbers of the boundary Reeb orbits satisfy a certain inequality, and we also make a technical assumption that the Reeb vector field has a particular ``nice'' form near the boundary of the surface. We then show that there exist Reeb orbits which intersect the interior of the surface, with a lower bound on the frequency of these intersections in terms of the symplectic area of the surface and the contact volume of the three-manifold. No genericity of the contact form is assumed. As a corollary of the main result, we obtain a generalization of various recent results relating the mean action of periodic orbits to the Calabi invariant for area-preserving surface diffeomorphisms.

papers.title: An Algebraic Approach to Periodicity and Complexity of Delone Sets
papers.abstract: We study the connection between local complexity and periodicity of Delone sets using an algebraic approach based on annihilators, that is, finite linear relations between translations of a configuration. We model colored Delone sets (Delone multisets) as $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations, that is, functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite range, and extend the notions of annihilators and periodizers from $\mathbb{Z}^d$-configurations to the geometric setting of Delone sets. Our main results describe the structure imposed by the existence of non-trivial annihilators. We show that any $\mathbb{R}^d$-configuration admitting non-trivial annihilators has an annihilator of a particularly simple form, namely a product of finitely many difference operators corresponding to translations in pairwise rationally independent directions.
